author: pwngh
well-prado
body:
## What

Wherever CI runs every obid-spec workflow, it now runs T3 Code's bugs too. "Every workflow" means the merge queue (on the Azure build VM since #2715), nightly, on demand, and a `full-suite` pull request.

T3 Code's bugs are the workflows under `tools/obid-spec/workflows/t3/`: bugs found in T3 Code, each turned into a test against obid. obid-spec leaves them out of every run that doesn't ask for them by name (`--tag t3`). So until now no CI run had ever run them. This adds one step, `obid-spec run --tag t3`, after the main run, only when the set is `all`.

## Why

An `expectedRed` mark says "this step fails today, because of bug #N". When the bug gets fixed, the step starts passing. obid-spec then fails the run so that someone takes the mark off. But that only happens when the workflow actually runs. The T3 workflows never ran in CI, so a fixed bug's mark could sit there indefinitely. The workflow would keep saying "still broken" about something that works, and a real regression behind a mark would go unseen.

That is what happened. On `dev` at 3f5aeff5 (2026-11-20), 5 of the 27 T3 workflows failed:
- 4 because their bugs had been fixed, but the marks were still on (#2648, #2657 twice, #2658);
- 1 on a PUBLISHING-44 branch-names step, which #2719 rewrote.

Nobody noticed until a run was done by hand.

The owner's words, 2026-11-20: **"Yes, run all"**, and on T3: **"EVERYTHING MUST WORK FLAWLESSLY THAT'S WHY WE HAVE T3CODE"**. `ci.yml` is a security path; those words are its approval, also quoted in a comment.

## How

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`:** the `obid-spec` job gets a new step after `obid-spec run`:
  - it runs `obid-spec run --tag t3`, only `if: env.OBID_SPEC_SET == 'all'`;
  - it uses the same `JOBS` as the main run: 12 at a time on `oby-azure`, 4 on GitHub's machines;
  - it uses the same `TMPDIR` and obid binary.

  A failure fails the job, and so `Check`.
- **The same fact, written where it's described:**
  - CI-67 in `docs/contracts/ci.md`: the step and its proof;
  - the `obid-spec` row in `docs/ci.md`;
  - the T3 section of `tools/obid-spec/README.md`.
- **No new workflow or scenario.** The obid-spec freeze is untouched.
- **What it costs:** on today's `dev` the T3 set is 37 workflows and took 59 s at 12 at a time on the VM.

### How we proved it

Red then green, `obid-spec run --tag t3 --jobs 12` on the build VM (`az-run`):

| obid | T3 workflows | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` 3f5aeff5 (2026-11-20, before #2719) | 27 | **5 failed** (4 "expected red … but it passed: the bug is fixed, so remove expectedRed", for #2648, #2657 ×2, #2658; plus the PUBLISHING-44 step) |
| #2719's head 14246a94 (the marks off) | 27 | 27 passed, 99 s |
| today's `dev` 624601cc, with this branch | 37 | **37 passed**, 0 failed, 59 s |

So the new step is green on today's `dev`, and it would have caught the stale marks.

Also run:
- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml`: no findings.
- `scripts/preflight.sh 624601cc` on the VM: brain and coverage passed; workflows, fmt and clippy skipped (no workflow or Rust changed); `preflight: clean`.

This PR carries `full-ci`. CI-67 doesn't put a `.github/` change in the `rust` lane, so its own run likely doesn't run obid-spec. The step's first CI run is then the next merge-queue run that reaches `rust`, or the next nightly. I'll link it here when it runs.

## Task and scenarios

CI-67 (docs/contracts/ci.md). No product behaviour changes.

## Surfaces

- [ ] obid (`core/`)
- [ ] the Electron app (`apps/electron`)
- [ ] the iPhone and Watch apps, and what they decode from obid's API (add-only)
- [ ] the API docs, `docs/api/<area>.md` (index `docs/runner-api.md`)
- [x] contracts in `docs/contracts/`: CI-67 says the step runs and gives its proof
- [ ] stored job and config files on disk
- [ ] the check (`scripts/oby-check.sh`, `tools/oby-check-blok`, `factory/checks.sh`)

## Dispatcher, not harness

none: CI only, nothing added to obid.

## Failure modes

- A T3 bug comes back: its step fails, the job fails, `Check` fails. Covered by the step itself.
- A T3 bug is fixed but its mark stays on: "expected red … but it passed" fails the step. Covered by the red run above.
- A slow or flaky T3 workflow holds up the queue. Mitigation: today they all run in 59 s; a flaky one gets marked `flaky` with its issue (OBIDSPEC-10).

## Security path

Yes: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (MERGING-15). The owner's words are quoted above and in a comment.

author: bearylogical
body:
## Problem
UOB card exports that span two statement cycles repeat a block of posted rows with the same `Ref No`. The Nov 15 export (Aug 4 – Nov 15) listed **91 rows twice**. `parsers._finalise` gave each repeat a suffixed id (`ref-X-1`) and imported it as a second transaction.

Neither the rule finder nor the AI hunt flagged these pairs: both skip any pair where the two rows have different bank references, and `ref-X` vs `ref-X-1` counted as different.

## Fix
- `parsers._finalise` drops a row that repeats a seen bank ref with the same date and amount, and says so in the statement evidence ("N rows the bank listed twice … skipped").
- `review.bank_ref` / `review.distinct_refs` compare refs without the occurrence suffix. `find_existing_duplicates` now reports such pairs as **high** confidence ("the same bank reference imported twice") and suggests deleting the suffixed copy. `hunt.loose_duplicate_pairs` and `propose_duplicate` use the same check, and the hunt prompt explains the case.

## Testing
- New tests in `test_parsers.py`, `test_review_reconcile.py` and `test_hunt.py`; all 188 backend tests pass.
- Ran the real export through the fixed parser: 91 repeats dropped, each charge imported once.

## Notes
- Deploy this together with `e1b4fac` (branch `claude/deduplication-ai-hunt-issue-a577b6`), which fixes the `_account_last4` NameError that made every `POST /review/hunt` return 500.
- The 91 doubles already in Actual will be queued by a Review scan after deploy. Deletions aren't bulk-approved, so they have to be approved one at a time.

author: smithdavedesign
body:
Two more things the live shots of the social network showed (PRD #1906; follows #1945):

**"X's world": names ran into each other and off the edge.** Each off-screen person's name went beside their dot whatever was there. On Nell Abiodun's world, "Amara Okoye" ran over "Zenobia" and "Kofi Dabo" ran off the right edge. `lib/social/world-picture.ts` `nameLayout` now places the picture's names together:
- order: the inner circle's names first, then the close ring's (under their faces), then the off-screen people's;
- each person's name goes beside their dot: the outer side, else the inner side, else under the dot;
- every name stays off the centre's face, inside the place labels round the edge, and clear of the names already down.

A name that fits nowhere is left off; the list below names everyone. Tests cover each case: a face's name and a person's, a name turned inward at the edge, an overlap moved or left off, nothing over the centre, and only the inner and close rings named.

**A phone's sky had no place names.** The canvas hid them below zoom 0.5, which is the whole sky on a phone. Now that names can't overlap (#1945), a zoomed-out sky names the 6 most shared places, where they fit. Places are ranked by how many share them, since every place's star is the same size.

After it deploys, the README's screenshots get retaken with `scripts/social-live.mjs`.

author: valdijanio
body:
G0.30k, parte a: **CI noturno de regressão**. Os laboratórios que rodam sem root, comparados com a última noite verde, com a issue "Regressão noturna". Opção escolhida à noite (rodada autônoma: a recomendada, sem esperar o escopo); os laboratórios com root ou KVM ficam na gap nova G0.30o.

## O que entra

- **Job `regression`** no `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, no runner próprio (`[self-hosted, corerouter]`), só na `main` (schedule 06:17 UTC ou à mão). Histórico na branch `nightly-data` (`nights/<data>-<commit>.<green|red>.jsonl`), escrita só pelo job; artefato `nightly-regression` com tudo; resumo no `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.
- **`scripts/nightly-regress.sh`**: compila o release, baixa sem root as ferramentas do laboratório de DNS dos pacotes assinados do Ubuntu (`apt-get download` + `dpkg-deb -x`, guardadas no disco de cache) e roda `dns-stress-lab.sh --userns --tests qps,hostile,ops --duration 10`. Escreve `metrics.jsonl`, `report.md`, `commits.txt` (desde a última noite verde) e `verdict` (`ok`, `regressed`, `broken`).
- **`dns-stress-lab.sh`** grava `metrics.jsonl` (helper `metric`): vazão na saturação e p99 na metade de cada cenário do `qps`, p99 de cada comando do `ops` com carga, RSS do daemon depois de cada teste.
- **`cargo xtask nightly compare`** (Rust, `xtask/src/nightly.rs`, testes): margem **por métrica** pela cerca superior `Q3 + 3 × IQR` das variações entre noites verdes seguidas (últimas 30), nunca abaixo de 3 %. Métrica com menos de 5 variações ainda **calibra**: fora de 15 % aparece no relatório, mas não deixa a noite vermelha. Entrada hostil: tamanhos limitados, erro com no máximo 120 caracteres da linha.
- **Issue "Regressão noturna"** (rótulo `regressao-noturna`): abre ou comenta com as métricas que pioraram, os dois valores, a margem e os commits desde a última noite verde; uma noite de volta ao nível a fecha. Laboratório que falha: a noite não conta e o `alert` existente abre "CI noturno quebrado" (agora ignora job `skipped`). Nível novo esperado: workflow à mão com `accept`.
- **Runner**: o hook aceita também `schedule` e `workflow_dispatch` em `refs/heads/main` (o `schedule` sempre roda o workflow da `main`: código confiável); testes do hook atualizados. `reset` e o subcomando novo **`cargo xtask ci-runner hooks`** regravam os hooks do checkout na VM (escreve ao lado e renomeia: um job nunca lê metade).
- `.github/actionlint.yaml` com o rótulo `corerouter` (o `actionlint` local passa em todos os workflows).

## Pesquisa

- **rustc-perf** (perf.rust-lang.org, `docs/comparison-analysis.md` do rust-lang/rustc-perf): mudança significativa acima de `Q3 + 3 × IQR` das mudanças históricas; magnitude por faixas. **Adotado**: a cerca por métrica, calibrada pelo histórico de noites verdes.
- **LLVM LNT**: a documentação pública (llvm.org/docs/lnt, `tests.html`) não descreve o método de detecção; não usado.
- **Melhorias propostas e adotadas**: margem que aprende o ruído (em vez de um número fixo, que daria alarme falso: duas rodadas do mesmo build no host carregado diferiram até 23× num p99 e 47 % em vazão, **medido**); a noite vermelha nunca vira base; aceite explícito de nível novo; lista de commits suspeitos no corpo da issue.
- **Fora (gap G0.30o)**: `ospf-stress-lab.sh` (root + BNG Blaster), `cargo xtask os boot-test` e `install-test` (QEMU + KVM). Conferido no runner: `/dev/kvm` existe (`root:kvm`), mas o `runner` não está no grupo `kvm` e não há QEMU; o OSPF precisa de root, que o runner não tem por desenho.

## Conferido

- `cargo test -p xtask nightly` (5 testes) e `cargo test -p xtask hook`.
- O roteiro inteiro neste host, duas "noites" seguidas (`--duration 5`): a 1ª `ok` (23 métricas, todas novas), gravada como verde; a 2ª comparou as 23, saiu `ok` com 12 em "Ainda calibrando" e a lista de commits desde a 1ª.
- No runner, por `cargo xtask ci-runner ssh`: o `apt-get download` dos 24 pacotes funciona sem root; `nft`, `tc`, `taskset` e `python3` estão lá.
- `cargo xtask ci --affected` (completo: mexe em `xtask/`) verde.

## Não conferido

- O job no GitHub: o `schedule` e o `workflow_dispatch` usam o workflow da `main`, então ele só roda depois do merge. Ele fica **pulado até a variável do repositório `NIGHTLY_REGRESSION=on`**, a ligar depois de `cargo xtask ci-runner hooks` (sem o hook novo o runner recusaria o `schedule`). Passos depois do merge: `cargo xtask ci-runner hooks` e `gh variable set NIGHTLY_REGRESSION -R valdijanio/CoreRouter --body on`; a primeira noite pode ser disparada à mão (Actions → nightly → Run workflow).

## Desempenho e paralelismo

Fora do caminho do produto. A comparação é O(métricas × noites) com ≤ 30 noites. O laboratório leva ~5 min por noite com 10 s por medição (**estimado** pelos ~3 min com 5 s neste host).

## Extras e riscos

- Risco: o runner divide a VM com os lotes da fila; um lote na madrugada aumenta o ruído (a margem calibra, mas uma noite com lote pode passar da cerca). Mitigação: só métrica calibrada reprova; o comentário traz os números para o operador julgar.
- Risco: o job escreve na branch `nightly-data` com o `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`contents: write`, só nesse job).

author: avifenesh
body:
Stacked on #1395 (and #1396 at e6f9dc4e40, merged in). Inkling 2 Mini onboarding: the native sm_120a GPU route (plan PR6 + PR7). Receipts: `research/modelplan-onboarding-inkling2mini-20261121/gpu-route/README.md`.

## What it is
- `src/inkling2_gpu.rs` + `cu/inkling2_gpu.cu`: the typed inkling2 plan on one GPU. The weights stay resident as stored (17.59 GiB). The tensor contract is bound before upload. There are 48 cache slots, relative-bias attention with the per-query sink (fixed shared memory, no context-sized scratch), and double-buffered conv histories so that a forward is atomic. The loop controllers, depth mix and the softcap-30 truncated head are included. Runtime policy reads the plan.
- The declared class (the default) runs on #1396's act-quant kernels. The float class is bring-up only.
- `ink2-gpu` runner (tape scoring, forced router and MoE input, chunkings, `--inject-failure`, `--attn-probe`, `--contract-check`, memory accounting with driver-free admission) and `ink2-gpu-gate` (18 cells, also in kernel-check).

## Results (RTX 5090 Laptop, sm_120a)
- **Float vs f64 oracle:** p2 worst slot 2.8e-6. p3 (8k) worst slot 2.1e-6, KL 8.2e-13, every router row equal.
- **p3 drift:** the drift against the f32 oracle is the f32 oracle's own error. The f32 oracle shows the same pattern against f64. The attention probe puts the GPU's attention 2.5e-8 from f64 over 8260 keys.
- **Declared, after the #1396 merge:**
  - forced MoE: p1 has 42/48 slots bit-equal to the simulation; p2 worst slot 6.8e-4.
  - KL vs the f64 oracle: p2 0.098, p3 0.026.
  - the kernel cell is bit for bit with the reference block, with red arms.
- **Invariants, both classes:** chunked prefill vs one token per call is bit-identical, and atomicity holds (0 of 2784 digests differ after an injected failure).
- **Red arms rejected:** dequant-bf16, conv-state, wrong floor, commit-on-error, the two declared MoE arms, and the contract arms. ties-high is caught by the constructed-tie cell.
- **Memory:** the ceiling is 75,562 positions with f32 KV at chunk 512 (driver free 4.61 GiB before KV). Larger contexts are refused before allocation.
- **Timed decode at full clocks**, with clamp check and 250 ms telemetry, N=3: 4.34 tok/s float, 5.36 tok/s declared.

## Open
- Routing: lane F traced the router-scale anomaly to out-of-distribution scoring; in distribution the reference router is at its optimum. The hold is lifted, and the route keeps the reference routing.
- No multi-sequence batching yet.
- The drafter is not resident.
- Performance is lane P's work.
- Landing needs the sm_120a and sm_121a cell records: build.rs, Cargo.toml, lib.rs, kernel_check.rs and the #1396 fixtures reach every target. The new change-impact rule keeps the route files themselves pack-local once it is on main.

No native qualification: development push. Support state unchanged.

author: finrei28
body:
The admin dashboard's four figures were each counting the wrong thing. Now they count today in Auckland, and sales count what customers paid after discounts. The cards sit four across on a desktop, each with a line saying what it counts.

The owner chose what to fix, how Current orders and Collected today count, the wording in both languages and the layout on 2026-11-21. They also asked that sales show what customers actually pay.

## What was wrong

| Card | Counted | Now counts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current Orders | Every PENDING order of any day. An order the kitchen had accepted dropped out, and a booking for next week counted. | **Current orders:** every order not collected or cancelled that is due by the end of today, overdue ones included. It matches the kitchen app's Upcoming and Current lists together. |
| Orders Completed | Every order ever marked ready (`completedAt` set), all time. An order collected without being marked ready was never counted. | **Collected today:** orders picked up today, by `pickedUpAt`, as the kitchen app's Past Orders files them. |
| Sales Today | Orders placed on the server's day. That is UTC on Vercel, so in daylight saving "today" ran from 1 PM to 1 PM: for the first hour of trading it still showed the afternoon before. | **Sales today:** orders placed today, Auckland time. |
| Sales Today, Total Sales | `priceInCents` alone. An app order stores its price before discounts there and the discount in `discountedAmountInCents`, so app discounts counted as sales. | What customers paid: price less discount. A website order stores what was paid and no discount, so the same sum is right for both. |

- **"Today" is the Auckland day**, from `todayNZ`/`startOfDayNZ`/`endOfDayNZ` in `~/lib/aucklandDay`. The order server fixed the same 1 PM-to-1 PM bug in its own Past Orders.
- **"What customers paid" follows the order server.** `calculateCartPrice` in the order server charges `beforeDiscountInCents - discountInCents` and stores those two in the two columns. An order paid entirely in points comes to $0.
- **A cancelled order is still not a sale,** as before.

## How

- `~/lib/dashboard` holds the day (`dashboardDay`), the money (`paidInCents`) and the open statuses, with no database, so CI can test them.
- `~/server/dashboard` (`getDashboardFigures`) runs the four reads in parallel. It is outside the orders router because Vitest cannot load that router.
- `order.getDashboardFigures` replaces the four procedures `getCurrentOrders`, `getCompletedOrders`, `getSalesToday` and `getTotalSales`. Nothing else called them. One query means the cards always agree on what "now" is, and the page prefetches one query instead of four.
- **The cards** (`dashboardCard.tsx`):
  - Each shows a large figure and a line under it saying what it counts, in both languages. The sales lines say "after discounts".
  - The layout is one column on a phone, two by two from `sm` and four across from `xl`.
  - They sit in the navbar's own container (`max-w-7xl px-4`). `container` has no padding here and put them against both edges at 1280px.

## Tests

Written first, against a stub that kept the old behaviour. 10 of the 13 new cases failed on it.
- `src/lib/dashboard.test.ts` (7, unit): the Auckland day at lunchtime on a date UTC still calls the day before; both ends of the day; winter time; price less discount for an app order, a website order and no orders; the open statuses.
- `src/server/dashboard.integration.test.ts` (6, test database):
  - current orders by status and day;
  - collected today by `pickedUpAt`, including one never marked ready;
  - today's sales from Auckland midnight, leaving out yesterday at 9 PM, which falls on the same UTC date;
  - sales after discounts, including an order paid in points;
  - total sales leaving out cancelled orders;
  - an empty shop.

Results:
- New suites: 13/13 pass with the process in UTC, Pacific/Auckland and America/Los_Angeles.
- The suite as CI runs it: 785 passed, 127 skipped.
- With the test database (`eversweet_web_test`): 912 passed, none skipped.
- `npm run typecheck` passes. ESLint is clean on the changed files, and `check:tokens` passes.

## Screenshots

Before and after at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440, in English and Chinese (private): https://claude.ai/artifact/LGeNhKnjyFF89aUdhx8ax3

- **Before** is a checkout of `main`, **after** is this branch, both from a local `next dev` against `eversweet_dev`.
- Five sample orders were added for today so the figures had something to count, then deleted.
- The page lists both sets of figures on the same data. Before said 1 order completed and $25.40 from 2 orders today; after says 2 collected and $74.30 from 5. No hydration errors in any shot.

## Scan

Eight files in three commits: the figures and their tests, the dashboard switched to them, and a CLAUDE.md sharp edge.
- **Nothing else called the four removed procedures** (searched `src`). The page's prefetch and the component's `useSuspenseQuery` use the same input-less query, so the cache key matches.
- **The four reads still run in parallel,** now inside one procedure (`Promise.all`), where the page used to prefetch four procedures in parallel. That is the same number of database round trips, and the same pooled connections at once.
- **Overdue orders stay current until someone deals with them.** An order never accepted counts every day until it is collected or cancelled, as it stays on the kitchen app's Upcoming list. If production holds old unaccepted test orders, they show here too, and cancelling them in the staff app clears them.
- **Not changed, and out of scope:** the admin Orders and Past Orders tables still show `priceInCents`, so an app order appears at its price before discounts. The Orders page lists PENDING and READY only, so an accepted order or one being made is missing there. Both are offered as follow-ups.
- **The new files are Prettier-clean.** `page.tsx` differs from Prettier only in the CRLF line endings of this Windows checkout; git stores LF.
- **Admin layout:** only the dashboard's own container and grid change. The navbar and the other pages are untouched.

## Rollout

Website only; no migration and no order server change. The new procedure reads columns that already exist.

## Review

Greptile 5/5 on 24a99e4, with no findings and no inline comments. All five checks pass: lint and typecheck, verify-legal, Greptile and both Vercel checks. CI skips the database suites, which ran locally as above. No replies were posted on GitHub.

author: sjawhar-agent[bot]
body:
On 2026-11-21 Sami called the office unit twice with "Wispr, what's the status of INFRA-1027?", and one call went unanswered. The live transcript wrote the name as "Mister", "Miss Burr", "Lispr" and "Miss Murray" across today's calls, and only "Whisper" woke it. Deepgram's Nova-3 keyterms take a spelling. "Wispr" is no word the model knows how to sound, but "Whisper" is, and the wake phrase already reads "Whisper" at the start of a sentence before a comma, the end of the text, or a question word.

The live request now carries "Whisper" as a keyterm right after "Wispr". The wake phrase also reads "Lispr" as the name. "Mister" and the like are a person's address, so they still never wake it.

## Measured first

A probe in this change spoke calls and meeting sentences with Deepgram's Aura-2 voices. It sent each through Deepgram's live endpoint with the office unit's exact options: Nova-3, the default configuration, a speaker, and Dispatch's 21 project keys. It ran each twice: as main sends them, and with "Whisper" added. The Supervisor's wake detection ran on every interim and final result.

- Calls: "Whisper, …", spelled as people say the name, 4 phrasings in each of 10 voices (40 calls).
- Sentences that are no call: 20 meeting-like sentences with "whisper" or "mister" in the middle, each in 2 voices (40 sentences).

| | Calls that woke Wispr | False wakes, sentences that are no call |
|---|---|---|
| Main: no "Whisper" keyterm, and "Lispr" not read | 39 of 40 | 0 of 40 (110 s of speech) |
| "Lispr" read, no "Whisper" keyterm | 40 of 40 | 0 of 40 |
| This change: "Whisper" keyterm, and "Lispr" read | 40 of 40 | 0 of 40 |

- **Without the keyterm:** of the 30 calls whose final begins with the name, Nova-3 wrote "Wispr" 18 times, "Whisper" 11 times and "Lispr" once. That one was "Lispr, go ahead.", the same in every result of the call, and main's wake phrase misses it.
- **With the keyterm:** all 30 such finals begin with "Whisper". The other 10 calls begin "Hey, …" or put the name in a result of its own, and woke both ways.
- **Sentences that are no call:**
  - All 20 sentences with "whisper" in the middle kept the word in their final, in both runs. None woke Wispr, because the name only counts at the start of a sentence. A rule that ignored the position would have counted all 20, so the counter could see a false wake.
  - All 20 sentences with "Mister" kept "Mister" in both runs: the keyterm turned none into "Whisper".

Synthetic speech is cleaner than the room. None of today's room mishearings ("Mister", "Miss Burr") happened on it.

## False wakes over hours of meeting speech

A second probe spoke 19 meetings of the AMI corpus, from their manual transcripts: the meetings whose own speakers say "whisper" or "mister". Each speaker spoke in an Aura-2 voice, and one of the 20 sentences above came every 4 minutes. That is 11.80 hours of speech, with 160 of those sentences. The probe streamed it through the same live options, in 78 sockets of 10 minutes per run, with and without the keyterm. It counted a false wake for each stretch of results, up to a final, of which any woke the Supervisor's detector.

| | False wakes in 11.80 h | Per hour | One-sided 95% upper bound | Finals that say "whisper" or "mister" |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main: no "Whisper" keyterm | 1 | 0.08 | 0.40 per hour | 188 of 10,187 |
| This change: "Whisper" keyterm | 0 | 0.00 | 0.25 per hour | 187 of 10,220 |

Both upper bounds are below the spec's 0.5 false wakes per hour. The one false wake, without the keyterm, was an AMI speaker's "Oops. Whisper won't be transcribed": the live transcript wrote "Wispr won't …", and the detector took the name at the start of a sentence. That shows the counter can see a false wake. With the keyterm, no result woke.

The runs used two Deepgram member keys minted under the admin key on sami-devbox, each for its run only: `api_key_id` c1523ea7-b414-4225-b1e7-d8612204e9de (one hour) and 003782e2-798b-41df-938a-8a06752da08e (three hours). Each was deleted when its run ended, and each delete returned success. No recording left the office unit; the AMI speech is synthetic.

## Verification

- RAN (sami-devbox, `TestProbeWakeKeyterm`, 271 s): the call results above. The per-run transcripts of the synthetic clips are on the devbox, in `/mnt/nvme/sami/ghost-wispr-evidence/wake-probes/wake/out/`.
- RAN (sami-devbox, `TestProbeWakeFalseRate`, 5,565 s): the false-wake table above. The summary and every waking stretch are in `/mnt/nvme/sami/ghost-wispr-evidence/wake-probes/wake/falserate/`, and the AMI transcripts it read in `/mnt/nvme/sami/ghost-wispr-evidence/wake-probes/ami/`.
- RAN: the wake phrase and keyterm tests (`internal/wake/transcript`), watched failing before the change: Lispr not read, no Whisper after Wispr.
- RAN (rebased onto main at 1e5002c: #133, #151, and the join's keyterm Configure): main's join tests (TestKeytermsChangeOnJoin, TestOneConfigureWaitsForItsAnswer, TestARefusedListIsNotTheStreams, TestASecondRefusalWaitsForTheNextChange, and the command's TestAJoinConfiguresTheLiveStream, TestARefusedConfigureIsSentAgain, TestASecondRefusalWaitsForTheNextChange) expected lists with the wake phrases alone, and failed on the rebased change with "Whisper" in them; a commit adds "Whisper" after "Wispr" to the lists they expect. On sami-devbox (a git checkout of 21bbef7, Go 1.25.0, race detector, 2 CPUs): the wake phrase tests passed 20 of 20 and the keyterm and Configure tests 10 of 10, every one of the 46 packages with tests passed (`go test -race -tags kws ./...`), golangci-lint 0 issues, gofmt and `go vet ./...` clean; CI is green at 21bbef7. `TestAPausesSettlementIsWorkTheStopWaitsFor`, which failed once at a load average near 900 before the rebase, passed 5 of 5.
- BLOCKED until the office unit runs this head: a call by voice in the room.

author: tiendc
body:
Follow-up to #398, which merged while this was being written. The guard I fixed there still had the hole it was closing.

## The hole

`--ignored` going missing is written by libtest as

```
test chromes_http3_goes_through_tracewing_on_a_real_adapter ... ignored, wants `unshare` and Chrome, ...
```

which begins **exactly** like the line a run that happened writes. So #398's

```sh
grep -q '^test chromes_http3_goes_through_tracewing_on_a_real_adapter \.\.\.' live.log
```

matches a skipped test too — and would have passed in precisely the case the guard exists for: `--ignored` dropped, nothing run, `cargo test` exits 0, `linux-e2e` green with the live test never executed.

## The fix, and that it can fail

Two claims, said separately because they are two:

```sh
N='chromes_http3_goes_through_tracewing_on_a_real_adapter'
grep -q "^test $N \.\.\." live.log
! grep -q "^test $N \.\.\. ignored" live.log
```

Proved against two logs of the two shapes:

| log | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the test ran (`... ` then the door's address, then `ok`) | accepted | accepted |
| the test was skipped (`... ignored, wants …`) | **accepted** | refused |

## How it was found

By reading the passing run's own log rather than trusting that it went green. The run that made #398 mergeable passed on the real line, so nothing failed and nothing would have — the hole only opens the day somebody drops `--ignored`, which is the day the guard is the only thing left.

For the record of what #398's `linux-e2e` history actually was, since a green run now hides it:

| run | the Chrome test | the step |
|---|---|---|
| `5ba206f` | **failed** (page assertion) | 101, cargo's |
| `9918fa8` | **failed** (`net::ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR`) | 101, cargo's |
| `bb333a0` | passed, 24 s | 1, the old grep rejecting a pass |
| `143f60b` | passed | green |

So the Chrome test has failed two of the four times it has run on a hosted runner. **That is still open**, and this PR does not address it. It passes here every time: alone, in the runner's own sequence with every live test, pinned to one core, and with an unreachable IPv6 offered first in the test's `/etc/hosts` — so the difference is the runner, not the ordering, the speed, or the address family. #398's assertion now carries what was caught by the way in and what reached the real server, so the next failure should say which half of the chain broke.

body:
## What changed

- **README rewritten as a short landing page** (~450 → ~170 lines): a one-line pitch, "Your own cloud agent station", then a plain-language "What is Meridian?", a feature list, a desktop-first quick start, supported agents, a short "How it works", and a brief security note.
- **"What is Meridian?"** introduces Station, Capsule, and Thread. It explains lead Threads as long-running conversations that keep context and hand work to subagents, and says that each Capsule and Thread runs the real agent you picked (including mixed agents, like a Claude Code lead with Codex subagents).
- **Wording fixes:** Capsules are now called sandboxes (container, gVisor, or microVM, per ADR 0050), and the desktop app, browser, and terminal are presented as equal clients.
- **Features added:** routines (linked to ADR 0057) and Project notes.
- **New `docs/install.md`** holds everything moved out of the README, mostly word for word: Homebrew, the desktop app (updates and uninstall), release archives, building from source, provider connections, and troubleshooting.
- **Screenshots:** retook `ui-home.png` and `ui-thread.png` from the current UI, and added `ui-lead.png` (a lead with subagents).
- `docs/docker-development.md` pointed at a README section that no longer exists; it now links to the Compose section in `operations.md`.

## Why

The old README read as a full manual. The goal is a page that explains Meridian in simple terms and gets people to try it, with the detail one click away.

## Notes for reviewers

- The security note keeps the "not for untrusted multi-tenant hosting" warning that `AGENTS.md` requires, and narrows an approval claim to "no branch is pushed or pull request opened until you approve the exact changes".
- The screenshots come from the frontend's dev-only `?shots=1` fixture, captured at 1440×900 @2x with headless Chrome. In the lead fixture, the tab says "Idle" while the chat shows "Working…", a small fixture inconsistency.
- `ui-harnesses.png`, `ui-team.png`, and `desktop-import.png` are no longer referenced anywhere and are still from the older UI. I left them in place.
- Docs-only change; no code touched.

author: clintongormley
body:
## What changes

Maintainers can prepare a declaration and tag a patch or new minor on a protected maintenance branch cut from an older release of the same major. The release command checks that the latest lower stable release is in the branch's history before asking for a signature and again before tagging. It requires green push CI at the exact branch tip.

The publish job checks the tag's Git history and branch protection, leaving it eligible for a retry if a sibling release is tagged later. The release keeps its own immutable declaration. Signing, producer checks and full tag CI still gate publication. A maintenance release leaves GitHub's Latest slot alone.

Use the release command for every tag. Its predecessor check applies before the tag is created. The repository owner must add the maintenance ruleset from the release guide before using this path. The existing declaration blocker still applies, and the first live publication remains open. The A950 backlog links to the release guide.

## Request and review

The owner's words of 20 November at 22:45, as relayed in Lane F questions.md, were “we should be able to release bug fixes on any older branch at any time. and even a new minor releae on an older major version”. Claude reviewed the one-page plan and the watcher cleared it at 04:47. The watcher resolved the same-major rule and the publish retry rule at 05:15. Claude's two run-it reviews took 468 and 328 seconds.

## Changed test checks

- `scripts/ci-workflow.test.mjs:4337` and `scripts/check-signoff.test.mjs:317` now require the main and maintenance branch triggers from the plan. The PR checkout still pins the head, and the sign-off step still runs on PRs and pushes to main.
- `scripts/ci-workflow.test.mjs:4263` and `:5679` now require full Git history with blobs fetched on demand for root guards and publishing. The prior check used a shallow checkout with tags, which could give the wrong answer about release ancestry.
- `scripts/ci-workflow.test.mjs:7556` now requires the publish step to admit protected maintenance history and refuse incomplete or unprotected history. The real Git cases still require the exact remote tag annotation and a direct commit pointer.

## Verification

A real `pnpm release tag 1.2.1` pushed the annotated tag to a disposable local Git remote after the normal hook passed, including seven package typechecks. GitHub and the declaration validator were stand-ins for that rehearsal. The unchanged fiscal golden and immutability suites passed 20 tests. Removing the higher-version refusal or the protected-branch check made the corresponding tests fail in a disposable checkout.

The fresh read of the fixes took 134 seconds. A real Git probe also confirmed that the CLI refuses a new major before asking for a signature. Six focused suites passed 932 tests with an unrelated Git directory set in the caller. Root verification passed 23,193 tests with one skip and reached 98% statements, 98.60% lines, 98.83% functions and 96.58% branches.

author: olety
body:
Fixes [RECOVERY-BOX-CANCEL-RELEASE-STARTED-AT] (P2, OPUS-WAYBACK; asked by OPUS-OWNERKEY-P1 for oneiron-cloud #228, review round 2 P1 2). Base: main 54f7ce11c55b, after native stack #9866 landed in train 1248.

A control-plane snapshot restore gives the recovery box's release receipts out again. A retried owner Cancel that names only the old receipt can therefore void a new release that took the same receipt. oneiron-cloud #228 makes POST /node/recovery-box/cancel take `release_started_at` (integer ms: the `at` of the recovery_started act the device saw) beside `release_receipt`, and only together with it. With both, the box voids only the release that matches both. With the receipt alone, the box keeps today's match on the receipt.

## What it does
- **New type.** `RecoveryBoxRelease { receipt: u64, started_at_ms: Option<u64> }` (re-exported at `oneiron::world_keys`) names the pending release a Cancel stops. A start cannot travel without its receipt, which is the box's own rule.
- **Proof.** In `RecoveryBoxCancelProof`, `release: Option<RecoveryBoxRelease>` replaces `release_receipt: Option<u64>`. `Vault::sign_recovery_box_cancel_as(authority, release)` takes it.
- **Transcript.** The signed transcript gains tag 2: the receipt, then the start, each as a BE u64. Tags 0 (none, eight zero bytes) and 1 (the receipt) are unchanged. A Cancel without a start therefore signs exactly the bytes it signed before, and an owner device that reads no start still verifies at a node that knows starts. The tag fixes the length, so no two layouts collide.
- **Node.** `Vault::cancel_box_recovery_as` checks the proof as before: owner, own live owner key and not R's kind, `verify_strict` over the transcript, and 300 s freshness. Because the start is signed, a start that is changed or dropped after signing fails the signature check. The node then passes `proof.release` (receipt and start, as signed) to the box.
- **Trait.** `RecoveryBoxHold::cancel_pending_box_release(&self, cancelled_by, release: Option<RecoveryBoxRelease>)`. `NoRecoveryBox` and the two test box stubs are changed to match.

## For the box client
`HypnosRecoveryBoxHold` (OPUS-WAYBACK-BOX, #9198, not on main) sends `release.receipt` as `release_receipt` and `release.started_at_ms`, when it is Some, as `release_started_at`. Its route parses both into `RecoveryBoxRelease` and refuses a start that comes without a receipt. Every caller of `sign_recovery_box_cancel_as` / `cancel_box_recovery_as` on main is a test. No server route calls them yet.

## Tests (`crates/oneiron/tests/owner_root_recovery_wait.rs`)
- New: `a_cancel_names_its_release_by_receipt_and_start_and_the_box_gets_both`. The device signs a receipt and a start, and the box gets both as signed. A start moved by 1 ms after signing, or dropped after signing, is refused as `CANCEL_PROOF_NOT_VALID`, and nothing reaches the box.
- New: `a_cancel_without_a_start_signs_the_bytes_it_signed_before`. All three transcript layouts are built by hand. Tags 0 and 1 are byte for byte main's layout before this PR.
- The six box Cancel tests now use `receipt_only(n)` where they used `Some(n)`. Their asserts are unchanged.

Red = `opus-wayback/recovery-box-cancel-release-started-at-red` a00bc2d48b55: this head plus a mutation in which the transcript signs a receipt with a start as a receipt alone. By reading, the two new tests fail there and the rest pass. Green = this head, pin `opus-wayback/recovery-box-cancel-release-started-at-pin1` 964191540be1: all pass. Both runs are queued as proof runs after the merge (READY-PROOF-VS-MERGE-BAR = A):
`RUSTFLAGS="--cfg oneiron_test_support" cargo test --locked -p oneiron --all-features --test owner_root_recovery_wait`.

## Notes
- Stored change: keep. No row and no stored field: the proof travels to the node and is never stored.
- Wire compatibility: the transcript for a Cancel without a start is unchanged, so proofs from devices that read no start still verify.
- Verb: none. A box Cancel is an owner act, and no Grant action names it.
- Files: `authority/recovery_hold/box_cancel.rs` (247 -> 281), `world_keys/vault_key/recovery_preset/recovery_box_hold.rs` (211 -> 228), three re-export lists (`world_keys/mod.rs`, `world_keys/vault_key.rs`, `world_keys/vault_key/recovery_preset.rs`), and two test files. No file crosses 800 lines (`vault_key.rs` was already 825 on main; the rustfmt reflow adds one line). rustfmt 1.100 is clean; NAME-CHECK hits=0.

author: dalaun
body:
Before: the Keystone and cascade checks could tell whether a spend traces to the mission, and S1 caught a direct benefit to a disqualified person. Nothing graded a proposed spend against the rest of the private foundation rules (IRC 4941 to 4945), and nothing looked for moves that pass the rules but bend their intent.

After: every proposed spend gets one of four outcomes (allow, block, needs counsel, insufficient) from four stages: mission trace (the existing Keystone shapes, reused), the letter of Chapter 42, a hack test (Schneier, *A Hacker's Mind*: "Hacks follow the rules of a system but subvert its goals or intent"), and the outcome. Every check names the societal pressure that enforces it (*Liars and Outliers*), and P1 fails any check that only conscience enforces. 23 synthetic proposals are graded against an answer key, and CI runs them.

How: `decision/spend-decision-model.ttl` holds the outcomes, pressures and the check catalog (stage, outcome on failure, enforcer, source). `decision/spend-decision-shapes.ttl` holds the SHACL checks for stages 0, 2 and 3 plus P1. `decide_spend.py` runs the Keystone shapes on the node each proposal assesses and the new shapes on the proposal, takes the most severe outcome (block > insufficient > needs counsel > allow), and grades against `tests/decision/expected.ttl`. A bounded-scorer slot (the Jev pattern: no / yes / cannot tell) can only raise an outcome. The plain-language page is `docs/wiki/Spend-Decision-Model.md`, linked from Home. The Keystone workflow gains two steps.

Findings worth reading first (the wiki page has sources):
1. Since 1969, self-dealing is a flat rule; IRS training text says it is "immaterial whether the transaction results in a benefit or a detriment to the private foundation." So a fair-priced deal with an insider is a block, not a counsel question. The hack test matters at the edges: siblings are outside 4946(d)'s "members of family", minority stakes sit under the 35 percent line, and value can pass through a third party.
2. The family trust and business trust need a disqualified-person answer from counsel; the model treats them as disqualified until then.
3. The existing A1 asset-to-program check would block an ordinary endowment investment. Investments skip stage 1 here; keeping or narrowing A1 is the owner's call.

Not verified: Treasury regulations, the 4943 exceptions, the public-inspection rule, and the Schneier books themselves (read through his essay and a review). Design and education, not legal or tax advice; counsel reviews.

Local run: `python3 decide_spend.py` → 23 proposals, all match the answer key; `python3 validate_keystone.py` unchanged and passing; OWL lint 0 problems.

Draft only. The owner merges.

body:
A selector that matches nothing on a page whose render had settled came back as `errorCode: "timeout"` ("Timeout after 137500ms"). The caller was told to raise a `timeout` that could not help.

Example: `{"url":"https://example.com","formats":["markdown"],"cssSelector":"h1"}`. example.com has no h1; its `# Example Domain` heading is the `<title>` prepend.
- The LightPanda snapshot is flagged truncated, because the nav budget fired after the page had settled (`settled=true in_flight=0`).
- The empty selection makes the markdown empty.
- `is_empty_truncated_render` read that pair as a render that ran out of time.
- 137500 ms is the ladder-extended request budget, not time spent.

What changes:
- A truncated render with empty markdown now answers as the selector miss (`success:false`, warning `selector_no_match`) when all three hold:
  - the page had settled (`budget_settled`)
  - the snapshot is not thin by the renderer's own measure (`detector::looks_like_thin_html`, which ignores script and style)
  - the caller's selector matched nothing
- Still a timeout:
  - an unsettled render, where the element may still have been loading
  - a settled shell with no text
  - any empty render without a selector miss
- Walls are decided before this check, as before.
- `crw_extract::SELECTOR_NO_MATCH` names the warning.

Both outcomes are failures for billing: `/v1` returns `success:false`, and `/v2` returns `SCRAPE_ALL_ENGINES_FAILED`.

author: nathanvale
body:
## Summary

The symbol gate tests in `tests/template/names-check/symbol-gate.test.ts` run git, child processes and `stagedTexts` calls, each bounded at 4 s, 10 s or 20 s, under Bun's 5 s default test timeout. That breaks `docs/standards/test-harness.md`: every child bound must sit below the test timeout, and the test timeout must cover the sum of sequential child bounds.

Each such test now takes a `processWatchdog(n)` timeout (n x 20 s + 10 s), as the sibling tests in `check-names.test.ts` do. This follows the kernel fix (commit f30c032, PR 74), with every sequential bound counted in this file, including the git calls inside the scripts. Pure in-process tests are untouched. No script and no other file changed. Two commits: the watchdog, then the resizing.

## Evidence

Bounds counted: fixture `git()` 4 s (`sourceRepository` 16 s: init, add, commit, add); each git read in `glossary.ts` and `staged-texts.ts` 10 s (`stagedTexts` 20 s); `check(["--staged"])` 8 calls, 80 s; `check(["--against", "HEAD"])` 3 calls, 30 s; spawned fixture children 20 s each.

Sum of sequential bounds, then timeout:

- 11 tests that use only `sourceRepository` with non-staged checks: 16 s, 30 s (n=1). These are refuses exported name, camel-case plurals, default export, leading underscores, immediate members, destructured keys, async returns, public method returns, locals and private members, constructor parameters and unions, consumed exports.
- Recorded hits independent of line: 16 s, 30 s (n=1).
- Hosted `--against` check: 16 + 4 + 4 + 30 = 54 s, 70 s (n=3).
- Missing surface files: 16 + 5 git reads (50) = 66 s, 90 s (n=4).
- Surface, glossary and hits from the index: 16 + 80 = 96 s, 110 s (n=5).
- Recorded approval: 16 + 4 + 4 + 2 x 30 = 84 s, 110 s (n=5).
- Production names check entry: 3 fixture children + 1 add + 1 check = 5 x 20 = 100 s, 110 s (n=5).
- Re-exports followed: 20 + staged `publicNameProblems` with 4 re-exported files (10 + 20 + 40 + 20 = 90) = 110 s, 130 s (n=6).
- Partially staged source: 16 + 4 + 4 + 20 + 80 + 4 + 80 = 208 s, 230 s (n=11).

Each timeout is the smallest n with at least 10 s of slack over the sum.

Gates, with `KERNEL_REPOSITORY` set to an absolute path of a kernel clone at `origin/main`:

- `bun run check`: pass, 1190 tests, 0 fail.
- `bun run check:commits origin/main`: 2 commits, all green.
- `bun run fault-replay --changed-since origin/main`: 10 of 10 planted faults killed.

## Parked follow-ups (rule 13)

P3:

- `processWatchdog(n)` calls pass a bare run count; a named constant or a
  comment with each test's sequential sum would make the sizing readable.

## Merge Danger

Low. Test-only change. A timeout is a ceiling, so passing tests are unaffected. Nothing in the README, version or release surface changes.

author: dev-perceptric
body:
Stops raw database and server errors from showing in the app, and makes deploys add new tables on their own.

## Why
The Brand page showed "Could not find the table 'public.brand_kits' in the schema cache". Two causes: the app printed database text as is, and the live database never got migrations 021 and later, because deploys never ran the SQL files.

## What changed
**Plain errors**
- `src/lib/plainError.ts`, copied from Omniscient. Our own short lines pass. Database, setup, network and code messages become "Something went wrong. Try again." The original goes to the console once.
- `ErrorText`, `callApi` and `getApi` run every message through it, so all 45 error lines are covered, now and later.
- `src/lib/routeError.ts`: logs the full error to the server log and Sentry, answers with one plain line. Used in workspace delete and invite, billing checkout and portal.
- Team, Social, Approvals and Brand used to hide a failed load or show it raw. They now show a plain line ("We couldn't load approvals. Try again.").
- The error line is now one short red line with an alert icon. The pink box is gone.

**Database updates on deploy**
- `web/scripts/migrate.mjs` runs schema.sql and the numbered migrations the database hasn't had yet, each in a transaction, and records them in `public.schema_migrations` (RLS on, no policies). An advisory lock keeps two runs apart.
- A database made by hand before this (like the live one) has no record yet. schema.sql counts as done, and every numbered migration runs again. That's safe: each one only adds what is missing. The test proves it.
- `deploy/deploy-web.sh` runs it in the new image after `pull` and before `up -d`. If it fails, the old app keeps running. It only runs when `MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL` is set in the server's `.env`. The app container never gets that value.
- The image now carries `supabase/` and `scripts/migrate.mjs`. `pg` moved to runtime packages.

## How I tested
- lint, typecheck, `npm test` (930 + 153 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, with a local Postgres so the RLS and migrate tests ran) and build.
- New tests: `tests/plainError.test.ts` (messages plus guards: no route sends `e.message`, no screen hides a failed load), `tests/migrate.test.ts` (order, a fresh database, a hand-made database run twice, ledger is server only), and deploy order checks in `tests/deploy.test.ts`.
- Ran `migrate.mjs` from a production-style install (`npm ci --omit=dev`) against a fresh database: 24 files, then "up to date".
- Browser check: the Brand page with a missing table now shows "We couldn't load your brand. Try again."

## Setup after merge
Add `MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL` to `/docker/morningtelos-web/.env` on the server. Until then, deploys skip the database step and say so.

body:
Fixes #3845

## Why

A clipboard can copy music and sound-effect clips, but gap paste rejected those tracks. Repeating a cue required rebuilding the source audio or cutting multiple clips out of it.

## What changed

- The existing Paste command accepts music and sound-effect tracks in gap mode. Each paste creates separate clips on the named tracks.

## Scope

- Gap paste uses the existing per-track overwrite and Undo behavior. Ripple paste continues to accept dialogue clips.

- On the installed CLI, the base refused gap paste for both roles. The fix placed the same recording at 4 and 8 seconds, moved only the second copy, and restored each prior state with one Undo.
- The CLI proof preserved dialogue clips and transcript, the other track, the episode length, and the raw WAV. The focused pytest regression checks both roles and one typed command per paste.

author: liracode
body:
Back end of "Me lembra um dia antes" (#188, A06·4b inscrita, RF-F4.12). Stacked on #196's PR; the new commit is the last one.

### What it does
"Me lembra um dia antes" on the signed-up event (A06·4b inscrita, #186):

- PUT /api/events/{item_id}/reminder {"on": true|false}. Only on a signed-up
  event; turning it on only while the day before is still to come (the event
  starts in 2 days or more, as reminderDate in the front) and the curation
  has not cancelled the event (it is never reminded). Turning it off always
  works. Other cases answer 409 {"error": "reminder_not_available"}.
  Answers the event detail, which now has `reminder`.
- Undoing the sign-up, "Fui!", "Não deu" and the concluded attendance turn it
  off; "Tirar do filé" deletes the row with it. The database checks it too
  (ck_file_entries_reminder_only_when_signed_up).
- file_entries gets `reminder` and `reminder_sent_for`, the event date the
  reminder was sent for (migration). One row per girl and event (the
  existing unique constraints), so she gets one reminder per event date
  (RNF-F4.01); if the event moves to another day, another one goes out.
- reminders_due(session, today): signed up, reminder on, event tomorrow, not
  sent yet for that date, still in her filé, from both sources; a curated
  event the team deactivated (cancelled), that expired or that is no longer
  an event is not reminded, as in the suggestions. It reads the
  event date at the time of sending. The rows are locked (no SKIP LOCKED, so
  a row she is changing right then is not lost); two runs at once never send
  the same reminder. Each reminder carries her account (`user`), so the
  sending goes through can_send_email() like every e-mail to her (RN-30).
  The new EmailKind.EVENT_REMINDER is chosen per event, not in the account:
  the sender passes the row's choice (reminder_on=entry.reminder), and
  without it the reminder is not sent.
- mark_reminder_sent() is meant to be committed before sending, as the #275
  e-mails: when in doubt she misses one reminder, never gets two.
- reminder_email(): the event name, the date and the link back to it. The
  text is provisional: there is no Figma screen for the e-mail.

Still missing, on purpose: the SMTP sending and the scheduled route. They
come from #287 (app/core/email.py and the CRON_SECRET routes), which this
stack does not have; they will be a small follow-up once #287 is merged, and
#188 stays open until then. Until that follow-up, nothing reads the flag:
the front (#189) must not be wired to this route before it.

### Follow-up, on purpose
The e-mail sending and the daily cron route need the e-mail sender of #287 (`app/core/email.py`), which this stack does not have. Once #287 is merged, a small PR adds the cron route (reminders_due → mark_reminder_sent → commit → can_send_email → send). #188 stays open until then. The front (#187, already in develop) saves the choice, but no e-mail goes out before that follow-up.

### How to test
In `backend/`: `uv run ruff format --check`, `uv run ruff check`, `uv run mypy app tests`, `uv run pytest`. All five commits pass on their own (1095 tests on the last one). The migrations were checked on Postgres 16: upgrade, downgrade, upgrade and `alembic check`.

author: project-osi
body:
The Pi 4 candidate gate boots the 32-bit bcm2709 factory image and reuses the radio, GUI, offline upgrade, and power-cut checks. Candidate builds need a full green run for both boards before the real-device sheet goes to Phil.

The Pi 5 follow-up in #734 added the shared case table, capability check, and minimal power-cut cases, including probe derivation from private, verified candidate bytes. The Pi 4 gate requires 18 passes for #714 or 13 for the minimal v0.8.3 writer. It reads the capability from the booted factory image and lists the reason and required replacements for each N/A. The three SQLite cuts check a disk clone before restarting the original guest. Pi 5 uses its existing SQLite restart sequence.

Stage the factory archive, checksum, and offline deployment tree outside Git and /tmp. Keep the OpenWrt host tools in place when generating upgrade fixtures. Invoke the gate from a separate, pinned main checkout with the release-line artifacts. Step 5 reads the commit and image SHA-256 from both build receipts and refuses missing or inconsistent values. The run records the tools commit alongside the candidate commit and image checksum. [Pi 4 runbook](docs/build/raspi4-emulator-acceptance.md) · [Release workflow](docs/versioning-workflow.md#step-5--build-the-factory-images).

### Hygiene and licences

All six upstream downloads have commit and SHA-256 pins. The QEMU model additions carry GPL-2.0-or-later notices with GPLv2 text beside them. The armstub, device-tree tools, and Berkeley libraries carry BSD-3-Clause notices. keycodemapdb offers BSD-3-Clause or GPLv2. The OSI test driver is MIT-licensed. The strict tree and added-line scans passed.

### Verification

- At `330cee6fa1c70ffb010615fdcbd8ba5f4aaaa2f5`, eight Pi 4 and 32 Pi 5 host tests passed. The Pi 4 regression reproduced the false PASS on `dedabec8`. The historical flag and environment cannot override a recognized image capability. A missing replacement fails the minimal gate. Syntax, hygiene, inventory, and anti-slop checks passed.
- A host walkthrough from the `904491b1` checkout exercised both absolute gate paths and verified the separate candidate and tools commit receipts.
- The documented staging block passed in a fresh v0.8.3 checkout with the receipt commit. Removing that field failed before staging. Host runs verified both SquashFS layouts and the running init and writer in the cut markers. The derived-image VM cuts still need runtime evidence.
- The historical run on `234a3635` at the preceding review revision passed nine cases, including all three SQLite clone checks and the 0.8.0 upgrade. It yielded to the queued v0.8.3 builder during the 0.8.1 upgrade and exited 124. That run predates the shared applicability check.

### Assumptions to confirm

- The synthetic 0.8.0 and 0.8.1 fixtures use the pinned 0.8.2 Pi 4 kernel and packages. The real-device sheet covers a physical upgrade.
- The baseline uses the verified candidate archive. Minimal cuts use an init-only derivative of that archive and an instrumented bundle from the same offline release tree.

## Summary

Enable JReleaser's issue tracking so releases mark the issues and PRs they ship:

- `release.github.issues` enabled: every issue/PR referenced as `#N` in the changelog gets the `released` label, a release comment and the release milestone (`applyMilestone: ALWAYS` — only when it has no milestone yet).
- `release.github.milestone.name` set to `{{projectVersion}}`. Milestones are named `1.3.1`, `1.4.0`, …; JReleaser's default `{{tagName}}` would look for `v1.3.1` and never close the milestone.

Keys and values verified against the [JReleaser GitHub release reference](https://jreleaser.org/guide/latest/reference/release/github.html) (`issues.enabled/comment/applyMilestone/label`, `milestone.name/close`).

Local `jreleaser full-release --dry-run` (JReleaser 1.26.0) on a clone at `v1.3.1` with this config and `JRELEASER_PROJECT_VERSION=1.3.1`:

```
[INFO]  Extracting issues from changelog
[INFO]  Releasing to https://github.com/operaton/operaton-mcp@main
[INFO]  Marking 4 issue(s) as released
[INFO]  JReleaser succeeded after 0.264 s
```

`issues.txt` contained `113, 114, 116, 117`, as expected for 1.3.1. The resolved config in `trace.log` shows `milestone.name: {{projectVersion}}`, `close: true`, and the issues block as configured. author: yatesv
body:
Phase 2 — the signature Fold transition, now the default.

- Screens fold in and out in 3D with a depth-blur (iPhone Duo style): a per-screen `graphicsLayer` with `rotationY` + camera distance + `RenderEffect` blur, driven by the `AnimatedContent` transition; a fade carries the timing and see-through. Content stays anchored while the frame tilts around it.
- Covers all in-app navigation; the whole app folds in on open (`AppOpenFold`) and folds away on close (`overrideActivityTransition`, API 34+).
- New default via a `designVersion = 2` migration (old `slide` default → `fold`); new installs default to fold.
- **Fold intensity** slider (Subtle → Dramatic) in Motion & feel.
- Auto-off under Android reduce-motion; blur guarded to API 31+ with a clean fallback.
- Geometry lives in a pure `foldFrame()` with 5 unit tests.

84 tests + release build pass.

author: bipoxdxd
body:
## O quê
Item "Arquivos: defesa em profundidade em caminhos e tamanhos" do #442, PR 1 (subitens b, c, k). Os demais (coleta do worker, retenção de uploads, Media Mill, nomes) vêm em PRs próprios.

- **(b)** `files/storage.py`: `_open_directory` desce da raiz nível a nível com `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` e `dir_fd` (um FD por vez, fechado em erro; criação com `os.mkdir(dir_fd=, 0o700)`, `EEXIST` aceito). `open`, `stat`, `delete`, o temporário em `.tmp`, o `os.link` (`src_dir_fd`/`dst_dir_fd`, `follow_symlinks=False`) e o `fsync` do diretório passam a usá-lo. `ELOOP`/`ENOTDIR` viram `ObjectTamperedError`. `files/retention.py`: `remove_file_after_commit` trata esse erro como arquivo não removido (alerta `purge_file_not_removed`), sem interromper a purga.
- **(c, k)** `entrypoints/api/artifacts.py`: download e preview comparam `fstat` com `ticket.size_bytes`; divergente → log "adulterado", fecha, `finish()` e 410. O preview deixa de levantar `RuntimeError` (500).

## Testes
Vermelho antes: `open` lia fora da raiz, `create_exclusive`/`delete` falhavam com `NotADirectoryError`, download 200 com corpo truncado, preview `RuntimeError`. Nove sabotagens derrubam os testes (seguir symlink no meio, sem `ENOTDIR`, FD vazado, sem `EEXIST`, `.tmp` pelo caminho, retenção só `OSError`, download sem conferência ou sem `finish()`, preview com `RuntimeError`).
Local: 1860 passed (runs, files, api/identity/db que usam o storage); ruff; mypy (681); lint-imports.

## Riscos
Objetos e diretórios reais não mudam; um diretório do caminho que seja symlink passa a dar 410/alerta em vez de ser seguido. Custo: 2–5 `open`/`close` a mais por operação. `sweep_stale_temporaries` segue pelo caminho de `.tmp` (só apaga `<hex32>.part`), fora deste PR.

Refs #442

author: kinfe123
body:
## Problem In islands mode, the first client navigation from a page is slower than RSC's in every section of `benchmarks/server-components-payload`. Navigations after it are as fast or faster. The benchmark reports the median of ten navigations, so the first one didn't show. On a page with no client component that hydrates at load (docs, blog, guide), a hover over a link loaded only the client entry and React. The router, the route table and the hovered page's prefetch all waited for the click, and then ran one after another: ``` hover: farm-client.js, react.js click: farm-client-routes.js, farm-client-router.js, then fetch /blog/b1 ``` ## Root cause Two listeners respond to the same hover: - The boot script listens for link intent (`mouseover`, `focusin`, `pointerdown`) and loads the client entry. - The client entry's lazy router stand-in listens for the same events to load the router (`farmRouterIntent`). The stand-in's listeners only exist once the entry has run, which is after the hover that loaded it. So the router waited for the next intent event, usually the click's `pointerdown`. The browser test "Links in server components prefetch once the router loads" documented this as expected: "a first hover loads the client entry, and the next one the production router". ## Change When the stand-in runs, it checks for a link that is still hovered or focused (`a[href]:hover, a[href]:focus`) and treats it as the intent that loaded the entry. Now one hover loads the router and the route table and prefetches the page: ``` hover: farm-client.js, react.js, farm-client-routes.js, farm-client-router.js, fetch /blog/b1 click: (nothing for blog and docs) ``` A page whose islands hydrate on load, with no link under the pointer, still never loads the router. The stand-in's existing `farmRouterIntent` filters still apply: hash links and absolute URLs don't count. ## Safety and compatibility - This only affects the production islands client entry, the one that splits the router. RSC mode and dev already load the router with the page. - There's no new option or public API. - A link the visitor hovers but never clicks now loads the router while it's under the pointer. Before, the router loaded on the next `mouseover`, `focusin` or `pointerdown` over a link. ## Verification - New unit tests in `lazy-router-stand-in.test.ts`: - "loads the router at once when the link that loaded the entry is still focused". It fails without the change. - "leaves the router unloaded when no link is focused or under the pointer". - `islands-client-entry.test.ts` and `lazy-router-stand-in.test.ts`: 20 passed. - The browser test "Links in server components prefetch once the router loads" now hovers once instead of twice. It fails without the change (the prefetch never happens) and passes with it. - Islands production Playwright suite (`FARM_SERVER_COMPONENTS_MODE=islands`, `playwright.server-components.config.ts`): 136 passed, 8 skipped. - Dev islands, tests matching "router": 2 passed, 3 skipped. - `oxfmt` and `oxlint` on the changed files: clean. First navigation after a cold visit, `benchmarks/server-components-payload` production builds: - Chrome with 4x CPU throttling. The pointer rests on "Next" for 150 ms before the click. - 12 rounds, with the three builds interleaved in alternating order. - Medians in ms. "Before" is `main`. | Section | RSC | Islands, before | Islands, after | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | guide | 182 | 295 | 256 | | blog | 186 | 284 | 216 | | docs | 124 | 158 | 152 | This machine had other work running (load average 50–70), so individual samples are noisy; the full lists are below. The second navigation is unchanged (guide 120 → 128, blog 114 → 109, docs 75 → 76).
Samples (ms) ``` guide islands-base 295,298,329,248,232,180,238,360,309,298,203,212 guide islands-fix 406,256,478,308,220,250,214,294,412,211,206,240 guide rsc 180,572,263,333,182,150,170,373,214,155,163,179 blog islands-base 301,182,343,214,517,330,284,326,169,209,249,168 blog islands-fix 299,150,170,140,172,247,297,391,248,183,216,171 blog rsc 257,431,183,155,150,143,194,278,137,308,186,153 docs islands-base 158,384,216,147,113,180,241,128,159,112,125,128 docs islands-fix 140,603,131,108,220,293,177,301,127,100,152,94 docs rsc 124,77,124,92,158,140,132,108,108,109,123,143 ```
Islands still trails RSC on the first navigation. The hover has to download and run the whole client entry (271 KB raw, 81.5 KB brotli), including `react-dom`, even for a navigation that only swaps HTML. RSC loaded that upfront. That's a separate change. **Not verified:** Windows, Cloudflare and Vercel targets (this changes only browser code), and touch devices (there's no hover; `pointerdown` already loads the router there). ## Documentation and release None. --- ## Summary by cubic Speeds up the first client-side navigation in islands mode by loading the router on the hover that loads the client entry, so the route table and page prefetch no longer wait for the click. Previously, a hover loaded only the client entry and React. The router, route table, and prefetch ran in series after the click, slowing the first navigation versus RSC. - The lazy router stand-in now checks for a link still hovered or focused when it runs and treats that as the loading intent. - A link that's hovered without a click now loads the router; before, it loaded on the next intent event. - Only affects the production islands client entry; RSC mode and dev already load the router with the page, and there's no new option or public API. Written for commit cd255c1daa86f145944665c08ce1cfc030821ff6. Summary will update on new commits.

author: alexandremendoncaalvaro
body:
## Summary
- Near the auto-compact point the `agentic-session` plugin now asks for a handoff, waits for the whole file, runs `/clear` and resumes from it in the same session, in place of a compaction. No keypress, so it also works in `claude -p`, and the file goes under `<home>/.agentic/handoffs/`, so it works on Windows.
- On by default, as the owner asked; the plugin option `autoHandoff` or `AGENTIC_AUTO_HANDOFF=off` turns it off. Nothing blocks: no tool call is intercepted and no typed prompt is rewritten. Compaction stays as the safety net.
- `ad-handoff` gains `/ad-handoff --auto [path]` on both hosts: compact template, end marker, no question, one-line answer.

```
fill >= start point ──> ask for handoff (turn end, or note inside a long turn)
        │
        ▼
whole file? (marker last, headings, length) ──no──> session goes on, compaction is the net
        │ yes
        ▼
/clear ──> resume prompt names the file ──> rest rule (no loop)
```

## Evidence
- Before (measured, GROUND-0047 E5): a long `claude -p` turn without the cycle compacts repeatedly and loses the task.
- After: real `claude -p` run on the final code (Windows 11, Claude Code 2.1.327, start point 55): three rollovers, each a clear and a resume from its own file, 0 compactions, exit code 0, the task's answer last.
- Not measured: the interactive terminal, the desktop app, and builds older than 2.1.327 (they share the hooks; recorded in ADR-0098 and the README).

## Merge danger
- Two-way door, but with immediate reach: the plugin ships from `main`, so every installed `agentic-session` starts rolling over on its next update. One option turns it off. The npm package changes only the `ad-handoff` skill text.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run verify` locally: 1684 pass, 0 fail (pre-push gate, Windows, this HEAD)
- [x] `ad-review`, fresh context, both axes, three passes: 0 Blockers; the last pass 0 Concerns
- [ ] CI matrix (Ubuntu and Windows, Node 22.13 / 24)

## Links
- task-0127 (`doc/tasks/0127-automatic-context-rollover.md`), follow-up task-0128
- ADR-0098, amending ADR-0088
- GROUND-0047 (`doc/research/0047-ground-automatic-context-rollover.md`)

author: leoverto
body:
Closes #1896
Closes #1898
Closes #2159

No statements were changed. There is one new helper lemma, placed directly above `sLocalInfiniteRestriction_norm`.

- New `sLocalInfiniteRestriction_normTwist` (`Sec3.lean`): restricting `chartₛ(1) s` to an archimedean place gives `(infiniteNorm(w) g)^s`. The proof unfolds `sIdeleNorm` on the inserted unit and evaluates the product with `Finset.prod_eq_single`: only the factor at `w` survives, and every other factor is `‖1‖ = 1`.
- `sLocalInfiniteRestriction_norm`: the case `s = 1` of the helper.
- `sLocalFiniteRestriction_norm`: the same computation at a finite place.
- `sLocalEpsilonFactor_archimedean_trivial` (`Sec3b.lean`): with `S = ∅` the finite product is empty. By the helper, each archimedean restriction of `emptyChart s` has real shape `(s, 0)` or complex shape `(s, 0)`. Uniqueness of the Euler parameters then makes every infinite epsilon factor `I ^ 0 = 1`.

`#print axioms`:
```
sLocalInfiniteRestriction_normTwist: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
sLocalInfiniteRestriction_norm: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
sLocalFiniteRestriction_norm: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
sLocalEpsilonFactor_archimedean_trivial: [propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
```
The `sorryAx` in the last one comes only from the definition `sLocalEpsilonFactor`. Through `finiteLocalEpsilonFactor` it refers to `finiteLocalTateFactor`, which is chosen from the still-open `finiteLocalTateFactor_existsUnique`. The finite product is empty here, so the proof never uses it.

author: ulm0
body:
Found by the update e2e in an isolated dind with the real ghcr images: every published image (0.8.0 to 0.11.0) has org.opencontainers.image.version = "v0.x.y", while the update demands "0.x.y". So the Update key and auto-update always refused with "is version v0.11.0, not 0.11.0: nothing was changed". The unit tests used stand-in images with a plain label.

- image.yml publish job: metadata tags type=semver,pattern={{version}}, so the label is plain. A repo-files test asserts the config.
- dockerupdate.ts labelVersion() accepts one leading v before x.y.z on the pull check, the recorded from, UNDO and the helper.
- The consequence is written in the fragment and not-verified.md: containers up to 0.11.0 can't self-update to an image built before this fix; 0.11.1 is the first reachable one. Meanwhile use `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`.

author: ruleofcodedev
body:
## What

Code Complexity Control now reads every function from the TypeScript syntax tree and measures each one on its **own** body (#430), and applies the founder's threshold decisions for 8.0.0:

- `maxFileLines` (300) counts **lines of code** — comment and blank lines are not counted;
- a **data file** (at most two functions) is not held to `maxFileLines`;
- "too many functions" (> 20) is reported only when a function in the file is **over the complexity limit** — never for the count alone.

## Why

The text detector found bodies by brace matching over source with only the comments removed:

- an outer function was charged with every callback written inside it (16 of 121 "function complexity" findings in the self-audit triage);
- `if`, `?`, `||` and `{` inside strings and regex literals were counted and used for brace matching (23 more);
- an expression-bodied arrow and a function whose return type is an inline object literal were never measured.

Without a loadable `typescript` the `.ts/.tsx` files are now reported as **not read** (judged nothing), the same way the testing laws do since #427, instead of being measured with a regex. The set of decision points is unchanged (`??` and optional chaining are still not counted).

Code lines are counted through `source-view.ts` (comments found only after the parsed literals are blanked); that file is byte-identical in the other #424 PRs, so the copies merge cleanly. A blank line inside a multi-line template is not a code line (as ESLint's `max-lines` with `skipBlankLines`).

## Red / green (law level)

`tests/regression/complexity-reads-the-syntax-tree.test.ts` — 10 tests, through `CodeComplexityControlLaw.check` on temp projects:

| | old checker (`git show origin/develop:…` copied back) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| result | **10 failed** | **10 passed** |

Existing tests whose fixtures were 0-function "logic" files (now data files) or relied on the old "≥ 10 decision points" ceiling were updated to the new rule; their intent is kept.

## Self-audit of this repository, this law only

| | violations |
|---|---|
| before (origin/develop) | 284 (125 file too long + 38 too many functions + 121 function complexity) |
| after | 160 (44 file too long + 30 too many functions + 86 function complexity) |

Function complexity: 45 findings gone (nested callbacks / text), 10 new ones that the text detector never measured (e.g. `ts-classes.ts` `memberEnd` 11, `path-patterns.ts` `normalizePathPattern` 11). What remains is real debt.

## Verification (all eight #424/#425/#430/#431/#432 branches merged together on origin/develop 69d6929)

- Full jest: 725 suites, 16961 tests passed.
- Release canary: green; applicable laws python 97 / angular 120 / ngrx 131 / ionic 150 / react 134 / node 77 (unchanged).
- Full self-audit of this repository (`audit --mode=full --json`), origin/develop 69d6929 → merged: 0 failed, warning laws 43 → 41. This PR's law(s):

| law | violations before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Code Complexity Control | 288 | 160 |

  No other law gained a finding. (The per-law numbers above in this description were measured on the older develop cc031e7; develop has since fixed some debt itself.)
- QA corpora, only the laws these PRs change, base vs merged: synthetic matrix 230 fixtures, Ionic 97, Next 166 — **no fixture gained a finding**; only removals (`unknown[]`, bodies under the duplication floor).

Refs #430

author: 00-aakash-00
body:
Docs pass after #156, which added the **Settings**, **Organization** and **Settings**, **Sign-in** pages. Until now the docs said that GitHub, Google and OpenID Connect sign-in need `server.public_url`, but not where providers are added or what the organization settings do.

New page `docs/self-hosting/sign-in.md`, "Sign-in and the organization":
- **The organization.** The name, project access (**Every project**, the default, or **Only projects they're added to**), and sign-up by invitation. With **Allowed email domains**, someone at a listed domain joins as a viewer when their provider verifies the address.
- **Sign-in providers.**
  - `server.public_url` is required; without it, providers show **Not offered**.
  - The **Add provider** fields include Issuer URL and Extra scopes for OpenID Connect only; Crucible always asks for `openid`, `email` and `profile`.
  - The provider's own allowed domains apply to first sign-ins only.
  - The callback URL `<server.public_url>/api/v1/auth/oauth/<provider id>/callback` is registered with each kind of provider.
  - The actions are **Edit** (button text and domains only; to use another client ID or issuer, add the provider again, then delete the old one), **Replace secret**, **Turn off**/**Turn on** and **Delete**.
- **A caution, approved by the lead.** Password sign-in stays on unless it is turned off through the API (`PATCH org` with `"password_login_enabled": false`). With it off, keep a provider turned on: Crucible does not stop the last way to sign in from being removed. The defaults and the unguarded paths are checked in `crucible-control` `types.rs` (`password_login_enabled: true`) and in `update_org`, `update_provider` and `delete_provider` in `crucible-auth` `service/admin.rs`.
- **How a provider sign-in finds the person.** A linked account first. Otherwise a verified email is required, within the provider's domains when it lists any. Then the sign-in links an existing account, or accepts an open invitation with its roles, or joins as a viewer by the organization's domain. Anything else is refused.

Wiring: rows in `docs/README.md` and `docs/self-hosting/README.md`, and one sentence in the quickstart's sign-in bullet that points to the page.

Checked against main:
- UI labels and descriptions are quoted from `ui/src/features/settings/organization.tsx` and `sign-in-providers.tsx`: states, actions, the field descriptions, the edit dialog's "add the provider again, then delete this one" and the delete dialog's text.
- The sign-in flow follows `crates/crucible-auth/src/service/provider_flow.rs`: linked accounts first; then the verified email and the provider's `allowed_domains`; then an existing user, an open invitation, or the org's `allowed_email_domains` as `OrgRole::Viewer`. No provider is offered without `server.public_url`, and only enabled ones are.
- The callback URL is `redirect_uri` in `crates/crucible-auth/src/service/admin.rs`.

body:
Sync status now tells you when a source is excluded from automatic sync. `gbrain dream`, autopilot cycles and doctor's freshness check leave a sync-off source alone, so only an explicit `gbrain sync --source ` syncs it.
