author: chris-dare-dev
body:
Progress toward #1676 (deliverable 3a, second part: the 01XT statements on `Proj R[Xᵢ]` that the existing Čech computation supports).

**Stacked on #2000.** This PR's base is `pj1-4a-deliverable-3`, so the diff shows only the new work. Merge #2000 first; GitHub then retargets this PR to `main`.

## What was proved

New file `Cohomology/Cech/ProjectiveSpaceRing.lean`, namespace `AlgebraicGeometry.Proj`, for a commutative ring `R`:

- **`twistingSheafH0LinearEquiv`** (`[Nonempty ι]`, `d : ℕ`): `(linearCoherentH R (Proj R[Xᵢ]) 0).obj (projectiveSpaceTwist ι R d) ≃ₗ[R] homogeneousSubmodule ι R d`. This is Stacks 01XT in degree 0, `R`-linear for the canonical action of the base ring on cohomology. It is the composite of `coherentHZeroSectionsLinearEquiv` with the new `polynomialTwistingGlobalSectionsLinearEquiv`.
- **`polynomialTwistingGlobalSectionsAddEquiv_smul`**: the existing global-section comparison `p ↦ p / 1` is `R`-linear for the canonical action on global sections, the one the structure morphism to `Spec R` induces. That action is multiplication by the global function `r`, which acts on each fiber of an associated sheaf as scalar multiplication (`varietyScalarAction_apply_fiber`). After passing to the natural shift through `twistingSheafOfNatIso`, which is the identity on numerators, linearity is checked point by point (`polynomialToNatGlobalSections_smul_apply`).
- **`twistingSheaf_H0_subsingleton_of_neg`** (`[Nontrivial ι]`, `d < 0`) and **`twistingSheaf_H_subsingleton`** (`0 < q`, `q + 1 < card ι`): the vanishing results of `Cech/NegativeTwist.lean` and `Cech/Vanishing.lean`, restated against `linearCoherentH`.

In `ProjectiveSpectrum/Modules/ProjectiveSpace.lean`:

- **`polynomialToNatGlobalSections_apply`** (new): the section of `p` is `p / 1` at every point.
- **`polynomialToNatGlobalSections_surjective`** and the equivalences built on it now take `[Nonempty ι]` instead of `[Nontrivial ι]`. With a single variable, a numerator over `Xᵢⁿ` is homogeneous of degree `n + d`, so all its monomials are divisible by `Xᵢⁿ`, and no second chart is needed. This matches the issue's statement, which assumes only `Nonempty`. Existing callers that pass `Nontrivial` are unaffected.

## Source

Stacks Project, Lemma 30.8.1 (Tag 01XT), for any ring, "as `R`-modules"; EGA III 2.1.12.

## Deviations from the issue

- `twistingSheaf_H_subsingleton` assumes `q + 1 < card ι` (that is, `0 < q < N`) rather than the issue's `q ≠ card ι - 1`. Vanishing above `N` is not proved: the repository computes with the full ordered Čech complex, and its vanishing above `N` is still missing.
- `twistingSheaf_H0_subsingleton_of_neg` carries `[Nontrivial ι]`, as the issue's agent comment noted. With one variable `Proj R[X] = Spec R` and every twist has `R` as global sections.
- `twistingSheafH0LinearEquiv` drops the issue's `[Fintype ι]`, which the proof does not use.

## Verification (local, not CI)

- `lake build` with `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=2` passes, with no warnings, on the new module, the `Cohomology/Cech` umbrella and the importers of `Modules/ProjectiveSpace`, including `Cohomology/Finiteness/{Projective,ProjectiveVariety,RestrictedTwistPresentation,ProjectiveSpaceTopFinite}` and `Variety/Projective`.
- A scratch check typechecks `twistingSheafH0LinearEquiv` at one variable (`ι = Unit`).
- `#print axioms` on every new declaration lists only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
- `lake exe runLinter` passes on both changed modules.
- `scripts/precheck.sh --no-build`: every gate passes.

## Remaining in #1676

- `twistingSheaf_Htop_free`: `H^N` is free over any ring, through the inverse-monomial basis. The repository has finite generation over a Noetherian base (`module_finite_linearCoherentH_projectiveSpaceTwist`).
- `twistingSheaf_Htop_subsingleton`: `H^N(O(d)) = 0` for `d > -card ι`.
- Vanishing above `N`.

  All three need the full-block classes of the top degree to be independent modulo coboundaries.
- **3b:** the transport to `ℙ(n; Spec R)` along `ProjectiveSpace.SpecIso`, and the base change of Stacks 01XV for `H^0` and `H^N`.

author: phillipchaffee
body:
## Why

Nothing in this repo runs a model, so no gate can say whether a change to a skill, rule, agent, or hook makes agents behave better or worse. [`skill-evals`](https://github.com/PhillipChaffee/skill-evals) does that and is now on npm. This PR makes it available in the repo, so real eval cases can be added next.

## TL;DR

Installs `skill-evals` 0.0.1 as a dev dependency and adds an `evals` script. **It adds no eval cases.** The four example cases an earlier version of this PR carried are removed; real ones will come in a separate change.

```bash
npm install
```

```bash
npm run evals -- check
```

## What to review

Four files, 48 lines added.

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json`, `package-lock.json` | `skill-evals` 0.0.1 as the only dev dependency, pinned exactly, and the `evals` script. The lockfile is new and holds one package. |
| `tests/opencode-and-pi-plugins.test.mjs` | **One assertion changed.** The manifest test required no `devDependencies`; it now requires exactly `skill-evals`. It still requires no runtime `dependencies`. |
| `README.md` | A short section: how to run it, and that cases go in `evals/cases/` |

The branch was rebuilt on the current `main` as a single commit.

## Evidence

- `./scripts/validate.sh` passed; `node --test tests/*.mjs` 37 passed, 0 failed; `markdownlint-cli2` 0 issues.
- `npm ci` reports 0 vulnerabilities.
- `npm run evals -- check` ran the published package on Claude Code and loaded the kit from this checkout.

## Limits

- **The dev dependency does not reach users of the kit.** Harnesses that install the kit do not install dev dependencies.
- `npm run evals -- score` has nothing to score until cases exist.
- Runs are unattended with full permissions in the harness. The README says so.

author: ottojung
body:
Separate **trusted edge service** for five separately statically hosted apps, following merged skrynia-apps safety PR #300. New standalone Rust crate `v3-trusted-edge-gateway`, no CLI or kernel/Program0 business logic. Authenticates request Host/Origin and independent per-app edge bearer, loads operator private 32-byte root token from an owner-only file only AFTER authenticating request, prepends `0x01 || token` to opaque binary POST body to loopback-only native kernel, streams bounded request+response, does not send edge credentials upstream, disallows proxy env/redirects; defaults to no production deployment. Ordinary nonzero WASM remains responsible for all app object grants/CAS/auth; Program0 still only verifies token/strips header/forwards.

**Independently executed on authorized marceline-dev against real compiled kernel+Program0+WAT echo guest (not mock)**: `SKRYNIA_V3_SERVER_BIN=/workspace/skrynia-v3-integration-kit/target/debug/skrynia-server SKRYNIA_V3_PROGRAM0_WASM=/workspace/skrynia-tools-v3-crossbuild/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/skrynia_program0.wasm CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo test --manifest-path v3-trusted-edge-gateway/Cargo.toml --test live -- --nocapture` → **3/3 PASS**, ~1.78s. Covers authorized opaque bytes, wrong/missing bearer, Host/Origin/sibling mismatch, no root token in stderr, 13MiB genuine concurrently uploaded/read echo with exact byte equality, client cancellation and subsequent request liveness. Reproduced and fixed TWO live test harness faults: draining stderr while child still running blocked forever; prematurely calling `Shutdown::Write` before response finished caused truncated HTTP echo. This branch contains fixes (verified remote source). Agent-reported `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --no-run`, `cargo check` PASS; Clippy non-strict reported 2 `io_other_error` warnings, and some new source files still exceed project <=50 nonblank lines/file (must split/meet source lints). No GitHub workflow file due missing workflow OAuth scope.

**KEEP DRAFT / NOT RELEASE-READY:** must independently review strict Clippy, structural source lints, input overflow handling, config secret permissions and numeric loopback/upstream redirect resilience, unique edge bearer per app (shared bearer across apps would permit scope confusion), origin spoof by non-browser clients, app guest authorization and real native app browser integration. Current gateway credentials are test-only and edge is NOT deployed; P0 root callback filesystem privilege bypass remains confirmed and separately release-blocking (Antonina `hAxVrL5ZstxkNOF5O2mBvS-refreshed`). No production/TLS/DNS/real secrets/Ivanka changes. Antonina `uuy7k4jCuQ8pewXerGbBve-aptly` and `w4wgIqJnlASKGYrl1UGd8H-realise`.

author: btxbtwn
body:
## Why

In the Listing Editor's **General** tab, the **Measurements (in)** section (`Top`/`Pants`/`Skirt`, `Pit to Pit`, `Length`, `Sleeve`, `Waist`, `Rise`, `Inseam`, `Leg Opening`, `Hip`, and `Other measurements`) is rendered by `ItemDetails` and persisted on `Conversation.notes` rather than `ListingRevision.listing_json`.

Because `chat_forms.forms_prompt()` only built `forms["general"]["fields"]` from `listing-editor-fields.json` and `item_decisions_prompt()` omits blank measurements, listing chat could not see empty General measurement inputs and told sellers they did not exist. And even when referenced, `option_lookup` and `chat_listing.apply_listing_payload()` only targeted and wrote `listing_json`.

## What Changed

- **`anteroom/server/anteroom/services/general_measurements.py`**: Added the General **Measurements (in)** schema (`measurements.garment`, `measurements.top.{pitToPit,length,sleeve}`, `measurements.pants.{waist,rise,inseam,legOpening}`, `measurements.skirt.{waist,hip,length}`, `measurements.other`), active garment selection matching `itemDetailsData.ts`, plain-numeric inch normalization for Web/iOS compatibility, legacy `shorts` → `pants` preservation, and `Conversation.notes` merge payload builder.
- **`anteroom/server/anteroom/services/chat_forms.py`**: Loaded `Conversation.notes` alongside the latest revision and appended `measurement_form_fields(listing, notes)` to `forms["general"]["fields"]` so chat sees all General measurement fields (even when blank) and can declare them in `_field_targets`.

body:
Four small cleanup releases and one dependency swap. None of them changes app behaviour.

| Version | Change |
|---|---|
| 1.51.9 | One streaming SHA-256 helper (`cap_fs::sha256_stream` / `sha256_rewound`) replaces six copies of the same loop. Hash values, file positions after hashing, and error mapping are unchanged. |
| 1.51.10 | Fixed regexes in concrete document generation and template manifest checks compile once (`LazyLock`) instead of on every call. Patterns built from a cell reference stay per-call. |
| 1.51.11 | The full RFI code pattern, the strict `-RFI-` pattern, and the template code rule each have one definition. Each caller keeps its own normalisation. |
| 1.51.12 | The CI frontend job runs Vitest once, with coverage, instead of twice. The step uses `shell: bash`, so pipefail still fails the job on a test failure. |
| 1.51.13 | Replaces `chrono` with `jiff`. RUSTSEC-2026-0543 marks chrono unmaintained, which made `cargo deny` fail on every branch. Journal and queue timestamps, plan stamps, RFI Log dates and Excel dates produce the same text. A side-by-side chrono/jiff test over every pattern used found one difference: jiff reads the two-digit year `69` as 1969. `parse_date` keeps the earlier 2069 meaning, and a new unit test covers it. |

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

<!-- Describe how you validated the behavior. Add automated tests wherever possible, but list manual validation steps taken as well -->
## Validation Steps Performed

<details>
<summary>AI-generated summary</summary>

Layer 2 of a 2-PR stack (base: layer 1 #52256, slow hotkey watchdog). Tracking issue: #52255.

**What changes**
- `WH_KEYBOARD_LL` moves to a dedicated hook thread that only calls a fast `should_handle_hotkey(id)` check and returns a `HotkeyDisposition`: `PassThrough`, `InvokeAndPassThrough` or `InvokeAndSwallow`.
- Module actions (`invoke_hotkey(id)`) are queued to a new header-only `HotkeyDispatch::Dispatcher` (`src/runner/hotkey_dispatcher.h`).
  - The runner's main thread drains the queue in FIFO order. A private message-only window wakes it, so modal loops also drain the queue.
  - The main thread is the worker so that actions stay serialized with `enable`/`disable`/`set_config`, which modules rely on.
- The hook waits up to 50 ms for the queued action before injecting the 0xFF key-up and swallowing the key. Fast actions therefore still run while the runner holds the foreground rights from the key press, and slow actions no longer stall input or latch modifiers.
- Win-key-hold timers now live on a message-only window owned by the hook thread, and their actions run on the worker. The WM_HOTKEY/`OnHotkeyEx` path already ran on the main thread and is unchanged.
- Slow-hotkey watchdog:
  - Actions are now timed on the worker (watchdog path "keyboard hook" or "key hold timer").
  - A slow `should_handle_hotkey` check is reported via a queued item, so nothing is logged on the hook thread.
- Lifecycle:
  - `Stop()` drops pending actions and joins the hook thread with a 2 s timeout before modules are unloaded.
  - Exceptions thrown by actions are caught and logged, and don't stop later actions.

**Interface / ABI**
- `HotkeyDisposition`, `should_handle_hotkey()` and `invoke_hotkey()` are appended at the end of `PowertoyModuleIface`. They have defaults, so the existing vtable slots don't change.
- Defaults:
  - `should_handle_hotkey()` returns `is_enabled() ? InvokeAndSwallow : PassThrough`.
  - `invoke_hotkey()` calls `on_hotkey()`.
- All modules load in-process via `powertoy_create()` and are built from this repo.

**on_hotkey return-value audit**
- Matches the default (returns its enabled state): AdvancedPaste, CropAndLock, ColorPicker, PowerOCR, RegistryPreview, MeasureTool, MousePointerCrosshairs, LightSwitch, KeyboardManager, MouseJump, CursorWrap, AltWindowCycle.
- ShortcutGuide uses Win-key hold only, and the return value is ignored.
- Needs an override:
  - **Peek**: split into a hook-side check and an action. The check uses a window-class heuristic (`CabinetWClass`/`ExploreWClass`/desktop/Peek pid) instead of the ShellWindows COM enumeration. Space mode still passes the key through.
  - **AlwaysOnTop**: the opacity hotkeys pass through unless the foreground window is pinned.
  - **PowerToys Run**: passes through unless the centralized hook setting is on, and still invokes to auto-start the process.

**Tests**
- New `Runner.UnitTests/HotkeyDispatcherTests.cpp` covers:
  - FIFO order, from a single thread and across threads
  - exception isolation, for both actions and the observer
  - Shutdown dropping pending work, rejecting new work, and releasing waiters
  - WaitForCompletion timeout and success
  - nested drain
  - wake callback
  - default shim swallow/invoke semantics
- Built with `tools\build\build.cmd -Platform x64 -Configuration Release` in `src\runner`, `src\modules\peek\peek`, `src\modules\launcher\Microsoft.Launcher`, `src\modules\alwaysontop\AlwaysOnTopModuleInterface` and `src\runner\UnitTests`. All exited 0.
- `vstest.console.exe x64\Release\tests\Runner\Runner.UnitTests.dll /Platform:x64`: 40/40 passed.
- Full `PowerToys.slnx` x64 Release build (exit 0). The dev runner ran live on a machine that reproduces the stuck-modifier bug. Input was injected with SendInput through `winapp ui send-keys --via send-input`, and modifier state was checked with `GetAsyncKeyState` after each step:
  - Advanced Paste (Ctrl+Alt+V, auto-copy on, with the *old* AP module that lacks #52252), done twice. The UI opened, "Paste as JSON" pasted into Notepad, all modifiers were up, and a following plain Ctrl+V pasted normally. The watchdog logged `AdvancedPaste ... took 837 ms via keyboard hook`, and the action ran on the main thread instead of inside the hook.
  - AlwaysOnTop (Win+Ctrl+T): pin and unpin toggled WS_EX_TOPMOST.
  - ColorPicker (Win+Shift+C): opened and closed with Esc.
  - Peek in space mode: Space in Explorer opened Peek. In Notepad the key passed through and Peek did not open.
  - Shortcut Guide (Win+Shift+/, WM_HOTKEY path): opened.
  - A plain Win tap opened Start.
  - No modifiers stuck after any step, and the runner logged no new errors.
- Not validated live: the Win-key hold timer, PowerToys Run (disabled on this machine), and MouseJump.

**Known caveats**
- An action slower than 50 ms may lose foreground rights after the key press is released, for example MouseJump's first launch.
- A modal action blocks later hotkeys

author: chhxbchhxb
body:
Closes #9029

## Summary

`retry_last` / `undo_last` shrink the **cached** Session object in memory
under `LOCK`, release `LOCK`, and only then `save()`. In that window the
cached object holds fewer messages than its sidecar — exactly the shape
`_cached_session_lags_disk` (`api/models.py`) reads as a stale cache — so a
concurrent full `GET /api/session` reloads the old file over the shrunk
object. Retry's save still writes the truncated transcript to disk, but the
cache keeps the reloaded copy: the next reader gets the removed reply back,
and its next save writes it to disk again.

I re-verified the root cause on upstream master commit `688022476`: the
mutate-under-LOCK / save-outside-LOCK shape is still there
(`api/session_ops.py` `retry_last` ~1105, `undo_last` ~1188; the shrink at
~1158 / ~1224, `s.save()` at ~1184 / ~1245), and the freshness check still
keys purely on `disk_count > cached_count` (`api/models.py`
`_cached_session_lags_disk` ~6933, call site ~7473), so the shrink window is
live on current master.

## Fix shape

Issue option A — **don't publish the shrunk object before it is durable**:

- `_detach_session_for_intentional_shrink(sid)` pops the session from the
  LRU right after the in-memory truncation (still under the per-session
  agent lock), and `_republish_session_after_shrink(sid, session)` puts the
  saved object back once `save()` returns.
- The window becomes a **cache miss** instead of a stale hit: concurrent
  readers cold-load the sidecar — still the old, un-shrunk content, which is
  the correct pre-save semantics — and the shrunk object enters the cache
  only when disk agrees with it.

Why A over B (teaching the freshness check about intentional shrink): that
check exists to catch "the sidecar is ahead of the cache through another
writer". A count-based exemption cannot distinguish that from an intentional
shrink without a new persisted signal — the existing
`_stamp_intentional_shrink_generation` / `truncation_watermark` marks are
in-memory only and not cheaply verifiable from the sidecar prefix. Option A
never touches `_cached_session_lags_disk`, so a genuinely stale cache still
reloads (pinned by the new control-group test), and there is no new
data-loss surface: if `save()` raises, the object is republished and the
cache/disk divergence is caught by the existing freshness check on the next
read.

`_publish_saved_session` in `api/routes.py` now delegates to the shared
`_republish_session_after_shrink` (identical body, one definition).

## Scope

Only `retry_last` / `undo_last` are patched. `/api/session/truncate` and
`/api/session/clear` have the same shrink-then-save shape, but they already
republish the saved object after their save, which covers the window — the
new truncate-route test guards that behavior. The regenerate path
(`apply_regeneration_plan`, `defer_save=True`) defers persistence into the
stream pipeline and is left alone.

## Verification

Deterministic repro (no sleeps): `Session.save` is patched so one full
`get_session()` runs at the exact moment the in-memory object is truncated
but the sidecar is not yet rewritten.

Test command (repo-local `.venv` per `scripts/test.sh`):

```
env -u NODE_CHANNEL_FD -u HERMES_WEBUI_TEST_STATE_DIR \
    HERMES_WEBUI_PYTHON="$PWD/.venv/bin/python" TMPDIR=/tmp \
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_issue9029_retry_undo_concurrent_read.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
```

RED (unpatched master, production diff stashed, new tests kept):

```
FAILED tests/test_issue9029_retry_undo_concurrent_read.py::test_retry_concurrent_full_read_in_window_does_not_restore_removed_reply
FAILED tests/test_issue9029_retry_undo_concurrent_read.py::test_undo_concurrent_full_read_in_window_does_not_restore_removed_reply
2 failed, 2 passed in 3.34s
```

(the 2 passing pre-fix are the stale-cache control group and the
truncate-route guard — expected to pass before the fix, see Scope)

GREEN (with the fix):

```
4 passed in 2.14s
```

Regression — 32 files: retry/undo/truncation/watermark/session-cache/
freshness suites, incl. `test_issue2914_truncation_watermark.py`,
`test_issue5532_clear_truncation_watermark.py`,
`test_8310_truncate_drops_stale_counts.py`:

```
506 passed, 1 skipped, 1 warning in 17.12s
```

`ruff check` on the four touched files: same 16 pre-existing findings as
unpatched master (verified by stashing the production diff), zero new.

## Contract change

None. No API/schema/config change; the only behavioral difference is that a
full read landing inside the shrink window sees the pre-save sidecar
(cache miss) instead of a reloaded stale object.

## Risks

- The detach/republish pair runs under the per-session agent lock, so no
  other writer can publish a newer object for that id in between; the
  `finally` guarantees the saved object is republished even if `save()`
  raises.
- Window-period reads now cold-load the sidecar (one extra JSON parse for
  that id, only inside the window), instead of taking the reload path —
  same order of cost as the behavior it replaces.

## Model Used

Claude (Anthropic) via Hermes Agent; verification by direct pytest runs
(RED/GREEN双侧 + 32-file regression + ruff baseline diff).

body:
> Re-opened on the cleaned `main` (ADR-020): same files and commits as #38, replayed onto the history without AI co-author lines. GitHub closed #38 when its branch was archived.

## What and why

Defines the format of every route file in `data/routes/` and checks it automatically, so routes for M2 can be added safely and the 3D viewer (M3) and acclimatization checker (M5) can rely on the shape. Plan: `docs/plans/m0-m2-plan.md` (#6). Decision record: ADR-017.

Closes #6

- **`docs/data-schema.md`**: one GeoJSON FeatureCollection per route, with one `route` LineString and one `stop` Point per overnight stop, in walking order.
  - Positions live only in the geometry (`[lon, lat]`).
  - There is no rest-day field: nights at a stop = next stop's `day` − this stop's `day`, and the first stop is day 1.
  - Every altitude names a Source ID from `route-sources.md`.
  - `TODO` values and unknown property names are rejected.
- **`data-prep/prep/schema.py`**: a plain-Python validator that returns every problem as a readable message. `python -m prep.schema` checks all route files.
- **`data-prep/tests/test_schema.py`**: one test per rule on synthetic data, plus a test that validates every real file in `data/routes/`. It's skipped until the first route lands, then CI guards every route PR.
- **`app/src/features/routes/types.ts`**: matching TypeScript types and `isRouteFeature` / `isStopFeature` type guards, with a Vitest test.
- **Docs**: Unique's viva notes (validator walkthrough, worked examples, questions 7–16, exercises 5–7), ADR-017, glossary, progress log. I also corrected the `route-data` skill and the M0–M2 plan to match the schema.

All test data is synthetic ("Test Route", "Stop A", source `TEST`). This PR adds no real altitudes.

## How to test

```bash
cd data-prep
.venv\Scripts\activate
ruff check . && pytest -q
python -m prep.schema
cd ../app
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test
```

To see the validator's messages, copy the example in `docs/data-schema.md` to `data/routes/test-route.geojson` and change something (for example swap a position to `[28.0, 85.0]`), then run `python -m prep.schema`. Delete the file afterwards.

## Evidence (local, Windows)

```
data-prep> ruff check .           → All checks passed!
data-prep> ruff format --check .  → 7 files already formatted
data-prep> pytest -q              → 59 passed, 1 skipped (real-files test: no route files yet)
data-prep> python -m prep.schema  → No .geojson files in data/routes yet.
app> npm run lint                 → All matched files use Prettier code style!
app> npm run typecheck            → no errors
app> npm test                     → Test Files 2 passed · Tests 5 passed
```

The example in `docs/data-schema.md` passes the validator: `validate_route(...) == []`.

**Screenshot:** none. This PR changes no UI.

**Review:**
- The code-reviewer subagent ran before this PR. Its findings are fixed in the second commit: a crash on list-valued sources, a crash on UTF-16 files, the first-stop-day-1 rule, type guards and extra tests.
- The viva-examiner subagent then checked Unique's notes against the code. The third commit fills the gaps it found and corrects wrong statements, including the Douglas–Peucker description and overclaims about CI blocking merges.

**For Unique:** please read `docs/viva/unique-ghimire.md` ("Code details", "Limits", "AI use in this part"), run the tests yourself, and answer question 18 in your own words.

## Checklist

- [x] Header comment on new files; doc comments on functions
- [x] No UI strings added
- [x] No invented data; fixtures are clearly synthetic
- [x] docs/PROGRESS.md and Unique's viva notes updated

## Summary
The #99 pin proved the control-plane tool names stay inside the strictest common
provider grammar, but the failure mode remained "discover at the first real API
call, with a 400". This adds the operational surface, in both places the ticket
names, from ONE shared pure source (`extension/src/toolnames.ts`: grammar, the
moved `TOOL_NAMES` single source re-exported by tools.ts, provider resolution,
report shape) so doctor, the seat and the #99 unit pin cannot drift:

- **doctor.sh** gains the probe (offline, static — no live API call): prints
  `ok provider tool-name grammar (N tools)`, or one
  `PROBLEM provider <X> rejects tool name <Y> (grammar ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$)`
  per offending name, counted in the ready tally via a new `problem()` line
  (same discipline as `missing()`). Compute-then-tally like the factory/policy
  reports: a pure-node one-shot prints one JSON, doctor applies the lines.
- **session_start** (orchestrator only) emits one non-blocking warning line when
  the ACTIVE provider is a known grammar-strict one (OpenAI-completions shape:
  openai-named family + pinned `kimi`/`moonshot`) and a name would fail.
  Permissive and UNKNOWN providers stay silent; doctor carries the
  provider-agnostic check.

New documented seams (not child seams): `MULTIPI_PROVIDER` (active
provider/model, wins over pi's `PI_PROVIDER` shell-tool session env; empty =
unset) and `MULTIPI_PROBE_TOOL_NAMES` (colon-separated; empty = unset) — the
diagnostic what-if seam both surfaces honour, through which every
deliberately-broken test name is driven (no real rename is ever mutated).

Closes #107

## Decisions
See `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry 2026-11-20 #107: one shared pure source instead of
doctor importing tools.ts (keeps the pi runtime out of the offline one-shot);
`MULTIPI_PROVIDER` precedence (pi injects PI_* into tool shells only); short
observed-based strict classification (openai-family substring + kimi/moonshot)
with unknown = permissive for the warning seat but NOT for doctor's static
check; the probe seam for broken-name tests; doctor's `problem()` counting line.

## Test evidence
RED committed first (ae3c4a8): toolnames module missing (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND),
strict-provider warning test failing on 0 warnings, hook-set pin failing at 4
seats. GREEN after implementation:

- `node --test tests/unit/toolnames.test.ts tests/unit/index.test.ts tests/unit/tools.test.ts tests/unit/installsync.test.ts`
  → `ℹ tests 86 / pass 86 / fail 0`
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean
- `make shellcheck` → clean (no findings)
- doctor ad-hoc matrix in the dogfood repo (scrubbed PATH, as the gate runs it):
  baseline `ok provider tool-name grammar (6 tools)`; `MULTIPI_PROVIDER=openai`
  → `provider openai (grammar-strict)` context line, still ready;
  `MULTIPI_PROVIDER=openai MULTIPI_PROBE_TOOL_NAMES="devloop_dispatch:devloop.bad"`
  → `PROBLEM provider openai (grammar-strict) rejects tool name devloop.bad (grammar ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$)`,
  problem count +1; `env -u PI_PROVIDER MULTIPI_PROBE_TOOL_NAMES="devloop.bad"`
  → `PROBLEM provider unknown rejects tool name devloop.bad`, count +1.
  The four matching smoke assertions (tests/smoke.sh, doctor section) were added
  for the batch gate.

Tests per criterion: doctor PROBLEM + rc (smoke doctor-probe block; pure half in
toolnames.test.ts); session_start warns on strict + bad name / silent on
permissive and unknown (index.test.ts probe-seat tests); offline static
validation (no process/network in toolnames.ts; doctor one-shot is a static
import); docs (AGENTS.md doctor bullet + env-seam list, devloop-setup skill +
`.pi` mirror, byte-identical extension mirror re-verified via installsync).

Note for the gate: unit tests in this worktree require a scrubbed PATH
(`dl_scrub_policy_shims`) — the armed dogfood shims self-deny fixture git
(oneshot:foreign-repo); the gate already scrubs via MULTIPI_GATE_SCRUB_POLICY_SHIMS.

robotdan
body:
## Summary

`server.sse.tls` (`enabled`, `cert_file`, `key_file`) was declared in `Config` and its cert and key were required when `enabled: true`, but nothing read it. Both the SSE and HTTP servers start with `httpServer.ListenAndServe()` (`internal/gateway/server.go:825` and `:963`), so turning it on still served plain HTTP while the operator believed they had TLS.

This removes the field, its validation, and the aspirational `tls` block in `DESIGN.md`. Because ignoring the key would keep that false belief alive, startup now fails if `server.sse.tls` is in the config file or any `MAYBE_DONT_SERVER_SSE_TLS_*` env var is set:

```
server.sse.tls is not supported and has been removed; terminate TLS in a reverse proxy in front of the gateway, then remove server.sse.tls from your config
```

The env vars are scanned directly because the field no longer exists in the struct, so neither viper nor `applyEnvironmentOverrides` would surface them. There was no existing removed-key pattern in `config.go` to follow (the only "deprecated" handling is a stderr warning for `validation.ai.provider`), so the error is added to `loadErrors` and reported with the other validation errors.

## Breaking change

Configs containing `server.sse.tls`, even with `enabled: false`, now fail to start. Release notes should tell users to delete the block and terminate TLS in a reverse proxy.

## Testing

- `TestLoadConfig_RemovedSSETLSRejected` covers TLS enabled in the file, TLS disabled in the file, `MAYBE_DONT_SERVER_SSE_TLS_ENABLED`, `MAYBE_DONT_SERVER_SSE_TLS_CERT_FILE`, and no TLS key (loads normally). It failed before the change and passes after.
- `make fmt`, `make lint` (0 issues), `make test` pass.
- Built the binary and confirmed `gateway start` exits with the error above for a config with `server.sse.tls.enabled: true`.

## Docs

- [ ] Check maybedont.ai/docs for any mention of `server.sse.tls` and replace it with reverse-proxy guidance.

body:
Closes #14 (US-201). Phase 6, strict TDD, outside-in.

## What
`MaturityNotInPastValidator` (`@Order(500)`, after the version rule): maturity before today gives `MATURITY_IN_PAST`. **Today itself is valid** (A-13), and the rule applies to every version (A-14). It is skipped when the date can't be parsed, because the format rule already reports that. "Today" comes from the injected `Clock`.

## How it was built
1. **Acceptance tests first** (service level, against an empty stub), each shown red: US-201.1 (rejected, not stored, **counted as `trade_outcomes_total{reason="MATURITY_IN_PAST"}`**), US-201.3 (v2 with past maturity leaves v1 untouched), US-201.4 (one `LowerVersionException` carrying both reasons).
2. **Unit cycles:** fake it (always a violation) → triangulate with the boundary test (today and later are valid) → the real comparison. The "skip invalid dates" test passed on its first run, so it was verified by replacing the parse guard with a lenient parse.
3. **Wiring:** red until the rule was a bean ordered after the version rule.

Observability comes for free from the shared ingestion metrics and log line, and is asserted in the acceptance test.

## Checks
`./mvnw verify`: 103 unit + 20 integration runs green; coverage gate met; traceability check passes (US-201.1–201.4 ✅); test review updated.

author: ross0x01
body:
## Production evidence

Six Browser Preview GETs returned 503 after an earlier frame and both affected sessions later served frames. Three exact receipts showed the selected plain OPEN still running when the status helper reached its six-second deadline. The remaining failures have different evidence. No typed WAIT was present in the matched cohort.

## What changed

An opted-in passive fresh Browser Preview GET uses the existing 202 deferral when the exact selected plain OPEN is still active at the existing helper deadline. It reuses the owned listener and live wrapper proof. The renderer retains the last frame at its original age with existing loading wording and keeps the normal refresh cadence. A fresh image still requires a screenshot. The WAIT response contract, ownership, input and takeover, confirmed closes, and strict failures are preserved.

## Expected cost/customer impact

Affects people already viewing an active Cloud Agent browser whose same-session navigation overlaps a passive refresh deadline. They can keep the prior frame and see the existing connecting state while navigation finishes. No change to model usage, sandbox provisioning, pricing, or the number of provider calls per refresh. Deferral uses the existing normal polling cadence instead of error backoff, so an affected slow navigation may send additional preview polls within the existing client budget. No material cost change is expected, and no dollar estimate is supported by this narrow cohort.

## Validation

Focused Jest passed 1,433 tests. The configured hook passed staged formatting and lint, TypeScript, 1,916 related Jest tests, and 32 tooling checks. The change is limited to the passive Preview UI and the web capture helper.

## Preview/demo

Tested exact head `7d7d8cf4329293baeb99659f3ce522bd2a9217c4` on the isolated Vercel Preview and Trigger Preview worker `20261121.1`. The dedicated Preview Agent ran a delayed loopback navigation and a separate WAIT. One browser session recorded three OPEN and seven WAIT deferrals, plus three HTTP 200s, with a fresh-request 200 after WAIT. The final Agent reply persisted after reload. [Preview verification](https://github.com/hackerai-tech/hackerai/pull/2406#issuecomment-7057445686)

## Recovery tested

The current production helper reproduced exit 3 at the existing six-second deadline during a held second plain OPEN in Linux Chromium. On the candidate the strict control still timed out, the opted-in status returned the OPEN deferral at that same deadline, and a fresh JPEG followed release. A separate held WAIT deferred immediately and also produced a fresh JPEG after release. Existing helper and route tests cover missing proof, completed/failed or changed OPEN, stale selection, and confirmed close.

## Rollback

Revert this PR's squash commit through the normal reviewed main pipeline and verify the prior response behavior at the production apex. The old and new negotiation paths tolerate deploy skew. No schema changes, data migration, or customer repair is needed.

`scripts/okay_run.py` plus the `okay_run` tool load a scene, press Play and run N frames at a fixed step with scripted input: keys, mouse, mouse-look, sticks, and clicks on UI buttons by name. Each run writes:

author: lc-wing
body: ## What this PR does Step 1 of the six Plan 2 Phase A steps: download the official sources the plan names, save them with provenance, and write the Day-1 audit (plan section 2.1). All 211 changed files are under `plan_2_tourism_hotel/`; `plan_5_spatial_equity/` is untouched. No source was blocked, and no value is simulated or imputed. ## Headline numbers | Item | Result | | --- | --- | | Panel window | 2010-01 to 2026-09: 201 months × 4 star classes = 804 tier-months (120 pre-pandemic, 1 transition, 35 pandemic, 45 post-pandemic months) | | DSEC series | 34 monthly series; all 16 star-class series (occupancy, rooms, establishments, guests × 4) have a value in every month | | DSEC accounting checks | same-day + overnight = total, sea + land + air = total, and four-class sums = hotel totals (rooms, establishments, guests), each exact in 201 of 201 months | | Database vs latest `.xlsx` releases | 22 of 22 printed values match (hotel tables Sept 2026, visitor tables Oct 2026) | | Holiday notices | 17 annual State Council notices + 3 amending notices → 115 holiday periods; 94 of 94 periods with a stated length parse to that length; 492 holiday days in the window | | Typhoon signals | 104 SMG reports, 367 signal records; 44 days with signal No. 8 or above, in 26 months | | SMG cross-checks | annual signal table agrees in 16 of 16 years (2010–2025); 2026 monthly climate summaries agree in 9 of 9 months | ## Star-class continuity (the check the plan asks for) - DSEC publishes the four classes under the same labels in all 201 months. - The class below 2-star changed its label (`Guest-houses` to 2021-12, `Economical accommodation establishments` from 2022-01). It is outside the four classes analysed. - Membership of a class is not fixed. The number of operating establishments in a class changed in 87 tier-months, and guest rooms moved by 10% or more in 22 tier-months (12 pre-pandemic, 8 pandemic, 2 post-pandemic). The largest is 3-star in 2016-09: 2,528 to 5,477 rooms. - DSEC's table note says the data exclude establishments that suspended business or did not serve the public, which is where the pandemic-period swings come from. - The database does not say whether a change is a re-rating or an opening/closure. Nothing is merged, dropped, or re-labelled; guest rooms per class are in the data so later steps can control for supply. ## Sources | Data | Source | | --- | --- | | Visitors and hotel series | DSEC Time Series Database (the database behind `id=402` and `id=403`), plus the latest monthly `.xlsx` releases | | Mainland holidays | State Council notices on gov.cn, 2010–2026 | | Typhoon signals | SMG tropical cyclone reports, annual signal table, monthly climate summaries | `data/raw/data_provenance.json` records URL, download time, size, and SHA-256 for all 176 raw files. DICJ gaming revenue is optional in the plan and is not used. ## Things to know when reviewing - **SMG PDFs are not committed.** The 113 PDFs total about 160 MB. The repo keeps the text extracted from each one, and the provenance file keeps each PDF's URL, size, and SHA-256. `--skip-download` works from the committed text. - **Holiday period rule.** A period is the days a notice declares off, joined with adjoining weekend days the notice does not declare as working days. This decides the length of the 20 periods where a notice names a single day ("与周末连休", a "补休" day, or neither). The other 95 are date ranges taken as written, including the extended 2020 Spring Festival. - **Typhoon day rule.** A calendar day on which signal No. 8 or above was in force for any length of time. - **A parsing bug the cross-check caught.** Some SMG PDFs encode 北 as a compatibility character, which hid two No. 8 records in 2017. The text is now normalised, and a line that looks like a signal record but cannot be read stops the run. - Average length of stay starts in 2011-01, so it is missing for the 12 months of 2010. body:
## Problem

Related issue: N/A
Validation tasks: none

Other clients: N/A (web admin dashboard only; no client has this widget)

On the admin dashboard, each Now Playing session card shows a row of tags (play method, Jellyfin pill, client label, route, profile) capped at one line. With Settings → Accessibility → Text size set to Large or Extra large, or with a larger browser default font, the bottom edge of every tag gets cut off. The cap is a fixed 18px. The pills' line height and padding are in rem, so they grow with text size while the cap stays at 18px.

## Approach

Write the cap in rem: `calc(1rem + 2px)`. That is the row's 0.75rem line height, the pills' 0.25rem of vertical padding, and their 2px of border. At the default 16px root it's still 18px. The row also gives every pill its own 0.75rem line height (`[&>*]:leading-3`). Without that, the profile pill's own `leading-[1.1]` on 9px text is taller than 0.75rem below a browser font of about 13px and would outgrow the cap. With both changes the cap equals every pill's height at any text size, so the first line shows whole and tags that wrap stay hidden.

The pills' `text-[9px]` font size doesn't change here; #4861 converts it to rem. The two changes are independent, but they touch neighbouring lines, so whichever merges second may need a rebase.

## Validation

- I rendered the real widget in headless Chromium from a temporary dev-only harness page with stubbed sessions; the page isn't committed. I measured the tag row height against each first-line pill at a 12px browser font, at default, Large, and Extra large text size, and at a 24px browser font, on `main` and on this branch.
  - `main`: the row stays 18px while the pills are 20, 22, and 26px at Large, Extra large, and 24px, so 2, 4, and 8px get clipped.
  - This branch: the row matches the pill height at every size (14, 18, 20, 22, 26px) and nothing on the first line is clipped. Pills that wrap to a second line stay hidden.
- At default size, the before and after captures are pixel-identical.
- ESLint and Prettier pass on the changed file. Web CI passes.
- Not checked on a live server. The proof is the harness measurements and captures.

Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/now-playing-tag-row-text-scale/

## Risks

None identified. The card gets taller only when the text is larger than default, and only by the amount that was being clipped.

body:
## Summary
E17-S03 Processing settings (MFC-132, sub-task MFC-914). Decisions below were confirmed with the user.

- Five registered App-scope settings in Settings, Processing: `processing.ioConcurrency` (1-16, default 4), `processing.cpuConcurrency` (1-32, default from `IHardwareInfo.DefaultParallelism`), `processing.aiConcurrency` (1-4, default 1), `processing.resumeOnOpen` (Automatic / Ask), `processing.confirmQuitWhileProcessing` (default on). `ProcessingSettings` (Abstractions) holds the definitions; the CPU default is built from the hardware at startup. "Reset this category" is the "reset to recommended" action.
- **Runtime concurrency (E05-S01-T02):** `JobSystem` listens to the store and calls `SetPoolLimit` on the running scheduler, so a changed limit applies at once (more work starts now; a lower limit applies as work finishes). A limit changed while a library was starting is re-applied after the scheduler becomes current. `JobSystem` takes a `Func<ISettingsStore>` because the store reads the open library, which depends on the job system (DI cycle).
- Replaced the typed `AppSettings.Processing` record by the registered settings; `JobSystem` and `QuitGuard` read the store. The old `processing` section of `settings.json` is moved into `values` on load (idempotent, no schema bump; this keeps "Don't ask again" choices).
- **Resume UI** (needed so "wait until I start it" doesn't stall processing): when a library opens paused, the status bar shows "Processing paused" and the processing queue shows a "Resume processing" button.
- No screenshots: the settings window and the processing panel open as separate windows, which the smoke tool can't capture. The real app ran a script that opens both (exit 0, no binding warnings).

## Tests added
| Test class / test | What it covers | Case |
|---|---|---|
| `JobSystemTests.ChangingAPoolLimit_AppliesToTheRunningSchedulerWithoutARestart` | Each pool limit change reaches the running scheduler | happy path |
| `JobSystemTests.RaisingTheLimit_StartsMoreQueuedWorkAtOnce_AndResettingGoesBackToTheRecommendedLimit` | Raising CPU 1 to 3 starts two more queued items at once; reset returns to the recommended limit | happy path |
| `JobSystemTests.ALimitChangedBeforeAnyLibraryOpens_IsUsedWhenOneDoes`, `GetPoolLimits_UsesSettingsOrTheDefaults`, resume-mode tests | Limits read at start; defaults; Ask pauses | edge |
| `ProcessingSettingsTests` | Defaults, hardware default clamped, ranges rejected, reset, all five registered by `AddInfrastructure` | happy path / edge / failure |
| `JsonSettingsServiceTests.Current_TypedProcessingSection_MovesIntoTheRegisteredValues` | Old `processing` section moves into values; existing values win; section removed | edge |
| `QuitGuardTests` (updated) | Confirmation and "Don't ask again" through the store | happy path |
| `ProcessingPanelViewModelTests` (Resume, no paused scheduler) | Resume calls the scheduler and clears the notice | happy path / edge |
| `ProcessingStatusSegmentTests.Segment_ShowsWhileProcessingWaitsForResume_AndHidesAfterwards` | Paused status shows with unfinished jobs, hides after Resume | happy path |

## Review
`code-review` at **high** (runtime concurrency change). It found no concurrency or lifetime bugs; it did find: the paused status never showed because a paused start has unfinished jobs (fixed, test now uses a non-empty summary); the upgrade lost "Don't ask again" (fixed with the migration above); and nits (hardcoded setting count, banner overlapping the title, help text not saying new work waits while paused), all fixed. Not changed: after Resume the status bar text refreshes with the next progress event.

## Drafted DECISIONS.md entries
**DNEW-1 — Processing settings replace the typed processing record.** Pool limits, resume mode and the quit confirmation are registered settings (`processing.*`, App scope); `AppSettings.Processing` is removed, and an old `processing` section is moved into the values on load without a schema bump.

**DNEW-2 — Pool limit ranges and defaults.** I/O 1-16 (default 4), CPU 1-32 (default from the hardware), AI 1-4 (default 1). "Reset this category" on Processing is the reset-to-recommended action.

**DNEW-3 — Prompted resumption has a Resume button.** With "wait until I start it", the status bar shows "Processing paused" and the processing queue shows Resume processing; all new work waits too until then.

author: rustyrazorblade
body:
Fixes the `:integrationTest` failures that turned main's `PR Checks` red, plus three more flakes that repeat runs turned up.

## `PackerSsmImageIntegrationTest > the packaged Dockerfile builds an image whose plugin runs and that still runs Packer`

**Failure** (runs 44815503993, 44639482207): `DockerClientException: ... lease does not exist: not found`.

**Root cause.** With Docker's containerd image store, an image prune deletes every lease labelled for pruning before it prunes, whatever filter it carries. That includes the content leases of in-flight pulls and builds. In the integration tier Ryuk is disabled (`TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true`), so Testcontainers runs its JVM-hook reaper, and that reaper prunes images at every fork JVM's exit. With parallel forks and `forkEvery`, a fork exits while another fork builds the Packer SSM image, and the build loses its lease.

Reproduced: `docker build` alongside a concurrent label-filtered `docker image prune` that matches nothing failed 3 of 3 times. In CI, both failures overlap the other fork's exit.

**Fix (production code).** `Docker.buildImage` retries a single build through resilience4j's checked decorator. It uses a new `providers/docker/DockerBuildRetry` policy: 3 attempts, 1 s then 2 s backoff, and a retry only when containerd's lease-lost message is in the daemon's error. The project `DockerException` wrapper, whose message holds the build output, is skipped, so a step that prints the phrase and fails is not retried. A failing `RUN` step, a missing base image, or any other error still fails on the first attempt. A warning is logged only when a retry is actually scheduled. A failure reports only the output of the last attempt.

## `PodReadinessWaitIntegrationTest > initializationError`

**Failure** (run 44833749047): `AssertionError: no default ServiceAccount in readiness-wait after 60s`.

**Root cause.** A temporary repeat-run workflow ran 10 shards × 3 passes of the K3s classes. It caught the failure twice, in `PodReadinessWaitIntegrationTest` and in `K8sBackendWorkloadsIntegrationTest`, both of which go through `SharedK3s.createNamespace`. That run included new diagnostics. In both cases a direct GET at timeout found the ServiceAccount in place, created the same second the wait began, and the node was Ready. fabric8's `waitUntilCondition` is informer-based: it lists, then watches. Its watch never delivered the account, so the wait timed out on an object that already existed.

**Fix.** `SharedK3s.createNamespace` now waits with a plain GET poll, with the same 60 s budget and no watch; a read error is retried within the budget and becomes the cause of the timeout error. The timeout report now includes that direct read, the controller-manager lease, and the K3s log tail without the orphaned-cgroup spam that every co-hosted K3s produces. `PodReadinessWaitIntegrationTest.tearDown` no longer hides a setup failure behind an uninitialized `lateinit` error.

## Other flakes found by the repeat runs

- **`K3sEmbeddedEtcdIntegrationTest`**: "the API server did not report etcd healthy 180 seconds after the restart". etcd refused its own member: `expect https://172.17.0.6:2380, found https://172.17.0.8:2380`. Once any class in the fork has called `Testcontainers.exposeHostPorts`, every new container is also attached to the port-forwarding container's default-bridge network. K3s then advertised that bridge address, and the restart changed it. The test now pins `node-ip` to its fixed address, which is how an EC2 node with a single private IP behaves.
- **`PyroscopeAgentReplayIntegrationTest`**: one 422 "service is unavailable" upload, 15 s after the agent started and before the outage. The agent started as soon as the first server's `/ready` passed. On a first start with an empty volume, `/ready` passes inside the window where the server still refuses pushes (the start window in the issue 991 design). The test now waits until that server stores a push before it starts the agent. The failure report now includes both servers' log tails.

## Evidence after the fix

- Packer under a reaper-like burst prune locally: 10 of 10 passed, and 4 of the 10 hit the race and recovered through the retry.
- CI repeat run 44874198582 (10 shards × 3 passes, 7,200 test cases, each of the four classes run 30 times): no failures.

author: allamiro
body: ## Summary **Merges after #871, which merges after #836.** This branch is built on #871's branch, so until those two merge, the diff here includes theirs. This PR's own change is the last commit, f42a9e02. E6 of the production bar (#739): "a tested procedure for losing the engine host, and a supported single-replica engine deployment". The issue's pass/fail line has three parts: | Part of #739 | Here | |---|---| | A drill kills the engine host (and separately only its pod), starts a standby on the same PostgreSQL ledger after the old one is fenced, and the archive shows zero holes within the stated recovery time | **Yes, in the engine crash sweep:** a new `postgres-kafka-host-loss` leg for the host. The existing `postgres-kafka` leg, the same process killed with its work directory kept, is the pod. | | A Helm chart or documented unit file runs one engine with probes, limits and a `Recreate` strategy | **Documented, not deployed by CI:** `examples/systemd/vtop-engine.service`, and `examples/kubernetes/vtop-engine.yaml` (one replica, `Recreate`, probes, requests and limits). There is no engine chart. | | The page | `docs/deploy/engine-host-loss.md` | Refs #739. Its "drill in CI" is met by the nightly leg. I am leaving the closing decision to the maintainer, because the deployment is a documented example and not a chart that CI deploys. ## What changed and why **`scripts/live-chaos/engine/run-sweep.sh`: `ENGINE_SWEEP_FAULT=host_loss`.** - It is refused unless the ledger is PostgreSQL and the source is Kafka, the topology where something survives the host to recover onto. - At each failpoint the engine is killed there (the host dies), and the commit rule is checked at the instant of the kill. - The dead engine's work directory is then **deleted**: staged batches, multipart sessions and its host-local lock are gone. - A **standby** starts from a copy of the config that names a new work directory, on the same ledger, consumer group and bucket. The fence is the kill: the old engine is known dead before the standby starts, as an operator powers the old host off first. - The standby must commit every record within the point's bound. Then the leg checks the commit rule again, the engine's coverage audit, and every record in the store: none missing, duplicates only where the at-least-once window is open. - Every leg's summary and log now report the time **from the kill to every record committed**. **`.github/workflows/engine-crash-sweep.yml`.** The `postgres-kafka-host-loss` leg (features `failpoints,postgres`), nightly and on dispatch. Like the other non-primary legs, it also runs on a pull request that changes the workflow. **Docs:** - `docs/deploy/engine-host-loss.md` (new, in the nav): the topology a standby needs (ledger, source, store, config, digest directory off the host), the procedure (fence, start, wait, `vtopctl audit-coverage`), what recovery does with the old engine's batches, how it is tested and the measured times, the two examples, and what is not covered. - `docs/deploy/index.md`: the PostgreSQL row links to it. - `docs/LIVE_CHAOS_VALIDATION.md`: the new leg, how to run it, and its time. **Examples:** - `examples/systemd/vtop-engine.service`: `Restart=on-failure`, `MemoryMax`, `CPUQuota`, an orderly `SIGTERM` stop with a 120 s grace period, the state-store URL from an environment file, and hardening. - `examples/kubernetes/vtop-engine.yaml`: - `replicas: 1`, `strategy: Recreate`; - liveness on `/healthz` and readiness on `/readyz`. The comment says readiness means the process started, not that recovery finished, because that is what `/readyz` reports; - requests and limits, non-root, read-only root filesystem; - an `emptyDir` work directory, so a replacement pod is the standby; - an `emptyDir` at `/data/state`, because the image's entrypoint requires it to be writable. ## Evidence **All 21 points of the new leg passed locally, with no duplicate at any point.** Setup: - Kafka (`apache/kafka:4.3.1`), the lab's MinIO and `postgres:18-alpine` at 0.5 to 0.7 CPU each; - a debug `vtopctl` with `failpoints,postgres` in a container capped at two CPUs. From the kill to every record committed by the standby: **8 to 12 s**, 50 records per point. Each point took 10 to 15 s; the whole leg took 244 s. ``` === engine crash sweep (kafka source, postgres ledger, fault: host_loss): 21 of 21 points, 50 records each, 244s === before_insert PASS 12s duplicates 0 (allowed 0) recovered in 9s ... mid_object_put PASS 11s duplicates 0 (allowed 0) recovered in 8s after_manifest_put_before_ledger PASS 15s duplicates 0 (allowed 20) recovered in 11s before_source_commit PASS 12s duplicates 0 (allowed 20) recovered in 8s after_source_commit_before_ledger PASS 11s duplicates 0 (allowed 20) recovered in 8s after_ledger_source_committed PASS 11s duplicates 0 (allowed 20) recovered in 8s ``` **Also run:** - the sweep_checks unit tests (39); - shellcheck v0.11.0 over `lib.sh` and `engine/*.sh`: clean; - actionlint 1.7.7: only the known notices; - check-naming.sh under bash 5.3, the substantiation lint, and `mkdocs build --strict`. The Kubernetes example parses, with one replica and `Recreate`. It is not applied anywhere in CI. ## Not covered - Fencing is the operator's. Nothing in the engine stops a second engine on another host; the page says so in step 1. - A PostgreSQL failover is not drilled, and neither is a store outage combined with a host loss. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a `host_loss` fault to the engine crash sweep and the syslog spool leg: at each failpoint the engine is SIGKILLed, its work directory deleted, and a standby with a new work directory starts on the same PostgreSQL ledger, Kafka group, and bucket and must commit every record within the point's bound. The spool leg runs the same sweep against a spool file read through the spool source, with the commit rule on the ledger's cursor. - Runs only against PostgreSQL + Kafka, the topology where something survives the host for the standby to recover onto. - Deletes the dead engine's work directory (staged batches, multipart sessions, host-local lock) so the standby cannot see them. - Checks the commit rule at the kill, the coverage audit after recovery, and every record in the store for holes; reports time from kill to full commit. - Adds the `postgres-kafka-host-loss` and `sqlite-spool` legs to the nightly workflow and on dispatch. **Docs and examples** - `docs/deploy/engine-host-loss.md` covers the required topology, the fence-then-start procedure, what recovery does with old batches, and what is not covered. - `examples/systemd/vtop-engine.service` and `examples/kubernetes/vtop-engine.yaml` run one engine per ledger; documented, not deployed by CI, and the Kubernetes image tag is a placeholder because release images up to v0.10.2 cannot open a PostgreSQL ledger. - The Deployment tolerates node unreachable and not-ready taints without a time limit, so it keeps its pod until the operator fences the node instead of letting Kubernetes start a replacement after 300 seconds. - Host fencing is the operator's responsibility; nothing in the engine stops a second engine on another host. Written for commit 98ea14832bf15e4e665354505106331d452af4a3. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
## What

The `Content-Disposition` reader no longer needs `node:*`. `RequestUtility.parseContentDisposition` becomes `HttpResponseReader.parseContentDisposition` (same options, same answer). `ContentDispositionTypes` and `TContentDispositionType` move from `request.utility.ts` (imports `node:fs`, `node:path`) to `common/constants/http.ts`, so `RequestUtility` and a browser client share one browser-safe constant.

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `RequestUtility.parseContentDisposition` | `HttpResponseReader.parseContentDisposition` |
| `ContentDispositionTypes`, `TContentDispositionType` in `utilities/request.utility.ts` | same names, in `common/constants/http.ts` (still exported from `@venizia/ignis-helpers`, so no import changes) |

`RequestUtility.buildContentDispositionHeader` stays (it uses `node:path`).

## Deviation from the brief

The brief said to move `ContentDispositionTypes` onto `HttpResponseReader`. A constants class on a reader would break the rule that constants live with the HTTP constants, so it sits beside `HTTP` in `common/constants/http.ts` instead. Same name, same public import, no changelog line for it. Say if you want it on the reader anyway.

## Changelog

Breaking `parse-content-disposition-in-reader` + migration block (rename the call; `devz codemod namespace-functions` rewrites the old bare function name, and its mapping now targets `HttpResponseReader`).

## Tests

`content-disposition.test.ts` moves to the new member (same cases, round trip with `buildContentDispositionHeader`); `string-domain-constants.test.ts` imports the constant from its new file. All gates green locally.

## Dropped to keep it small

No alias on `RequestUtility`; no change to how the header is built or parsed.

body:
Closes #75. Stacked on #73 (merge #72 → #73 → this).

## What
- **`prk -update`** (also `--update` and `update`), with options `-check`, `-yes` and `-dry-run` (one or two dashes):
  1. Reads `https://api.github.com/repos/Patrick-W-McMahon/ProofRunKit/releases/latest` and compares it with this build.
  2. Picks the `ProofRunKit-*x64*.msi` asset and requires `<msi>.sha256`. A missing or mismatched checksum refuses the update with exit 6, and nothing is written.
  3. Asks for confirmation unless `-yes`, writes the MSI to `%TEMP%`, starts `%SystemRoot%\System32\msiexec.exe /i "<msi>" /passive` detached, and exits 0 so MajorUpgrade can replace prk.
- **`prk -version`** (also `-v`, `--version` and `version`):
  - The first line is unchanged, so the existing tests still match.
  - A second line says up to date, update available, or "Could not check for updates: <reason>". It always exits 0.
  - `-offline` / `--offline` or `PRK_OFFLINE=1` skips the check.
- **Code layout:**
  - Pure parts: a small JSON reader, release versions, asset choice (safe file names, https only), `.sha256` parsing, and SHA-256 in C (`prk_sha256.h`).
  - `run_update_command` works only through injected `UpdateServices`.
  - The WinHTTP and msiexec code lives in the new `prk_update_system` library, which is **linked only into proofrunkit/prk**. The self-test exe has no network or installer code.
  - Linux and macOS report "not supported on this platform yet". x86 Windows can check but refuses to install (#74).
- **New exit code:** 6 = update failed (see `docs/exit-codes.md`).
- **Installer scripts:** `installer/build-msi-x64.ps1` writes `<msi>.sha256` (`<hash>  <name>`, ASCII). `verify-msi-x64.ps1` checks it, or warns when it is missing.
- **Docs:** new `docs/update.md` (including the release checklist); `installer-windows-x64.md`, README, ARCHITECTURE, exit codes and the help text are updated.

## Tests (no network anywhere)
- **Self-test +11** (`update.*`): SHA-256 FIPS vectors, JSON, versions, the release document and asset choice, checksum files, CLI parsing of every spelling, and the command through a fake HTTP layer. The fake covers up to date, check only, dry run, declined, install, `-yes`, mismatch, bad or missing checksum, 404 (no release), network error, HTTP 403, unsupported platform, check-only allowed while install is unsupported, and the `-version` status lines and offline mode.
- **CTest +2:** `prk_version_single_dash` (`prk -v -offline`, version line only) and `prk_update_needs_network`. **Every CTest test now runs with `PRK_OFFLINE=1`.**
- **Box:** gcc -Werror, clang ASan/UBSan and the C fallback each passed 45/45. MinGW x86_64 and i686 build. Wine x64 self-test: 148 tests, 144 passed, 4 skipped.
- **Manual check under Wine (not in CTest):** WinHTTP reached the real API; `prk -version` printed "Could not check for updates: no release has been published yet" and exited 0.

**Expected on Windows x64:** self-test 148/148, CTest 45/45. x86 is known-failing because of the antivirus (#74, deferred).

## First release (needs Patrick; no tag or release created here)
Tag `vX.Y.Z`, published (not a draft or pre-release). Attach `ProofRunKit-X.Y.Z-win-x64.msi` **and** `ProofRunKit-X.Y.Z-win-x64.msi.sha256` from `build-msi-x64.ps1`.

author: wildcatdownstairs
body:
## What and why

On Windows, an editor panel or tool window that loads a plugin's own web page (`web = "…"`, such as a minimap) showed a white background under a dark theme. WebView2 (Chromium) paints an opaque backdrop behind an iframe whose `color-scheme` differs from the embedding page's, and the workbench is `color-scheme: dark` while a web view page had none: the bridge set `data-theme` on its root, but only `html` view documents get the `BASE_STYLE` rule that turns that into a `color-scheme`. The bridge now sets the frame root's `color-scheme` along with `data-theme`, so web views stay transparent as `plugins/README.md` promises. macOS (WebKit) draws no such backdrop, which is why it only showed on Windows.

## How it was verified

- Windows 11, `pnpm dev:app`, Islands Dark, the unchanged Minimap plugin 0.1.4 from the marketplace, same file and window size:

| Before (`main`) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![White minimap on main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wildcatDownstairs/openidea/pr-assets/web-view-color-scheme-host-before-minimap.jpg) | ![Transparent minimap with the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wildcatDownstairs/openidea/pr-assets/web-view-color-scheme-host-after-minimap.jpg) |
| ![Editor and minimap on main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wildcatDownstairs/openidea/pr-assets/web-view-color-scheme-host-before-editor.jpg) | ![Editor and minimap with the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wildcatDownstairs/openidea/pr-assets/web-view-color-scheme-host-after-editor.jpg) |

- Reduced it in Chromium first: a transparent iframe with no `color-scheme` inside a `color-scheme: dark` page renders white; with `color-scheme: dark` it is transparent.
- `pnpm vitest run src/features/plugins`: 424 passed, 1 failed — `market.test.ts › formats downloads compactly`, which fails the same way on `main` on this machine (Node 27 formats `1234` without the compact suffix); unrelated.
- `oxfmt --check` on the changed file.

## Review focus

The fix is in the shared bridge, so `html` view documents now get the inline `color-scheme` too; it matches what their `BASE_STYLE` already sets.

author: abedamouneh
body:
## Task
T-570 including T-336: Plan, start and close a cycle from one Backlog screen · https://portal.rtylr.com/flow/p/8/list?openTask=%22570%22

## Problem
Cycles could be created but no task could be put into one. A cycle had no goal, no start or complete step and no carry over, there was no backlog screen, and a new cycle became active just because its dates covered today, so a project could end up with two active cycles. The task panel showed the cycle as read only and the cycle filter matched nothing.

## Fix
API
- Cycles carry goal, started_at, completed_at, totals by status bucket, estimate_minutes and carried_over.
- New: `GET /cycles/{id}`, `POST /cycles/{id}/start` (1 to 4 weeks plus goal; 409 if the project already has an active cycle), `POST /cycles/{id}/complete` (per unfinished task: next cycle, backlog or cancel, one transaction, recorded as carry over), `PUT /cycles/tasks/order` (place a task in a cycle or the backlog before or after a neighbour), `GET /cycles/{id}/capacity`.
- Capacity per person: working days minus approved HR leave, times 8 hours, against summed estimates. Leave is read through a Flow port backed by HR's module API, never HR tables; if it fails, capacity says leave was not applied.
- Tasks return cycle_id, cycle_name and plan_rank; create and update take cycle_id (0 back to backlog).
- A new cycle is upcoming until started. Reads need viewer, writes member, task moves member on the task; scoped by business_id.
- Fix: v2 createCycle had no role check; it now needs project member. v2 updateCycle no longer blanks the name.
- Migration `flow/v18_cycle_planning.sql`: guarded, idempotent, additive.

Portal
- Backlog tab: active cycle, upcoming cycles, unplanned work; dates, goal, counts, committed vs available hours (amber from 90%, red over 100%), per person capacity with leave days, "carried over from".
- Drag between and within sections with the board's drag helpers; Alt+arrow by keyboard; optimistic and live through realtime.
- "+ Create" per section (quick create gains a cycle), Start and Complete dialogs, New cycle button, editable Cycle field in the task panel. EN, FR, AR.

## How to test
1. Project > Backlog > New cycle twice; drag backlog tasks into the first cycle, reorder, reload; check another browser updates live.
2. Start the first cycle (1 week + goal): the second cycle's Start is disabled with a reason.
3. Capacity: someone with approved leave shows fewer available hours.
4. Complete the cycle: unfinished tasks default to the next cycle, which shows "carried over from".
5. Change a task's Cycle in the side panel; filter List by cycle.

## Checks
- Lint: golangci-lint new from main clean; portal eslint clean on changed files (existing routes.tsx error only)
- Typecheck: go build/vet clean; portal typecheck clean
- Tests: flow workspaces DB tests pass (6 new); auth matrix new cycle move case passes (pre-existing flow projects edit/assign failures on main); TestArchitecture baseline; Flow vitest 1474 pass; e2e flow-board 16/16, new flow-backlog 2/2
- Manually checked in Chrome: on prod after deploy

## Screenshots
None.

## Notes
- Starting and completing need project member (same as create/update).
- 8 hour working day: Flow has no per business working hours setting yet.
- French name for Backlog is "Carnet".

author: trivenico
body:
## Summary

Closes the device-revocation race in issue #565 and carries the same fencing boundary into the authenticated resource-reservation service.

- Add pairing-service operations that hold a SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` lock while an authenticated heartbeat, capacity publication, outbox retry, reservation admission/renewal, or presence snapshot is committed.
- Make revocation use that same lock. If an in-flight heartbeat/reservation obtains the lock first, it completes before revocation; if revocation obtains it first, later operations fail closed.
- Retain device-agent history while returning `revoked=true` and `online=false` for revoked devices.
- When the reservation service is configured, invalidate active reservations inside the revocation transaction's pre-commit callback. If invalidation fails, revocation rolls back rather than leaving mismatched authority.
- Require an active paired device for new reservations and lease renewals. Release remains possible for cleanup.
- Keep lock ordering consistent: pairing DB -> device-agent DB -> reservation ledger. The reservation ledger never calls back into the device-agent DB.

## Regression coverage

- Heartbeat/revocation interleaving proves revocation cannot return ahead of an authenticated heartbeat already holding the pairing lock.
- Revoked devices remain in history but are never reported online.
- API response exposes revoked status and denies subsequent heartbeats.
- Active leases are invalidated at revocation; new reservations, renewals, and capacity publications fail after revocation.
- Existing owner isolation, source-sequence watermark, concurrency and idempotency tests remain in place.

## Scope and safety

- This is still a device/resource foundation, not remote inference dispatch. It does not enable arbitrary commands or automatically replay work.
- The optional reservation service must be wired into `DeviceAgentService` for revocation to eagerly release ledger rows; the reservation API independently checks paired-device state for admission and renewal.
- Stacked on `feature/device-agent-client` (PR #603); draft until exact-head cross-platform CI and integration review complete.
- No local tests were run in this session.
- Add a rollback regression proving a failed reservation-ledger invalidation leaves the pairing credential active rather than partially revoking the device.


### Validation update — exact head `30495cd8f2d6678890eee7ac1cba8f065929b829`

- Full Yuki quality-gates Python 3.11 Ubuntu job passed after correcting the five pre-existing test expectations to match the new fail-closed paired-device authorization behavior.
- Python 3.11 Windows is in progress and macOS is queued. Focused workflow checks are still running; no full cross-platform pass is claimed yet.

author: tyler-loy
body:
Phase 30 step 1 from `docs/design/shard-ha.md`: detection, which phase 20 found is most of the failover window. Fixes #201.

## Changes

- **Deadline check (#201).** The hub checked for dead nodes every `FailureTimeoutMs/2`, so a death landed 1.0–1.5 timeouts after the last heartbeat.
  - A deadline check now runs every `FailureTimeoutMs/20` (clamped to 25–250 ms) against the in-memory monotonic table that step 0 introduced. It touches membership only to declare a death.
  - The coarse store sweep remains, for nodes not heard from since a hub restart.
  - Both paths declare under one lock, and a declared node leaves the table, so nothing is declared twice.
- **`Cluster:FastFailoverOnLinkLoss`** (new, **off by default**, live). A node whose link closed and stayed closed for one heartbeat interval is declared dead (1759). The interval is a grace so that a network blip that reconnects doesn't move shards.
  - **Safe only on shared storage that enforces exclusive file locks across hosts.** The node may be alive and leased, and only its log lock keeps the new owner out until it dies or parks at lease expiry (step 0). CONFIGURATION.md says so.
  - Per-term log segments (the replica step) will remove that requirement, and then the default can flip.
- **Load tool:** `failover --fast-failover`, and failed calls are now reported by reason.

## Measured (`failover --rows 100000 --repeat 3 --clients 4`, defaults)

| | Detect | Server window | Client restore max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before (phase 20) | 10.6–13.4 s | 12–14 s | 14.1 s |
| Deadline check | 9.0–9.9 s | 10.1–11.7 s | 12.0 s |
| `--fast-failover` | 1.0–1.2 s | 1.9–3.2 s | 3.3 s |

Detect is measured from the kill. The last heartbeat landed up to a second before it, which is why the deadline-check row reads 9–10 s.

The remaining failed calls in these runs are the per-identity rate limiter turning away the burst of calls the gateway held through the window. These runs also exposed a gateway bug on `main` that occasionally disconnected a client; it's fixed separately in #226.

## Tests

New `DetectionTests`:
- a stopped node is declared dead within 1.3× the timeout (the old check could take up to 1.5×);
- with fast failover, a killed node is declared dead in seconds against a 30 s timeout, and its shard opens on the survivor;
- fast failover is off by default.

The detection, fence and failover tests (13 in all) pass 6 of 6 rounds with the Core suite running alongside. Full Release suite passes.

author: bthehero
body:
Some US deals, mostly add-ons, have no price in a region after edition matching ([BtheHero/ggdata#24](https://github.com/BtheHero/ggdata/pull/24)), usually because their store code says nothing about the product (`…_00-0716578793176238`). Each such deal now gets the deal from the region's own deal list with the same name, if it meets all of these:
- it's for the same consoles;
- each store has exactly one deal of that name;
- where the game's editions in that region are known, the region's product belongs to the same game (it shares one of their title ids), so a generic name like "Gold Edition 6 in 1" can't match another publisher's product.

The paired deal is taken out of `extra` (the region's deals not on sale in the US), so it isn't listed twice. It's put back at the start of each run, so the pairing is redone every time.

**Tested** on UK and Japan data: 12 deals paired in the UK and 7 in Japan (for example the Samurai Warriors 4 costume sets, the Gas Station Simulator Junkyard DLC and the Breakout brick packs), all checked to be the same product. Most of the deals still without a price aren't on sale in those regions, so the region's deal list has nothing to match them against.

author: agentydragon
body:
Goal: #parsimony

## Decision for you

`supervision` copies `systemd.Observation`, `ExitState` and `StartState` field for field into `SystemdObservation`, `SystemdExitState` and `SystemdStartState`, with a converter that casts the enums by number. Keep that copy, or use the internal types once? `supervision/process_resources.go` keeps the status contract in `supervision` on purpose. That note came from #17287, the PR that created the internal type.

## What

One commit: 5 files, +16 −88, net **−72**. `Status.Systemd` and the controller's observation resource hold `systemd.Observation` directly. Removed: the three types with their constants and `String` methods, and `systemdObservationFromHandle`. The `observation.go` comment no longer says "not durable state": the controller retains the newest observation in `Status` until the owner destroys the attempt.

## Why I think the boundary is not needed

- `rg` for `SystemdObservation`, `SystemdStartState`, `SystemdExitState` and their constants finds nothing outside the `supervision` package. The only reader of `Status.Systemd` is `ManagedProcess.BackendDescription`, and the only test is `controller_test.go`.
- The two sets of structs, enum values and `String` methods are identical, so `BackendDescription` prints the same text. `Snapshot` was already the internal `systemd.UnitSnapshot`, so the copy never hid the internal package.
- The numeric-cast converter is a drift hazard: a new internal enum value would print as "invalid" in `BackendDescription`.
- The kept contract matters only to a reader outside the package that must name the enum values. None exists. `systemd` is internal, so such a reader would need an exported predicate when it appears.

## Tests

The two `controller_test.go` tests that feed observations use `systemd.Observation` and `systemd.ExitObserved`. No assertion changes.

## Checks

Remote, green (`bbapi invocation status`: `success: true`): [`661867e5`](https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/661867e5-2cf1-407d-b34c-06462bfb3e4e), 27 of 27 on the combined branch before I split it. It includes `supervision:{supervision_test,pid1_process_test}`, `supervision/internal/systemd:systemd_test`, `session:session_test`, `internal/workspace:workspace_test`, `codexexecserver:codexexecserver_test` and `coordinator_test`. Build [`58d9b5f7`](https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/58d9b5f7-b00a-4692-9603-c37a25f370e7) covers both manual fixtures and the changed libraries.

## Risks

If an outside reader appears, export a predicate then. This is a package-boundary change, so I left it for your call rather than a plain parsimony PR.

## Overlap

No open PR touches these files.

## 0101 Review speed-ups and Allow 200 more
- **Accept all from one send:** it confirms first, with a count per list. Each group is all or nothing; other groups still go in.
- **Tick boxes:** "Accept ticked" and "Reject ticked" sit in a bar at the bottom of the screen. Ticking one row ticks its whole group.
- **Keys:** Up/Down or J/K, A, R and Space. JavaScript only adds the keys; every button still works without it.
