author: s-kvng
body:
## Problem

On Android, with **Video** chosen in Quotes' share sheet, the small preview card (`ShareCard` with `playing`) can show solid black while the loop behind the sheet is fine. Found while testing #900 (the Android exporter). The exported video itself is not affected.

## Change

```diff
 <ShareSheet>
   <ShareCard playing>
-    <BackgroundLayer play />                          // VideoView: SurfaceView
+    <BackgroundLayer play surfaceType="textureView" /> // VideoView: TextureView
```

- `BackgroundLayer` takes an optional `surfaceType` and passes it to `LoopVideo`'s `VideoView`. When it's undefined, the default SurfaceView stays, so the full-screen loop, the background tiles and the kept cards don't change.
- `ShareCard` always asks for `"textureView"`. Only the sheet's preview card ever plays a loop (the off-screen capture cards don't play), and the value never changes at runtime, which expo-video requires.
- Why: a SurfaceView sits behind the window and cuts a hole through everything drawn under it. Here that hides the poster `BackgroundLayer` draws under the video, and the wrapper's opacity-0 fade doesn't hide the hole. The card shows the SurfaceView's own black surface until frames land. A TextureView draws inside the view tree, so the poster shows until the first frame, then the fade-in runs.
- iOS: `NativeTextureVideoView` is `null` off Android, so `VideoView` renders the same native view as before.

## Surfaces touched

- [x] Mobile (`apps/mobile`)
- [ ] Web (`apps/web`)
- [ ] Admin (`apps/admin`)
- [ ] Desktop (`apps/desktop`)
- [ ] CLI (`apps/cli`)
- [ ] Backend contract (`packages/backend`: schema, function args or return shapes; must stay compatible with shipped mobile builds)
- [ ] Docs (`apps/docs`, READMEs, AGENTS.md)

Web, desktop, admin and CLI have no Quotes share. No backend or docs change.

## Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. JS only, so it ships by OTA.

**Blast radius:** small. Only the share preview card on Android. If TextureView misbehaved on some device, the card would show the poster instead of the loop. Export is unchanged.

## Verification

Tested on an API 35 arm64 emulator (`Xolace_Test_API_35`) booted with `-gpu swiftshader_indirect` to avoid the host-GPU `Failed to find ColorBuffer` problem from #900's testing. No physical Android phone was available.

- **Before (SurfaceView):** with expo-video's cache cleared, opening Share showed a black card while the player had already logged `readyToPlay` and `onFirstFrameRender`. Over a 30 s timed run with the cache cleared, the card was black in 4 of 10 captures after the sheet opened (for example at 13 s, 28 s and 30 s), and video in the rest.
- **After (TextureView):** the card plays the loop with its rounded corners, across several reopens and a cold start. In the same 30 s timed run with the cache cleared, 1 of 10 captures was black.
- Checked that the clip itself has no dark frames: 9 s, 270 frames, mean luma about 62 on every frame.
- `bun run check:changed`: Biome, `check-types` for `@xolace/mobile` and dependents, and file length all pass.

**Could not verify:**
- **A real Android phone.** The software-GPU emulator is slow and noisy. With a warm cache, the SurfaceView preview also played. A run with throttled network, meant to show the poster vs. black side by side, failed when the emulator hung ("System UI isn't responding"). Please check on a device: open Share on a loop background with Video selected. The card should show the poster, then the moving loop, never black.
- **iOS was not run.** It is unchanged by construction: `surfaceType` is dropped there, and `VideoView` renders the same native view.

## Model & harness

- Model: Claude Opus 5.5
- Harness / tool: Claude Code (desktop), side session started from #900's session
- How much was agent-written, and what a human reviewed: all agent-written; needs human review and a device check.

author: shad0wcrawl3r
marevol
body:
## Problem

A stored `{bcrypt}` hash with the `$2b$` prefix (Python bcrypt, OpenBSD, Spring Security `BCryptPasswordEncoder`) or the `$2y$` prefix (PHP, `htpasswd -B`) is never verified: login always answers 401.

Cause: the vendored `org.codelibs.fess.crypto.bcrypt.BCrypt.hashpw` accepts only the `$2$` and `$2a$` versions and throws `IllegalArgumentException("Invalid salt revision")` for any other, and `BcryptPasswordEncoder.matches` treats that as a malformed stored hash and returns false. `checkpw` also compares the recomputed string with the stored one, so the version must be the same on both sides.

## Change

- `BcryptPasswordEncoder.matches` rewrites a `$2b$` / `$2y$` prefix to `$2a$` before verifying, so both sides of the comparison use `$2a$`. The algorithms are identical for every password the encoder accepts (at most 72 bytes). The change is in the encoder, not the vendored class, which stays a verbatim copy.
- `$2x$` (the sign-extension bug of crypt_blowfish) is deliberately not accepted.
- New hashes are still written as `$2a$`. `needsUpgrade` / cost parsing read the cost field and work for any version, so an imported `$2b$`/`$2y$` hash is re-hashed to `$2a$` at login only when its cost is below `app.password.bcrypt.cost`, as for `$2a$` today.
- `UPGRADING.md` (15.10): one paragraph.

## Tests

Hashes made by independent implementations are embedded as literals: Python `bcrypt` (`$2b$`) and `htpasswd -B` (`$2y$`), ASCII and UTF-8 passwords, cost 4 to 10.

- `BcryptPasswordEncoderTest`: both prefixes verify; wrong, one-character-off and empty passwords are refused; the same hash text under `$2a$` agrees; `$2x$`, `$2c$`, `$2B$`, `$3b$`, a missing `$` and a non-numeric cost are false; `needsUpgrade` / `parseCost`; `encode` still writes `$2a$`.
- `PasswordHashHelperTest`: `{bcrypt}$2b$...` and `{bcrypt}$2y$...` verify and refuse, `{bcrypt}$2x$...` refuses, truncated hashes are false, `upgradeEncoding` follows the cost.
- Before the change the verifying tests fail; after it they pass.

author: albertorestifo
body:
## Summary

Cuts per-PR CI time and merges the nearly identical nightly and release workflows.

The Windows package job took ~29 of the ~31 minutes on every PR and every push to master. Most PRs only touch `lib/`/`test/`, and that job checks almost none of it.

## Changes

- **ci.yml**
  - The Windows package job runs on a PR only when packaging inputs change (`tauri/`, `scripts/`, `config/`, `mix.exs`/`mix.lock`, CI files). Pushes to master skip it, since nightly packages master every day. It can still be run by hand (`workflow_dispatch`).
  - Uses the Tauri CLI pinned in `tauri/package-lock.json` instead of `cargo install tauri-cli` (~10 min).
  - Adds a Rust cache and drops the duplicate sidecar release builds.
  - A new push to a PR cancels its previous run.
- **claude-code-review.yml:** reviews once, when a PR opens or leaves draft, not on every push.
- **build-desktop.yml (new):** a reusable workflow shared by nightly and release. It has one job per platform instead of six jobs passing artifacts. avrdude is now checksum-verified on Linux too.
- **nightly.yml:** compares against the last successful nightly run instead of a cached SHA.
- **Cleanups:**
  - Removes harden-runner, which was in audit mode only.
  - Removes the template boilerplate in `claude.yml`.
  - Groups Dependabot updates into one PR per ecosystem.
- **claude-weekly-docs.yml removed.** Its last two scheduled runs failed in under a second.

## Testing

- `mix precommit` passes. The `test/ci/` workflow tests now point at `build-desktop.yml`.
- This PR's Windows job exercises the new `npx tauri build` path.
- A nightly run is dispatched on this branch to exercise `build-desktop.yml` on both platforms. Check that `SENTRY_DSN` resolves to `***`.
- The release leg can't be tested without publishing a release. Its publish step is unchanged apart from reading `version` and `release_id` from inputs.

author: longdevlife
body:
## Behavior

Brief new Person tracks can produce separate MF05/MF06 cases. Add optional consecutive admission before creating subject segments: new_track_confirmation_frames defaults to1; higher values require consecutive unambiguous strong observations. Confirmed tracks may use weak continuity observations, but absence/discontinuity retires the numeric ID before reconfirmation so downstream PPE/Zone state cannot transfer between subjects.

Pending tracks remain internal PPE competitors, preventing shared PPE from being assigned to a confirmed neighbor. Raw detection batches remain unchanged. Confirmation starts at the actual current frame, without backfill, retrospective episode merging, identity inference or permission decisions. Default runtime assembly is unchanged.

## Verification

- New regression suite covers admission, discontinuity, missing/reappearance, competing PPE ownership, strict configuration bounds and empty v1.7 frames.
- Integrated regression reproduced inherited Zone occupancy after short absence, then passed after numeric ID retirement.
- Full frozen vision suite:2040passed,2expected POSIX-only skips on Windows.
- Lock/environment, Ruff lint/format, build and vision configuration/import smoke passed.
- Independent review cleared the revised subject-boundary behavior.

Metadata-only replay of1599 already admitted observation frames produced38 segment starts withN1,21withN3 and13withN5. This omits other raw detector candidates and has no annotated truth: it is a diagnostic, not accuracy or live notification acceptance.

## Limits

No runtime activation/model/DB/deployed profile changes. Higher confirmation delays or misses brief real people; persistent false detections can still pass. Physical/crowd/latency evaluation and reviewed profile selection remain required before operational adoption. No camera recordings, weights or private metadata are in the PR.

body:
## Summary

With `zod-aot generate --auto-discover`, the generated file read the source schema as `(__src_X as any).schema`. Only a `compile()` wrapper has that property. A plain Zod export found by auto-discover does not, so the expression was `undefined`:

| Case | Before |
|---|---|
| Schema with a fallback (e.g. a refine that captures a variable) | Import throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'shape')` from `var __rf=[(__src_X as any).schema.shape[...]]`. This happens with and without `--no-zod-compat`. |
| No fallback, zodCompat (default) | `__mkv(fn, undefined)` builds a bare object with four parse methods. `.shape` and the rest of the Zod API are missing, even though the #316 annotation types it as the Zod schema. |
| No fallback, `--no-zod-compat` | Worked. |

Fix:
- `discoverSchemas()` records `exportKind: "compiled" | "plain"` on each `DiscoveredSchema`.
- `compileSchemas()` copies it to `CompiledSchemaInfo`.
- The CLI emitter uses `__src_X` itself for plain exports, and keeps `.schema` for `compile()` exports.
- The unplugin path is unchanged. It passes the source-level expression to `generateIIFE` and never reads `.schema`.

## Tests

- New `tests/cli/generated-runtime.test.ts` covers `compile()` and `--auto-discover`, each with zodCompat on and off. It generates with the real `generateFile()`, imports the output, and checks three things against a schema with a capturing refine:
  - The import does not throw.
  - The refine still applies.
  - With zodCompat, `.shape` is present.
  - Both auto-discover cases fail on `main` with the `undefined.shape` error.
- `tests/cli/emitter.test.ts` gains a mixed-file case that checks the emitted expressions for both kinds.
- `pnpm test` on Node after a build: 1910 passed. `bunx --bun vitest run` without a build: 1906 passed. `pnpm -r typecheck` and `pnpm check` pass.
- `benchmarks/suites/size/cli.ts` measures plain schemas, so it now sets `exportKind: "plain"`.

## Not in this PR

Review found a separate issue that predates this change. Members of a default-export object (`export default { A: ... }`) are discovered, but the emitter imports them as named exports (`import { A as __src_A }`), and those don't exist.

author: justyannicc
body:
## Problem

`prepare:upstream` runs `framework:build` in every job. It generates the authoring Worker's skills and framework reference into `apps/hosted/cloud/.generated/executor-authoring.json`, and takes 15–19 s on the self-hosted box. That is the largest part of a warm prepare once #1445 removes the carry replay. Every job of one Check builds the same file from the same tree.

## Change

**A shared step cache, `scripts/shared-step-cache.ts`.** The first job of a Check builds a step under a lock; the others wait for its entry and restore it.
- **Where:** on the box's CI runners, the cache is `$BASALT_BOX_SHARED/<name>/<run id>`, used only when `RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT` is `self-hosted` and the box's shared directory exists. Anywhere else, hosted runners and local runs included, the step builds as before and nothing is written.
- **The lock:** the same design as #1576's `e2e:prepare` carry. A directory appears with its owner already inside, by an atomic rename, and scratch names carry the owner token, since box containers repeat process ids. A holder releases its own lock on every exit, a failed build included. A waiter says it's waiting. A lock older than its bound (5 minutes, or `BASALT_STEP_LOCK_STALE_MS`) is a dead holder's and is taken over.
- **Entries** are written beside their final path and renamed, so a reader never sees a partial one.
- **The cache never fails a job.** If it can't be read or written, or the key can't be computed, the step builds as it would without one.

**`framework:build` uses it,** keyed on:
- the patched upstream worktree's Git tree, taken through a temporary index so the checkout's own index is untouched (0.9 s against the 19 s build);
- the dependency generation key `installUpstreamDependencies` already returns;
- Node and Bun.

Any change to the tree or the dependencies gives a new key.

**One directory per Check run** keeps Checks from reusing each other's output by accident. It isn't a boundary between jobs, since every CI container on the box can write the shared mount. That is no wider than the host-escape risk the box carries until CI jobs run in their own microVM.

## Scope

Tracked in #1392. It follows the CI batch unless it's frozen before that batch is composed.

## Verification

`scripts/shared-step-cache.test.ts`, written first and run red against a stub that always builds. The concurrent and failure cases use real child processes.

| Test | Stub (today's behaviour) | This change |
|---|---|---|
| With no cache named, the step builds every time and nothing is written | ✔ | ✔ |
| A restored entry answers only its own key | ✖ | ✔ |
| Two jobs at once build the step once and end with the same output | ✖ | ✔ |
| A failed build releases its lock; a dead holder's lock is taken over after the bound; a live one is waited for | ✖ | ✔ |
| The box's shared directory names the cache; elsewhere there is none | ✖ | ✔ |
| The worktree key follows tracked and unignored files, not ignored ones, and leaves the checkout's index alone | – | ✔ |
| A cache that fails, or a key that can't be computed, falls back to building | ✔ | ✔ |

- 7/7, twice in a row.
- No type errors in the changed files, and the style gate is clean.

**Not measured yet:** `prepare:upstream` on the box before and after, on a real Check. Before is the box owner's measurement: 15–19 s for `framework:build`.

author: conorluddy
body:
PR 2 of the inspiration intake plan. Stacked on #224.

## Commands

| Command | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `vcr inspiration add <file\|dir>…` | Copies each local file to the ignored `inspiration/files/<id>/`, hashes it, measures what a tool can and writes `inspiration/items/<id>.json`. Idempotent on sha256; re-adding restores a missing copy. A directory is walked; unsupported files are skipped with a warning. Nothing is fetched |
| `vcr inspiration add --colours "#0B1F3A,#F2A33A" --title …` | A named colour set, no file |
| `vcr inspiration annotate <id>` | Changes stated fields only: note, aspects, use, rights, attribution, source, creator, accessed, title |
| `vcr inspiration list` | One line per item; `--kind --aspect --use --unannotated --unobserved --limit --offset`; `{ total, offset, limit, items }` with `--json` |
| `vcr inspiration show <id>` | Stated, then measured (with tool and version), then judged, then the absolute file path and contact sheet |
| `vcr inspiration remove <id> [--yes]` | Plans first, names briefs that cite the item, deletes only the record and its copies |

Mutations return `{ data, changes[], warnings[] }`.

## Measured facts

- Image: width, height and up to six dominant colours with share, from ImageMagick.
- Video: width, height, duration, fps, has audio from ffprobe; a 4x3 contact sheet from ffmpeg.
- Font: family, subfamily, weight class, italic and the embedded licence string, read from the sfnt `name` and `OS/2` tables by VCR itself (TTF, OTF, TTC). WOFF and WOFF2 give a warning and no facts.
- A missing tool adds the item anyway and warns.

## Behaviour worth reviewing

- `--use asset` is refused without `--rights`. `--rights unknown` is accepted and then fails `vcr validate`.
- `--note` and `--title` are refused when one call would add several files.
- Flags on a re-add of an existing file are ignored with a warning pointing at `annotate`.
- A bulk add gives one "N items have no note" warning that tells the agent to ask the user, not to write one.

## Wiring

- `vcr workspace init` ignores `inspiration/files/`; `add` adds the entry itself in an older workspace.
- `vcr storage` reports a sixth class, `inspiration`. `vcr storage clear inspiration` is refused, and the clear guard now also protects `inspiration/`. Plugin PRD §6.5 and ST-01 updated.

## Checks

`pnpm vcr plugin build`, `pnpm validate` (0 diagnostics), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (390 passed; 25 new). By hand in a scratch git workspace: added an image, a short video, a font and a colour set; `git status` showed only `inspiration/items/*.json`, `.gitignore` and `vcr.json`.

author: ehmoussi
body:
The web server's limits (`session_ttl`, `max_sessions`, `session_idle`, `max_saved_sessions`, `max_download_streams`, `max_session_download_streams`, `shutdown_timeout`, `filter_patterns`) were class variables of `WebApplication`. An app could change them only in a subclass. So an app started with `run(build_main_view)` always kept the defaults.

## Changes

- **`WebSettings`** is a new frozen `attrs` class in `composeui.core.application` (public). It has one field per limit, with the same defaults as before. Each field's comment says what it limits, what happens past it, and when to change it. It imports nothing from the web backend.
- **`run(..., web_settings=WebSettings(...))`** gives the settings to the web backend's application only. Qt and Textual ignore them, so the same call runs on every backend. A `--reload` server runs the program again, so it gets the settings again.
- **`WebApplication` and `WebModelApplication`** take `settings=`, read from `self.settings`. The class variables are removed.
- **Breaking change:** a subclass that still sets one of the old names fails with a `TypeError` when its class is defined. The message names the setting and where it goes now. Without the check, such a value would be ignored without a word. For example, `filter_patterns = False`, which a public app sets so that a crafted regular expression can't block every session, would stop working.
- **`StreamPlaces`** takes its defaults from `WebSettings`. `MAX_STREAMS` and `MAX_SESSION_STREAMS` are removed.
- **The two web benchmarks** (`idle_sessions.py`, `hibernation_soak.py`) pass their limits as a `WebSettings`.

## Documentation

- **User guide:** a new section, "Change the server's limits", in `running-the-app.md`, with a runnable example. The bullets that told users to subclass now show `WebSettings`.
- **Old names:** updated in the user guide's page list, `llms.txt`, `widgets.md`, the technical guide, the docstrings, the `web-security` skill, and the users' agent skill.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** a line under "Changed", with the breaking change.

## Tests

- `test_run_gives_the_web_settings_to_the_web_backend_only` (`tests/test_application.py`) runs `run()` on each backend, with and without a model. The web's application holds the settings given. Qt and Textual build without them. It fails if the settings go to every backend, or if the model application drops them.
- `test_a_web_app_refuses_a_subclass_that_sets_a_setting_as_a_class_variable` (`tests/test_webrenderer.py`) fails without the check.
- **Existing web tests** that set the class variables in subclasses now pass a `WebSettings`. They cover the session lifetime, the session limit, sessions on disk, download streams, the shutdown timeout and filter patterns. What they check is unchanged.

`make check`, `make typecheck`, `make test` (100% coverage), `make docs` and `make browser-test` pass on Python 3.9.

author: trinhquocviet
body:
## Summary

This PR adds two user-configurable features to the Lot60-BLE firmware. Both are stored in flash and configurable over the existing HID configuration protocol (Report `0x3F`):

1. **Custom Bluetooth device name.** UTF-8, up to 16 bytes. Each BLE host slot advertises it with a `_0` / `_1` / `_2` suffix.
2. **Per-connection profiles.** Each connection (BLE 0, BLE 1, BLE 2, USB) can pick its own base layer and modifier swaps. The keyboard switches profile automatically when the active BLE slot or the USB state changes.

It also adds the build and flash helper scripts and the hardware research notes used to develop and test these features.

Releases: [`v1.2.2.0`](https://github.com/trinhquocviet/lotlab-nrf52-keyboard/releases/tag/v1.2.2.0) (`29ef0a7`) and [`v1.3.0.0`](https://github.com/trinhquocviet/lotlab-nrf52-keyboard/releases/tag/v1.3.0.0) (`726791c`), both built by `Release.yml`.

## Changes

### BLE device name (`ble_services.c`, `store_config.c`)
- The GAP device name and the advertising data are refreshed when the BLE host slot changes. Before this change, every slot advertised the same name.
- The name is built in a fixed 24-byte stack buffer, replacing the variable-length array. The slot suffix comes from the new `switch_device_get_id()`.
- If no custom name is set, the default `DEVICE_NAME` (with the MAC-based suffix) is used.
- If the custom name does not fit in the advertising packet (`NRF_ERROR_DATA_SIZE`), or if `sd_ble_gap_device_name_set` fails, the firmware falls back to the default name.
- New `ble_device_name_refresh()` updates the name at runtime and re-encodes the advertising data while no host is connected.
- `switch_device_select()` now ignores out-of-range slot IDs.

author: toddy55
body:
## What this changes
On the last check, OpenStreetMap returned 123 courses, 1,725 holes and greens, and 3,752 bunkers, water and fairways. It then failed on the final, least important step (suburb names), and the whole download was thrown away. This PR stops that happening.

- **Each later download can fail on its own.** If holes, hazards or suburb names don't come back, each course keeps that data from the previous list instead of losing everything.
- **Every build starts from the live list.** The build loads the course list that's already live first, then puts the new download on top.
- **More retries.** If all three servers fail, it waits a minute and tries all three again.
- **Sense check.** If fewer than 80% of the previous courses come back, the previous list is kept.
- **Daily refresh.** It runs daily at 3:23am Brisbane time instead of monthly, so a bad day on the servers is fixed by the next morning.

## Testing
- All 64 tests pass.
- I simulated a run where the courses download but every later step fails. The holes, water and suburb were kept from the previous list.

author: ericboucher
body:
## Problem
Site pages (e.g. https://aqualink.org/sites/3503) load slowly. Timing every API call the site page makes against production:

| Endpoint | TTFB |
|---|---|
| `sites/3503`, `latest_data`, `daily_data`, `surveys`, `spotter_position`, `wind-wave-data-hindcast`, `time-series` data | 0.13–0.4 s |
| **`time-series/sites/3503/range`** | **10.6–12.7 s** |

It takes about 10 s for other sites too (1006, 3400), even though site 3503 has only 5 NOAA daily metrics. So App Engine is fine and this one query is slow.

`getDataRangeQuery` joins `sources` on `site_id` and runs `MIN/MAX(timestamp)` over `time_series`. No index on `time_series` starts with `source_id`: the indexes are `(metric, source_id, timestamp DESC)`, the unique `(metric, source_id, timestamp)` and `(timestamp)`. So Postgres scans the whole table sequentially on every call.

## Fix
The query now starts from the site's sources, crosses them with the metric enum, and uses a `LATERAL` MIN/MAX per (metric, source). Each lookup is a 1-row backward scan on the existing `(metric, source_id, timestamp DESC)` index. No migration is needed, and the grouping, ordering and response shape are unchanged. `surveyPointId` is now a bound parameter instead of being interpolated into the SQL.

## Verification
On a local Postgres 16 with 8.4M synthetic `time_series` rows, 4,000 sites, and duplicate spotter sensors that share type/depth:
- The old and new queries return identical rows for several sites, with and without the survey-point filter.
- Plan: old = Parallel Seq Scan over the whole table (~400 ms at this size, and it grows with the table). New = Index Only Scan Backward, **1.8 ms**.

I could not run the e2e suite in my environment because `yarn install` can't fetch `xlsx` from cdn.sheetjs.com, so I'm relying on CI for that.

- **Composer:** a + button attaches photos (image picker) or files (document picker). Limits are checked before anything uploads: 100 MB per file, blocked file types, and at most 10 files per message. Picked files appear as chips you can remove.
- **Offline-first:**
  - Picked files are copied into app storage straight away (local schema v4, `message_files`), so a message queued offline keeps its bytes across restarts.
  - The outbox uploads each file (ticket, raw `PUT`, complete) and then sends the message with `attachmentIds`.
  - A retry resumes with the files not yet uploaded.
- **Display:**
  - Images show inline and other files show as cards (icon, name, size). Both open through short-lived signed links.
  - Your own files display from the local copy, so nothing is downloaded again.
  - A file still waiting to upload says so.
  - A file-only message shows a 📎 preview in the conversation list.
- **Housekeeping:** local copies with no message left are pruned on start. Native file access lives in `src/lib/localFiles.ts`, with a fetch-based web variant used for the web preview and in unit tests.
- Adds `expo-image-picker` (with a photos permission string), `expo-document-picker` and `expo-file-system`.

## Verification
`scripts/e2e-real-server.cjs` against the API from main: 22 of 22 checks pass. The 6 new checks cover:
- 2 attachments sent, with names and types kept.
- Uploaded bytes download intact through the signed URL.
- A photo from another member loads through its signed link.
- A file queued offline is uploaded and sent after you reconnect.

Unit tests: 48 pass, including 3 new for attachments (queued display, upload once with resume, server snapshot). Typecheck and format:check pass. Not run on a device yet; the native upload path (`File.upload`, binary PUT) is typechecked but only exercised on web here.

author: brad0
body:
MIPS I has no trunc.w.fmt. fptosi from float selected trunc.w.s anyway,
since its pattern was marked ISA_MIPS1, and fptosi from double failed
to select.

On MIPS I use cvt.w.fmt with the rounding mode set to round toward
zero, then restore the FCSR. This is the same sequence the assembler
uses for the trunc.w.fmt macro.

cfc1/ctc1 have the same delay as mfc1/mtc1 before MIPS IV, so add them
to the FPU delay slot hazard list. This puts a nop after cfc1 before its
result is used and after ctc1 before the next FPU instruction.

author: aicest
body:
## Summary

```diff
 configure(GITHUB_TOKEN)
-  GET /user                       # installation-scoped Actions token: 403
+  GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}       # the capability the plugin needs

 configure(GITLAB_TOKEN)
-  GET /user                       # project/CI-job tokens may be denied
+  GET /projects/{owner}/{repo}    # the capability the plugin needs
```

The credential pre-flights introduced in #20 verified tokens by reading the
authenticated user — an identity endpoint. The installation-scoped
`GITHUB_TOKEN` provided by GitHub Actions authenticates but is forbidden
from reading it (`403 Resource not accessible by integration`), so every
Release run since e4504a70 fails during `configure`, before any release is
created. The pre-flights now verify the capability the plugins actually
need — access to the repository or project they release to — which user,
installation, project, and CI job tokens can all read.

`verifyToken(token)` becomes `verifyToken(token, repository)` in both
packages; the signature is unreleased (the failed release never published
e4504a70), so no public API breaks. An unresolved repository skips the
pre-flight, preserving the existing publish-stage failure. The npm
pre-flight was audited too and needs no change: pnpm 12 `whoami` honors
`--registry` and reads the `pnpm_config_*` token injected by `prepareAuth`
(verified against a local registry stub).

## Evidence

- **Before:** Release run 44883169127 on `main` (e4504a70) fails in
  `configure`:
  `[error] Release complete: The GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable could not be verified.`
  (cause: `403 Resource not accessible by integration` on `GET /user`)
  **After:** 124/124 github+gitlab suite tests, 32/32 integration tests,
  `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm build` pass; new pins cover the repository/project
  pre-flight on both plugins.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverts cleanly; no data or published history is touched.

**Blast Radius:** release tooling

Affects every ReelOut release run and any consumer of the exported
`verifyToken` helpers. The unreleased signature change is the only public
surface moved.

## Bước 1/5 — Lõi "Cài lại Windows" (không cần USB)

Xoá ổ Windows đang chạy rồi cài mới từ file ISO/WIM, kiểu WinToHDD. Đây là cài mới, không cài song song.

### Gồm
- `src/ITHelpdeskTool.Reinstall.Core` (netstandard2.0, dùng chung cho app .NET 10 và bản nhẹ .NET 4.8):
  - Môi trường cài WinPE dựng từ `boot.wim` của ISO (không cần ADK), khởi động một lần bằng bcdedit ramdisk. Lỗi xảy ra trước khi xoá thì máy tự về Windows cũ.
  - `apply.cmd`: format ổ, hoặc xoá mọi thứ trừ thư mục đệm; `dism /Apply-Image`; thêm driver; `bcdboot`.
  - `unattend.xml` và `FirstLogon.ps1`: tạo tài khoản, áp tinh chỉnh, cài phần mềm, tự chép lại dữ liệu đã sao lưu.
  - Kiểm tra trước khi cài:
    - BitLocker / mã hoá thiết bị, có tắt mã hoá và lưu khoá khôi phục.
    - Tài khoản Microsoft, máy của tổ chức (Entra / Intune / domain, phải xác nhận).
    - Pin, RAID/RST, ổ đệm.
    - Điều kiện Windows 11 và độ tương thích bản cài.
  - Sao lưu chọn mục (robocopy, bỏ qua file chỉ có trên OneDrive): thư mục người dùng, Wi-Fi, bookmark, danh sách phần mềm.
  - Máy chỉ có ổ C:: tự thu nhỏ C: tạo phân vùng ITH-STAGING, cài xong gộp lại; không thu nhỏ được thì đặt đệm ngay trên `C:\ITH`.
- `src/ITHelpdeskTool.Reinstall.Cli`: `ithreinstall.exe` (net48), các lệnh `info`, `check`, `backup`, `prepare`, `arm`, `cancel`, `decrypt`.
- Tinh chỉnh nguy hiểm mặc định không chọn. Không kèm activate hay crack.

### Kiểm thử
- Unit test: `tests/ITHelpdeskTool.Reinstall.Tests`.
- E2E trên máy ảo QEMU/KVM của GitHub Actions (`reinstall-e2e.yml`). Run 44880563362 đạt 5/5 kịch bản:
  - `uefi/happy`, `bios/happy`: ổ đệm riêng, cài trọn vòng tới Desktop mới, chép lại Desktop/Documents, cài 7-Zip.
  - `uefi/auto`: một ổ, thu nhỏ C: rồi gộp lại.
  - `bios/samedrive`: đệm ngay trên `C:\ITH`.
  - `uefi/safe`: lỗi trước khi xoá thì về Windows cũ, dữ liệu còn nguyên.
- Chưa chạy trên máy thật.

Chưa có giao diện; bước 2 sẽ thêm trang "Cài lại Windows" vào app.

## Problem and resulting behavior

Selected structural SQL assertions were outside full native qualification, pure boundaries lacked bounded regression guards, and current architecture records contained stale descriptions. This PR integrates isolated SQL profiles and strengthens pure, codec/replay, compiler and browser-storage verification. Review corrections improve generated inputs, crate admission, compiler wrapper isolation and lost-context cleanup. The latest follow-up also closes confirmed collection-construction guard gaps and fixes transaction/WebSocket test-harness lifetime ownership.

The proposed head is `034c36f24971ee6907cc3d5db3f8a4db7d1097fc`: 18 focused commits, including four in the latest follow-up. It addresses #106 and supports #49. The PR was merged under explicit maintainer approval on November 21, 2026; its merge commit is `3ab0c491fbddbcf5439c5a9e60d24ef11af2a1b4`.

## Scope and definition of done

Included: isolated foundation and composed WorkItem/Selection SQL controls; recursive pure inventory and target admission; compiler-resolved API/type controls; deterministic domain membership; bounded codec/replay properties; exact declared-minimum compiler checks; browser-storage/failure controls; current documentation, issue updates and independent exact-head review.

The maintainer explicitly approved prohibiting HashSet and HashMap types throughout pure libraries, including aliases and deterministic custom hashers. This is a conservative policy restriction: deterministic hash collections are not inherently impure. BTree alternatives remain allowed.

Completion requires implementation, relevant affected checks, required configured gates, source/evidence consistency, issue/documentation updates and a final summary. Wider upgrades, events, disaster recovery, release scanners, architectural acceptance and general browser support remain separate obligations.

## Coherent delivery and review map

The PR changes 38 files (+2459/-68), chiefly verification tooling, tests and documentation. The standard is generated from its register and preamble. No lockfile, support declaration or product schema changed. Domain membership collections preserve emitted source-traversal order. The components contribute to one verification outcome; focused commits and this map support review without duplicating expensive qualification.

| Component | Review boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Structural SQL | Fresh serial clusters, composed assertions, actual-role constraints, admission, deadlines, diagnostics and owned cleanup |
| Pure guard/domain | Recursive Cargo/Go inventory, unsupported-target rejection, resolved API/type restrictions and deterministic membership |
| Generated properties | SplitMix64 vectors/low-byte controls, valid-envelope Unicode/JSON/u64 properties, retained replay/retirement and authorization precedence |

## Actual validation

| --- | --- |

| Controllers | 20 focused Python controllers and 22 engineering-document controllers passed in the correction work. The latest follow-up passed 22 Node protocol/cleanup/instrumentation controls; these use fakes and launch no browser |
| Pure behavior/properties | Earlier affected runs passed 159 task-contract tests and four Selection properties, formatting and strict affected-crate all-target Clippy. The final guard passed with 23 actual compiler controls in its required staged gate |
| Constructor probes | Rust 1.99.1 / Clippy 0.1.99 accepted six default-hasher from/default/collect paths under the earlier guard. The isolated candidate rejected those paths and both deterministic-hasher controls; paired BTree controls passed. All 12 collection programs match the final guard inputs |
| Declared compilers | Earlier revised checks passed Rust 1.75.0 (seven non-authority crates) and 1.88.0 (authority), locked/offline/all-target. An intentional unneutralized command reached a rejecting wrapper; both neutralized groups passed without wrapper invocation. Those sources are unchanged in the latest follow-up |
| Actual browser | Earlier Windows Chrome 157.0.8103.80 storage and closed-first-context cleanup passed with independent database absence and owned target/Job/profile cleanup. This observation retains its original source identity; it does not qualify the latest lifecycle changes in a live browser |
| Delivery review/gates | All required staged gates passed. The latest three code gates took approximately 203, 198 and 197 seconds; the final prose-only commit correctly required no test run. Independent composition review covered the exact proposed head and found no substantive unresolved findings |
| Hosted CI | [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/MrQuality/kehila/actions/runs/44923636907): formatting, Rust lint, standalone A0, shared verification/engineering/Go static checks, event-base enforcement and Windows client checks succeeded. Full native runtime steps were skipped under development scope and are not counted as qualification. |

Sources: [delivery and evidence limits](https://github.com/MrQuality/kehila/blob/034c36f24971ee6907cc3d5db3f8a4db7d1097fc/docs/implementation/architecture-verification.md), [testing guide](https://github.com/MrQuality/kehila/blob/034c36f24971ee6907cc3d5db3f8a4db7d1097fc/docs/TESTING.md), [browser component contract](https://github.com/MrQuality/kehila/blob/034c36f24971ee6907cc3d5db3f8a4db7d1097fc/tests/browser/README.md).

author: tokuhirom
body:
Part of #15780 (`.origin` coverage), measured against rakudo 2026.11. This branch is stacked on #18483. Until that PR merges, its commit also shows here.

## What

- **Aliased named assertions with arguments** (`<alias=word("a")>`): `regex_alias_origins` now places the inner `Regex::Assertion::Named::Args`, its `Name` and its argument list. The argument list goes through `regex_call_origins::place`.
- **Regex literal arguments** (`<v(/\d+/)>`): `regex_call_origins::bracketed_len` now reads a `/.../` in term position to its closing slash. Before, the backslash inside stopped the scan, so the call and the `QuotedRegex` argument stayed unplaced.
- **Escaped characters in a character class** (`<-[\x[22]]>`, and range bounds such as `<[\x[41]..\x[5A]]>`): the new `regex_escape_origins::escaped_len` reads `\x` (hex), `\o` (octal) and `\c` (decimal) codepoints, bare or bracketed. The enumeration walk now places a `CharClass::Specified` element written this way, and range bounds written as escapes. `regex_origins` gains only the two match arms and a `bound` helper.

## Tests

- `t/rakuast/rakuast-origin-regex-alias-args-escapes.t` gives identical output under `raku` and mutsu.
- New unit test `regex_escape_origins::tests::escapes`.
- `scripts/dev status gate-20261121-090958-snln`: **passed**. Quick profile, focus `t/rakuast t/syntax t/lang t/regex t/grammar` (2360 files). The branch, checks, clippy, cargo-test and t-focus stages all passed.

body:
Un billet « Appel à exposants marché de noël au colosse ! » (Ville de Saint-André) se lisait comme un avis aux exposants, pas comme une sortie. La règle est de marketing.

**Ce qui change**
- Quand le titre commence par « Appel à exposants » ou « Appel à candidatures », et que chaque jour du billet a ses heures pour le public, l'événement est donné par le nom de sa sortie, dans les majuscules d'usage : « Marché de Noël au Colosse ». Ces majuscules d'usage sont l'initiale, les fêtes (Noël, Pâques…) et les noms de lieux de la commune tels que le répertoire des lieux les écrit.
- Dessous : « annoncé par la Ville de Saint-André dans un appel à exposants », avec le lien du billet. On le voit sur la liste (/evenements, /communes/…) et sur la page de l'événement.
- Sans heures pour le public, ou sans nom de sortie, le billet n'est pas donné comme une sortie : ses dates sont le plus souvent celles de l'appel (« candidatures avant le 30/11 »).
- La règle s'applique dans l'outil, sur ce qu'il lit de tous les agendas. Ce qui est stocké par source ne change pas.

**Révision** : rendu `agenda` 44, parce que les pages des événements changent.

**NOUVEAUTES** (mots de marketing) : « Événements : une sortie annoncée par un appel à exposants est donnée sous son nom, avec ses heures pour le public et le lien du billet. »

**Ancienne adresse** : la page de l'événement sous son ancien titre (/evenements/appel-a-exposants-…-<clé>) est redirigée en 301 vers la nouvelle, par sa clé (ficheIssue). C'est testé dans test/appel.test.ts.

**Tests** : `test/appel.test.ts` (8 tests). Suite complète : 328 fichiers, 3600 tests verts.

Outils IA : aligné (outil evenements) : il donne le même nom et le champ `annonce` (« annoncé par … dans un appel à exposants »), avec `lien`, comme la page.

## What

Adds `.github/workflows/selftests.yml`, the repository's first workflow. It covers step A3 and the first half of step A4 of the roadmap proposed in #3, which is not merged.

- **Triggers:** pull requests, and pushes to `main`.
- **Setup:**
  - `actions/checkout@v5` with `persist-credentials: false`.
  - `actions/setup-python@v6` pinned to Python 3.11. Both are the Node 24 majors.
  - Token scope `contents: read`. No secrets, no dependency install, no network access after setup.
- **Step 1, self-tests:**
  - `tests/phase2/r1_normalizer.py` (6 cases)
  - `tests/phase2/r1_compressor.py` (2 round-trips)
  - `tests/v0.2/strip_test_b_markers.py --selftest` (14 cases)
- **Step 2, regenerate committed outputs:**
  - `tests/v0.2/scoring/_unseal.py` rewrites the two `*_unsealed.tsv`.
  - `tests/phase2/r1_ab/derive_b_prime_double.py` rewrites `test_b_prime/` and `test_b_doubleprime/`.
- **Step 3, check:** fails if `git diff --exit-code` reports a change or if `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` lists any file.

`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` keeps `__pycache__/` out of the tree. Without it, step 3 would fail, because `r1_compressor.py` imports `r1_normalizer` and the repository has no `.gitignore` yet (A1).

The diff is this one new file. It changes no spec text, script, data, score or verdict.

## How it was verified

Local runs used Python 3.11.18 with the standard library only, in a fresh clone of this branch (`356c076`).

- **The three `run:` blocks**, read from the YAML and run with `bash -e` as Actions does, all exit 0:
  - self-tests: 6/6, 2/2 and 14/14 pass;
  - `_unseal.py`: 60 rows per rater;
  - `derive_b_prime_double.py`: ALL PASS;

- **The step 3 script, run on two altered trees**, exits 1 both times:
  - a committed output (`test_b_prime/mab1.md`) altered and then regenerated: it prints the diff;
  - a stray untracked `__pycache__/x.pyc`: it lists the file.
- **The YAML** was parsed with PyYAML. No schema linter (actionlint or similar) was run.
- **On GitHub**, this PR's run is the workflow's first. Check run `selftests` on `356c076` concluded `success` in 6 s with 0 annotations, so there was no Node 20 deprecation warning.

The CEO owns push gates ([AGENTS.md:13](https://github.com/Mythmaker28/aoven-protocol/blob/0eaaba60c7fc63657db89b8db1e97742b274f11b/AGENTS.md?plain=1#L13)). The question asked in #3, whether hygiene PRs may be merged here without review, has no answer yet. This PR therefore waits for the owner.

author: jaredwy
body:
## Original problem

`telemetry::resource_metrics::tests::a_span_window_charges_what_the_process_used_while_it_was_open` sometimes fails under a normal parallel `cargo test`. A span window reads counters shared by the whole process. The scheduler's tests add runtime busy time to the same counter while they run, so the exact `runtime_busy_ms == 3.0` check fails whenever one of them steps while the window is open.

## Linked issue

None.

## Diagnostics

- On macOS, a full `cargo test -p skippy-serving --lib` run failed this test at `resource_metrics.rs:751` (1349 passed, 1 failed).
- Run alone with `--exact`, it passed three times out of three.
- `RUNTIME_BUSY_NANOS` is a process-wide static, and `record_compute` in `frontend/iteration_scheduler.rs` adds to it for every plan it executes.

## Fix

`SpanWindow::close` now hands the readings it takes to a new `charge`. The test calls `charge` with fixed readings, the way `rates_come_from_the_interval_between_readings` already does. That lets it check CPU time and the footprint change exactly; before, it checked only that CPU time was not negative. What spans report is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `cargo clippy -p skippy-serving --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes, and three full `cargo test -p skippy-serving --lib` runs pass.
- [x] No UI change.
- [x] I agree to license my contributions under the Apache License, Version 2.0.

author: transilluminate
body:
Scoring fixes from the wild-4 triage (mismatch, plausible and wrong_work groups): floors and caps in `crates/core/src/matching/` and one guard in `crates/engine/src/verdict.rs`. One commit per rule. No FFI or CLI JSON shape changes.

## Rules

1. **Identifier + authors, title from free text** (`assess.rs`). If the claimed identifiers are all the record's, the authors corroborate (≥ 0.75, which includes the stranger-capped partial), no title was given as a field, the text's title mismatches, and none of year, volume or page is wrong, the floor is plausible. The title is listed as the difference. Labels, descriptions and short forms no longer become `id_disagrees`.
2. **Identifier + exact place** (`assess.rs`, `verdict.rs`). If the identifiers are all the record's and the journal, volume and first page match, the floor is plausible unless the title and the authors both mismatch. From a candidate placed like that (title or authors not both wrong), `id_elsewhere` no longer redirects to a candidate whose ids or page disagree.
3. **The identifier counts as a field for `SINGLE_FIELD_CAP`** (`caps.rs`, `assess.rs`). This applies when the identifier is the record's and every cited field is Match or Unknown. `Title. arXiv:ID` now verifies, as the bare id already did. A title alone (books, reviews) is still capped.
4. **Short titles and ellipses** (`text.rs`, `assess.rs`).
   - A title found in free text only as a main title or first sentence of fewer than 3 content words, or as a whole one-word title, drops to partial. That stops it feeding `near_miss`. It stays a match when authors, ids, place or journal corroborate.
   - A record title's opening words (≥ 3 content words) followed by `…` or `...` score partial.
5. **Chapter for book** (optional; `assess.rs`). A chapter is capped at 0.8 when its book's title is found in the text and no chapter mark is cited ("In:", editors, a page), unless its own title is cited before the book's. The book's record then ranks first.

## A/B (offline replay, 11 corpora, vs 0.38.3)

Total: 96 changed. **39 FIXED, 26 UP, 27 same-ok, 4 still-wrong; 0 BROKE, 0 BROKE(false-verified), 0 DOWN.** No `providers_failed` flips.

| corpus | FIXED | UP | same-ok | still-wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wild-4 | 24 | 21 | 7 | 3 |
| wild-3 | 10 | 5 | 18 | 0 |
| wild-2 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| wild-1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| holdout-5 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| holdout-1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

What each rule added on top of the one before:
- **Rule 1:** 32 FIXED (wild-4 20, wild-3 8, wild-2 4), 24 same-ok. The first version broke holdout-6 #802: another paper's DOI beside a namesake surname. The volume/page guard removed that break.
- **Rule 2:** 6 FIXED (wild-4 #361, #367, #369; wild-3 #396, #461; wild-1 #16), 1 same-ok (a chimera, which is allowed). The first version broke wild-4 #21, a wrong PMID beside the right DOI. Requiring every claimed id to match removed that break.
- **Rule 3:** 26 UP (wild-4 21, wild-3 5), all `unconfirmed` → `id_agrees`.
- **Rule 4:**
  - 1 FIXED (wild-4 #23, an ellipsis);
  - 3 UP (#361, #427, #433);
  - 3 still-wrong, all mismatch/closest → not_found: #320, #543, #619. They were false accusations. Fixing them fully needs ISBN cells and book series, which are other WPs.
  - The first version also demoted whole two-word titles, which broke holdout-6 #700. Whole titles are now short only at one word.
- **Rule 5:** 2 same-ok with the right work now best (wild-4 #538, #623). The first version took 7 real chapters (StatPearls, "In Critical Readings…") down to plausible. The chapter-title-first guard removed all 7.

Rows checked by hand: wild-4 #25, #100, #427, #467, #367, #369; wild-3 #604, #843; wild-4 #484, #659, #674. Each has the right verdict and the right work.

## Intent

R8.6: fault suites for the proactive takeover (ADR 0021), and fixes for the faults they found. The switch stays off.

Spec: docs/specs/proactive-takeover-faults/SPEC.md

## Alternatives rejected

Capping the header inside the shared fence (lazy takes would be refused too): the cap is per read, `named_within`, and refuses before reading the body. A second fence for the dead-log pass: it now reads through the node's shared `Predecessors`.

## Invariants

Requests scale with nodes and bytes: the pass adds one descriptor GET per index a death names, no LIST; the dead-log pass after a pass costs 7 requests fewer (15 to 8). Fencing unchanged (head CAS, log conditional creates).

high: touches the S3 request pattern of takeover and fencing reads. No default changes. ADR: [0021](docs/adr/0021-proactive-takeover-from-the-node-log.md).

author: kimdre
body:
## Summary

Part 5 of ADR-0049: the CloudPanel import of PHP settings (the "Import" bullet of the ADR).

- **Plan mapping:** `plan.PHPSettingsOf` maps the old pool's allowlisted `php_value`/`php_admin_value` settings onto `agentapi.PHPSettings`.
  - When a key has both, `php_admin_value` wins, as in FPM.
  - Values equal to the Hostashi default stay unset, so they keep following the default.
- **Clamping:** values out of bounds are clamped. "No limit" becomes the upper bound: `memory_limit = -1`, `max_execution_time = 0` and `post_max_size = 0`.
  - Unreadable values fall back to the default, for example a time zone that is not a valid zone name or an `error_reporting` expression without a matching preset.
  - A `post_max_size` below the upload size is raised.
  - Every changed value is named in the review reason `php_settings_changed`.
- **Not taken over:** keys outside the allowlist are listed in `php_settings_not_taken`. Keys the Hostashi pool sets itself are left out of that list: `open_basedir`, temp and session paths, `disable_functions`.
- **Body size:** if the old vhost's `client_max_body_size` differs from the new effective `post_max_size`, the review reason is `body_size`.
- **Site creation:** `cpmigrate.NewSite.PHPSettings` carries the settings. `siteCreator` sets them with `SetPHPSettings` after creating the site. The plan shows `phpSettings` (count) and `phpSettingsOn`, and the audit records `phpSettings`.
- **Scanner:** it now also keeps `max_file_uploads` and `session.gc_maxlifetime`, which are both on the allowlist.
- **Wiki:** a section "Sites from CloudPanel" on the PHP settings page.

The fixture's pool, with 256M, 64M and 64M plus `client_max_body_size 64m`, matches the defaults, so its plan is unchanged.

## Tests

- New `plan/phpsettings_test.go` covers the mapping, clamping and review reasons.
- `cpmigrate` and `serve` tests check that the settings reach the new site.
- The scanner test covers the two new keys.
- golangci-lint reports 0 issues on the changed packages.

Unblocks the pre-push full check in cloud sessions, needed for spec #521's integration branch.

## Summary

`test_it_fails_closed_without_the_agent_cli_or_the_harness` builds a PATH of symlinks to the driver's tools, with no `claude` and no `sh`. Hosted agent sessions put an `rm` wrapper script first on PATH. Linked into that bare PATH, it can't find its interpreter, so the driver's exit trap failed with 127, and the full check failed in every cloud session. The test now links the first candidate on PATH that is a program, not a `#!` script.

```diff
-    ln -s "$(command -v "$tool")" "tools/$tool"
+    # first candidate from `type -a -P "$tool"` that does not start with "#!"
+    ln -s "$found" "tools/$tool"
```

## Evidence

- Before: `scripts/eval-batch/test.sh` → `FAIL test_it_fails_closed_without_the_agent_cli_or_the_harness: no claude: exit code 127, not 1`, 20 passed, 1 failed (this cloud container).
- After: 21 passed, 0 failed.
- `scripts/check.sh` (full, pre-push hook) passed. Skipped: PowerShell parse (pwsh not installed; CI runs it).
- CI: pending.

## Merge risk

Two-way door. Blast radius: none (test-only). The test checks the same behaviour: it still fails closed with no `claude` and no harness, and it isn't weakened.

body:
Part 7b: the Flutter app foundation. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-21-07b-app-foundation.md`. Design direction: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-immersive-market-design.md` (the immersive market itself is not built here).

**What the app does today**
- Sign-up with a one-time code, sign-in, and password recovery (no hint whether a number has an account).
- A shell with a Market placeholder and an Account page (version, terms, privacy and support links; only https links open).
- An address book: list, add, delete, with Abuja area councils.
- An update-required / maintenance notice driven by `GET /app/config`.
- Palette "Abuja Dusk", platform system font, 200% text and 48dp targets covered by widget tests.

**Built on:** Flutter 3.50.1, Riverpod, go_router, dio, secure storage.

**Data protection**
- The token lives only in the platform keystore. On iOS it is kept on this device only, and a fresh install clears a token an earlier install left behind. Android backup is off.
- Nothing in `lib/` logs. Passwords, codes and phones never go into routes. Errors and models redact `toString()`.
- One person's addresses are never written into another person's session after a sign-out and sign-in.

body:
Closes #60

## Resumen

- Archivos de traducción `es.ts` (fuente de los tipos) y `en.ts` en `src/lib/i18n/messages/`.
- `createTranslate` con claves, variables y plurales tipados (`Intl.PluralRules`). Una clave inexistente, una variable que falta o una que sobra no compilan.
- `getTranslate(language)` para el servidor sin petición; `useTranslate()` en componentes, alimentado por el loader de la raíz, que solo envía los textos del idioma de la página.
- La home (título, descripción y texto), el 404 y el error general salen de traducciones en `/` y `/en/`.
- Tests: unitarios de textos y plurales, tipos con `@ts-expect-error`, home, y servidor construido (`/en/` no trae español; 404 por idioma). Playwright: capturas y axe de `/en/`, sin advertencias de hidratación.

Sin dependencias nuevas.

## ⚠ No verificado

- Las capturas de línea base de `/en/` en Linux no se generaron (se trabajó en Windows). Hay que correr `visual-baselines.yml` a mano en este PR para aceptarlas.
- Camilo debe revisar las traducciones al inglés de `en.ts`.
- La paridad de variables entre idiomas se queda para la guardia del #61.

## Revisión y cambios posteriores

El worker abrió este PR sin dejar constancia de su revisión y sin marcar las casillas del issue. Se revisó entero después, con `code-reviewer`: APPROVED en la segunda ronda.

- **Hallazgo alto, corregido.** La página de error dependía de las traducciones, que llegan con los datos de la raíz. Cuando el fallo ocurría antes de que existieran (un método que React Router rechaza, un error en el middleware o en el loader de la raíz), la página de error lanzaba también. `OPTIONS /en/` respondía "Unexpected Server Error". Ahora sus cuatro textos viven en `src/lib/i18n/messages/errors.ts`, viajan con el código y el `ErrorBoundary` los lee sin proveedor.
- **Hallazgo alto, descartado con evidencia.** El revisor dedujo que al navegar de `/` a `/en/` sin recargar los textos no cambiarían. No pasa: en modo framework con SSR React Router vuelve a pedir los loaders en cada navegación (`route-module.md`, sección `shouldRevalidate`), y una prueba nueva de Playwright que navega sin recargar pasa sin ningún `shouldRevalidate`. El revisor retiró el hallazgo.
- Pruebas nuevas: `src/root.test.tsx`, dos casos de `OPTIONS` en `production-build.test.ts`, un valor con llaves que no se vuelve a expandir y una variable ausente que lanza.

### Decisión para revisar

**Los cuatro textos de la página de error llegan al navegador en todos los idiomas.** Es una excepción al criterio de que el navegador solo recibe los textos del idioma de la página. Por eso esa casilla del issue queda sin marcar: la decide Camilo. Todo el resto del contenido sigue viajando solo en un idioma.

### Sin aplicar

- El título de la home sigue partido en tres claves para pintar el 60 en rojo. Es frágil para otro orden de palabras, pero esa home es provisional y la reemplaza W3.
- Faltan casos de tipos para un plural sin `count` o con una variable de más.

En local, tras los cambios: 625 pruebas unitarias, Playwright 57 de 57, lint y tipos en verde.

author: alilxxey
body:
This PR targets the feature branch of jiwoochris/artex-global#51. It addresses token persistence in the ChatGPT sign-in feature requested in jiwoochris/artex-global#50.

When the issuer rotates a refresh token and writing the credentials to disk fails, the first access-token request reports the write error. A second request can return the newly cached access token even though the replacement refresh token exists only in memory. Restarting the process at that point can leave the installation with an invalid refresh token.

The change keeps a failed save pending under the manager lock. Later access-token requests retry the local write before using the cached token or contacting the issuer again. If the process exits before storage recovers, the user may still need to sign in again.

The regression test makes the token store unwritable, checks that two successive calls return an error and no token, restores storage, and reloads the saved credentials. It also checks that the issuer received exactly one refresh request.

Verified with Go:
- The regression test failed on the original feature branch at the second call.
- `go test -race -count=3 ./chatgptplan` passed with the fix.
- `go vet ./chatgptplan` passed.

These tests use local OAuth fixtures.

author: falistos
body:
The owner asks "where are we?" about 120 times a month, and leads read their workers one `task_status` or `t3_thread_read` at a time. `t3_thread_list` has no parent filter, so no single read shows a lead's fleet.

## What changes

- **`t3_fleet` (MCP, read-only).** For the calling thread, it lists every child recorded on its task records: subagents, delegated tasks in this environment (same project or another one, #24), and tasks on linked environments. Each child has its title, link, environment label, model, work state (`working`, `waiting_for_children`, `needs_answer`, `failed`, `done`), its pending question and approval counts, its PRs with their state, its last progress line and its last activity time. The result also gives the counts for each state and the number of open PRs. Children that need an answer come first, then failed, then working ones. `limit` defaults to 20 and is capped at 50.
  - A child in this environment is read from its shell, with one batched `getShellSnapshot`. Its pending requests are counted from the `runtimeRequests` records, read only for children whose shell shows a pending request. A waiting secret or link card (`userOnly`) counts as a question. Its last progress line is the last assistant reply of its latest run (one run's messages), else `task.progress ?? task.result`. An archived or deleted child is left out, as the strip leaves it out.
  - A provider-native subagent (Claude `Agent`, Codex `spawn_agent`) runs no run on its own thread, so its state and progress come from its task record (`status`, `progress`, `result`). The strip leaves these subagents out, because their shell alone cannot tell whether they are working or have failed.
  - A child on a linked environment is read from its task record here (`remoteChild`, `progress`, `result`), with no call to that environment. Its question and approval counts are `null`.
  - The read acknowledges nothing, unlike `task_status`.
- **`fleetWorkState`** in contracts. The server and the client both use it, so the tool and the strip classify a child the same way. A turn blocked in `t3_thread_wait` or a waiting `delegate_task` reads as `waiting_for_children`, not `working`.
- `t3_fleet` is in Claude's read-only allow-list (`CLAUDE_READ_ONLY_T3_MCP_ALLOWED_TOOLS`), so Plan mode does not ask for it. It is also in `t3McpToolPresentation.ts`, under the existing `task-status` summary ("Checked task status"), so no new summary string was needed.
- **Strip above the composer (web).** It appears on a thread that has children. It shows a "N waiting for an answer" button that opens the child that has waited longest, then the running, failed and done counts and the open PR count. `createThreadFleetAtom` (client-runtime) derives it from the shells already on the client. There is no new polling, and the atom keeps its value while a child only streams, so the strip renders only when a count changes.
- Docs: a `t3_fleet` section in `docs/orchestration-v2/orchestrator-mcp-server.md`. `agentContextBudget.json`: `mcpToolListJsonBytes` 58768 → 59151 (+383) for the new tool, measured after the rebase on main.

## Decisions

- D? **"Launched" children = cross-project `delegate_task` children.** The brief names "launched threads with a launcher link from lot launchwake". Launchwake (#24) decided against a launcher link: a launch in another project is now a `delegate_task` with a task record. `t3_thread_launch` threads still record nothing at their launcher, so they are not listed (documented).
- D? **"Blocked" in the strip is the "waiting for an answer" button.** A blocked child is one with a pending question or approval, so showing both would repeat the same number. Children waiting on their own children count as running.
- D? **Pending requests count without the live-run check** that `threadShell`'s approval roll-up applies. A question still pending after its run ended can still be answered, and the owner wants to see it. Only `auth_refresh` and `dynamic_tool_call` are excluded.
- D? **A child followed up with `t3_thread_send` appears once**, under its newest task record.
- D? **Every task record is read, and every local child gets a shell, with no cap.** `t3_thread_list` with a status filter makes the same choice. The output is bounded by `limit`, but building the shells is not. A lead with hundreds of children pays for that once per call (see Limits).
- D? **The integration test is in `RemoteDelegation.test.ts`.** That harness is the only one with the real OrchestratorV2, the MCP toolkit, a linked box and a cross-project local child. The test is appended at the end of the file. The approvals lot may also touch this file, so expect at most a trivial end-of-file conflict.
- D? **Files outside the brief's list, each needed to wire the feature:** `packages/client-runtime/package.json` (subpath export `./state/thread-fleet`), `apps/web/src/state/threads.ts` (the atom instance, next to `childThreadApprovalsAtom`), `apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx` (mounts the strip above `ChildThreadApprovals`), `agentContextBudget.json` and the doc above. `threadShell.ts` and the files of the approvals lot are untouched.

## Tests

- `apps/server/src/peer/RemoteDelegation.test.ts` "t3_fleet reads every child of the parent, here and there, in one call" runs through the real OrchestratorV2 and the in-process MCP server. It covers:
  - a task on a linked box (`working`, label "Box", counts `null`);
  - a cross-project local child with a pending command approval, a linked PR and an assistant reply (`needs_answer`, `pendingApprovals: 1`, one open PR, `lastProgress` from the reply);
  - a running provider-native subagent (`working`, `lastProgress` from its record);
  - a finished subagent (`done`, `lastProgress` from its result).

  It also checks the counts, the order, and that `limit: 1` keeps the child that needs an answer. Without `t3_fleet` in the toolkit it fails, and with the first round's service the native and `lastProgress` assertions fail.
- `packages/contracts/src/orchestratorMcp.test.ts`: a table for `fleetWorkState`, including a running turn blocked on its children.
- `packages/client-runtime/src/state/threadFleet.test.ts` covers:
  - the roll-up: every state, awaited background work, a user-only secret card, the auth-refresh exclusion, the oldest waiting child, PR dedup and merged PRs;
  - the child filter: other parent, other environment, side chat, archived, provider-native subagent;
  - atom stability while a child streams.

## Screenshots

On a dev server with the `Replay (dev)` provider: a lead in one project delegated an e2e run to another local project. The strip shows "1 running" while the child runs, then "1 done". The PNGs are on dev2 at `/home/agent/t3-boost/reports/fleet-strip-running.png` and `fleet-strip-done.png`. They are not uploaded here: dev2 has no upload path, and the lead holds copies. The "waiting for an answer" state is covered by the unit tests: no free replay scenario makes a child ask a question.

## Limits and follow-ups

- Mobile strip (out of scope).
- `t3_fleet` builds a shell for every local child. If leads with hundreds of children turn out slow, cap it to the active children plus the `limit` most recent.
- Evals for the new tool description were not run: they use paid models (to replay: `cd evals && pnpm mcp-tool-use --out runs/fleet`). No eval case was added.

Opus 5.5 (Claude Code, in T3 Code)

body:
## Breaking changes
- The OSIRIS JSON Producer is renamed from vManage to Cisco Catalyst
  SD-WAN Manager, including its emitted identity:
  - CLI: `osirisjson-producer cisco catalyst-sdwan-manager` (was `cisco vmanage`)
  - Go package: `osiris/network/cisco/catalyst-sd-wan-manager`
  - provider name `cisco.catalystsdwanmanager`, extension namespace
    `osiris.cisco.catalystsdwanmanager`
  - extension keys use the current naming (e.g. `connected_manager`)
- Sites are emitted as `logical.site` groups, one document per
  selected site.
- `--purpose documentation` now emits only an explicit field
  allowlist; detail fields are `--purpose audit` only.
- Tenants are no longer reported as `metadata.scope.accounts`.

API values from before the Catalyst rebranding (`vmanage`, `vsmart`,
`vbond`, `connectedVManages`, ...) are decoded as the API sends them;
they pass through unchanged only into `provider.type` and
`properties.model`. The testdata/ README documents them.

## Highlights

- **Cross-site graph:** every site document keeps the OMP sessions and
  SD-WAN tunnels it takes part in, carrying the remote ends as neighbor
  resources with the same IDs in every document, so a consumer merging
  documents by ID obtains one graph. Canonical bidirectional OMP
  connections, VPN-distinct interfaces, dual-stack reconciliation, no
  empty IDs, order-independent output.
- **Collection:** classified errors, bounded response bodies, capped
  Retry-After, one retry for timeouts and 5xx reads, one session
  renewal per run, parallel throttled peer lookups, and a coverage
  record in `metadata` (`complete`, per-operation coverage, graph
  counters). `--require-complete` fails on a partial document.
- **Safety:** recursive raw-body redaction with caps, no response
  bodies, queries or URLs in diagnostics, same-origin redirects only,
  contained atomic 0600 output publication.
- **Fixtures:** synthetic `lab_sdwan`, `lab_cross_site` and per-release
  `contract_20_18`, `contract_26_1`, `contract_26_2` scenarios with
  byte-for-byte goldens at both purposes.
- **Test data policy scanner:** runs git from fixed system directories
  instead of `PATH`.
- Repository INSTALL instructions rewritten and README including
  updated planned roadmap and quick installation instructions with
  Cisco DevNet sandbox example.

## Notes

- Supported Cisco SD-WAN API Manager releases 20.18, 26.1 and 26.2 are
  covered at documented-contract level, documents carry
  `api_profile: "unverified"` because the producer does not discover
  the Manager release.

author: wangguangxin
body:
No tracking issue yet.

### Description

**Problem.** Spark's LZ4 codec checksums every stream with the JNI `StreamingXXHash32` when the native library is loaded. In lz4-java 1.8.0 that class has a finalizer, so creating one registers it under the JVM-wide finalizer lock. The multithreaded shuffle creates one per record when writing and one per block when reading, so with tens of thousands of partitions writer and task threads queue on that lock. On q06, 46% of writer thread samples in stage 35 and 44% of task thread samples in stage 40 were BLOCKED in `Finalizer.register`.

**Fix.** When the `SerializerManager` in use would wrap shuffle streams in plain LZ4 (no encryption), build the same LZ4 block streams with the pure Java XXHash32, which has no finalizer. This applies to the threaded writer and to the fetcher's stream wrapper. Seed, block size and flags match Spark's `LZ4CompressionCodec`, so the bytes are identical and either side reads the other. The manager is probed rather than the configuration, so callers that pass their own manager are followed.

When ported onto `main`, the writer call site moved to the current, per-record writer.

**User-facing changes.** None.

**Testing.**
- Writer, reader, unregister and coalesce suites (39 tests) passed on the development branch.
- A standalone check also passed:
  - For 8 sizes from 0 B to 1 MiB, the output bytes are identical to Spark's codec.
  - Streams read correctly in both directions.
  - Corruption is detected.
  - zstd and uncompressed managers fall back to the `SerializerManager`.
- Re-run on this branch (cherry-picked onto `main`), Spark 3.5.3 build, all passed: `RapidsShuffleThreadedReaderSuite` + `GpuShuffleCoalesceSuite` 8, `RapidsShuffleThreadedWriterSuite` + `RapidsShuffleManagerUnregisterSuite` 31. Integration tests have not been run.

## What and why

Opening an app never cleared the Notifications items counted on its badge (agent notes tagged `app:<id>` with the app set to Badge). Nothing inside the app shows them, so the badge stayed stuck (Messenger showed 9 for days while its Inbox said "No unread chats"; Second Hand 3).

author: wangguangxin
body:
No tracking issue yet.

### Description

**Problem.** Every block read by the multithreaded shuffle reader allocates and frees a host buffer through `HostAlloc`. Its accounting and allocation path all synchronized on the singleton: `tryAllocNonPinned` held the monitor across `malloc` and cleaner registration, and the release paths, `checkSize`, `canNeverSucceed` and `getSingleton` took it on every call. With many partitions every reader and task thread of an executor serializes on it. On q04 (12000 partitions), the final aggregation stage averaged 53.5 threads per executor waiting on this monitor, and task threads were 53% BLOCKED in `releaseNonPinned`.

**Fix.** Track the non-pinned, pageable and pinned totals in `AtomicLong`s. Reserve non-pinned budget with a CAS loop and `malloc` outside any lock, returning the reservation if `malloc` throws. Drop the monitor from the read-only size checks, and read the singleton through a volatile field. `initialize` keeps its lock.

This is a port of the change the measurements were taken with onto the current `HostAlloc`, which now also has a pageable pool (#16740). The pageable counter gets the same treatment.

**User-facing changes.** None.

**Testing.**
- Measured version: `com.nvidia.spark.rapids.spill` suites (217 tests) passed on top of it. The port onto the current `HostAlloc` has not been compiled or tested yet.
- Re-run on this branch (cherry-picked onto `main`), Spark 3.5.3 build, all passed: spill package (8 suites) 217, `RowToColumnarIteratorRetrySuite` 30, `HostColumnToGpuRetrySuite` 3 (250 passed; the 7 `LargeHostMemorySuite` tests are opt-in and were skipped). Integration tests have not been run.

### Performance

Measured on one host (352 CPUs, 2x RTX PRO 6000) with the stress suite: SSB SF3000 queries with 12000 (q04) and 20000 (q06) shuffle partitions, multithreaded shuffle, 8 executors x 16 cores. The measured jars also contained the other changes of this series (see each table), one run per configuration unless noted. Result fingerprints were identical in every run.

| q04 (12000 partitions), conn=8, 2 executors x 32 cores | before | this change + SparkResourceAdaptor handle change (cudf-spark-jni) |
|---|---|---|
| final aggregation stage | 616 s | 441 s |
| query | 1539 s | 1405 s |
| threads waiting on the HostAlloc / SparkResourceAdaptor monitors | 53.5 / 19.7 per executor | 0 |

author: mojatter
body:
Closes #265.

tree's JSON decoding kept the last value of a name repeated in one object, without an error, while YAML decoding (#258, #261) and `ToNode` (#264) reject the same input. `MarshalViaJSON` inherited it, so keys that encode to the same JSON name lost a value there: `map[string]int{"\xff": 1, "\xfe": 2}` (both become `"\ufffd"`), or `map[any]any{1: "a", "1": "b"}` with Go 1.27, whose `json.Marshal` writes both as `"1"`. A repeated name now fails with `duplicate object member name "a"`, the wording `encoding/json/v2` uses by default:

- This covers `DecodeJSON` (tq input), `UnmarshalJSON`, `MarshalViaJSON` and the `UnmarshalJSON` methods of `Map`, `Array` and `Any`, at any depth and for names spelled with escapes (`"a"` and `"\u0061"`).
- `Map.UnmarshalJSON` still merges into the keys the map already holds: only a name repeated within the input is an error, and the map keeps the keys set before it.
- Edit values and YAML input are unchanged; they already rejected repeated keys.

Release notes: JSON input that repeats a name in one object is an error instead of keeping the last value (jq keeps the last value); `echo '{"a":1,"a":2}' | tq .` now fails as `tq -y .` already did.

Not changed: `json.Decoder.Token` reads invalid UTF-8 and lone surrogates in a name as U+FFFD, so names that differ only there are now rejected as a repeat of `"\ufffd"`, as json/v2 reports them under `AllowInvalidUTF8` (by default json/v2 rejects the invalid UTF-8 itself). Encoding is unchanged too: `MarshalJSON` writes invalid UTF-8 in a key as U+FFFD, so a Map holding both `"\xff"` and `"\xfe"` (e.g. from YAML `!!binary` keys) encodes to JSON that tree now rejects when it is decoded back into a tree node; json/v2 refuses to marshal such keys by default.

author: ikook-wang
body:
Related #629

Debian 13 镜像的三个下载地址（Debian 官方源、南京大学镜像、中国科学技术大学镜像）都失败时，界面只显示「准备 Debian 13 镜像失败：程序提前结束（退出码 1），未返回可识别的原因」。原因有两层：

- `cage setup` 输出错误前会做诊断脱敏，URL 和主机名都变成 `[url]` / `[host]`，看不出是哪个镜像站；
- 工作台只把已知模式转成用户可见的说明，Lima 的多地址下载错误不在其中，于是退回到退出码。

### 改动

- `internal/vm`：新增 `ImageDownloadSummary`，解析 Lima 拼接的 ``failed to download `URL`: 原因``。每个地址归为固定代码，格式为 `镜像:原因:进度`：
  - 镜像为 `official` / `nju` / `ustc` / `other`；
  - 原因为 `http-NNN` / `eof` / `timeout` / `tls` / `dns` / `refused` / `checksum` / `other`；
  - 进度为 `kept` / `none`，依据可续传下载器的 `partial data retained` 判断。
  
  输出一行 `CAGE_IMAGE_DOWNLOAD_FAILED ...`，不含 URL、主机名或服务器响应，所以不受脱敏影响。`cageDebianImages` 改为与它共用同一份镜像列表。
- `cage setup`：步骤失败且属于镜像下载失败时，在原有 `Error:` 之后多输出这一行。
- 工作台：`executionFailure` 先用严格的正则匹配这一行，只接受固定代码，带其他文本的行一律不认，然后生成说明，例如：

  > 准备 Debian 13 镜像失败：Debian 镜像的下载地址都未能完成下载：Debian 官方源（连接被中途断开，已保留下载进度）；南京大学镜像（HTTP 429，请求过于频繁，已保留下载进度）；中国科学技术大学镜像（HTTP 403，服务器拒绝访问）。这通常与所选代理出口和镜像站之间的连接有关。请在网络与代理设置中换一个节点，或稍后再继续安装；已下载的部分会保留，继续安装时从断点续传。

issue 里提到的「选择本地已校验镜像」入口不在本 PR 范围内。

### 验证

- `TestImageDownloadSummaryFromDownloaderErrors`：用本地 HTTP 服务分别返回 429、403 和中途断开，经 Lima 实际的 `fileutils.DownloadFile` 下载，再按 `instance.Prepare` 的方式合并错误，得到 `other:http-429:kept other:http-403:none other:eof:kept`。429 和断开会重试并保留进度，403 直接失败。摘要中没有地址。
- `TestImageDownloadSummaryNamesDebianMirrors`：三个镜像站、按状态文字报告的 HTTP 错误、校验不符，以及与镜像下载无关的错误。
- `TestImageDownloadFailureNamesEachMirror` / `TestImageDownloadFailureRejectsOtherText`：说明文字的内容；摘要行附带其他文本、出现未知代码或前面有其他内容时都不被接受。
- `go test ./internal/vm ./internal/cli ./internal/workbench` 通过（按 CI 方式把随附 QEMU 加入 PATH），`go vet` 无告警。

Service `alertmanager.monitoring:9093`, pod `alertmanager-0`, PVC 2Gi `longhorn-standard`.
- New ExternalSecrets `alertmanager-pushover` and `alertmanager-healthchecks` (new Secret names, because two apps cannot own the same Secret). Mounted under `/etc/alertmanager-secrets/`, outside the read-only config mount. The old ExternalSecrets stay until the next PR so a revert still works.
- The Alertmanager CiliumNetworkPolicy moves to the new chart (same name and rules).
- A trimmed `PrometheusRule` for the new Alertmanager (reload failure, failed notifications, down, crashloop). The kube-prometheus-stack `alertmanager.rules` group selects `job="prometheus-alertmanager"`, which no longer exists, so it is switched off. Cluster-membership alerts are left out (single replica).
- kube-prometheus-stack: bundled Alertmanager off, Prometheus sends to `alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093` via `additionalAlertManagerConfigs`, and its Grafana Alertmanager datasource is off (it pointed at the removed service and was not reachable from the Grafana CNP anyway).
- Docs: service name and file paths in `monitoring-alerting.md` and `troubleshooting.md`.

## Checked
- `helm template` of the new chart and of kube-prometheus-stack 93.3.0 with the new values: no `Alertmanager` CR, no `alertmanager.rules` rule, no Alertmanager datasource, additional Alertmanager config decodes to the new target; the new config, secret mounts and storage render as intended. `helm lint` passes.

author: wangguangxin
body:
No tracking issue yet.

### Description

**Problem.** With the previous lock removed, the next serialization point for the multithreaded reader was the `SpillableHostStore` monitor: every block's host buffer is tracked (`trackNoSpill`) and removed under it, and `removeFromHostStore` also took the `SpillFramework` lock. On q06 (20000 partitions), stage 40 task threads were 29% BLOCKED in `SpillableHostStore.remove`, and reader threads were 11% in `trackNoSpill`.

**Fix.** Keep host store handles in a `ConcurrentHashMap`-backed set with an `AtomicLong` total. When the store has a limit, reserve space with a CAS. Sort a snapshot by task priority only when spilling. `removeFromHostStore` reads a volatile field instead of taking the `SpillFramework` lock.

**User-facing changes.** None.

**Testing.**
- `com.nvidia.spark.rapids.spill` package: 8 suites, 217 tests passed on the development branch.
- Re-run on this branch (cherry-picked onto `main`), Spark 3.5.3 build, all passed: spill package (8 suites) 217 (the 7 opt-in `LargeHostMemorySuite` tests were skipped). Integration tests have not been run.

### Performance

Measured on one host (352 CPUs, 2x RTX PRO 6000) with the stress suite: SSB SF3000 queries with 12000 (q04) and 20000 (q06) shuffle partitions, multithreaded shuffle, 8 executors x 16 cores. The measured jars also contained the other changes of this series (see each table), one run per configuration unless noted. Result fingerprints were identical in every run.

| q06 (20000 partitions), 4 executors per GPU | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| stage 40 | 457 s | 374 s |
| query | 1419 s | 1292 s |
| threads waiting on the host store monitor | 9.8 per dump | 0 |

q04: no measurable difference (mean of two runs, 634 vs 644 s).

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code. A human must review the complete diff and this description before merge.
