author: bdcbqa314159
body:
On the phone a project's photographs are the same size now.

| | landscape | upright |
|---|---|---|
| 390px, before | 390x520 | **390x260** — one twice the other |
| 390px, now | 389x260 | **196x260** — one horizon |
| 1400px | 999x667 | 501x667 |

**Why it only ever showed on the phone.** A wide slide is short, so its
HEIGHT binds every photograph and they come out alike by themselves —
which is why the desktop already looked uniform. A phone's slide is
tall and narrow, so the WIDTH binds instead and an upright photograph
comes out twice the height of a landscape one. Same rule, different
shape of screen, and on one of them it reads as an accident.

So the height is chosen rather than fallen into: **the tallest they can
all be while the widest of them still fits**. Nothing is cropped.

**What it costs, plainly.** An upright photograph on a phone is 196x260
where it was 390x520. That is the price of "the same size" without
cropping — the only way to have them identical AND large is
`object-fit: cover`, which cuts the sides off every landscape. Still
one line if you want to see it.

**And a conflict the check found in my own change.** Forcing a common
height stretched the photograph that runs out of pixels first: the
stand-ins are 667px tall and the desktop slide is 801, so three of four
were drawn larger than they are. The horizon is capped by the shortest
photograph's own pixels now — `999x667` rather than `1200x801`. It
rarely binds: a photograph of 2000px on the long edge is taller than
any slide, which is what `content-check.py` asks for at the gate.

`src/horizon.ts` is the arithmetic and `tools/horizon-check.mjs` holds
it at **13 points** — a phone, a desktop, all-upright and all-landscape
sets, a panorama that brings everyone down to where it fits, the pixel
ceiling binding and not binding, and nothing measured yet. Two
mutations caught: the horizon not applied (`261,519px tall — different
sizes in the same carousel`) and the ceiling removed (`drawn larger
than the pixels it has`).

Measured from the markup, not the pixels: every photograph carries its
`width` and `height`, so the shapes are known before anything loads and
the horizon does not move under the reader when a file arrives. It is
measured again on resize, because a phone turned on its side is a
different slide.

author: siy
body:
## What

`ops/bb/install-bb-temper-local.sh <new-file> <dest> <expected-md5>` replaces a local tool file, here the Mac's `~/temper-wt/bb-temper`, **by rename**. It copies `<new-file>` to a temp file in `<dest>`'s own directory, so the move is a `rename(2)` on one filesystem. It then chmods the temp file 0755, checks its md5 and runs `mv -f` over `<dest>`. The old file is kept as `<dest>.bak-<its md5>`; bb-drift skips `<known>.bak*`.

- **Refusals:** a source that isn't at `<expected-md5>` is refused with exit 9 and `<dest>` untouched; a bad usage exits 2. If `<dest>` is already at that md5, the script prints `unchanged`: no rename, no .bak.
- **Why (CTO 2026-11-21):** bash reads a running script incrementally. Writing onto the live path (`cp`, `>`) changes the bytes under every bb-temper invocation in flight, so a lane mid-run executes a splice of two versions. A rename leaves running processes on the old inode.
- **Its caller** is the owner's `install-bb-70.sh` Mac step. That script replaces the #42-era `~/temper-wt/bb-temper` (5188a359) with main's version, and checks afterwards that the .bak exists.

## Rows (BbLocalInstallIT)

- `aReaderOpenedBeforeTheInstall_keepsReadingTheOldFile_theDestIsANewInode`:
  - A channel opened on `<dest>` BEFORE the install still reads exactly the old bytes after it.
  - `<dest>` is a new inode with mode rwxr-xr-x, and it holds the new bytes.
  - `.bak-<old md5>` holds the old bytes.
  - No temp file is left behind.
- `aSourceNotAtTheExpectedMd5_isRefused_andTheDestIsUntouched`: rc 9, and `<dest>`'s content and inode are unchanged; no .bak.
- `aDestAlreadyAtTheExpectedMd5_isUnchanged_noBakNoRename`.

## Evidence

- Bb*IT at 27104d33d: rc 0, 572 testcases, 0 failures, 1 skipped (BbTestGuardIT's non-UTF-8 name row; bigboy's ZFS refuses the name) (1795259533445594614-1149075).
- Probe, branch 04e1236a0: `mv -f "$tmp" "$dest"` replaced by `cp "$tmp" "$dest"`, ticket 1795261256103380539-3396009: rc 1, exactly 1 of 3 red, `aReaderOpenedBeforeTheInstall_keepsReadingTheOldFile_theDestIsANewInode` (the reader opened before the install read the NEW bytes).
- Smoke-run on macOS (bash 3.2, BSD mktemp/md5), plain shell: the inode changed, .bak was kept, a second run printed `unchanged`, and a wrong md5 was refused with rc 9.

author: klubrake
body:
## Description

Closes #5829

**The problem.** Some Terminal switches end in Error because the Session's command picks its own conversation with the agent's session flag (`--resume <id>`, for example) while AoE also holds one. In that case the row's `last_error` gives the remedy. That message exists only in memory, so reconciling from disk, or restarting the daemon, drops it. The next poll then finds no pane and shows "tmux session is gone. The agent process may have exited or been killed." That message is wrong, and it doesn't say how to fix the Session.

**What changes**
- When the poller explains an Error for a pane that is gone, ended, or behind an unreachable tmux server, it first checks whether every Terminal launch of this row would be refused: the command carries the agent's session flag and AoE's conversation resumes.
  - **If so,** the message says what happened to the pane and then gives both remedies. For example: "The tmux session is gone. Terminal view can't start this Session again: ...".
  - **Otherwise** the message is unchanged.
- The check reads only fields that are saved to disk, so nothing new is stored and no migration is needed. It stops matching on its own once either remedy is applied: the flag is removed from the command or arguments, or `aoe session set-session-id <id> ""` clears AoE's id.
- A gone pane is still recognised with the remedy appended. `aoe session wait` (`is_terminated`) and the structured-view switch (`clear_stale_tmux_error`) now share one predicate, `reports_tmux_session_gone`, instead of comparing against `TMUX_SESSION_GONE_ERROR` exactly. So once the tmux server exits, the Session still reads as terminated.
- A hookless pane that ended, and so reaches Error through detection, gets the remedy too, after what ended it: the adapter's diagnostic when there is one, otherwise "The terminal ended." An error the agent shows while it is still running keeps its diagnostic alone.
- The 409 for the switch and the poller now take the remedy text from one function, `Instance::command_selector_remedy`. The switch's refusal predicate reuses `Instance::command_selector_refuses_launch`.

The change is limited to the poller's error text. Launches, the 409 and the switch outcome behave as before. `docs/structured-view.md` already documents both remedies and stays accurate.

- [ ] New Feature
- [x] Bug Fix
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Infrastructure / CI

- [x] Documentation was updated where necessary

**TUI / CLI (e2e test)**
- [ ] N/A: this PR doesn't change TUI rendering, a CLI subcommand, or session lifecycle
- [ ] Added or updated an e2e test under `tests/e2e/`
- [x] Skipped a test, because: only the poller's error message changes. The tests below drive the real poller with tmux's session cache forced into each state, which an e2e test couldn't reach deterministically: an ended pane, a gone session, an unreachable server.

**Rust tests**
- `an_ended_pane_whose_restart_is_refused_names_the_remedy` (session): one table over the poller.
  - **The conflicting row:** with its tmux session gone, the server unreachable, or its pane dead, it latches Error with the matching message plus the remedy.
  - **The flag removed, or AoE's id cleared:** the row gets the plain tmux message.
  - **A live pane:** explains nothing.
  - **A later poll with the tmux server unreachable:** keeps the explanation, `is_terminated` stays true, and the structured-view switch clears it.
  - **A hookless pane that ended,** a real tmux pane painting an idle Claude frame: the conflicting row gets the remedy, and the row with the flag removed doesn't.
- `an_owed_switch_the_command_selector_refuses_ends_and_a_restart_launches` (acp) is extended.
  - **Reconciled from disk:** after the owed switch ends in Error, the row's first poll ends its `last_error` with the remedy. This replaces the old assert that the remedy was gone.
  - **Daemon restart:** a row loaded from disk shows Error with no message, and its first poll gives the remedy back.
  - **After either remedy and a restart:** the row no longer matches the check.

Revert proofs, each failing its named check:
- the poller change reverted: both tests get only the plain tmux message;
- the exact gone-pane match restored: `is_terminated` turns false;
- the hookless remedy removed: the conflicting row gets only the pane summary.

When a Terminal session cannot restart, the error text now gives the fix. This applies when the pane is gone, ended, or behind an unreachable tmux server. It also requires that the launch command has a session selector while AoE holds a conversation ID. The message names both remedies: remove the selector, or run `aoe session set-session-id <id> ""`. The message is rebuilt from saved session fields, so it returns after reconciliation or a daemon restart. No new data is stored. Launch, 409, and switch behavior do not change.

Benefit: users can find the recovery steps without the original response.

Limit: the change covers error text only. It does not change handoff cleanup, so the handoff-cleanup part of the linked issue is not addressed.

Technical details: `view.rs` now uses `Instance::command_selector_remedy`. `session_id.rs` adds `command_selector_refuses_launch` and `command_selector_remedy`. `status_update.rs` builds the ending explanation and adds the remedy for gone, unreachable, and dead panes. `status.rs` adds `reports_tmux_session_gone` and `TMUX_SESSION_GONE_LEAD`. `cli/session.rs` uses the new helper in `is_terminated`. `mod.rs` files add re-exports. The PR reports passing tests. I did not re-run them.

author: alecthomson
body:
flint pinned `RACS-tools<4.5` because bringing Stokes cubes to a common resolution before RM-synthesis failed with "Target beam … cannot be reached" (https://github.com/AlecThomson/fitscube/issues/72). Both causes are now fixed upstream:

- **fitscube 2.12.1** (https://github.com/AlecThomson/fitscube/pull/76) writes the beam of each extracted plane as the beam table holds it. Before, a float32 conversion rounded it up by about 1e-8″.
- **RACS-tools 4.6.0** (https://github.com/AlecThomson/RACS-tools/pull/94) accepts float32 round-off when it checks that a target beam contains an input beam.

## Changes
- `RACS-tools>=4.4.0,<4.5` → `RACS-tools>=4.6.0`.
- `fitscube[pgzip]>=2.11` → `fitscube[pgzip]>=2.12.1`.
- `uv.lock` updated for both, and nothing else changed.

RACS-tools 4.6.0 needs Python ≥ 3.11, which flint already requires.

## Testing
`uv sync --frozen --all-extras`, then `tests/test_convol.py`, `tests/test_cube.py`, `tests/test_rmsynth.py`, `tests/test_total_resolution.py` and `tests/test_prefect_rmsynth_flow.py`:

| RACS-tools | fitscube | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4.5.0 | 2.12.1 | 143 passed, 1 failed: `test_resolve_common_resolution_cubes_convolves` ("cannot be reached") |
| 4.6.0 | 2.12.1 | 144 passed |

So the fitscube fix alone is not enough. The RACS-tools floor of 4.6.0 is what makes this test pass.

author: cosmicspork
body:
## Why

Agents reach hora through its MCP tools, and the page and CLI reach it through the HTTP API. Both were mostly built from the operation registry in `src/ops.rs`, but two routes were hand-written handlers with no operation behind them, so agents could not do what they do:

- `GET /api/state`: today's local date and UTC offset, projects, the running timer, and the draft and pending-proposal counts. Agents need the local date and offset to log naive times correctly, and had no way to read them.
- `GET /api/export`: CSV or JSONL export.

Nothing stopped the next hand-written route from drifting the same way.

## What changes

- Two new read operations, which are tools too: `time_overview` (what `/api/state` returns) and `time_export` (`{format, filename, content_type, entries, content}`). `/api/state` and `/api/export` now just run them. A GET route runs its operation with the query string as arguments, and `/api/export` serves the result as a download, with the same headers and filename as before.
- The routers come from one table, `http::ROUTES`. Each route serves either any operation by name (`/api/ops/{name}`, `/api/agent/ops/{name}`), the registry listing, or one named read operation. A GET route refuses an operation that writes, since GET skips the Origin check that mutations get.
- `hora overview` and `hora export` CLI commands. `export` prints the file's text, so `hora export ... > november.csv` works.
- `tracon-plugin.toml` declares both new tools as `read`.
- New `tests/parity.rs`:
  - every operation is a tool, unless it is in `NOT_TOOLS` with a written reason. That list must name exactly the operator-only operations, so flipping `operator_only` either way fails the test until the reason is added or removed;
  - every route in `ROUTES` serves operations that exist, a GET alias serves only a read operation that is a tool, and a route with no operation (the two registry listings) has a reason in `ROUTES_WITHOUT_TOOL`;
  - `src/` contains no `.route("...")` call except the non-API page and MCP routes listed in `NOT_API`, so a route can't be added outside the table;
  - every operation name and `api/...` path the page (`spa/src`) and the CLI (`src/main.rs`, `src/client.rs`) use exists.
  The existing manifest test in `tests/package.rs` still holds `[[tool]]` to `tools/list`.

## Operator-only operations stay out of the tools

`time_confirm`, `proposal_accept`, `proposal_reject`, `project_create` and `project_update` are excluded from the tools, each with its reason in `NOT_TOOLS`, rather than offered as `consequential` tools run from an approval card. Reasons:

- These are the operator's decisions about agents' work, and hora's page is already where they are made: the drafts queue and proposal cards show authors, refs and history. An approval card would give the same decision a second place to happen.
- As tools they would have to treat an approved agent call as the operator's act. That would add a third kind of actor to the store's rules, implement `tracon/preview` for them (allow requires a shown preview), and check `approval_id` on every call. It's possible, but it's a change to the authority model, not a gap in parity.
- It matches what is already there: the manifest comment, the README, and the store refusing these to agents.

The plan already lists a timesheet approval card for drafts as later work. If that lands, it can start from this list: `time_confirm` moves out of `NOT_TOOLS` and becomes a consequential tool.

## Behaviour changes to note

- `GET /api/state` and `GET /api/export` now refuse unknown query parameters (400 `invalid_request`), because the operations' inputs use `deny_unknown_fields`. The page sends only known ones.
- An invalid export `format` still answers 400 `invalid_request`, with serde's "unknown variant" message instead of "format is csv or jsonl".
- `http::to_csv` moved to `ops::to_csv`.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked` (55 tests) all pass. In `spa/`, `bun run check`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass. The SPA itself is unchanged.
- New tests: `tests/plugin.rs` calls `time_overview` and `time_export` as MCP tools on the built binary in plugin mode with signed contexts, and checks the overview equals the signed operator's `GET /api/state`. `tests/http.rs` checks `/api/state` and `/api/export` match their operations, including the download headers and CSV quoting.
- Mutation-checked the parity test by temporarily adding a hand-written `.route`, marking `time_export` operator-only, calling an unknown op and an unknown path from `api.ts`, and pointing `/api/state` at `time_log`. Each one failed the intended test. Adding an op without a manifest entry failed `tests/package.rs`.
- Ran `hora serve` on a scratch data directory and port and used the CLI as an agent: `log` (draft by `agent:parity-check`), `overview`, `call time_overview` (identical to `GET /api/state`), `export` (CSV with quoting), `GET /api/export?format=jsonl` (headers and filename), the agent ops listing, and `call time_confirm` (refused, 403).

## Limits

- Not exercised on a live Tracon node. The plugin path was covered only by the test harness's stand-in node.
- hora has no standalone `mcp` stdio mode, so there was nothing to bring into line there. If one is added, it should serve `plugin::tools()` so the parity test covers it.
- Tool schemas don't yet mark free-text fields with `x-tracon-format`, and hora answers no `tracon/preview`. Neither matters while the tools are allowed by name, as the README suggests. Both would matter for asked calls.

author: lukeevanstech
body:
## Summary

The library-cleanup judges (`curatorjudge`, `curatortvjudge`) delete on the model's verdict, so a verdict from a fallback model is not acceptable. `claude` falls back to the local model when the provider budget is spent or the provider key expires, and a key's `models` list does not stop a router fallback. This adds the gateway side only: a group that is in no fallback chain, and a key scoped to it.

```diff
 routerSettings.fallbacks / context_window_fallbacks      (unchanged)
   self-hosted -> claude -> openrouter/auto
   claude      -> self-hosted -> openrouter/auto
+  claude-opus -> none: the error reaches the caller

 litellm/app/
 ├── models/
+│   └── claude-opus.yaml   # anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, same key and provider budget as claude
 └── virtualkeys/
+    └── curator.yaml       # scope: claude-opus only; PushSecret -> litellm item, LITELLM_CURATOR_API_KEY
```

The four `LiteLLMClaude*` alerts selected on the Sonnet model name, so a second Anthropic group escaped three of them:

```diff
 LiteLLMClaudeBudgetMetricAbsent
-  success_responses{litellm_model_name="claude-sonnet-5-5"} with no budget gauge
+  success_responses{api_provider="anthropic"} with no budget gauge
 LiteLLMClaudeSpendFast
-  24h spend{model="claude-sonnet-5-5"} > 20
+  24h spend{api_provider="anthropic"} > 20
 LiteLLMClaudeRequestRejected
   successful_fallbacks{400, Anthropic.*}
+  or failure_responses{400, api_provider="anthropic"}
 LiteLLMClaudeBudgetLow
-  "claude traffic moves to self-hosted when it runs out"
+  "when it runs out claude traffic moves to self-hosted and claude-opus calls fail"
```

`RequestRejected` read only the fallback counter, which a group with no fallback never touches: its 400 reaches the caller and shows only as a failed response. The budget is per provider, so the budget and spend alerts now select on the provider as well.

Docs: the group in the AI / LLM stack page's group list, the two judges in the consumers table, and the alerting notes on the LiteLLM page. The judges' own switch to this key is a separate change, so nothing calls the group until that merges. The consumers table says so in a note under the judge rows, which that change should delete.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the extended alert unit tests run against the rule on `main`. The new group is invisible to three alerts:

  ```text
  LiteLLMClaudeRequestRejected     35m  exp 1 alert, got []   # Anthropic 400 on a group with no fallback
  LiteLLMClaudeBudgetMetricAbsent  50m  exp 1 alert, got []   # claude-opus calls only, no budget gauge
  LiteLLMClaudeSpendFast           26h  exp 1 alert, got []   # 0.5 USD/h on each group, 24 USD/day together
  ```

  **After:** `67 PrometheusRule manifests checked, 11 test files run`, exit 0. The new tests include shapes that must stay quiet: a 400 from the local model, an Anthropic 500, a key refused for a model outside its scope, and local-model calls with no gauge.

- The old and new expressions evaluated against live Prometheus agree today: no alert either way, and the 24h Anthropic spend reads the same by provider as by model name.
- A server-side dry run accepts the new `LiteLLMModel`, `LiteLLMVirtualKey` and `PushSecret`. The Flux Kustomization renders with both fallback lists unchanged.
- The virtual-key docs check fails without the consumers row (`key curator has no row`) and passes with it.

Not exercised: a real Anthropic 400 on the new group. The failure counter's label shape is read from live series of the same metric for another provider.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting removes the group and the key. The mirrored `LITELLM_CURATOR_API_KEY` field would stay on the 1Password item until deleted by hand.

**Blast Radius:** gateway

A new model changes the rendered config, so the operator rolls the single LiteLLM pod once: requests in flight are dropped and its counters restart. Existing groups, keys and fallback chains are unchanged. Opus 5.5 spend counts against the same monthly provider budget as `claude`, at twice the per-token price.

근본 원인: CPU 배율 보정이 한도를 넘은 순간의 느림을 못 잡거나(값 1.00) 시험이 한도 근처로 무겁다(미확인) → **확인: 측정 쪽이다.** 배율 측정을 고친다. 한도(1.5초)는 그대로다.

## 근거 — 측정이 느린 실행기를 못 잡았다

「새 배율(흉내)」은 이 PR 의 방식을 junit 으로 흉내 낸 값이다 — 평가하는 실행은 기준에서 빼고, junit 에서 그 시험보다 앞에 나온 시험들만 썼다(비교 80~175개). 전체 262조각에서 조각 끝 배율은 10분위 0.65 … 1.37 로, 원래 #1163 이 본 세 무리가 그대로 나온다.

author: destroyerban
body:
# RF-103 — El widget «Valor del inventario» le muestra al Productor el valor de su finca

Closes #1196

## Qué cambia

Incidencia «INC-M08-380-G002 · RF-103: el widget «Valor del inventario» del Productor sale en $0 aunque la finca está valorada» (TC-M08-G002, subcaso TC-M08-003). El diagnóstico del ticket es correcto y se confirmó en PostgreSQL con RLS.

El permiso `indicadores_valor_inventario` le abre el widget al Productor, pero los datos se leían con su sesión. `SqlAlchemyValoracionRepository.activos_valorados()` parte de `modulo6.reconocimientos_iniciales`, cuya política SELECT (`4fa0e24ea021_rls_modulo_06`) es `fn_tiene_permiso('reconocimiento_inicial', 'R')`. Lo mismo pasa con `calculos_valor_razonable` y `valoraciones_por_costos`. El Productor no tiene esos permisos y recibía cero filas.

| Regla del RF | RF exige | Estaba | Ahora (confirmado) |
|---|---|---|---|
| RF-103, contenido del Productor | Valor total del inventario biológico en COP, desde M06 | `SIN_DATOS`, `valor_total 0`, `activos 0` | `OK` con el valor de su finca (en la prueba: `1365472.3`, 1 activo) |
| `indicadores_valor_inventario` (#1173) | El Productor ve el valor sin abrirle la valoración de Finanzas | Con permiso del widget pero sin datos | Solo totales; sin permisos nuevos de Finanzas |
| Alcance por finca (RF-25) | Solo las fincas del usuario | Lo acotaba la RLS | Lo acota el filtro por fincas permitidas; una finca ajena responde `403 FINCA_NO_AUTORIZADA` |

**Algo a tener en cuenta:** esa RLS de M06 filtra **por permiso, no por finca**. Al Contador lo acotaban a sus fincas los joins con `modulo2.activos_biologicos` y `modulo9.infraestructuras`/`fincas`. Leer como sistema sin más le abriría todas las fincas a cualquiera, así que el filtro de fincas se aplica de forma explícita.

## Sin autorización de DBA

No hay migración ni cambios de permisos. La lectura como sistema usa `como_sistema` (`src/shared/database.py`), el mismo patrón de #1154.

## Cambios

**Base de datos:** ninguno.

**Código:**
- `src/reporting/domain/repositories/datos_widget_repository.py`: `activos_valorados(id_finca, fincas_permitidas)`, donde `None` es alcance global.
- `src/reporting/infrastructure/repositories/datos_widget_repository.py`:
  - Lee los activos valorados dentro de `como_sistema(self.db)`.
  - Filtra por la finca pedida y por `fincas_permitidas`.
  - Al salir se restaura la identidad del usuario.
- `src/reporting/application/use_cases/dashboard/obtener_datos_widget_use_case.py`:
  - `_valor_inventario` pasa `permitidas`, que sale de `AlcanceFincaAdapter.listar_ids_fincas_permitidas`: `None` solo para el rol protegido y, para el resto, `modulo9.usuarios_fincas` activas, la misma regla de `fn_fincas_del_usuario`.
  - La validación de la finca (`403`) no cambia.

**Documentación:** `anotaciones/modulo_8/inc_m08_380_g002_valor_inventario_productor.md`.

**Tabla de seguimiento**

| Archivo | Fila agregada |
|---|---|
| `src/reporting/domain/repositories/datos_widget_repository.py` | `2026-11-21 \| destroyerban \| INC-M08-380-G002 RF-103: activos valorados acotados a las fincas del usuario` |
| `src/reporting/infrastructure/repositories/datos_widget_repository.py` | `2026-11-21 \| destroyerban \| INC-M08-380-G002 RF-103: valor del inventario leído como sistema y acotado a las fincas del usuario` |
| `src/reporting/application/use_cases/dashboard/obtener_datos_widget_use_case.py` | `2026-11-21 \| destroyerban \| INC-M08-380-G002 RF-103: el valor del inventario se acota a las fincas permitidas` |
| `tests/reporting/test_m08_rf103_dashboard_widgets.py` | `2026-11-21 \| destroyerban \| INC-M08-380-G002 RF-103: el valor del inventario recibe las fincas permitidas` |
| `tests/integration/test_inc_m08_380_g002_valor_inventario_productor.py` | `2026-11-21 \| destroyerban \| INC-M08-380-G002 RF-103: el Productor ve el valor del inventario de su finca` |

## Documentación por prueba

**Unitarias** (`tests/reporting/test_m08_rf103_dashboard_widgets.py`, repositorios falsos):

| # | Prueba | Evalúa | Esperado |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `test_valor_del_inventario_se_consulta_con_las_fincas_del_usuario` | Productor con finca activa 3 y fincas `[3, 4]` | El repositorio recibe `(3, [3, 4])` |
| 2 | `test_valor_del_inventario_sin_finca_activa_usa_todas_las_fincas_permitidas` | Contador sin finca activa | Recibe `(None, [3, 4])` |
| 3 | `test_valor_del_inventario_con_alcance_global_no_acota` | Rol con alcance global | Recibe `(None, None)` |

**Integración** (`tests/integration/test_inc_m08_380_g002_valor_inventario_productor.py`, como `sgpmp_app` con la identidad de un Productor asignado a una finca; hay un segundo animal valorado en otra finca del mismo titular):

| # | Prueba | Evalúa | Esperado |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | `test_productor_ve_el_valor_de_su_finca_aunque_no_lea_la_valoracion` | Premisa, arreglo, alcance e identidad | Con su sesión, M06 devuelve `[]`. El widget da `OK`, `valor_total 1365472.3`, `activos 1`. Sin finca activa también suma solo su finca. Después de leer como sistema, M06 vuelve a devolver `[]` |
| 5 | `test_finca_ajena_responde_403` | Finca del mismo titular no asignada | `AuthorizationError` (403) |

```
con el arreglo:   93 passed   (integración nueva + tests/reporting)
sin el arreglo:   1 failed, 1 passed
                  AssertionError: assert 'SIN_DATOS' == 'OK'   ← lo mismo que TC-M08-003 en TEST
```

## Suite completa

Se corrió en la imagen del backend (Linux), contra una BD efímera con `alembic upgrade head`, porque `tests/conftest.py` importa `fcntl` y no arranca en Windows. Las migraciones no crean los GRANT de `sgpmp_app`, así que se le dieron los mismos que tiene en DEV: USAGE y SELECT en todos los esquemas.

```
python -m pytest tests/reporting tests/configuration tests/financial_valuation tests/integration/test_inc_m08_380_g002_valor_inventario_productor.py tests/integration/test_m08_rf104_rf107_integration.py tests/integration/test_m06_flujo_nic41_integration.py -q
1 failed, 1073 passed
```

El fallo es `test_m08_rf104_rf107_integration.py::test_escalamiento_auditoria_y_preferencias` (RF-105, `assert 1 == 4`). Ya fallaba antes de este cambio; está anotado en el PR de #1195.

## Fuera de alcance

- Los demás widgets financieros (`periodos_abiertos`, `reconocimientos_pendientes`, `precios_por_vencer`, `integraciones_fallidas`) son del Contador, que sí lee Finanzas; siguen con la sesión del usuario.
- `activos_valorados()` de M06 trae todos los activos valorados y el filtro de fincas se aplica en Python, igual que antes con el filtro de `id_finca`. Si el volumen crece, conviene llevar el filtro a SQL en M06.
- `test_escalamiento_auditoria_y_preferencias` (RF-105) y `fcntl` en `tests/conftest.py`, ya reportados en #1195.

## Re-prueba (TC-M08-003 en TEST)

- El Productor (176) y el Contador (178) piden `GET /dashboard/widgets/valor_inventario?id_finca=494` y ambos reciben `valor_total 1365472.3` y `activos 3`.
- El Productor con una finca que no tiene asignada recibe `403`.

## PR relacionado

Ninguno.

Ref: anotaciones/modulo_8/inc_m08_380_g002_valor_inventario_productor.md (RF-103)

## Üyelik sürtünmesini azaltma ve forum güvenlik düzeltmesi
- 12 yerine **minimum 8 karakter** (HTML + istemci + parola kurtarma), güçlü benzersiz şifre teşviki. Supabase Auth backend farklı bir minimum zorunlu tutuyorsa `/auth/v1/signup` 400 zayıf parola hatası artık anlaşılır gösterilir; backend minimumunu panelden doğrulama gerektirir.
- Site genelinde **üst navigasyonda görünür Üye ol** bağlantısı; 10 yerel dil rotasından ilgili forum kayıt alanına gider. Küçük ekran ve klavye erişimi için dokunma alanı ve mobil menü bağlantısı var.
- Forumun **ilk açılışı tartışmalar ve rehberler**: büyük kayıt ekranı otomatik açılmaz. Forumdaki katılım bölümünde misafirlere açık bir 'giriş yap veya üye ol' açılır alan vardır. `#forum-register-heading` ile bilinçli seçimde açılır.
- Misafirler yayımlanmış konuları okuyabilir; yeni konu/yanıt formu yalnız doğrulanmış Supabase oturumunda görünür. Sahte sessionStorage tokenı için `/auth/v1/user` doğrulaması korunur.
- OAuth, e-posta OTP/kod, şifreli giriş, kullanıcı profili, kayıt sonrası nötr avatar, moderasyon ve mevcut SEO/indexleme korunur. Parola kurtarma ve eski OTP error fallback'i gizli panel yüzünden kaybolmaz; geçerli Google oturumu sonrası kullanıcı forum içeriğine döner.

## Tespit edilen gerçek veritabanı erişim hatası
- `tc_forum_topics` ve `tc_forum_replies` RLS etkin, `anon` INSERT izni yok **(doğru)**. Ancak `authenticated` INSERT izni de eksik; gerçek üyeler bu nedenle gönderi yapamayabilir.
- Tek SQL migration: mevcut pending+author_id=auth.uid() RLS kontrollerini önceden doğrula; **yalnız authenticated INSERT** yetkisi ver, anon INSERT açık kalmaz. Onay/moderasyon/anti-spam tetikleyicileri yerinde kalır; forum verisi değiştirilmez.
- SQL geri alma: `REVOKE INSERT FROM authenticated` (kayıt silmez). Canlıda önce transaction ROLLBACK prova, CI sonrası migration, salt-okunur ACL doğrulama.

## Kalite kapıları
- Site build, Altın Entegrasyon Kuralı, üretim paketi güvenlik kontrolü, Playwright Chromium/Firefox/WebKit/mobil + axe taraması. Fail olursa merge yok.
- Testler: 7 karakterin reddi / 8 karakterin kabulü; misafir ilk açılışta post formunu göremez; üst menü mobil kayıt linki; yalnız talep edilirse kayıt açılır; login/logout, eski OTP, OAuth, forum puanları regresyonu.
- Kalan harici kontrol: Supabase > Authentication > Email provider'ın gerçek **Minimum password length** değeri 8 olmalı; bu araçla Auth dashboard ayarı güncellenemez ve yapılmış gibi gösterilmeyecek. Gerçek e-posta teslimi ayrıca kabul gerektirir.

author: tilladam
body:
Editing a property in the live preview's property panel reloads the preview, and the reload scrolled the panel back to the top.
Editing `x` and then `y` of an element meant scrolling back after each change.

- Keep the property rows out of the `element-loaded` condition, so that a reload doesn't rebuild the panel
- Show the "Select an Element" hint only when no element is loaded and there are no rows
- Clear the rows when a selection resolves to no element while none is loaded

This continues #13115 by dumestre.
The first commit is the one from that PR, unchanged.
The second one is the fix ogoffart asked for there: without it, the hint showed up together with property rows.

== Implementation Notes ==

A reload clears `Api.current-element` and keeps the properties model until it restores the selection.
Gating the rows on the element would bring the scroll reset back, so the hint depends on the model instead.
`set_selected_element` runs at the end of every load, and clears the model when it finds nothing to show.

The rows next to the hint were the sample model of `api.slint`.
They show up when the first load fails, for example when the file doesn't compile.

Tested by driving `slint-lsp` and its preview through the MCP server, with the headless backend on macOS.
The values are read from the element tree.

| | master | #13115 alone | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scroll offset after editing `x` at 1020px | 0px | 1020px | 1020px |
| Preview of a file that doesn't compile | hint | hint and sample rows | hint |

The new unit test fails without the change in `set_selected_element`.
The hint sits 4px higher than on master, because the empty rows layout keeps its top padding.

ChangeLog: live-preview: Fixed the property panel scrolling back to the top when a property is edited

## What changes

- **Haptics while warm** (`Recorder.swift`): call `setAllowHapticsAndSystemSoundsDuringRecording(true)` before activating `.playAndRecord`.
- **Opt-in "Stop after each recording"** (`Settings.swift`, `V2TApp.swift`, `DictationService.swift`): keep the 15-min default; when set to `-1`, cool down the mic on `stop()` (guarded by `beginBackgroundTask` so `finish()` isn't suspended) and stop the heartbeat once done/cancelled.
- **Mic & timer lifecycle** (`Recorder.swift`, `DictationService.swift`, `RecordingPanel.swift`, `KeyboardViewController.swift`): cool down on `AVAudioSession` interruptions and `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange`; reset `AVAudioEngine`/`AVAudioConverter` cleanly; stop `RecordingPanel`'s 30 Hz timer in `viewDidDisappear` / `willMove(toWindow: nil)`.
- **Tests** (`DictationEndTests.swift`): added tests for stop-after-recording and cancel-after-done.

Relates to #112.

## Why

Typing on the TestFlight build felt glitchy while the warm mic session stayed active (likely muted haptics/clicks during `.playAndRecord`), and there was no opt-in way to release the mic right after each dictation.

## Status / Not verified yet

- Swift 6 typechecked against iOS 26.4 Simulator SDK; **not yet run on a Simulator or physical iPhone**.

author: scuttletoby
body:
Follow-ups from the round-5 lenses on #237 (desk seed fetch): security lens237sr5 and correctness lens237cr5. All four items in #258 are fixed in code, docs, or both.

## What and why

1. **Doc line: a fix can wait for the step (item 1, cr5 nit 1 / sr5 nit 1).** The script header, the `TornLog` docstring, `fork-fleet.md` and the desk README now say that a fix made right after another new copy waits for the end of the step, up to 24 h. This trade-off is intended.
2. **An early try no longer restarts the wait (item 2, cr5 nit 2).** Root fix, not just a doc line. An early try (a new copy on the host during a back-off wait) still counts, so the next wait still doubles. It now keeps `last`, so the wait runs from the last try that waited, not from the early try. So an early try moves the next normal try at most one step later (h 5, not h 3, after an early try at h 1.5), and not at all at the 24 h cap. Before, each early try also restarted the wait from itself. The log line after a torn fetch gives the real time left (`TornLog.due`), not `2^(tries-1)` from now. An hourly broken remake now gets tries at h 0, 1, 2, 5, 6 (before: 0, 1, 2, 6, 7). The test that pins this schedule is updated.
3. **Sparse handlers (item 3, sr5 nit 2).**
   - `Info` now refuses every `_proc_gnusparse_*` that this Python's `tarfile.TarInfo` has, found by name at import. Before, only 00, 01 and 10 were listed by hand, so a later tarfile's new handler would not be overridden.
   - This goes past the lens suggestion: each run reads small probe tars with `Tar`/`Info` (`sparse_read`): one pax sparse tar of each form (0.0, 0.1, 1.0), an old-GNU sparse member, and a header over `HEADER_MOST`. The last two prove tarfile still calls `Info._proc_member`. Each probe must be torn by its own refusal. Anything else (read as a sparse member, read whole, torn by another limit, a tarfile error, or the probe cannot even be made) is named, and the run fetches nothing and exits 2, like a missing `PRIVATE` part (`check` shows it). Seeds past their age are still dropped.
4. **Quiet end of unpack (item 4, sr5 nit 3).**
   - `Info.fromtarfile` lets only `EOFHeaderError` (a block of zeros) end the tar. Any other header error now tears the seed: a bad checksum, a pax `size<0`, a stream that ends with no end blocks, or a bad header as the last block. Before, `TarFile.next()` ended the tar quietly at any of these after the first header, and a short seed was swapped in.
   - After the end, the rest of the stream is read through tarfile's own buffer (`t.fileobj`), and only zero bytes are accepted. These bytes still count toward the trailer's size and SHA-256. Normal end blocks and record padding pass.

Not changed: the host-down-for-good row (cr4 2, documented in #237) is not part of #258.

## State question

- **Runs again:** an early try keeps `last` and sets `early`, so a second new copy in the same step waits until the step ends. Tested: `test_an_early_try_keeps_the_wait_running_from_the_last_try_that_waited` (also: at the 24 h cap an early try moves nothing).
- **Stopped half-way:** `.torn.json` is saved before the fetch. The test reads it inside the fetch, which is what a run killed there leaves: `last` unchanged, tries + 1, `early` true. The next run waits for the step that was already running.
- **Old state:** a record #237 wrote, where an early try moved `last`, is read as it is. It waits from that `last` and is tried once the step ends (`test_an_old_record_whose_early_try_moved_last_still_waits`). A record without `early`, or without `copy`, behaves as before.
- **Empty or missing:** no record means no wait, as before. An empty stream, or one with no end blocks, is torn; before, it was a `ReadError` or a quiet end. A tar of only end blocks still unpacks as an empty seed.

## Tests

`.github/scripts/fork-fleet-desk-seed.test.py`: 7 new tests, plus the hourly-remake test now expects h 0, 1, 2, 5, 6 and checks the hours in the log line. 77 tests, OK on Linux, Python 3.12 (CI's) and 3.13.5.
- On the old script (origin/main), on Linux Python 3.12, the first 6 new and changed tests give 9 failures and 2 errors (the earlier count, 7 and 2, was from macOS and counted only 5 of the 7 tar-end subtests):
  - the early-try schedule
  - the hourly schedule
  - all 7 subtests of the tar end
  - `sparse_read` missing
  - `_proc_gnusparse_11` not overridden
- `test_an_old_record_whose_early_try_moved_last_still_waits` passes on both. It checks old state, not a change.
- Local runs are macOS, Python 3.14. This file is Linux-only: the same 5 tests fail on origin/main and on this branch (a hard link, a symlink over a folder, path length, RSS), and no other test fails. CI runs it on Linux.
- Also run locally: `fork-gate-trust-docs.test.py` (86 OK) and `fork-owned-reads.test.py` (4 OK). `fork-fleet-desk.test.py` and `fork-kit/desk/tests/install.test.py` are Linux-only; they fail the same way on origin/main on macOS, and CI runs them.
- `node .github/scripts/fork-seam-check.cjs --config-ref origin/main origin/main HEAD`: passes. Only fork files change.

**Spot-checks:** each fix line was removed alone, and its test went red:
- `last` kept on an early try -> `test_an_early_try_never_moves_the_next_try_later`
- the log line's hours from `due` -> `test_a_host_that_remakes_each_hour_never_meets_the_back_off`
- override every `_proc_gnusparse_*` (back to the 3 fixed names) -> `test_a_sparse_form_a_later_tarfile_adds_is_refused_too`
- `sparse_read` in `run` -> `test_a_python_that_reads_a_sparse_member_past_info_fetches_nothing` (all 3 forms)
- only a probe's own refusal counts (`refusal not in str(e)` removed) -> `test_only_its_own_refusal_proves_a_probe`
- `fromtarfile` turning header errors into `Torn` -> `test_only_a_block_of_zeros_ends_the_tar_and_only_zeros_follow`. The bad-header-as-last-block and no-end-blocks cases are caught only by this line; the bad checksum followed by more members is also caught by the zeros check.
- only zeros after the end -> the same test (bytes after the end blocks, bytes after the padding)

## Review round (lens A and B on 96604965, both SAFE)

Fixed in d666cd6bf9:
- Lens B major, lens A minor 4: the five doc lines that said an early try never moves the end of the wait now say what the code does (the wait doubles from the last try that waited, so the next normal try comes at most one step later, not at all at the 24 h cap). The test is renamed to `test_an_early_try_keeps_the_wait_running_from_the_last_try_that_waited`.
- Lens B minor 2, lens A minor 2: the probe tar is made inside the `try`. A tarfile that cannot write it now gives exit 2 and still drops seeds past their age (`test_a_probe_that_cannot_be_made_still_drops_an_old_seed_and_is_exit_2`; on the old script: a raw `ValueError`, exit 1).
- Lens B minor 3, lens A minor 1: only the probe's own refusal counts as refused. Another `Torn`, a tarfile error, or a member read whole is named and fails closed (`test_only_its_own_refusal_proves_a_probe`; fails on the old script).
- Lens A minor 3: two new probes, an old-GNU `S` member and a header over `HEADER_MOST`, prove tarfile still calls `Info._proc_member` (same test, `_proc_member` case).
- Lens B minor 4: the failure count above.

author: e-merging-digital
body:
Refs #1417 · décision propriétaire #7062226004.

### Pourquoi
La langue NL avait reçu une surcouche de routage personnalisée qui bloquait les liens natifs Drupal d'administration. Le propriétaire exige **Drupal natif par défaut**, sans développement ni contrôles non demandés.

### Diff minimal
- `NlVisibilityGuard.php` : les parcours natifs **`/nl/admin`, `/nl/user`, `/nl/canvas` et `/nl/node/add`** sont délégués à **Drupal Core** et à ses permissions existantes. Aucun router custom, aucun nouveau rôle/permission, suppression des regex de routes admin devenues inutiles. Le garde-fou existant reste cantonné aux pages éditoriales publiques NL.
- Retour à la définition de service précédente (aucune injection de router supplémentaire) et tests existants alignés avec la délégation à Drupal.
- La branche NL des textes déjà demandés pour les schémas de `/nl/ai-drupal`, CTA et ALT est conservée ; FR/EN inchangés.
- `AGENTS.md` : **règle durable du propriétaire** : utiliser d'abord les écrans et modules Drupal natifs (Language, Locale, Content Translation, Configuration Translation, menus et alias) ; aucun middleware, nouveau module, workflow ou contrôle additionnel sans demande explicite et besoin prouvé ; simplifier les couches qui gênent Drupal.

### Frontières de sécurité
Le contrôle **public** déjà existant qui évite l'affichage de traductions NL non publiées reste intact, tant qu'un remplacement standard équivalent n'est pas démontré. L'ajout d'une langue et la traduction d'interface sont **des opérations Drupal natives** ; cela ne nécessite aucune route personnalisée. L'action ci-dessus ne donne **aucun** droit administratif supplémentaire.

La PR est source-only. **Aucun déploiement PREPROD/PROD**, aucune mutation de DB et aucune publication de brouillons; CI, revue indépendante et promotion gouvernée distinctes obligatoires. Les liens éditoriaux encore en FR doivent être corrigés via les éditeurs/traductions natifs uniquement lorsqu'une destination NL publiée existe.

### DoD
CI sur HEAD final → revue indépendante → autorisation de fusion → livraison PREPROD native → vérifier `/nl/ai-drupal` et administration depuis la session de l'opérateur, sans contournement du refus d'accès authentifié de l'agent.

author: jaredforreal
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With pipeline parallelism and data parallelism both on, a FlashInfer autotune cache hit on some DP replicas of a stage but not others hangs startup. This change makes the replicas of a stage agree on the cache hit before skipping the tuning runs.

## Claims

- PP > 1 with DP > 1 no longer deadlocks in `flashinfer_autotune` when the replicas' cache files differ (one rank tuned, another did not, a partially written or older cache file).
- No change for PP = 1 or DP = 1. The extra cost is one CPU `all_gather_object` of a bool at startup.

## Validation

- Reproducer: an MoE model served with PP2 x DP4 + expert parallelism over two 4-GPU nodes, with an autotune cache directory primed by an earlier run in which only some ranks wrote their entries. Without the fix the server hangs: py-spy shows the tuning ranks in the DP padding sync (`sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding`) and the cache-hit ranks already further on. With the fix all 8 ranks retune and the server comes up.
- `pytest tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py`: 88 passed. The new `test_pp_stage_cache_hit_is_unanimous_across_dp_replicas` fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Details

- **Root cause**: with PP > 1, `tune_group` is the stage's TP group, so each DP replica decides "cache hit, skip the dummy runs" on its own. The dummy runs sync DP padding across the stage's replicas, so a replica that tunes waits forever for one that skipped.
- **Fix**: all-gather `cache_hit` over the DP group. Tune unless every replica hit. A replica that hit but must tune clears its loaded entries first, so it tunes the same shapes as the others.
- **Not covered by CI**: this needs PP x DP on multiple GPUs plus a stale cache. The unit test drives `flashinfer_autotune` with fake groups.

The bench driver could not start a new game on a Profile without a save: the menu opens with nothing selected, the first arrow key only wakes the keyboard, so the fixed Down, Enter, Enter landed on Continue and its box. On a Tale of Two Wastelands Profile it also pressed Enter on the start choice box ("Start in Capital Wasteland (Recommended)" / "Start in Mojave Wasteland"), which took Capital.

What changed (`scripts/fork/bench`):
- `menu_view.py` (new): reads the two pixel outline the game draws round the selected line off a picture of the nested screen (grim's PPM output, in memory, kept nowhere). The main menu's own boxes are not on `menu.stack`, so the picture is the only source of the selection. The mouse cursor over an outline's edge is handled.
- `drivers.new_game_from_menu`: per round one action by what the picture shows: no outline, Down (wake); above New, Down; below, Up; on New, Enter; the box that Enter opened, Enter (Yes is selected); a box it did not open, Escape; a message box on the stack, Enter. Done on `load.kind: the load is a new game`.
- `drivers.answer_start_choice`: reads which of the two lines is selected from the outline's place in the box's frame, moves to Mojave (`NV_BENCH_TTW_START=capital` picks the first, `off` leaves the box), and presses Enter only on the wanted line. No Escape is tapped while the box is up; the film after it is skipped; a start that opens the other film (`FNVIntro` / `Fallout INTRO Vsk`) ends the walk with a note. Active when the game folder's Data holds `TaleOfTwoWastelands.esm`.
- Driver and parse: the viewer log is read for `menu.stack`, `load.kind` and `movie.open`/`movie.close`. Without the game trace or grim the old fixed keys remain.
- `docs/fork/BENCH.md` describes the walk; `docs/fork/ADDRESS-SPACE.md` gets the two TTW rows and the decision.

Tests: `scripts/fork/tests/test_menu_walk.py` (23): pictures drawn from the measured outline geometry (no game picture is stored), a model of the keys on a Profile with and without a save, and a timeline of the TTW opening (choice answered before the opening is settled, no Escape over the box, other film refused, no box in time, folder without TTW untouched). The suite passes (382).

Live: after the last change the walk reached the play screen on a TTW Profile in 3 of 3 runs (one with a newer viewer, then the two runs below). Also a TTW Profile's `Fallout.ini` must carry the three values Raul writes when TTW is on; without them the choice never comes (noted in BENCH.md).

- `NV_GUEST_WINDOW=1GiB`: heap peak 259,500,416 B, PASS, 0 stops, player path 2,723 units.
Decision recorded: the guest heap is not widened (about 7.5% of the heap used, far below the 2.8 GB mark).

**Scope:** QA build configuration only. No production domain, Vercel, Stripe, Supabase writes, migrations or billing change.

Netlify CLI `deploy --remote --context deploy-preview` creates a draft with an immutable `DEPLOY_URL` rather than the preconfigured `qa-manual-<sha>` alias. The existing fail-closed environment guard accepts only PR previews and manual aliases, so it cannot validate a CLI remote draft.

- `netlify.toml` invokes the protected wrapper.
- Added synthetic positive and negative regressions for provider metadata and forbidden production, email, privileged database and billing settings.

From a clean worktree at the **approved merged SHA**, and the existing linked QA site, use `netlify deploy --remote --context deploy-preview --site e953293d-348c-41e8-b798-fcd1ece9c427` (no `--alias`, no `--prod`). **Critical:** Only permit deployment after exact-head required checks, independent qualified CODEOWNER approval, and validation that QA deploy-preview environment scopes are correct; do not authorize unrestricted Sentry or other egress. author: ankool29
body:
Deuxième des trois pull requests de l'étape 3. **Cette branche part de `reseaux-electricite` (#9)** : tant que #9 n'est pas fusionnée, le diff ci-dessous la contient aussi. Les commits propres à cette PR sont les deux derniers : « Reseaux etape 3 (2/3) : fluides » et le correctif « Fluides : un appareil endormi se reveille aussi quand son propre volume change ».

## Conception retenue

**Segments** (`crates/exode-core/src/fluids.rs`), sur le socle commun `networks.rs` :
- un segment est une composante connexe de conduites : un seul fluide, un volume, une température. Sa capacité est la somme de celles de ses conduites ;
- une fusion additionne les volumes (température : moyenne pondérée entière) ;
- une séparation au démontage répartit le volume au prorata des capacités (le reste va à la partie de plus petit identifiant). La part de la conduite démontée est comptée comme retirée dans le bilan matière ;
- **les segments sont délimités par les appareils**, et le fluide ne passe d'un volume à l'autre que par leurs raccords, avec un **débit plafonné** :
  - **pompe** (1×2) : de l'arrière vers l'avant seulement, si elle est alimentée en électricité ; arrêt si la sortie est pleine ou l'entrée vide ;
  - **vanne** : ouverte, elle égalise le remplissage de l'arrière vers l'avant (sens unique) ; fermée, elle bloque. Commande `Toggle` et bouton « Ouvrir / fermer » dans le panneau ;
  - **réservoir** (3×3, 4 raccords) : égalise son remplissage avec chaque segment raccordé ;
  - **pompe à eau** (1×2) : la case derrière elle doit être un lac. Elle pousse de l'eau à 15 °C : **seule entrée de matière** des fluides, comptée comme extraction.
- **plusieurs fluides** (eau, vapeur) ; **jamais de mélange** : une conduite qui relierait deux segments de fluides différents est refusée à la pose, et un transfert vers un autre fluide n'a pas lieu ;
- **conduite souterraine** : un raccord en surface, un tunnel jusqu'à 10 cases vers la première entrée qui lui fait face ;
- les appareils qui n'ont rien déplacé dorment, et se réveillent dès qu'un volume raccordé **ou leur propre volume** change. Le résultat est identique (même empreinte avec et sans mise en veille).

**Sauvegarde v4** (contenu des segments), avec conversion des v1 à v3.

**Godot** :
- Sprites rangés selon GRAPHICS-01 avec une fiche par bâtiment, générée depuis `metadata.json` : conduites en 16 pièces selon les voisins raccordés (masque N=1, E=2, S=4, W=8), conduite souterraine, pompe et pompe à eau (4 orientations, rotor animé en marche, voyants `_state`), vanne (pièce « fermée »), réservoir (calque `_niveau` teinté selon le fluide, opacité selon le remplissage).
- Panneau : segment, fluide, volume / capacité, température ; état des pompes ; vanne ouverte ou fermée.
- Pose en ligne pour les conduites ; nouveaux outils dans la barre ; scène de contrôle `fluides`, aussi vérifiée par l'autotest.

## Tests

- **La pompe impose le sens** : elle vide le réservoir A dans B. B plein, rien ne revient vers A. Sans électricité, elle ne pompe pas (état « pas d'énergie »).
- **La vanne fermée bloque** ; ouverte, les niveaux s'égalisent dans son sens ; jamais à contre-sens.
- **Le réservoir se remplit puis sature** : pompe à eau sur un vrai lac du monde → conduites → réservoir. Il atteint exactement sa capacité, la pompe à eau se bloque, et plus rien n'est extrait.
- Mélange refusé ; séparation au prorata (500 → 60 retirés, 120 + 120) ; réunion ; conduite souterraine sous des coffres.
- **Réveil** (correctif) : une pompe raccordée directement à un réservoir le remplit, et le réservoir transmet l'eau au suivant. Avant le correctif, il restait endormi ; le test échoue sans le correctif.
- **Conservation** : bilan matière vrai pendant 3 000 ticks, avec démontage et repose d'une conduite et une vanne fermée en route. **Déterminisme** : deux exécutions identiques. **Sauvegarde** en cours de route puis rechargement : 500 ticks identiques.
- **Conversion v3** : une sauvegarde produite par le code de #9 se recharge et continue **à l'identique** (même empreinte complète).
- 46 tests OK ; autotest Godot `SELFTEST OK` (scènes électricité et fluides).

## Chiffres (banc F4)

Mesures indicatives sur le serveur de développement (x86), pas sur téléphone. Il n'y avait pas de fluides avant : « avant » désigne ma première version, sans mise en veille ni lecture unique des volumes.

| 3 000 segments (4 conduites chacun) séparés par des vannes, alimentés par des réservoirs pleins | Première version | Après optimisation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 300 premiers ticks (l'eau avance, 2 700 appareils actifs) | 1,9 – 2,7 ms/tick | 1,0 – 1,4 ms/tick |
| moyenne sur 3 000 ticks (équilibre atteint, tous les appareils en veille à la fin) | – | ≈ 0,4 ms/tick |

Banc F1 inchangé (lignes saturées : 0,024 ms en mouvement, 0,003 ms bloquées).

## Points [O] rencontrés et choix provisoires

Signalés dans `content.json`, le README et `docs/A_CORRIGER.md` (points 19 à 22) :
- 1 unité de fluide = 1 kg ; volumes (conduite 100, réservoir 5 000) ; débits par tick (pompe 20, vanne 30, raccord de réservoir 40, pompe à eau 20) ;
- la pompe à eau ne consomme pas d'électricité ;
- la vanne est à sens unique (son sprite est orienté) ;
- les raccords occupent une case précise de leur côté (milieu arrondi), alors que le sprite les dessine au milieu exact pour les largeurs paires ;
- une conduite souterraine ne se tourne pas (à démonter puis reposer) ;
- pas de calque de niveau pour les conduites.

## Reste à faire

- Chaleur, chaudière, échangeur, turbine, combustible : PR 3 (#11).

author: kokoroou
body:
## Summary

The scene player used to guess the value of a switch or variable it did not know. It can now start from a save file the user opens instead. The idea came from rpgsave-converter in *awesome-game-file-format-reversing*.

- **`js/save.js`** (no DOM, tested in node): `readSave(name, bytes)` returns `{ name, switches, variables, self, actors, party, mapId }`.
  - MV `.rpgsave`: LZ-String base64 of JsonEx. `lzDecompressFromBase64` is a decoder only.
  - MZ `.rmmzsave`: zlib of JsonEx. NW.js writes the binary string to disk as UTF-8, so that form is tried first, then raw zlib.
  - VX Ace `.rvdata2`, VX `.rvdata`, XP `.rxdata`: Marshal streams written one after another (new `marshalLoadAll` in `rgss.js`), searched for `Game_Switches`, `Game_Variables`, `Game_SelfSwitches`, `Game_Actors`, `Game_Party` and `Game_Map`.
  - `jsonExDecode()` unwraps `@a`, drops `@` and `@c`, and turns `@r` into null.
- **`scene-script.js`**: when a save is open (`S.save`), `sceneState(list, ctx)` knows every switch and variable from the start. Unset ones are OFF or 0, as in the game. It also knows the self switches of `ctx = { mapId, evId }`, which only applies to map event pages. `sceneActor()` and `sceneParty()` take the save's actors and party over the game's starting ones.
- **UI**: a new toolbar button, **Use a save** (`#save-btn`). Once a save is open it reads "Save: name"; clicking it again drops the save. The player's subtitle adds "· from name". An unreadable file shows "Save not read" with the reason in the tooltip. The save is dropped when another game is opened.
- **Read-only**: the save lives in memory only and is never written back or sent anywhere. `privacy.html` does not change because no new kind of data leaves the device.
- **Docs**: a new FAQ entry (visible text and JSON-LD), plus README, `llms.txt` and CLAUDE.md.

## Testing

- `node scripts/check-site.mjs` → OK
- `node --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` → 108 pass, 0 fail. New tests are in `tests/save.test.mjs`:
  - an MV save made with real lz-string 1.5 output
  - an MZ save stored as a UTF-8 binary string and as raw zlib
  - an XP save of consecutive Marshal streams, with `Game_Actor` objects in the party
  - a VX Ace save of a header plus a contents Hash
  - rejection of files that are not saves
  - one scene that takes different branches with and without a save, including self switches per event
- The LZ-String decoder matches lz-string 1.5 on 3000 random strings and one large JSON document (checked outside the repo).
- Chromium, on a synthetic VX Ace game with a save written by Ruby 3.3 `Marshal.dump` (switch 1 OFF):
  - without the save the scene ends on "Switch on"; with it, "Switch off"
  - the button and the player's subtitle show the save name
  - a junk file shows "Save not read"
  - no page errors, and no horizontal scroll at phone width

## Notes / risks

- Self switches stay unknown for common events, because they have no event of their own.
- Skill and state conditions on actors are still guessed.
- The graph does not show the save's values yet; only the scene player uses them.
- Not tried with real game saves.

---

author: quick104
body:
## Problem

Related issue: N/A
Validation tasks: none

Other clients: Apple N/A (web-only layout fix); Android N/A (web-only layout fix); Roku N/A (web-only layout fix)

With an audiobook playing in the web app, an admin page scrolled to its end came back about one mini-bar height short of its end after the user opened Now Listening and collapsed it again. The mini bar then covered the page's last controls until the user scrolled. This change keeps the page at its end.

The admin shell pads the end of its pages by `--playback-bar-clearance`, which comes from the mini bar's measured `--audiobook-bar-height` (#4939). Now Listening replaces the mini bar while it's open, and the bar removed that property when it unmounted. The padding dropped by the bar's height, so the browser clamped the scroll position of a page at its end, and collapsing brought the padding back but not the scroll position. On a sandbox, the admin dashboard came back 119 px short of its end at 393 px wide and 121 px at 834 and 1440 px, and at 393 and 834 px the bar covered part of the last Recent Activity row. Collapsing with Escape did the same. The save bar's in-flow page spacer reads the same variable, so pages that use it shrank the same way in either shell.

## Approach

The mini bar now leaves its last measured height on the root when it unmounts, through a new `keepAfterUnmount` option on `useRootHeightProperty`. `AudiobookPlaybackProvider` removes the property once no audiobook is playing: stopping playback, a profile switch, and a player error all end that way. Switching books keeps it until the next bar measures its own, so the padding doesn't change between books either. The property name is one exported constant, `AUDIOBOOK_BAR_HEIGHT_PROPERTY`, used by both. The watch bar and the impersonation banner keep the hook's default and behave as before.

Keeping the mini bar mounted under Now Listening was the other option. Its cover tile shares a view-transition name with Now Listening's cover, and focus returns to that tile on collapse only because it remounts, so that route needs more changes.

If the window crosses the `sm` breakpoint while Now Listening is open, the kept height can be 2 px off until the bar measures again on collapse. That stays inside the 1rem the admin shell pads beyond the clearance.

## Validation

- Live, on a dev sandbox with a generated audiobook added as an Audiobooks library: reproduced on `e62100f9` at 393, 834, and 1440 px. On this branch the page stays at its end after collapsing at all three, by button and by Escape. A per-frame trace of the collapse found no transient scroll or height change. Mid-page collapse, closing the player at the page end, and the user shell's home feed behave the same in both builds. A phone rotated to landscape while Now Listening was open came back 2 px from its end, with the last control 59 px clear of the bar.
- Web: `eslint` (no new warnings), `prettier --check`, `pnpm run build`, and `pnpm run budget:check` pass. `vitest run` on Node 24: 3,128 of 3,132 pass; the 4 failures, in `AdminAccessGroups`, `AdminCollections.select`, and `PdfBundleCompatibility`, also fail on main on the same machine (timeouts under load, and the PDF test's optional canvas module isn't installed).
- Repository: `verify-local-paths`, `verify-bidi`, `verify-case-collisions`, and `verify-size-ratchet` pass. The Go gate wasn't run; no Go file changes.
- No test added: this is a layout fix outside the areas in "Decide what to test", and the live before and after is the proof.

## Evidence

Evidence: being published; the link follows in a moment.

Surface and build: web admin dashboard at 393 × 659, 834 × 1194, and 1440 × 900, and the user home feed at 393 × 659, dark theme; before `e62100f9`, after `189f9528`.

## Risks

Audiobooks are a beta feature. A future caller that passes `keepAfterUnmount` has to remove the property itself, or its height stays on the root; the option's doc comment says so.

## Checklist

- [x] I read and can explain the complete diff.
- [x] This pull request addresses one concern.
- [x] Each test this pull request adds meets "Decide what to test" in CONTRIBUTING.md.
- [x] The Evidence section shows every change a user can see, or how I checked a change nobody sees.

## Council review

Plan round on `b0d13721`: Sol (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh), Opus (claude-opus-5-5, high), and Gemini (gemini-4-neon, xhigh). Opus found the plan minimal, Gemini found its premises held, and Sol asked for a browser check of a resize while Now Listening is open (done: 2 px). Following Gemini, the property's removal moved from the player's unmount to the provider, so switching books never clears it.

Background review: running.

| Member | Round 1 |
| --- | --- |
| Sol (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh) | running |
| Opus (claude-opus-5-5, high) | running |
| Gemini (gemini-4-neon, xhigh) | running |

Visual review: 2 rounds, captures from `e62100f9` and `189f9528`

| Member | Round 1 | Round 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sol | better, 7/10 | better, 7/10 |
| Opus | better, 7/10 | better, 7/10 |
| Gemini | better, 6/10 | better, 6/10 |

Round 2 added the captures the members asked for: Escape collapse, mid-page collapse, closing the player at the page end, and the user shell. The user shell pair first showed the onboarding picker instead of the home feed; it was taken again on the home feed after round 2, with a per-frame trace, and checked by the implementer. Not in this change, and the same before and after: at narrow widths the mini bar draws its side controls over its transport, and Now Listening's "Back to player" label measures about 3.7:1 against its background without cover art. Each has its own follow-up. The other notes (the blank cover tile, Now Listening's lower controls below the fold on a short phone screen, the cover tile's focus style after Escape, and dashboard wording and layout) also predate this change.

## AI Disclosure

- Harness: Claude Code, run from T3 Code
- Tool(s): Claude Code subagents for the code review; Codex CLI and Antigravity for the cross-provider plan, visual, and background reviews; Playwright (headless Chromium) for the captures

body:
Closes #725

## Summary

When CI is red on a PR the orchestrator already pushed and it asks for publication again on the unchanged tree, arete no longer validates the diff, restages or pushes. It checks that review, checks and verification evidence are current. It then runs `gh run rerun --failed` once for the failed workflow run and goes back to watching CI. Green CI continues to ready-for-review and automerge. A second red CI on the same head ends the run failed with "CI failed twice on the unchanged head <sha>". If the rerun watch times out, the saved run and attempt are resumed on the next request without a second rerun. Replacement jobs are tracked per workflow run, so a newer red or pending same-name check from another workflow keeps the PR draft. All other publish paths are unchanged.

## Checked in use

**blocked**: The stubbed-GitHub controller scenarios for #725 behave as the issue asks. An unchanged-head `publication.request` reruns the failed run once and watches CI again. A second red CI fails the run with the new reason. The live GitHub rerun-to-automerge case is unverified, as the owner said it would be, and should be marked that way in the PR body.

Blocked by: A real PR whose CI fails on an unrelated class timeout gets one rerun on live GitHub and automerges on green: Not exercised live. The stubbed-transport tests above are the only evidence for this behavior.

- **Passed**: Publication request on the unchanged published head after red CI reruns the failed run once, watches CI again, and does not call require_valid_diff or push. A second red CI ends the run failed with 'CI failed twice on the unchanged head <sha>'. The same tests cover resumption after a timeout, stale evidence, and a newer check from another workflow.
  - How: sandbox uv run python -m unittest tests.test_workflow.UnchangedHeadCIRetryTests
  - Saw: Ran 16 tests in 2.272s, OK. The `gh run rerun 456 --failed` call was asserted once, require_valid_diff, restage and commit_and_push were asserted never called, and the second-red ending was ('failed', 'CI failed twice on the unchanged head <sha>'). The tests use stubbed GitHub transport.

- **Failed (environment)**: A real PR whose CI fails on an unrelated class timeout gets one rerun on live GitHub and automerges on green
  - How: Not run. The owner said there is no scratch PR and told me to mark this line unverified, with the stubbed evidence above, and to publish as ready.
  - Saw: Not exercised live. The stubbed-transport tests above are the only evidence for this behavior.

## Review

**approve**: Both earlier blockers are fixed on reading the code. I could not run tests: Bash was denied in this review session, so the 12 `UnchangedHeadCIRetryTests` rest on the verifier's stubbed run. The live GitHub rerun-to-automerge path is unverified, and the one-rerun-per-head logic is intricate, so the first real case after merge is the live check.


### Review notes (not blocking)

- [minor] tests/test_workflow.py: The retry evidence uses a fake GitHub transport and a mocked automerge. A live rerun through automerge is still unverified.
- [minor] arete/ci.py: `watch` now carries rerun tracking: attempt handling, superseded-job detection and per-run exact checks. It costs extra GitHub API calls per poll, one `actions_job` lookup for each non-rerun check that shares a rerun job name. A design you would simplify later, not a defect.

author: caomengxuan666
body:
## Root cause
`${#v}` and `${v:off:len}` walked the value's bytes with Rust's strict `std::str::from_utf8`, which rejects the pre-2003 extended UTF-8 range (4/5/6-byte sequences up to `U+7FFFFFFF`, e.g. `U+110000`..`U+7FFFFFFF`). GNU Bash delegates character length and substring stepping to libc's `mbrlen`, and glibc's UTF-8 decoder accepts that extended range as a single character.

GNU C citations (`third_party/bash/` @ `9c465866`):
- `${#name}` -> `parameter_brace_expand_length` (`subst.c:8258`) -> `MB_STRLEN` (`subst.c:8308/8323/8332`) -> `MBSLEN` (`include/shmbutil.h:48-49`) -> `mbstrlen` (`lib/sh/shmbchar.c:56-79`)
- `${var:off:len}` -> `parameter_brace_substring` (`subst.c:9050`) -> `mb_substring` (`subst.c:9022`) -> `ADVANCE_CHAR` (`include/shmbutil.h:114-147`)

## Fix
- `src/locale.rs`: add `utf8_mblen` (mirroring glibc `mbrlen`'s extended UTF-8 acceptance while rejecting overlongs, surrogates, lone continuations, and truncated sequences), add `multibyte_char_count`, and rewrite `multibyte_char_offsets` onto the same walk (+2 unit tests).
- `src/executor/expand_braced_indices.rs`: route `parameter_char_length` through `multibyte_char_count`.
- `tests/issue4035_extended_utf8_length.rs`: add 5 integration tests; update residual comment in `tests/issue3947_ansic_unicode_extended_utf8.rs`.

## Verification
- Verified byte-for-byte against WSL `/usr/local/bin/bash` 5.3.20 under both `LC_ALL=C.utf8` and `LC_ALL=C`.
- `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` clean on all 4 files.
- `cargo test --test issue4035_extended_utf8_length`: 5/5 pass.
- `cargo test --lib locale::`: 25/25 pass.

author: pzfreo
body:
This is the maintainer-approved CI change: draft pull requests run only fmt and lint, and full CI runs once a PR is ready. It sits on #339 (tools/verify.sh), which CONTRIBUTING.md now names, so merge #339 first.

**What changes:**
- `ready_for_review` is added to `pull_request.types` in ci.yml, crates.yml and python.yml.
- Every non-lint job gets `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false`:
  - ci.yml: advisories, wasm, linux and macos (the suite.yml calls);
  - crates.yml: package and semver;
  - python.yml: wheels and sdist. test and test-sdist skip through `needs`.
- In ci.yml's lint job, the test steps (the python unittests, as_compare, haecceity pmi_write, nist_roundtrip, doc-tests) are gated with `if: github.event.pull_request.draft != true`. On a draft, the lint job runs fmt, clippy and the feature-set `cargo check`s only.
- DCO is unchanged. Path filters, concurrency, the publish jobs, main pushes, dispatches and release events are unchanged.

**Draft vs ready behaviour:**
- Marking ready triggers all three workflows. The path filters are evaluated against the whole PR diff.
- Later pushes to a ready PR run everything.
- Re-running a draft-era run stays lint-only, because the payload still says draft. CONTRIBUTING.md says so.
- `main` has no required checks today. If some become required, a skipped draft job reads as passing until `ready_for_review` re-runs it.

**Review:** an independent read-only review checked every job and step gate, the null `pull_request` cases for push, dispatch and release, `needs` chains, concurrency and release PRs. It found the gating correct. Its doc findings are fixed in d5321d76.

**Checks:**
- All workflow YAML parses (`ruby -ryaml`); actionlint isn't installed here.
- `tools/verify.sh` on this branch: `VERIFY: PASS`.
- Real draft and ready behaviour needs a live PR to observe. This PR is the first.

author: hopekeeper
body:
## Bottom line

Rebalances 14 Ukrainian naval programs from #6459 and adds the Khadzhybey destroyer and wartime Lan missile boat. Ship restoration and construction now account for local shipyard control, Political Power, and Navy Experience. Seven existing projects offer a cheaper route with existing research or a longer route that funds the missing technology.

## Changes

- Check ownership and control of the relevant state and control of the shipyard, port, or repair plant province. Apply those checks to both research routes and to the relevant Varyag and carrier-aircraft decisions.
- Give the future corvette program, Project 58250, Project 11451, the Zaporizhzhia submarine, the Ukrayina cruiser, support ships, and Lahuna mutually exclusive research routes with matching calendar windows. The advanced corvette and cruiser configurations grant their additional technologies when selected.
- Consolidate influence changes for naval purchases, upgrades, and restoration. The Western refit of the Ukrayina applies its Russian influence penalty once.
- Surface the relevant stored-aircraft decisions when the Varyag returns to Ukraine or heads to China. Match the refit's point-defence missiles to the imported weapons described in its events. Preserve the existing carrier aircraft sale missions.
- Open Khadzhybey design before 2010 after five restoration programs or after the Ukrayina or Varyag enters service. The capital ships give different discounts, with the carrier taking precedence. Funding Project 58250 first adds five percentage points to both destroyer discounts. Finishing the destroyer design first cuts the corvette project's time by 20% and cost by 15%. Both Project 58250 routes open in 2008 and use the same corvette prerequisites.
- Let Ukraine choose the destroyer's turbines, strike missiles, air defence, and radar. The design announcement offers production with two Mykolaiv dockyards, or funding a second dockyard for $0.60 billion that opens the line a year later. The game rechecks control of the yard at completion.
- Add the Lan missile-boat program during a 2012–2018 war with Russia or its proxies. After development, Mykolaiv can open one line for eight boats, two for twelve, or four for twenty-four.
- Order English decision text, tooltips, and numbered events. Reuse the registered naval artwork and add shared cost labels for the research routes.

## Verification

- Checked 44 decisions and missions, 95 events, and 75 unique sprite references. Verified the province and state pairs, technology route timers and flags, and the required AI and option log blocks.
- Checked all 81 equipment combinations against the destroyer hull slots, the eight prior-project combinations, both Project 58250 research prices, and the three Lan production orders.
- Merged the updated branch with #6788 in a temporary Git object directory and confirmed that both the naval programs and the shared aviation museum effect are present. No merge conflicts.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Summary
- Settings now has two tabs, **Topics** and **Domains**. Balance, Sources and Cards are merged into Topics.
- **Stack rank:** you reorder topics by dragging or with the ↑/↓ buttons. A **Falloff** preset (Even, Gentle, Smooth, Steep) turns each topic's rank into its share of the feed. author: sjawhar-agent[bot]
body:
## What

Two of this branch's broker tests stood for the daemon broker's scope lease by a fixed path, `<runtimeDir>/broker.pid`. #102 (`fix/file-lock-sidecar-on-linux`, 6ce13375) moves the lease to a sidecar beside the runtime dir, `<runtimeDir>.broker.lock`, so that deleting the runtime dir does not free the scope. Composed with #102:

- `broker-shutdown-during-startup.test.ts`: `observeLeaseRelease` never sees the broker take `broker.pid`, so it observes nothing and the case fails.
- `broker-failure-cleanup.test.ts`: `FileLock.tryAcquire(broker.pid)` succeeds whether or not the broker let its lease go, so both lease checks pass and check nothing.

Both tests now take the lease path from the broker itself: the first native lock the broker acquires whose path begins with the runtime dir's (in the dir or beside it). The two cleanup cases throw if the broker took no such lock. The tests change; the broker does not.

This commit does not need to wait for #102: the tests check the lease on this branch alone and with #102.

## Evidence

Builds Jobs, unprivileged user, three runs per row. `comp` is release v18.18.6-sami.20261121-081625 (e6a9e3f4) merged with #102's 6ce13375 (one docs conflict resolved), with natives built from that tree. `member` is this branch's head, with natives built from 9058ab9d (the same Rust).

| Tree | Test | runc | gVisor |
|---|---|---|---|
| comp, tests unchanged | `broker-shutdown-during-startup` | 3 of 3 failed | 3 of 3 failed |
| comp, this commit | `broker-shutdown-during-startup` | 3 of 3 passed | 3 of 3 passed |
| comp, this commit | `broker-failure-cleanup` | 3 of 3 passed | 3 of 3 passed |
| comp + plant, tests unchanged | `broker-failure-cleanup` | 3 of 3 passed (it checks nothing) | 3 of 3 passed |
| comp + plant, this commit | `broker-failure-cleanup` | 3 of 3 failed (both lease cases) | 3 of 3 failed |
| member, this commit | `broker-shutdown-during-startup` | 3 of 3 passed | 3 of 3 passed |
| member, this commit | `broker-failure-cleanup` | 3 of 3 passed | 3 of 3 passed |
| member + plant, this commit | `broker-failure-cleanup` | 3 of 3 failed (both lease cases) | 3 of 3 failed |

The failing case without this commit is "serves no client and closes the server before the lease release when shutdown lands during the bind". `bun run check:ts` at this branch's head: exit 0.

The plant removes `lease.lock.release()` from `releaseBrokerLease`, so the broker keeps its scope lease after a failure.

Part of #1867.

The "Retrograde" tooltip in the Planetary cycles motion box now sits on the word "Retrograde" inside the option's own label, as the owner decided on 2026-11-21 ("wrap the word, not the button"). The word is a non-interactive `<span>`, so clicking it selects the option. No button sits inside the `<label>`. The popup is always mounted, `aria-hidden` and linked with `aria-describedby`, so the radio's accessible name stays exactly "Retrograde only (e.g. Venus’s inferior conjunctions)". The en and nl strings are unchanged: the word is found at render time with `splitGlossaryText`.

## Commits (brief steps 1 to 4)

1. `0e24f592` extracts the tooltip open state into `src/ui/primitives/use-tooltip-state.ts`. `Tooltip` keeps the same DOM and behaviour, and `test/ui-tooltip.test.tsx` passes unedited.
2. `9c0c2223` gives `Radio` an optional `term` (`RadioTerm { word, definition }`) and adds the new test `test/ui-radio-term.test.tsx`.
3. `6e32f8b6` makes `CyclesView`'s motion filter pass the word term and removes the sibling `GlossaryTerm`. It also tightens `test/ui-glossary.test.tsx`.
4. `e1318d95` extends the e2e coverage in `e2e/cycles-golden-path.spec.ts`.

`test/ui-glossary.test.tsx`, "the Cycles motion filter carries the retrograde tooltip", run for en and nl:

- **New:** the motion labels contain no `button`. The retrograde label's `.glossary-term .primitive-tooltip-trigger` text is exactly `Retrograde` (en) or `retrograde` (nl). That label's text, with the `aria-hidden` subtree removed, equals `motionRetrograde` exactly.
- **Reason:** the old check asserted the old placement, which the owner rejected. The new checks are stricter: an exact word, an exact name and no nested interactive element.
- **Added:** `splitGlossaryText(motionRetrograde, locale)` yields a `retrograde` segment in both en and nl (a parity check).

`e2e/cycles-golden-path.spec.ts`: the existing radio-name check is kept, and the same check is added with `exact: true`. Two new tests were added. No existing assertion was removed or weakened.

- `npm run build` and `node scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs`: 0. The eager JS is 527605 of 665600 bytes.
