author: puneet-swarup
body:
## What

Loom slice 3a: `src/loom/graph.js` — the dependency graph over the `imports`
table, per `src/loom_specs.md` §5.6. This is the layer between the extractors
(slice 2) and the indexer (slice 3b), and the first caller the indexer will have.

- **Edges.** `writeEdges(db, {relPath, imports, exists})` resolves an extractor's
  specifiers through `resolve.js` and *replaces* the file's `imports` rows, so a
  removed import disappears instead of lingering as a dependency the digest would
  report. Unresolved or external specifiers keep `resolved = NULL` — an edge not
  followed, never a guess. `opts.exists` keeps the module off the disk in tests.
- **Reads.** `importers()` / `dependencies()` return live, sorted, de-duplicated
  paths; tombstoned files appear in neither.
- **Role drift.** `rebuildGraph()` computes `importers_sig` (§5.6: `sha256` over
  the sorted importer paths, 16 hex chars) for every live file in one pass over
  `files` and `imports` joined in memory — the store interface has no `GROUP BY`,
  and 2,000 files must not become 2,000 queries. A signature that moves while
  `content_sha` does not sets `summaries.role_stale = 1`: the file's role changed
  and no re-read of the file could tell you that.

Three decisions the spec leaves implicit, recorded in `docs/LOOM.md`:

- the first computation is a **baseline**, not drift (otherwise the first index of
  any project marks every summary stale and halves its prose confidence);
- drift is **one-way** — only a fresh summary clears the flag;
- a file with no importers signs as `sha256('')[:16]`, since `''` is the
  "never computed" sentinel.

I1 holds throughout: every export catches and returns a neutral value, and a test
asserts the neutral result when the store handle is absent.

## Tests

- `tests/loom/graph.test.js` — **16 tests**: signature stability under reorder and
  duplicate rows, drift when an importer is added, first-run baseline, one-way
  drift, tombstones on both ends, unresolved edges counted but never followed,
  idempotence, neutral results with no store, edge replacement, and an end-to-end
  extract → resolve → graph pass.
- `npx jest tests/loom` — **271 passed, 2 skipped** (the SQLite backend skips where
  `node:sqlite` is absent, as before).
- `npm run typecheck` — clean. `node scripts/check-syntax.js` — clean.
- The graph suite runs on the JSON store unconditionally and on SQLite wherever
  the runtime provides it.
- `npm test` in full exceeds the sandbox's 300 s command limit, so the run covered
  the Loom suite, the markdown-scope suite (14) and typecheck locally; CI runs the
  full suite.

## Docs

`docs/LOOM.md` (slice table + a "dependency graph" section with the three
decisions), `CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased, `NEXT_SESSION.md` (T2 status, the
remaining-slice list re-cut into 3a/3b, and what is next).

## Not in this PR

No indexer, no digest, no agent-loop wiring — `refresh.js` (slice 3b) is the next
item and will call `graph.rebuildGraph()` as step 7 of §5.2. Nothing here touches
`src/adapters/` (I4).

body:
Start now sent the start, but the usage-limit guard held the crew run again immediately because it applied the limit before reading the user's yes (`confirmLimit`). The guard now lets a yes through. Not committed, and not yet tried in the running dev app.

**Cause.** The check-in was started by crew (`by: "crew"`), so wisp treats it as unattended. Start now (`runtime.release` → `release_held`) resends the same turn with `confirmLimit: true`, which ADR-0091 §5 says should go ahead. But `guard()` in `plugins/budget/host/src/lib.rs` applied the unattended-work limit (`wisp_budget_core::decide`) before it read `confirmLimit`. It put the same "Weekly 90%" hold back on the same turn, so the card never changed. Your dev database still shows turn `01a1fde7…` as `held`.

**Fix.** When `c.confirm_limit` is set, the guard skips that hold and goes straight to the Ask-near-the-limit check, which already honours the yes. Wisp's own automatic start at the reset is unchanged, because it doesn't send `confirmLimit`.

author: sgaduuw
body:
Item 5 on the roadmap, originally "an `.error` directive". The assembler has no conditionals, so a bare `.error` would fire every time it was reached. A check with a condition covers what trylobite needed it for.

## What

- **`.assert E, "MESSAGE"`** stops assembly with MESSAGE as the error, at that line, when E is 0. It is checked in pass two, once every symbol is known, so it can refer to labels defined after it.
- **`defined(NAME)`** gives 1 if NAME is a label or constant anywhere in the program, and 0 if not. It is only accepted in `.assert`. In pass one, an `.equ` would only see the symbols defined so far, so its answer would depend on where it was asked.
- **Comparisons** (`== != < <= > >=`) can join two sums. They bind loosest, give 1 or 0, and don't chain. With them a layout constant can be checked, as in `.assert PCB_SIZE == 117, "..."`.
- **Unknown escapes are errors.** Before, `\b` quietly became `b`. The escapes are `\n \t \0 \\ \' \"`, in strings and in character literals.
- Quoted operands are no longer scanned for local label references, so a message can say "1b".
- `docs/assembler.md` and CONTEXT.md are updated.

The trylobite follow-up is a one-line change to `include/kernel.s`, once this is pinned:
```
        .assert defined(RAM_PAGES), "include/kernel.s is part of a build: run shell.s or demo.s"
```

## Tests

- Conformance cases:
  - a failed `.assert` with its message and line;
  - `defined()` on a missing symbol;
  - `.assert` with the wrong number of operands;
  - `defined()` outside `.assert`;
  - chained comparisons;
  - an `.assert` that holds while using a later label;
  - every escape stored correctly, and unknown escapes refused in a string and in a character literal.
- Unit tests for each comparison's boundary and for `defined()`.
- I removed the pass-two check, the quoted-operand skip and the `defined` lookup, and changed each comparison and the escape refusal, one at a time; a test failed every time.
- `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` pass.

author: joelthornton
body:
Queue item 28 before this PR ("Repeated yes/no answers with small groups and a rare answer").

**The problem.** E75's likelihood-ratio test of a yes/no outcome (glmer through simr) rejects too often when one answer is rare in a cell. I ran a grid of 19 designs at alpha .05, with 2,000 simulated studies each:
- **About two of the rarer answers per person expected in the rarest cell:** 6.3% to 8.9%.
- **Four answers per person in each condition:** 5.0% to 5.15%.
- **The other designs:** 4.75% to 6.15%.

The script is `docs/validation/2026-11-21-e75-yes-no-rare-grid.R`, and the table is in `validation-log.md` (21 November 2026).

**Why a simulated check, not a rule on the inputs.** No threshold on the expected count separated the designs that exceed alpha from those that don't. So every yes/no run now also simulates its own design with the tested effect set to zero:
- the main effect of condition, or the group-by-condition interaction;
- the same simr likelihood-ratio test, at the same number of simulated studies.

**What is recorded.** The rate is recorded with its Monte Carlo SE (`repeated_glmm_type1()`, `result$type1`, the record the interrupted-time-series card already uses).

**What users see.** When the rate is more than two Monte Carlo SEs above alpha, the result's "Important limitation" box, the write-ups and the planning document say:
- how often the test was significant with no real difference;
- that part of the power comes from false positives;
- that more answers from each person in each condition bring it closer to alpha.

Nothing is shown when the rate is within random error of alpha. The power itself is unchanged. Cochran's Q, counts and ordered categories are not affected.

**Cost.** A yes/no run takes about twice as long, since it simulates twice.

**Docs.**
- the queue row is removed and later rows renumbered;
- `status.md`'s E75 sentence is updated;
- a decision is added in `decisions.d`;
- the change notes are in `news.d` and `whats-new.d`.

**Tests run locally:**
- engine: `backend-glmm` and `run-spec` both pass;
- app: `results` passes, apart from E39 and the mediation tests, which need regmedint, and that isn't installed here;
- app: `repo-consistency` passes.

**Validation.** I ran the glmm chunk locally (`scripts/run-validation.R --only glmm`) on this branch: 16 pass, 0 fail. The 2 skips are the published examples still to be transcribed. That includes both yes/no designs checked against an independent simulation, and the Type I error checks.

- `review-list`: page header with «Мої / Нерозподілені / Усі» as chips, split layout; the side column holds the filters, the batch bar and the queue rows (initials, title, recipient and sent date, level chip, due or overdue chip, notice and reviewer chips, a checkbox per row for batch decisions); the selection is `?request=<awardId>`; «До черги розгляду» below 960 px.

Frontend gate: lint clean, 1417 Vitest (140 in `features/reviews`), prod build. Backend unchanged (gate skips it).
E2E: full run 253 passed (privacy-centre ac2_3 passed on retry); after the review fixes `review|overdue|keyboard|layout` 41 passed (keyboard ac1_7 passed on retry). New cases: deep link and reload keep the selection, side by side at 1280, route and escalation in the pane, a decided request shows its state without actions.
Screen check `/reviews`, `?request=` of a waiting and of an approved award at 1280/360, light/dark, uk/en: no sideways scroll, 0 serious axe findings; console 404s are the expected `reviews.item` answers for requests not waiting at the caller's level.

## Review
Code review (medium): 10 findings. Fixed: the pane kept a stale request after a list refresh (now read again with the page and the listed row wins); A/R acted on a hidden first request below 960 px (the list owns the shown id, none until a row is opened); a held request reopened with Back could be decided again (actions disabled while held); a failed load read as «Запит не знайдено» (own message); duplicated fallback rule; dead `organization()`; `?request=1e3` parsed. author: josep-audenis
body:
Proposes ADR 0035, the design for Phase 6 increment 5 (ADR 0028 item 2.5). Docs only; nothing is built here, and the ADR stays **Proposed** until accepted.

## What it decides

- **Values.** `0`, `1`, `X`, `Z` per bit, as a second `unknown` word beside each net's value. A circuit with no unknown bit keeps today's values word for word.
- **`Z`** comes only from a disabled tri-state buffer and is seen on wires; every computing part reads it as `X`. An unconnected input still reads 0 and warns (a change from what `docs/simulation-model.md` planned).
- **Parts.** Gates never give more `X` than their inputs force (AND with a 0 is 0). An unknown clock is a possible edge whenever a flip-flop sees it: its bits that differ from `d` become `X`. A RAM write that cannot be known makes the cell, or every cell, `X`. A load's or Reset's settle is never an edge.
- **A tri-state buffer** (`tri`), format 12.
- **Several drivers** are allowed only when all are tri-state outputs, resolved by a symmetric table. Two gate outputs wired together stay a load error. A component's output pin may share a wire only if it is a *bus pin*: driven inside by tri-state outputs alone.
- **Unstable loops** settle to `X` instead of keeping the values they stopped at. The settle that fails reports the `unstable` error; afterwards a warning, `unsettled`, stays while the `X` lasts and stops nothing.
- **Cost.** At most 10% fewer ticks per second on `cpu-1k` and `counters-1k` natively, compared by alternating runs of the two builds, and recorded.
- **Five steps**, one pull request each, ending with a *Shared bus* example and its Playwright target.

Also: the ADR index and the roadmap point at it.

## From review

Four passes by a design reviewer, reading the ADR against the engine:

- A flip-flop under a toggling clock could keep a known value that was wrong, depending on the parity of the delta limit. An unknown clock is now a possible edge at every evaluation, compared with `d` in the snapshot and on the net.
- Stored state was not covered by the stage that turns a loop to `X`; Reset could leave registers at `X` behind a tri-state clock; a clock that settles unknown at a load was never looked at again. All three are ruled on in item 4 and item 8.
- A pin wired straight through a component could join two buses backwards. Bus pins (item 6) prevent it.
- The resolver's part, driver and port nets, the warning that follows `unstable`, every value that crosses the engine's edge, and a cost comparison that the benchmarks' noise allows are now stated.

author: nipun0bugs
body:
# Daymark – Full-Stack TODO Application

## 1. Summary

Built **Daymark**, a full-stack TODO management application that allows users to create, view, edit, complete, filter, and delete tasks through a clean and responsive interface.

The application uses React and Material UI on the frontend, with an Express.js REST API and MongoDB for persistent data storage.

### Key Features
- Create tasks with a title and description.
- View all tasks, including their completion status.
- Edit existing tasks.
- Mark tasks as completed or active.
- Delete tasks.
- Filter tasks by All, Active, and Completed.
- Display task statistics and completion progress.
- Provide loading, error, empty, and success feedback states.
- Validate input on both the frontend and backend.

## 2. Solution Rationale and Technical Decisions

### Frontend – React, Material UI, and TanStack Query
- **React:** Component-based architecture keeps the interface modular and maintainable.
- **Material UI:** Provides consistent UI components and styling.
- **TanStack Query:** Manages server state, caching, loading states, mutations, and query invalidation.
- **Optimistic Updates:** Task completion and deletion update the interface immediately. Previous cached data is restored if a request fails.
- **Zod:** Validates task input on the frontend before submission.
- **Reusable Components:** The task composer, task list, task item, filters, and feedback components are separated for maintainability.

### Backend – Node.js, Express.js, and MongoDB
- **Express.js:** Provides REST API endpoints for task operations.
- **MongoDB and Mongoose:** Provide persistent storage and schema-based data modelling.
- **Zod Validation:** Independently validates incoming requests, task fields, update payloads, and MongoDB ObjectId formats.
- **Middleware:** Helmet, CORS configuration, request-size limits, rate limiting, and centralized error handling.
- **RESTful API Design:**
  - `GET /api/todos` – Retrieve tasks.
  - `POST /api/todos` – Create a task.
  - `PUT /api/todos/:id` – Update a task.
  - `PATCH /api/todos/:id/done` – Update completion status.
  - `DELETE /api/todos/:id` – Delete a task.

### Important Engineering Decisions
1. **Independent backend validation:** Frontend validation improves user experience, while backend validation prevents invalid data from bypassing API rules.
2. **Optimistic updates with rollback:** Improves perceived responsiveness while preserving consistency when a request fails.
3. **Centralized error handling:** Keeps error responses consistent and avoids duplicating error-handling logic across controllers.
4. **Environment-based configuration:** Keeps database connection and application configuration outside the source code.
5. **Automated validation tests:** Node.js tests cover input validation, invalid payloads, partial updates, and ObjectId validation.

## 3. Platform Demo Video

**Demo video:** https://youtu.be/vu2QX98aXXs

The video demonstrates the Daymark platform and its main functionality.

## 4. Five-Minute Code Walkthrough

**Code walkthrough video:** [Add the 5-minute code walkthrough video link when available.]

The walkthrough covers the application architecture and key implementation decisions.

| Time | Topic |
|---|---|
| 0:00–0:35 | Project overview and technology stack |
| 0:35–1:20 | Frontend entry point, App component, and component structure |
| 1:20–2:05 | TanStack Query, API integration, caching, and optimistic updates |
| 2:05–2:45 | Express application setup, middleware, and API routes |
| 2:45–3:45 | Controllers, Mongoose model, and MongoDB operations |
| 3:45–4:30 | Zod validation, centralized error handling, and security |
| 4:30–5:00 | Testing, engineering decisions, and conclusion |

### Files Covered

**Frontend**
- `client/src/main.jsx`
- `client/src/App.jsx`
- `client/src/hooks/useTodos.js`
- `client/src/api.js`

**Backend**

**Testing**

## 5. Conclusion

This project demonstrates my ability to design and implement a full-stack application, structure reusable frontend components, build RESTful APIs, work with MongoDB, validate data, handle errors, and improve user experience through effective server-state management.

My focus was not only on implementing CRUD functionality, but also on writing maintainable, validated, and reliable application code.

**NOTE** Erasing or replacing the contents of this template will result in your pull
request being summarily closed without consideration!

## Changes

Fixes Lillecarl/anyio#9.

Since `9e481806`, Linux sets the socket mode with `fchmod()` before `bind()`, and `unix_bind()` masks it with the umask: `mode=0o666` under umask 022 gives `0o644`. The `fchmod()` before `bind()` stays, so the file is never more permissive than requested. A `chmod(..., follow_symlinks=False)` after `bind()` restores the bits the umask removed, as other platforms already do. It only ever widens the mode towards the requested one.

features

author: dzh166
body:
## Problem

`GithubRepoConfig` only normalized one specific shorthand: it prepended `https://github.com/` when the input contained exactly one `/`, i.e. `owner/repo`. Any other scheme-less form was kept verbatim:

```python
GithubRepoConfig(github_url="github.com/SWE-agent/test-repo").github_url
# 'github.com/SWE-agent/test-repo'   <- no scheme
```

`GithubRepoConfig.copy()` passes that string to `git remote add origin`, and git interprets a URL without a scheme (and without `user@host:path` syntax) as a local path, so the run dies during environment startup instead of cloning:

```
$ git fetch --depth 1 origin HEAD
fatal: 'github.com/SWE-agent/test-repo' does not appear to be a git repository
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
```

This is reachable through the public API twice over:

* `--env.repo.github_url=github.com/owner/repo` or `agent.env.repo.github_url` in a config file;
* batch runs: `SimpleBatchInstance.repo_name` is routed to `GithubRepoConfig` whenever `_is_github_repo_url()` matches, and that pattern matches scheme-less URLs (`tests/test_env_utils.py::test_is_github_repo_url` already asserts `_is_github_repo_url("github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/anything")`), so a batch file with `repo_name: github.com/owner/repo` produces a config that can never be cloned.

Note that the failure is silent at configuration time and only surfaces as a git error inside the container, and only when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is unset — with a token, `_get_url_with_token()` happens to build a valid `https://<token>@...` URL.

## Fix

`_ensure_github_url_scheme()` now normalizes all inputs before they are stored:

* URLs that already have a scheme, or scp-like `git@...` URLs, are returned unchanged;
* inputs starting with `github.com/` or `www.github.com/` get `https://` prepended;
* the existing `owner/repo` shorthand keeps its `https://github.com/...` behavior.

## Tests

`tests/test_env_utils.py::test_github_repo_config_adds_scheme` covers the three scheme-less forms, checks that the remote handed to git is the same normalized URL, and checks that already-qualified URLs (including `git@github.com:...`) are left alone.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/test_env_utils.py -q -k "not associated"
9 passed, 1 deselected

$ python repro-1.py     # before the fix
FAIL: 'github.com/SWE-agent/test-repo' keeps the scheme-less remote ...   exit 1
$ python repro-1.py     # after the fix
PASS: all scheme-less GitHub inputs get a cloneable remote URL            exit 0
```

author: michaelkrauty
body:
When the radio or tracking engine thread fails, the daemon logs the reason and exits so its supervisor restarts it. The exit waited at most 200 ms for the log writer thread and then exited anyway, so if the writer had not been scheduled in that time (a loaded or briefly frozen machine) the reason was lost even though stderr worked. A CI run of the worker-failure test hit this: the child exited with code 1 and an empty stderr.

The exit now gives up only when a write has been stuck or failing for 200 ms, which still bounds it when stderr is blocked or broken, or at once when the writer thread has ended, so a writer that panicked cannot hang the exit. A writer that has not run yet is waited for; the queue is already closed then, so the wait ends. The test-only wait that the recording cleanup test used to work around the same problem is removed, and the worker-failure test now prints the child's stderr when it fails.

A new test keeps the writer away from the queue for twice the deadline while stderr works; it fails without the fix, and so does the old deadline measured from the start of the exit. Another closes with no deadline after the writer panicked; it hangs without the ended check. With the worker-failure test's child frozen repeatedly (250 ms stops, 0.2 ms runs), the reason was missing in 7 of 200 runs before and in none of 200 after. CPU contention alone did not reproduce it locally. fmt, Clippy with -D warnings on Rust 1.100.0 and 1.85.0, the full test suite and scripts/check.sh pass on Linux.

author: blessings2008
body:
## Summary
- Require a server-side runtime-role inspector and an explicit tenant-table list whenever the API is configured with a school-membership resolver.
- Snapshot the inspector method, receiver and required-table list when the app is constructed so later dependency mutation cannot replace or narrow the startup check.
- Run the provider-neutral role-safety contract in Fastify's `onReady` lifecycle before the app accepts requests.
- Fail app construction when the safety dependency is missing or malformed, and fail readiness when the inspected role is privileged or the required tenant-table checks do not pass.
- Add regression coverage for missing inspection dependencies, privileged runtime roles and dependency mutation; update the implementation status and roadmap without marking pending live-runtime work complete.

## Dependency and scope
- This PR is stacked on [PR #37](https://github.com/blessings2008/Edumanager/pull/37), which adds the PostgreSQL 17 catalog inspector and disposable PostgreSQL CI integration test.
- It targets `test/postgres-runtime-role-inspector-integration`, not `main`, to preserve the existing stack.
- The startup gate is provider-neutral. It does not create a pool, read credentials, choose a new database provider, provision roles, add migrations, or enable tenant-owned data routes.
- The server entry point still does not configure a membership resolver, inspector or runtime pool. A live runtime role has not been inspected; RLS policy correctness, effective grants and cross-school row isolation remain pending.

## Validation
- GitHub Actions PR run [#44911042293](https://github.com/blessings2008/Edumanager/actions/runs/44911042293) — **passed**.
- `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` — passed.

body:
## Payment cards (Admin → Sozlamalar)

- **2 card slots by default**, or as many as are already saved.
- **"+ Karta qo'shish"** adds one slot at a time, up to `MAX_PAYMENT_CARDS` (4). The server action uses the same constant. The new slot's number field gets focus.
- Each slot has a "1-karta / 2-karta" heading and an **×** button to remove it. Field names (`number0…`) are renumbered automatically.
- After saving, the fields are rebuilt from the saved list.

## "Avto-tasdiqlashni sinash"

The admin wanted to check that automatic TOP activation works. The Telegram bot isn't connected, and an SMS can't be sent to the server from a phone. So there is now a test box in the "Avtomatik to'lov tasdiqlash" card:

- The admin types text that looks like a bank SMS.
- It goes through the **same** `parseAmounts` + `matchIncoming` used by the SMS forwarder and Telegram paths (source `test`).
- If the amount exactly matches a pending payment, the payment is approved and TOP turns on. The admin sees "✅ Avto-tasdiqlandi: <editor> — <amount> so'm".
- If nothing matches, the admin sees which amounts were found in the text.
- Safety:
  - A test amount with no pending payment is **not** stored as "money that arrived early", so a typo can't approve a future payment.
  - Admin only, and no more power than "Pul tushdi — tasdiqlash". It shows up in the history as `avto:test`.

## Testing (production build, local Postgres)

- Cards: 2 slots → add → 3 (focus moves to the new number field) → 4 (button hides) → removed two → saved and reloaded: the right 2 cards come back with the right types.
- Auto TOP:
  - An editor pressed "TOP ga chiqish" → pending payment of 50 181.
  - The admin entered "+50 001" → "Mos kutilayotgan to'lov yo'q", and nothing was stored.
  - The admin entered "+50 181.00 UZS" (with a balance line) → "✅ Avto-tasdiqlandi".
  - In the database: status `APPROVED`, the editor's TOP is on, and the history shows `avto:test`.

author: rasmussoot
body:
**What broke.** #3622 switched the anthropic rail to `latch_scope: model` (a Fable 429 cools only the Fable cell). The rail-wide latch that this morning's Fable weekly-limit 429 (05:08Z, coordinator intake) had written under the old account scope was persisted in `capacity_marks`, and `_reload` restored it on the rollout's restart (`reloaded 2 marks (1 cooled, 1 latched)`). Every platform reviewer admission then deferred `rail-latched` until 21:59:59Z (Fable's weekly reset) — #3624/#3625 sat unreviewed — although the account's 7d window was at 0.84 and opus (the reviewer heavy tier's first model) had room.

**Fix.** `Capacity._reload` keeps a `latched` mark only when the rail's current policy still latches — `latch_429_hold_s` set AND `latch_scope: account`, `observe()`'s own predicate. Cooled cells reload unchanged (the Fable cell stays cooled correctly).

**Spec/test.** New row in `sessions.md` §Kept across a restart ("a latch written under account scope does not reload once the rail declares model scope"); the test's roll can now start the second gateway on a policy with one `latch_scope` changed. Positive control: the row FAILS with the old `capacity.py`. `devbox run ci` (gateway) green.

Spec changes:
- `sessions.md` §Kept across a restart — new row "a latch written under account scope does not reload once the rail declares model scope" (dispatch on anthropic after the roll).
- `sessions.md` §Kept across a restart — new row "a latch does not reload once the rail drops its latch hold" (red against a scope-only guard).
- `sessions.md` §Kept across a restart — ⚖ clause added to "What a reload drops": a latch on a rail that no longer latches (no `latch_429_hold_s`, or a scope other than account) is dropped. Judgment: a model-scope rail never sets a latch (`observe()`), so a latch written under the old scope is exactly what the in-memory logic would not hold — the existing ⚖ principle applied to a scope change.
- `sessions.md` §Kept across a restart legend — `roll` may carry a policy change (`the policy now declares <rail> <admission key>: <value>`, `none` = removed).

**Live state.** Already un-wedged by hand in a maintenance window (stale row deleted, gateway restarted 13:44Z → `0 latched`); this PR stops the next scope change from repeating it.

Opened from a second jail — loose ends for the primary seat (no FU filed here): the gateway logs `catalog: docs parse failed (no Endpoints table (Model | Model ID))` at startup (Go docs read, keeps the last good snapshot); `reviewer-session.sh` header still says reviewers default to sonnet, while the gateway path serves opus.

author: cbirkbeck
body:
Adds the roadmap folder `TauCetiRoadmap/RiemannHypothesisForDirichletLFunctions/RieszSumsOverPrimesAndExceptionalZeros` (README, `Suggested.lean`), a sub-roadmap of the family `RiemannHypothesisForDirichletLFunctions`, whose end theorem is the Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions. The family follows the formal Lean proof of these theorems by Levent Alpöge (announced 20 November 2026); each sub-roadmap states as targets what that proof establishes, in the generality in which the statement holds, and says so where a route is not written out.

The distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions, and of prime ideals in ray classes, is governed by the zeros of Dirichlet and Hecke `L`-functions near the point `1`. This roadmap states the classical theorems of that subject in their published form, in which the possible exceptional real zero of a real character is kept as an explicit term rather than excluded: the logarithmic derivative `L′/L` near the line one, smoothed prime sums controlled by a box free of zeros, the prime number theorem for a character with its exceptional term, the Riesz remainder of a character, the Deuring–Heilbronn repulsion and Linnik's theorem, and prime ideals of a ray class in short intervals, uniformly in the field and the modulus. Where it uses the uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros of AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI (§0.34), it also states the exception-free forms: the Riesz remainder bound without its exceptional term (1.4i (c)) and the prime number theorem in progressions in Linnik's range without it (1.7b (iv)). Throughout, `χ` is a Dirichlet character, `L(s, χ)` its `L`-function and `Λ` the von Mangoldt function.

Where the formal proof establishes a weaker form of a statement, the README records that form beside the general statement under the heading *The form of the formal proof.*, with the label primed: 1.4e (a′), 1.4f (a′), 1.4h (b′)–(c′), 1.4i (b′) and (c′), 1.7a (b′) and 2.9b (iv) (c′). The general statement beside it is published or this roadmap's and implies it; a line *Status.* marks a statement that is this roadmap's own and not a statement of the formal proof. One form of the formal proof has no label: in the Convention of 1.7b, the gap `1 − β₁ ≥ c/(q² log q)`, which gives the lower bound for `π(x;a,q)` in 1.7b (iii) with `q³` in place of `q^(7/4)`; the gap `c_ε q^(−1/2−ε)` of AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §0.12 beside it implies it.

The published results of 1.7b carry locators into their sources: the repulsion into Linnik's second paper (§3, p. 348), Bombieri's *Le grand crible* (Théorème 16, p. 41) and Gallagher's 1970 paper ((27), p. 336); the prime number theorem in Linnik's range into Gallagher's Theorem 7 (p. 337), of which 1.7b (ii) is a single-modulus form with relative error; and Linnik's theorem into Linnik's first paper ((2), p. 139) and Bombieri (Théorème 13, p. 39). The README calls effective only the constant of the repulsion 1.7b (i), which follows from Bombieri's Théorème 16 and through it from his Théorème 14 (p. 40), whose constants he states to be effectively computable, and the gaps of 2.9b (iv), through AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §0.12 and Stark's threshold. The constants of 0.30b, of 1.4g (b), of 1.7b (ii)–(iv) and of the counts of 2.9b are only claimed to exist; the routes of the last three rest on zero-free regions whose constants are existential: ZerosOfLFunctions 6.3–6.4, and for 2.9b also the threshold of AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §2.43. `Suggested.lean` claims none of its constants to be effective and refers to the README for those that are.

The family index (`TauCetiRoadmap/RiemannHypothesisForDirichletLFunctions/README.md`, `Suggested.lean`, `metadata.toml`) lists the sub-roadmaps in merge order and is carried by every pull request of the family, so these pull requests conflict on it: the first of them to merge brings its copy to main, and each later one is rebased onto the index on main before it merges.

`Suggested.lean` states seven theorems with `sorry` proofs against the pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti. Three are the headlines: the exception-free prime number theorem for the Riesz remainder (`norm_rieszRemainder_le`, 1.4i (c)), Linnik's theorem (`exists_prime_modEq_le`, 1.7b (iii)) and the count of primes that are norms from an imaginary quadratic field in short intervals (`card_primes_norm_one_mod_shortInterval_ge`, 2.9b (iv) (c)). Beside them stand the forms of the formal proof 1.4i (c′) (`norm_rieszRemainder_le_of_no_real_zero`) and 2.9b (iv) (c′) (`card_primes_norm_one_mod_shortInterval_ge_of_discr_eq_neg_prime`), and the two statements of the formal proof on which Linnik's theorem rests: the Deuring–Heilbronn repulsion 1.7b (i) (`deuring_heilbronn_repulsion`) and Gallagher's prime number theorem in Linnik's range 1.7b (ii) (`gallagher_primeCount_linnik_range`). As stated in Lean, 1.4i (c′) follows from 1.4i (c) by discarding its zero-free hypothesis; its docstring says that the target is its proof by the route of 1.4i (c′), from 1.4i (a) without AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §0.34. The character prime number theorem with the exceptional term (1.4g (b)) is statable, but it is a corollary of AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §§0.18 and 0.34, so it stays a README target on the routes; the README's scope section records both directions of that comparison.

Dependencies. The README cites roadmaps by name and section; the Lean imports none of them. On main it draws on AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI, AnalyticNumberTheoryPartIII (Landau's local logarithmic-derivative lemma, 8.3, in the route of 0.30b), ZerosOfLFunctions, ClassFieldTheory, GlobalNumberFields, ArithmeticDirichletSeries, EffectiveBounds and ExplicitPrimeCounting (§§0.2, 0.7 and 4.2, for the integral representations of the Riesz remainders in 1.4i). Two suppliers are still in open pull requests and merge first: RiemannHypothesisStatementsAndConsequences, a sub-roadmap of the family (the Riesz sums of an `L`-series and the predicates of the Riemann hypotheses), and QuasiRiemannHypothesis (§5.3 in the route of 1.4e, §3.2 in 2.9b (ii), and §10.7 in the remarks of 1.4e and 1.4i).

AI assistance: written with Claude Code (Claude Opus and Claude Fable agents: reading of the formal proof, drafting, referee passes and repairs), with independent audits by a second model family.

Replaces pmnmalo/Silinx#5085, rebased on main after #5090 and #5087 merged; the force push to the old branch was refused.

Part of #4749, step 4 of the design in pmnmalo/Silinx#5068: the MCP.

**What changes**
- **Messages in the results.** `check_syntax`, `simulate` and `run_process` return `messages`, and so does `follow_project`'s `ownerActivity.runs`. They sit beside the fields these tools already return, which are unchanged. Each message is `{ text, severity, source, tool, location, action, process, run }`: `core/message.js`'s `messageData`, with the action given by its label and the text in English.
  - **check_syntax:** each diagnostic's line (source `check`, process `Check Syntax` / `Check Design`, location with its column), then the result's line (`ok` or `error`).
  - **simulate:** the notes about the model, the elaboration's warnings, and the design's messages with their file and line (note → info, error / failure → error, print → text). Then where the run stopped (`error` when the design failed) and the limit's warning. Source `sim`, process `Simulate Behavioral Model` (or the model's `Simulate Post-… Model`), as the interface's run names it.

author: daanvervacke
body:
## Changes

### Bug Fixes

- fix: wait for a pending token delivery on close. `TokenLifecycle` gains `aclose()`, which awaits an in-flight token-delivery task, and `EngieBeClient.close` calls it, so a queued `on_token_refresh` pair can no longer fire after the close or vanish with the event loop. The wait is guarded: a callback closing the client from inside its own delivery returns instead of waiting on itself, and a delivery cancelled by someone else does not push its cancel onto the closer.

## Why

The delivery of rotated pairs runs in its own task. Until now a close neither cancelled nor awaited it: a slow consumer callback could fire after the close returned, or the task could disappear with the event loop and the new token pair with it, leaving saved storage on the previous pair and the next refresh broken.

## Evidence

- Full gate green: ruff, mypy, bruno drift, 98 percent branch coverage, build and uv audit. Sphinx docs build green.
- New tests pin the close semantics through callback effects: a stalled delivery holds close until delivered, a delivery cancelled underneath a waiting close lets close finish and the session close, and a callback calling close completes without deadlock and leaves the client closed. The existing delivery tests keep passing unchanged.
- Live smoke on the author's account: an authenticated getter and the client close run clean, F3 changes no parse or wire behavior.

- [x] `uv run python -m scripts.check` passes completely.
- [x] The PR carries one of these labels: `breaking-change`, `new-feature`, `enhancement`, `bugfix`, `maintenance`, `documentation`, `dependencies`.
- [x] Every commit subject follows conventional commits. git-cliff generates `CHANGELOG.md` from them, so do not edit it by hand.

author: makisuo
body: ## Why The Mac app draws with WKWebView, which paces the page at 60 fps on 120 Hz ProMotion displays, so it felt laggy next to the native app. Tauri's experimental CEF runtime draws it with Chromium instead, at the display's rate. ## What - **Tauri 2 → 3.0.0-alpha.6.** Every plugin moves to its 3.x alpha, and the CLI is `@tauri-apps/cli-cef` 3.0.0-alpha.27. - **macOS runs on CEF** (`tauri-runtime-cef` 3.0.0-alpha.7). Windows and Linux keep the system webview through `tauri-runtime-wry`. The runtime is a per-target dependency, which is how tauri-build and the CLI pick it for each platform. - **`main` is CEF's entry point**, because Chromium runs the same executable as its helper processes. - **Chrome background services are disabled:** the optimization guide (hint fetches, model downloads, and the on-device model service, which the logs show starting a few minutes in) and the media router (Cast discovery on the local network). - **A debug build** started with `HAZEL_DEVTOOLS_PORT` serves the DevTools protocol, for profiling. Release builds never do. - **Release workflow:** cmake and ninja on the Mac runners, the CEF distribution cached between runs, GTK 4 headers on Ubuntu (Tauri 3 links gtk4), and a `build_only` dispatch input that builds every platform without creating a release. - **Desktop version 1.3.0.** ## Measured (debug build, M-series ProMotion Mac, signed in on the MapleDev org) - `requestAnimationFrame`: 8.3 ms median frame (120 Hz). WKWebView is capped at 60. - Scrolling #general for 300 frames: 8.3 ms median, 9.2 ms p95, 1 frame over 16.7 ms, and no long animation frames. - Load: first contentful paint at 220 ms, a 60 MB JS heap, 1.4k DOM nodes. - Sign-in still works. The keychain commands pass the ACL and an unknown command is refused (Tauri 3 no longer writes `permissions/autogenerated`; the ACL is built in). ## Tradeoffs - Tauri 3 and the CEF runtime are alphas. - The Mac app grows to about 390 MB (debug build). Its update download is about 166 MB instead of a few MB. - Chromium's helper processes are named "app Helper", after the binary. Renaming the binary would break the updater's relaunch from 1.2.0, so it stays for now. - The app's origin on Mac becomes `http://tauri.localhost` (the API already allows it; Windows uses it too). ## Verification - `cargo check` passes on macOS. The Mac app was built and run locally (above). - Windows and Linux can't be checked here, because `ring` needs a cross C compiler. A `build_only` run of the release workflow on this branch builds all four targets: https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/hazel/actions/runs/44910798206 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Shared links created from the desktop app now use the Hazel web app address instead of a local app address. This helps ensure links open from the expected web location, while links shared from regular web pages continue to use that page’s own address.

author: foamrider
body:
**Foamy Lock 1.5.0 for Omarchy 4.5.** Lock Studio can copy the lock screen's look to the SDDM login screen, and remove it again.

**What it does.** Lock Studio gets a **Login screen** page (Library → Scene), shown when SDDM is the display manager. **Copy to login screen** copies the applied look — preset, layout, glass, background, theme colours, language, time format, the background picture (capped at 3840 × 2160) and the profile picture — after a dialog and Omarchy's password prompt. Media, weather, status, the system panel, fingerprint sign-in and video backgrounds stay off the login screen. **Remove from login screen** undoes it. The README's new "Login screen (SDDM)" section has the details.

**How.**
- `sddm/`: an SDDM theme built from the lock's own element files. The lock's layout moved into `elements/LockLayout.qml`, shared by the lock and the login screen; the lock draws exactly as before (pixel comparison of all presets).
- The helper's new `studio login-screen status` and `stage`: whether SDDM is in use and which theme it selects (read as SDDM 0.21 reads its config, including Qt's locale-aware file order and `ThemeDir`), and a staging folder with the filtered look, the pictures and a manifest. The helper is rebuilt for x86-64 and AArch64.
- `sddm/foamy-lock-login-screen`: the publisher, run through `pkexec` with its own deadline. As root it reads the staging folder with the user's rights, checks every file against the manifest, replaces the theme in one step (`mv --exchange`), writes `/etc/sddm.conf.d/99-zz-foamy-lock.conf`, and changes or removes only what it can prove it installed. A failure puts the previous state back, or says plainly what it couldn't.

**Tested.**
- `tests/validate.sh` passed on the branch up to the last fix round; the final round's own branch passed it in full. The final merge's validation and the last two Codex review rounds were skipped at the owner's request.
- Publisher: 25 cases, including signals at every rename, failed rollbacks and foreign files. Studio harness: every state and result in English and Norwegian.
- Live: the greeter theme in SDDM's test mode here and on a second Omarchy PC; a real login (wrong, then right password) on that PC's real login screen; and Copy to login screen from Lock Studio through the real polkit prompt there.

**Known limits.** In the README: `/etc/sddm.conf` overrides every drop-in; a copy stopped hard can leave hidden folders that SDDM ignores.

author: salahmyn
body:
## Summary

On a real project, `lattice slice` joined `kid-insight.claude.createAnthropicClient` to `media-upload.handler.actionsFor.create`, which lives in a different edge function that kid-insight never imports. The call was `client.messages.create(…)` on an SDK object. It resolved **by name** to the only `create` in the language, read `resolved (unique)`, and made an enforcer look reached when it was not.

- **The rule (`loadedWith`, reachability:INV-9).** For TypeScript, JavaScript and Python, a member-call candidate is visible only when its module is **co-loaded** with the caller's: some module transitively imports both. Self counts.
  - Dependency injection keeps its edge: `index.ts` imports both `handler.ts` and the store it passes in.
  - Code under `_shared` that both functions import stays visible.
  - A test's imports co-load modules only for test callers.
- **What a filtered call reads.** No candidate left: `external`. One: `resolved`. Several: `ambiguous`.
- **Cost.** Ancestor sets are memoised bitsets, computed once per build. A 3,000-module synthetic repository builds in about 1.7 s.
- **Go and PHP are unchanged.** Go keeps its package rule. PHP records no imports.

The user guide's member-call section is updated. Four existing fixtures relied on the old by-name guess, so each now gets a module that imports both sides, which models real wiring. No assertion was weakened.

## Validation

- **Fail before the fix, pass after**, shown by short-circuiting `loadedWith`:
  - `TestMemberCallIgnoresAModuleNeverLoadedWithTheCaller` (0 cross-function call edges);
  - `TestTestImportingBothDoesNotJoinProductionCode`;
  - `TestMemberCallCoLoadedPython`;
  - `TestSliceFindsNoPathBetweenEdgeFunctions`.
- **Edges that must stay** (covered by tests): dependency injection, shared code, and two co-loaded candidates, which stay ambiguous.
- **This repository.** Validate is identical before and after (0 errors, 7 warnings), and so are the `SYMBOL_UNREACHED` findings. The repository is mostly Go.
- **Full chain.** Passes with master merged.

author: induwaraihalavithana
body:
Phase 1 of the ConferenceHub v3 rewrite: the backend foundation every later phase builds on. Backend only; the web app is unchanged.

## What's in it

- **Layered structure**, enforced in CI by import-linter: `api → services → repositories → db → models → core`. The API layer never imports the database layer; services, repositories, models and core never import FastAPI, Starlette or Strawberry.
- **MongoDB models** (Beanie): organizers, admins, auth sessions, password resets, notifications (TTL 180 days), activity log (TTL 1 year), feedback, contact messages. The full conference aggregate and registrations come with Phases 2 and 3.
- **Auth over GraphQL**: `register`, `verifyEmail`, `resendCode`, `login`, `adminLogin`, `refresh`, `logout`, `forgotPassword`, `resetPassword`, `changePassword`, and `me`.
  - 6-digit email codes, stored only as an HMAC: 15 minutes, 5 tries, resend once a minute (v2's rules).
  - 15-minute access and 30-day refresh tokens (PyJWT) in **httpOnly, SameSite=Lax** cookies. Refresh tokens **rotate on every use**, and presenting an old one revokes the session.
  - **Argon2id** (pwdlib). v2's PBKDF2 hashes are verified once and upgraded at the next sign-in.
  - Changing or resetting a password signs out other devices; suspended organizers are signed out at once.
  - "Resend code" and "forgot password" give the same answer whether or not an email is registered. Wrong email and wrong password look the same.
- **Errors as data**: every mutation returns a union of its result and `UserError`, with stable codes such as `CODE_INVALID` and `RATE_LIMITED` for the web app to translate.
- **Protection**: CSRF double-submit header on every mutation, Redis rate limits per IP, and GraphQL depth, token and alias limits. Introspection, GraphiQL and `/docs` are off in production. Start-up refuses a weak `SECRET_KEY`, and refuses insecure cookies in production.
- **Admin** created on first start from `ADMIN_EMAIL` / `ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD`. The password is environment-only and never logged or generated.
- **Observability**: structlog with a request ID on every log line and response header, plus optional Sentry with no personal data.
- **Security docs**: `docs/security-checklist.md` maps every OWASP Top 10 item to this app.
- **CI**: Redis service, `lint-imports`, `pip-audit` and `npm audit --omit=dev`. Dependabot opens weekly update PRs against `v3`.
- **README**: architecture diagram (Mermaid) and an auth summary in `api/README.md`.

## Checks

- ruff, ruff format, strict mypy and import-linter (3 contracts kept) are clean; both dependency audits are clean.
- **38 pytest tests** against real MongoDB and Redis:
  - sign-up and email codes: verification, lock-out after 5 wrong codes, the same answer for unknown emails;
  - sign-in and sessions: login rules, refresh rotation and reuse detection, httpOnly cookie flags;
  - passwords and accounts: reset and change sign out other devices, suspension, the v2 hash upgrade, the admin seed;
  - protections: CSRF refusal, rate limiting, query limits.
- Chrome, against the local API:
  - An organizer signed up, a wrong code was rejected and the right one accepted, then refresh, logout and login worked.
  - Page scripts could see only `cm_csrf`, never the session cookies. A mutation without the CSRF header was refused.
  - The real admin account signed in with its `.env` password, which was never printed.

## Not in this PR

- Real email sending: SMTP comes with the ARQ worker in Phase 3; until then, codes are written to the API log.
- The test that every error code has an EN/SI/TA translation: Phase 4, with the web app's translations.

Closes #8, closes #9, closes #10, closes #11, closes #12, closes #13, closes #14, closes #15.

author: fas89
body:
## Summary

Two small fixes that follow the temp-file write in Agenticstiger/forge-cli-sdk#23. Both are in code that has not been released.

1. **A planned setuid or setgid bit was lost.** The reference `apply()` sets the planned mode with `os.fchmod` on the open descriptor. A payload that fits the write buffer (a file system block, typically 4 KiB, and 128 KiB from Python 3.14, so most generated files) was still in that buffer, and reached the kernel when the file closed, after `fchmod`. A write by an unprivileged process makes the kernel drop the setuid and setgid bits, so a planned `0o4755` landed as `0o755`. Before #23 the mode was set after the bytes. The bytes are now flushed before the mode is set.
2. **The planted-symlink conformance check failed a correct plugin.** The check plants its links in `output_root` before it calls `apply()`, so they are files in the directory. A plugin that refuses to write into a directory that already holds files raised from `apply()`, and the check reported that as its own failure. A clean refusal now passes. A write through a link still fails, whether or not `apply()` goes on to raise.

## Reproduction (on `main`)

```
setuid file:     planned=0o4755  landed=0o755            # applied=1 failed=0
refusing plugin: the planted-symlink check fails with PluginError: output directory is not empty
```

On this branch the same two runs give `landed=0o4755`, and the check passes for the refusing plugin. (The first is `CustomScaffold(...).apply([write_file_action(path="tool", content=b"#!/bin/sh\n", mode=0o4755)])`; the second is a plugin whose `apply()` raises `PluginError` when `output_root` is not empty, run through `CustomScaffoldTestHarness`.)

## The change

- `_write_atomically` in `src/fluid_sdk/roles/custom_scaffold.py`: one `handle.flush()` before `os.fchmod`. Nothing else in the write changes: the temp file, the descriptor-based mode, the Windows fallback (the file is closed, so already flushed, before the path-based `chmod`), `os.replace`.
- `test_apply_does_not_write_through_planted_symlinks` in `src/fluid_sdk/testing/role_harnesses.py`: the call to `apply()` is wrapped in `contextlib.suppress(Exception)`, and the check on the victim files runs after it as before. `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` still propagate.
- Tests in `tests/unit/test_custom_scaffold_atomic_write.py`: the three special modes (setuid, setgid, both) survive a write, skipping where the user or file system cannot set the bit; a refusing plugin passes the check; a plugin that writes through a link and then refuses is still flagged.
- CHANGELOG: a Fixed entry for the mode, and the conformance-check entry says a clean refusal passes.

## What this is, what it isn't

- ✅ Restores the exact planned mode for a payload that fits the buffer, including the setuid and setgid bits.
- ✅ A plugin that correctly refuses a non-empty output directory passes the symlink check; one that writes through a planted link still fails it.
- ❌ No policy about which modes a plan may ask for: the exact planned mode was always applied.
- ❌ `suppress(Exception)` makes this one check silent about a plugin whose `apply()` raises for another reason. The rest of the harness still fails such a plugin (the write and idempotency checks), which a test run with an `apply()` that always raises confirms.
- ❌ No version bump or release.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/`: 217 passed, 1 skipped on Python 3.12 (the skip needs the host CLI installed); 216 passed, 2 skipped on 3.9, 3.10, 3.13 and 3.14 in clean virtualenvs (the second skip needs the SDK installed as a distribution). The example plugins' tests pass (31, 27 and 22).
- [x] `ruff check src/ tests/` and `black --check src/ tests/`: clean. The terminology guardrail passes (self-test, then the scan). `python -m build` and `twine check dist/*`: passed.
- [x] Mutation checks, each reverted afterwards: without the flush the three mode tests fail; without the `suppress`, both refusing-plugin cases fail; with `suppress` but no check on the victims after a refusal, the write-then-refuse test fails.
- [x] Each commit passes on its own.

## Security considerations

`apply()` writes files named by a plan into a directory whose contents may not be trusted. This change restores behaviour; it does not widen it.

- The planned mode, setuid and setgid bits included, was applied exactly before #23 (the mode was set after the bytes). It is the same mode again, so a plan can ask for nothing it could not ask for before. A setuid bit on a file the caller owns grants the caller nothing new, and as root the kernel keeps the bits on write either way.
- The temp file is still created with `mkstemp` (`O_CREAT | O_EXCL`, random name) and the mode is still set on the descriptor: a planted link is never opened and no path-based `chmod` can follow a swapped link. The flush adds no new step on a name.
- The harness change only affects what counts as a failure of the check; it never plants or follows anything new, and the victims are still asserted untouched.

## Breaking changes

None. A conformance check that failed a correct plugin now passes it; a plugin that writes through a planted link fails it as before.

## Borrow

Bug fix inside existing code: the design (temp file, `fchmod` on the descriptor, `os.replace`) is the previous change's, so there was no component to build.

Checked locally: the code before #23 (`write_bytes`, then `chmod`) set the mode after the bytes, which is why the bits survived. CPython's buffered writer, measured: a payload up to the buffer size stays in the buffer until close and a larger one is written through at once (the buffer is the file system's block size, 4 KiB here, and 128 KiB from Python 3.14), so the test uses a small payload, which is buffered on every version. Without the flush the new test fails on macOS, which is where the clearing was reproduced.

Searched and read: `atomicwrites` 1.4.1 (MIT, no longer maintained), the same pattern: a temp file from `mkstemp` in the target's directory, the descriptor synced before the rename (read in the Debian copy of its source; where it sets a mode was not found, so that part is unverified). For the kernel side, the 2015 Linux kernel mailing-list thread on clearing file privilege bits (`file_remove_privs`) describes setuid and setgid being cleared when a file is written; not re-read in the current kernel tree, so the Linux behaviour is from that thread and from the macOS reproduction.

Reuse strategy: adapt the pattern; the SDK is standard-library only, so no dependency. No `fsync`, as before; that is a separate question.

## Security notes

No blocking finding. The flush covers every path: nothing is pending at close, nothing rewrites the mode afterwards, and the Windows fallback is unaffected. The skip logic holds for a setgid parent directory and a group the user is not in, and the check is not vacuous for a plugin whose `apply()` always raises. A large-payload test case was dropped because a buffered writer writes a large payload straight through, so it never exercised the flush; the test comment says why.

author: hestia-lanes-agent[bot]
body:
Closes #35

This makes the judge's re-read of single-reader rows impossible to truncate, and withholds `pass` when it did not complete. This is option 5 from the #33 ruling. It follows the research comment on #35, including its widened trigger: "any re-read candidate has no verdict".

## What changed

- **Batching** (`src/judge.mjs`). `reread()` sends single-reader rows in batches of `rereadBatchSize(maxTokens)` = `floor(maxTokens / 300)` rows, one call per batch. That is 13 rows at the default 4096 cap. The size comes from the cap rather than being hard-coded, because the research could not tell why 22-34 rows overflowed 4096 tokens. A failed batch goes to `onBatchError`, and the later batches are still sent. A reply id from outside its own batch is ignored.
- **Spend check per call** (`src/run.mjs`). Before each re-read batch, the run compares the spend so far (`actual(ledger)`) plus that call's upper bound (`estimate`) with `--max-usd`. If it would go over, the re-read stops, and the remaining rows are recorded as `not re-read: --max-usd … would be exceeded`.
- **Pre-run estimate.** The estimate now prices several re-read batches instead of one call: one row per request plus two per tool (routing, teach-back, and one confusion row per tool). Confusion rows have no hard bound, so the per-call check above is what keeps the cap. I tried a larger bound (one confusion row per tool per reader). It pushed existing fixtures over their `--max-usd`, which means real runs would be refused at start.
- **Withhold** (`src/grade.mjs`). `decide()` takes `rereadGaps` (row id → cause). When a configured judge leaves any single-reader row without a verdict, `withheldPass` gets `re-read incomplete: N of M single-reader rows unverified (<count>: <cause>; …)`. The causes are a failed batch, a reply that dropped the row's id, or the spend stop. Each row's `reread` label names its own cause.
- **README**: the How it grades and Verdict sections, plus a note in the Cost section about how the re-read is priced.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A judge reply truncated at the output cap (teach-back succeeds, only the re-read is cut off) withholds `pass`, and `withheldPass` reports the number of unverified rows. Test: `test/reread.test.mjs` "a re-read cut off at the output cap…" (also checks `verdict.json` and `verdict.md`). This closes the gap the research comment found: the existing `judge-failure` test also broke teach-back.
- [x] With 68 single-reader rows (more than one reply holds), the rows are re-read across `ceil(68/13)` calls, each row is sent once, and every row gets a verdict. Test: "large payload: 68 single-reader rows…", plus a control showing the same 68 rows in one reply are cut off.
- [x] When the remaining `--max-usd` cannot cover the re-read, no re-read call is made, actual spend stays ≤ `--max-usd`, and `pass` is withheld. Test: "when the remaining --max-usd cannot cover the re-read…".
- [x] The docs list the incomplete re-read condition.

Extra coverage: a reply that drops ids, a failed middle batch that does not stop later batches, `beforeBatch`/`onStop`, an out-of-batch id ignored, the estimate staying ≥ actual on the batched run, and no judge (no new reason).

**Controls run:** I disabled the new withhold block, set the batch size to infinite, and disabled the spend check, one at a time. Each made its matching test fail (3, 1 and 1 failures).

## Not in this PR

There is no CHANGELOG entry, for the same reason as #36: `test/release.test.mjs` pins the CHANGELOG's first section to the tagged 0.1.0. The release PR should add entries for #34 and #35.

`npm test`: 168/168 pass locally. public-safe-lint is clean.

author: mluttikh
body:
Phase 3 item 2 of the design review: layout. Strip templates and their placement are left for a later PR.

## What's new

- **`direction=`**: how a wrap fills its cells.
  - `"h"` (rows, the default) or `"v"` (down the columns).
  - Two letters give any start corner and direction, e.g. `"lb"` fills rows from the bottom left, as lattice does.
  - A paged wrap fills each page the same way.
  - Available as a Fill setting and as `t.direction`.
- **`layout=`**: places a wrap's panels by hand, as R's geofacet does.
  - Give a table of the wrap column(s), `row` and `col` (counted from 1), or a dict `{level: (row, col)}`.
  - Cells without a panel stay empty, so a map's shape keeps.
  - The table may be a DuckDB query.
  - Errors on a panel with no place, two panels in one cell, or use with `cols=`, `direction=` or `rows=`.
  - With `page=`, every page has the same cells.
- **`space="free_x"|"free_y"|"free"`**: sizes panels by their range, as ggplot2's `space=` does.
  - Each column is as wide as its x range, each row as high as its y range, so a category or a unit has the same size in every panel.
  - Needs free scales along those lines; in a wrap, one row (or one column) of panels.
  - The settings panel offers only the shares that work with it.
  - Same layout in `layout.ts` and in `figure.py`.
- **`repeat=[...]`**: stacks columns as rows of panels.
  - The data is melted into `measure` and `value` with narwhals `unpivot`; from a database the melt is part of the query, so `load="pages"` works.
  - Rows keep the order given, each has its own y scale (`share_y="row"`), and strips name the columns by their labels.
  - `col=` and `page=` still facet.

## Checks

- `tests/test_layout.py`: 22 tests, in memory and from DuckDB.
- A vitest for `place`.
- `js/test/layout.mjs` (added to CI and the local runner): placement, empty cells, band widths, row heights and paged direction, in both renderers.
  - It also compares the browser's panel boxes with `figure.py`'s: same order and rows, heights within 3 px, width ratios within 2%.
  - Gutters aren't compared: the browser measures text and Python estimates it, which differs by a few pixels on main too.
- Results: ty, ruff, pytest (992), vitest (100), the docs build with gallery, and the browser suite (789 ok, 0 failed) all pass.

## Docs

- New sections in the layout guide.
- Cheat sheet entries, README and CHANGELOG.
- Three gallery cards: a map-shaped grid, columns stacked as rows, panels as wide as their categories.
- Decision record `docs/decisions/0012-layout-direction-tables-space-repeat.md`.

author: yqtian-se
body:
cannotInsertTailCall scans the candidate's block for a read of the register
used to expand PseudoTAIL (x6, or x7). MachineInstr::readsRegister counts the
operand of a DBG_VALUE, so a DBG_VALUE $x6 that LiveDebugValues propagates into
a return block makes the outliner emit a call and a return instead of a tail
call, and -g makes code larger at -Oz.

Skip debug instructions in the scan, as the generic outliner liveness helpers

author: nanako0129
body:
## ELI5

When Orca starts or reopens a managed Antigravity chat or bot, it sends the agent a few notes: which tools are off, the workspace rules, and the bot's own standing instructions (who it is, its memory, its tools). A bug let the first notes overwrite the last one, so the bot never got its instructions. Now the notes are combined, so the bot gets all of them.

## What Changed

**Before:** managed Antigravity chats and bots silently lost their standing instructions on every `session/new` and on reopen, even in workspaces with no rules files. In `acp-structured-handshake.ts`, `setup` carried `...acpSessionStartMeta(spec, meta)` and was spread *after* `_meta: sessionMeta`. Managed Antigravity always sets `spec.sessionMeta = { antigravity: { disabledTools: ['run_workflow'] } }`, so `setup._meta` always replaced the standing instructions.

**After:** the agent receives the disabled tools, workspace rules, and standing instructions together.

- `acpSessionStartMeta` (`src/main/acp/launch/acp-session-meta.ts`) takes ordered layers: spec meta, then workspace rules (`resolveSessionMeta`), then Orca standing instructions. Later layers still win key by key, and the `antigravity` key is still merged one level deep. The one special case is `antigravity.systemPrompt.append`: the Antigravity server reads a single append string, so each layer's append is joined in order with a blank line (workspace rules first, then standing instructions). This is a targeted join, not a generic recursive merge.
- `acp-structured-handshake.ts` no longer spreads `_meta` from `setup`. `session/new` and the reopen (`session/resume`/`session/load`) both build `_meta` through the helper. Reopen adds standing instructions only when `sessionMetaOnReopen` is set, as before.
- The single-argument call in `antigravity-sign-in-server.ts` is unchanged in behavior.

## Why

This fixes the dropped instructions at the one shared helper both handshake calls already use, instead of adding a second merge in the handshake. A generic recursive merge (with prototype-key guards) was considered and dropped: every layer is built inside Orca, and only `systemPrompt.append` needs combining, so a narrow join is simpler and easier to reason about. Host `agy` (no spec meta), Grok and Kiro (no `_meta` in `setup`) behave as before.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #46367

## Visual Proof

N/A. This changes the JSON `_meta` payload sent on ACP `session/new` / `session/load`, with no renderer or UI change. The behavior evidence (unit test before/after and a live server check) is under Testing.

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below
- [x] Every added test fails without this change and avoids the [test anti-patterns](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/docs/agents-md-refs/test-antipatterns.md)

- New test in `acp-structured-session-instructions.test.ts` checks the exact `_meta` on `session/new` and `session/load` when spec `disabledTools`, workspace rules and standing instructions are all present. On main it fails (the append is only `Workspace rules.`); on this branch it passes.
- Targeted vitest (macOS): `acp-structured-session-instructions`, `acp-structured-antigravity`, and `src/main/antigravity` pass, except the existing process-spawning tests (`posix-hook-invocation`, `antigravity-browser-helper`) that fail locally for an unrelated environment reason (exit 69 from a local toolchain shim) and also fail on main.
- Static gates clean on the touched files: oxlint, oxfmt, anti-slop oxlint, code-quality native plugins, ast-grep, and the changed-code quality gate.
- Live check on a separate macOS machine against the pinned managed server (agy-acp-server 1.5.2, sha256 matching the pin in `antigravity-acp-runtime.ts`): `session/new` with `disabledTools` plus `rules + "\n\n" + instructions` was accepted, and the model repeated a marker from each part. This drove the server over raw ACP rather than through a full Orca bot session; the reopen path is covered by the unit test.

## Performance

None, because `acpSessionStartMeta` runs once per ACP session open or reopen in the main process (not a hot path), with no new I/O, subprocesses, timers or polling. Node microbenchmark: typical case 0.034 us (main, instructions dropped) vs 0.67 us; no meta 0.013 vs 0.034 us; adversarial 88KB rules + 200KB instructions 27 us mean, 139 us max. Nothing comes near 16 ms.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

- Only `_meta` construction for ACP `session/new`, `session/load` and `session/resume` changes. The visible effect is that managed Antigravity system prompts now include the standing instructions, so they are longer (more tokens per turn). That is intended: on main those instructions were silently dropped. The workspace-rules part is unchanged (capped near 88KB).
- When two layers both carry `antigravity.systemPrompt`, it is rebuilt as `{ append }` only; no other `systemPrompt` subkeys exist today.
- Back out with a plain revert; no saved data or settings are touched.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable, or this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I explained what changed and why (ELI5, the user-facing before/after, the mechanism, and why over the alternatives)
- [x] I stated the risk: what could break, for whom, and how to back it out
- [x] Before/after screenshots or videos attached for UI changes, or `N/A` with reason
- [x] Self-reviewed for correctness, security, and performance
- [x] Cross-platform, SSH/remote, and path/shortcut impact considered (or N/A)
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass (or CI will cover; local preferred)

Original fix by @Nanako0129 in #46368. Their authorship is preserved on the commit.

author: sebelapetr
body:
## Summary

The trusted contact card no longer depends on the model choosing `insufficient_evidence` for an unknown. The Main draft gains a structured boolean, `unpublished`. Main sets it only when the specific fact the visitor asked for is not answered by the published records. It is not set for a missing date or other detail the visitor did not ask for, for saying the records list nothing more, for correcting a false premise, or for hedging. The deterministic Output Guard then attaches the card when `outcome == "insufficient_evidence" or show_contact or unpublished`. Ordinary evidenced answers keep `unpublished = false` and get no card. Refusals are unaffected, because a refused draft never reaches the guard as a draft.

This fixes the S03-cs repeat-1 shape. That answer used outcome `answered` and said the fact was not published, but it had no card.

## Mechanism

- `guardrails/output.py`: `Draft.unpublished`; `GUARD_VERSION` is now `output-guard-4`.
- `main_agent.py`: `DRAFT_SCHEMA` requires `unpublished`.
- `output_guard.py`: the card rule above, plus an `unpublished` span attribute.
- `prompts/chat.py`: rule 10 and the `- unpublished:` output field.
- `fakes.py`: fake drafts carry `unpublished` (default `false`).
- `AGENTS.md`: Output Guard summary, the #183 note "Contact card for every honest unknown", the subject fingerprints and the test list.

New fingerprints: chat prompt `450396fe118b`, Output Guard `output-guard-4+b761d86edfe7`, runtime `f346f0535286`. Security `e5818a597dbd`, tools `e401a41f1c46` and Main effort `medium` are unchanged.

## Verification

- Test-first:
  - The red commit 15d7d1a had 5 failures before the fix in 94f4b23. They covered the S03-cs repeat-1 shape getting the card, an evidenced answer getting none, unchanged `insufficient_evidence` answers, the schema field and the guard version.
  - The refusal regression test and the rule-10 rewrap landed later, in e955937. The refusal test (a refused draft gets no card from the flag) passed on its first run, so it guards against regressions and was not part of the red commit.
  - After review, red commit a33c7d6 asserts the narrowed field definition in the prompt. It failed until the fix that narrows the flag.
- `packages/llm-agent`: lint, typecheck and 709 tests green. The hard-coded config check and Prettier are green too.
- No paid eval was run.

## Offline impact estimate (no model calls, narrowed definition)

The pool is the last full run: 240 answers, 40 cases × 2 languages × 3 repeats. Stored records hold only the `ChatResult`, not the draft, so I inferred the flag from each answer's text against the narrowed definition. The new runtime fingerprint is different, so the pool is **not regradable**. A fresh full run is required before any threshold claim.

- **Cannot change (101):** 50 refusals, which bypass the guard; 33 `insufficient_evidence` answers that already had the card; 18 answers that already had a card.
- **Likely to gain the card (4):**
  - S03-cs r1, the target: the asked certifications are not published.
  - S18-cs r1–3: the deployment details the visitor explicitly asked for are not published.
  - None of the likely changes is a judged Q* answer.
- **Borderline (14, all judged Q*):**
  - **Q20-cs/en r1–3:** the asked mechanism is answered, but a finer step is said to be unpublished.
  - **Q12-cs r2, r3:** "how much has she read" goes unanswered beyond the status.
  - **Q13-cs/en r1–3:** "did she speak" is answered as "no talk recorded".
- **Possible but unlikely (16), all false-premise corrections that the definition now excludes:** S07-cs/en r1–3, S06-cs/en r1–3, S05-cs r1, r2 and S05-en r1, r3.
- **Expected unchanged under the narrowing:** the incidental negatives the review cited. These are Q07-en r1, r2 ("no other courses", "no start date"), Q12-en r1–3 ("no end date", "no page-by-page progress"), Q09-en r2 ("no end date published"), Q02 (name hedging), S16 and Q19-en r2.
- **Grading risk:**
  - Every affected case has contact expectation `optional`, so the code grader cannot fail them.
  - No case where the card is forbidden can change, because those cases are refusals.
  - The rubric judge sees `contact_card`, so the 14 borderline Q* answers carry the only judged risk.
- **Limit:** the card is enforced deterministically from the flag, but it still depends on Main setting the flag. Only the pending paid full run can confirm that S03-cs is fixed.

## Reviewer notes

- Check that rule 10 makes the flag narrow enough: only an asked-about fact that is not published, not general hedging.
- The paid rerun of the full comparison is still pending. The owner's provider balance is needed for it.

Part of #183

author: baeroe
body:
WEBU-2 (Phase 15, Task 25b): die PHP-Basis des Images geht von `serversideup/php` v5.0.4 auf **v5.1.5**.

## Version

- Alt: `serversideup/php:8.4.27-fpm-nginx-trixie-v5.0.4@sha256:c91d4ff3…5fff56`
- Neu: `serversideup/php:8.4.28-fpm-nginx-trixie-v5.1.5@sha256:c98282869232f27b765324f6b7d58daee3552f63df13dfaa7074c66e58930e6e` (Index mit linux/amd64 und linux/arm64, per `docker buildx imagetools inspect` bestätigt)
- Node, MariaDB, Meilisearch, Gotenberg unverändert.

## Warum v5.1.5 statt v5.1.1 (A414)

v5.1.1 (2026-11-05) ist die einzige v5.1.x, die älter als zwei Wochen ist. v5.1.5 ist vom 2026-11-19. A414 sagt: „Sicherheit vor Wartezeit: Ein Release, das eine bekannte Lücke schließt, geht der Zwei-Wochen-Regel vor, wenn es sonst nichts ändert (Diff geprüft).“ Das trifft hier zu:

- **v5.1.5**: PHP 8.4.28 mit 14 Fixes von php-src, darunter CVE-2026-129289 (FPM Request Smuggling, 9.2), CVE-2026-115560 und CVE-2026-126714 (Session-RCE), CVE-2026-129496 (Timezone-Cache-UAF), CVE-2026-129291 (FPM-epoll-UAF).
- **v5.1.4**: nginx 1.30.7 (9 CVEs).
- **v5.1.3** (GHSA-8wf6-vq49-m6w2): `try_files $uri =404` vor PHP-FPM und `security.limit_extensions = .php`.
- **v5.1.2**: betrifft nur `fpm-apache`.
- Diff `v5.1.1..v5.1.5` unter `src/`: nur `docker-php-serversideup-pool.conf` (`limit_extensions`), `site-opts.d/http(s).conf.template` (`try_files`) und `fpm-apache/Dockerfile`. Dazu habe ich beide Images Datei für Datei und per `dpkg-query` verglichen: sonst nur PHP 8.4.28, nginx 1.30.7 und `zlib1g` aus den trixie-Paketen.
- v5.2.x (neue Funktionen) bleibt draußen. Die Ergänzung zu A414 steht in den Rulings.

## Was sich an der Basis seit v5.0.4 geändert hat

- **v5.0.5**: Rechte nur in `fpm`/`frankenphp`.
- **v5.1.0**: Die Basis kompiliert PHP selbst aus den Dockerfiles von docker-library. Die configure-Optionen sind identisch bis auf `PHP_BUILD_PROVIDER`. Dazu `install-php-extensions` 2.12.6 statt 2.12.0, Signaturen und SBOM sowie Helfer-Skripte.
- **v5.1.1**: nur FrankenPHP.
- `libbrotli1` installiert die Basis seit v5.1.0 nicht mehr selbst. Es kommt aus den trixie-Paketen ihres Build-Tags, im Image weiter **1.1.0-2+deb13u1** (arm64 und amd64). Der Smoke-Kommentar sagt jetzt, dass die Version mit einer neuen Basis wandern kann.

## Verglichen und gleich geblieben (v5.0.4 → v5.1.5)

- `server-opts.d/security.conf`: identisch. Unsere Kopie bleibt die der Basis **ohne HSTS** (Kopfkommentar nennt v5.1.5).
- `performance.conf`, `nginx.conf.template`, `trusted-proxy`: identisch. `site-opts.d` hat nur das neue `try_files` in der PHP-Location.
- `/etc/entrypoint.d` (auch `10-init-webserver-config.sh`), `healthcheck-queue`, `healthcheck-schedule`, `php-fpm-healthcheck`: identisch.
- Debug-Dateien: gleicher Pfad und Eigentümer, das Dockerfile setzt sie weiter auf root 644.
- `php -m` der Basis identisch, ebenso die Härtung in `serversideup-docker-php.ini` und die Umgebung (bis auf `PHP_VERSION`/`PHP_URL`/`PHP_SHA256`).

## `try_files` und `limit_extensions` gegen unser Routing

Kein Konflikt. Laravel geht über `location /` → `/index.php?$query_string`, und `/index.php` existiert. Geprüft:

- `/login` gibt 200, `/index.php` gibt 302 wie vorher, `/nope.php` und `/uploads/x.phar/y.php` geben 404.
- Der Smoke deckt Routen-Cache (Keys, Kennungen, 301 früherer Keys), Uploads, `/app/` (WebSocket), `/mcp`, PDF und Vorschauen ab, alles grün.
- `php-fpm-healthcheck` (FPM-Ping `/healthcheck`) ok.

## Offene Umleitung über `/index.php/` (GHSA-3634-2fr7-xpw4)

- Die Basis (auch v5.1.5) antwortet auf `/index.php/%5Cevil.example` mit `301 Location: /\evil.example`, Browser lesen das als fremden Host. Am nackten Basis-Image nachgestellt. Behoben ist es erst in v5.2.1.
- `server-opts.d/*.conf` wird in `site-opts.d/http.conf` **hinter** den Regex-Locations der Basis eingebunden (`nginx -T` geprüft). Die erste passende Regex gewinnt, eine eigene Regex-Location könnte also nie vorher greifen.
- Darum steht in `docker/nginx/server-opts.d/werkbuch.conf` ein Präfix `location ^~ /index.php/ { return 404; }`. Mit `^~` prüft nginx keine Regex mehr.
- werkbuch verlinkt nie `/index.php/<rest>`, darum 404 für den ganzen Pfad statt einer Liste gefährlicher Zeichen. `/index.php` selbst (Front-Controller) bleibt unberührt.
- Neue Smoke-Probe „no open redirect“: `/index.php/%5Cevil.example`, `//evil.example`, `%09/evil.example`, `/projects` geben je 404 ohne `Location`. `ImageTest` hält die Location fest.
- Mit einer Basis ab v5.2.1 kann sie wieder gehen.
