author: domdomegg
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This PR body was truncated due to platform limits.

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [cert-manager](https://cert-manager.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager)) | minor | `v1.20.3` → `v1.21.3` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>cert-manager/cert-manager (cert-manager)</summary>

### [`v1.21.3`](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/tag/v1.21.3)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/compare/v1.21.2...v1.21.3)

cert-manager is the easiest way to automatically manage certificates in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

v1.21.3 removes trust in the compromised eMudhra CA (see [eMudhra Compromise](https://cert-manager.io/docs/trust/trust-manager/#emudhra-compromise)). The updated base images no longer include the "emSign ECC Root CA - G3" root certificate. Go 1.26.10 also makes `crypto/x509` reject certificate chains that pass through the compromised intermediates ([CVE-2026-111943](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6809)).

It also fixes an ACME ARI renewal loop, stops the controller copying a private key from a Secret that the Certificate does not own, and quotes the proxy values in the Helm chart. It updates Go and several dependencies to fix reported security vulnerabilities.

All users should upgrade.

#### Changes by Kind

##### Bug or Regression

- Added `status.acme.ari.certID` to track issuance of new certs and re-fetch ARI from CA. This fixes a renewal loop where a stale ARI window from the previous certificate triggered repeated re-issuance until the CA rate limit was hit. ([#​9292](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9292), [@​hjoshi123](https://redirect.github.com/hjoshi123))
- Helm chart: quote the `http_proxy`, `https_proxy` and `no_proxy` values when rendering the controller Deployment env vars, so values like `*.example.com` no longer break the manifest. ([#​9407](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9407), [@​pujitha24](https://redirect.github.com/pujitha24))
- The `requestmanager` and `issuing` controllers now only consume the Secret named by `status.nextPrivateKeySecretName` when it carries the `cert-manager.io/next-private-key` label and is owned by the Certificate, matching the invariant the `keymanager` controller already enforces. Previously a principal able to write the `certificates/status` subresource, but not to read Secrets, could name any Secret in the namespace and have its private key copied into `spec.secretName`. The `keymanager` controller no longer creates the next private key Secret under the name in `status.nextPrivateKeySecretName`. It always uses a generated name, records a `NotOwned` Warning event when the field names a Secret it does not own, and repoints the field at the Secret it owns rather than deleting that Secret when the two disagree. The Secret named by `spec.secretName` is never treated as a next private key Secret, even if `spec.secretTemplate` labels it as one. ([#​9368](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9368), [@​wallrj](https://redirect.github.com/wallrj))

##### Other (Cleanup or Flake)

- Upgrade Go to 1.26.9, fixing CVEs in the crypto/tls, net/http, net/textproto and html/template packages. ([#​9444](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9444), [@​wallrj-cyberark](https://redirect.github.com/wallrj-cyberark))
- Upgrade Go to 1.26.10, fixing a CVE in the crypto/x509 package. ([#​9501](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9501), [@​wallrj-cyberark](https://redirect.github.com/wallrj-cyberark))
- Bump `golang.org/x/net` to v0.60.0 to fix reported security vulnerabilities ([#​9451](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9451))
- Bump `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace` and `otlptracegrpc` to v1.45.0 to fix a reported security vulnerability ([#​9374](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9374), [#​9375](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9375))
- Update distroless base images, removing the compromised "emSign ECC Root CA - G3" root certificate ([#​9351](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9351), [#​9414](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9414), [#​9493](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9493), [#​9495](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9495))

### [`v1.21.2`](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/tag/v1.21.2)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/compare/v1.21.1...v1.21.2)

cert-manager is the easiest way to automatically manage certificates in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

v1.21.2 fixes controller and webhook panics, data races, ACME renewal and HTTP-01 solver bugs, and a Gateway API dnsNames bug. It stops the ACME and Vault issuers copying untrusted HTTP response bodies into status conditions and Events, and tightens ambient AWS credential use for namespaced Vault Issuers. It also updates Go and several dependencies to fix reported security vulnerabilities.

All users should upgrade.

#### Changes by Kind

##### Bug or Regression

- ACME Issuer response bodies are no longer reflected into Issuer status conditions or Kubernetes Events. Only ACME problem documents are surfaced (bounded in length); other responses are reported by HTTP status code alone, with the full error available in the controller logs. ([#​9239](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9239), [@​FelixPhipps](https://redirect.github.com/FelixPhipps))
- Cap ACME server response bodies at 16 MiB to guard against unbounded-body denial-of-service. ([#​9222](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9222), [@​FelixPhipps](https://redirect.github.com/FelixPhipps))
- De-duplicate dnsNames when multiple Gateway/ListenerSet listeners share a Secret ([#​9234](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9234), [@​speer](https://redirect.github.com/speer))
- Fix certificate renewal windows using February 29 cron schedules across non-leap century years. ([#​9240](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9240), [@​wieghx](https://redirect.github.com/wieghx))
- Fix validating webhook panics when AdmissionReview requests omit optional fields, by routing identity, approval, and resource validation on the always-present Resource/SubResource fields and denying (rather than silently allowing) requests with an unset or mismatched resource. As a side effect, validation is now also enforced for equivalent-converted requests on non-v1 API versions, which previously could skip validation. ([#​9235](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9235), [@​lunarwhite](https://redirect.github.com/lunarwhite))
- Fixed HTTP-01 solver cleanup so that a solver ingress, pod or service that has already been deleted no longer fails the cleanup with a NotFound error. ([#​9278](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9278), [@​arpitjain099](https://redirect.github.com/arpitjain099))
- Fixed a bug where `replaces` field was being populated for the wrong issuer on issuer changes ([#​9236](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9236), [@​hjoshi123](https://redirect.github.com/hjoshi123))
- Fixed a data race in the ACME HTTP-01 self-check that could occur when custom DNS servers were configured. ([#​9313](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9313), [@​shashankvarma499](https://redirect.github.com/shashankvarma499))
- Fixed a panic in the certificates-issuing controller when a CertificateRequ

body:
## What this adds

Not a device, a taskbar widget option (fixes #63, addresses #1681):

- **Position on the taskbar** submenu: *Next to the notification area*, presets of 40 / 80 / 120 / 160 / 200 px, and **Custom...** for any whole number from -1000 to 3000 px. Negative values move the widget towards (or over) the notification area. The value is stored in the existing `TaskbarOffset` setting the widget already reads, so values people set by hand keep working and show as "Custom (N px)...".
- **Make room for other taskbar widgets** (checkbox in the same submenu, on by default): other apps can put their own small windows into the taskbar next to the tray (network graphs like Networx, countdowns, ...). The widget now steps past such windows (visible children of `Shell_TrayWnd` owned by neither Explorer nor BatteryHub, narrower than a third of the taskbar) when they sit where the strip would go, the same way it already steps past the Widgets button. Works for horizontal, vertical and right-to-left taskbars. If two apps both do this, the first to re-position takes the outer spot and the other stays put, so they settle within a second.

New strings are in `lang/_template.txt`. The custom value editor (`src/offset_dialog.cpp`) follows the rename dialog's pattern.

## Where the protocol comes from

No device protocol involved.

## Tested on real hardware?

Yes, Windows 11 with a classic (ReBar) taskbar, next to another app's taskbar widget:

- Built with MinGW-w64 (g++ 16.2, the build.bat flags): no warnings.
- Make room on: the strip moved left of the other widget and stayed there (no back-and-forth over 10+ s, also with both apps making room).
- Presets, Custom... with positive and negative values, and invalid input (asks for a whole number) all behave as expected; Make room off restores the old placement.

## About the safety check flag

"registry / startup changes" is flagged for the new lines in `src/main.cpp` that save the position: `RegSetKeyValueW` / `RegDeleteKeyValueW` on BatteryHub's own key `HKCU\Software\WirelessBattery`, value `TaskbarOffset` (the value `widget.cpp` already reads), plus `MakeRoomForOtherWidgets` through the existing `SaveBoolSetting` helper. Nothing touches startup entries or any other key.

## Checklist

- [x] Only read-only battery queries are sent; no settings, lighting or firmware are changed
- [x] Only devices recognised by vendor/product ID (or a protocol-specific collection) are touched
- [x] No network access, no launching other programs, no new files outside `src/`, `docs/` or `README.md` (plus the new phrases in `lang/_template.txt`)
- [x] No binaries or generated files are included
- [x] No `Co-authored-by` lines crediting AI tools (Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT ...) in the commit messages
- [x] Changes to `.github/`, `installer/`, `build.bat` or `Makefile` are explained above (none)

author: phongih
body:
Center setup wizard, shaped like the EduOS campus wizard: steps on the left, a required checklist on the right, a draft kept in this browser with "restored · discard", and a review step.

Owner decisions (21/11):
- **Center (branch) inside an existing organization only.** The organization is the tenant root from EduOS / IIOS; OGC does not create tenants.
- **Staff step = assign existing teachers to classes.** No accounts, no access grants (IIOS / G2-C).
- **Fees = optional, mock price list.** Nothing is charged or invoiced.

**Steps**
1. **Center info:** name, code (unique in the org), brand (of this org), city, address.
2. **Courses:** from the org's catalog.
3. **Rooms & days:** rooms with seats (1–60, unique names), opening days and hours in center time.
4. **Classes & teachers:** name, course, room, weekdays, start time, minutes, teacher. Problems are shown in plain words, e.g. "meets on a day the center is closed", "is outside opening hours", "needs a teacher".
5. **Fees (optional):** VND per course or per month.
6. **Review & open.** The button stays disabled until the checklist is 5/5.

**Contract** `centerSetup.ts` (additive): `CenterSetupDraft`, `centerSetupChecklist` and `classIssues` (pure, shared by UI and adapter), `CenterSetupPort` (`getSetupContext`, `createCenter`, `getFees`).

**Mock adapter** `mockCenterSetup.ts`
- Staff only, own org only.
- Re-checks the whole draft server-side, including that the brand, courses and teachers belong to the org.
- On open it creates the center (Directory lists it, its code is taken), its classes (`<name> — <days>`, the chosen teacher, empty roster), and **4 weeks of sessions** in `sessionStore`. Center operations, the teacher dashboard and attendance pick these up immediately.
- `sessionStore.reset()` removes created centers, classes and rosters (tests, page reload).
- The fee list is shown on the center's Directory page, labelled "mock — nothing is charged".

**Known limits**
- New classes' sessions are titled "ENG-A2 — Session n". Make-up "join another class of the same unit" matches by unit title, so these sessions are not join options yet (unit plans per course are a later step).
- Seat limits are captured per room but not enforced for joins yet.
- Editing an existing center is a follow-up.

**Tests:** web 370. Checklist rules, plain-word class issues, staff-only, server-side re-check (foreign brand), invalid fee, open → directory + taken code + 4 Saturday 09:00 ICT sessions + Ben's dashboard + operations + attendance + fees scope, reset. UI: full walk-through gated by the checklist, draft restore / discard, closed to teachers. New E2E `center-setup-journey` 3/3. Local CI: all gates passed.

Synthetic data and mock adapters only; no gate, SQL, IIOS or governance file touched.

author: thefallen0000
body:
# S134 — PR body

**Título sugerido:** `feat(lorebooks): complete the versioned lorebook library (S134)`

## What does this change do?

Completes the lorebook library that S133 left as a basic directory. A lorebook is
now a first-class resource: full version history, restore-as-new-version, usage
grouped by character, link-to-character from the book, soft delete with a warning,
standalone import/export per book and version with `origin_id`/`source_key`
matching, and an alternate-greeting picker when starting a conversation.

It also closes the S133 follow-ups tied to this area: SQL pagination and
in-use/unused filtering on the shelf, real usage counts, batched linked-lorebook
summaries on character detail (no N+1) and stable synthetic entry ids.

## Why is it needed?

The deferred endpoints of `docs/16` §9 (`restore`, `DELETE`, `usage`, `link`,
`import`, export by version) did not exist, and the UI showed «S134» placeholders
instead of actions. A user could not restore a version, see which characters use a
book, link it from the book, delete it safely, re-import it restoring its history,
export a concrete version or choose an alternate greeting.

Approved contract: `docs/10-slices/S134-progress.md` (RFC, `91b0bd7`). Test plan:
`docs/10-slices/S134-test-plan.md` (`ef5ee20`).

## What changed

### Backend

- `POST /api/lorebooks/:id/versions/:versionId/restore`: creates a new version from
  an old snapshot; restoring the current version is a 200 no-op.
- `DELETE /api/lorebooks/:id`: soft delete (`deleted_at`), 404 when missing or
  already deleted; versions and character versions stay untouched.
- `GET /api/lorebooks/:id/usage?versionId=`: "In use by" (`==` selected version)
  and "History" (older versions), grouped by character, batched without N+1.
- `POST /api/lorebooks/:id/link`: one new character version via copy-from-prev;
  409 `LOREBOOK_LINK_UNCHANGED` when nothing would change.
- `POST /api/lorebooks/import/preview` and `POST /api/lorebooks/import`: dry-run
  matching by `origin_id` then `source_key`, explicit `reuse` / `restore` /
  `new-version` / `new-book` action, 409 `IMPORT_ACTION_MISMATCH` /
  `IMPORT_STALE_MATCH`. The card import (`PUT /characters/:id/card`) keeps the S133
  behavior and does not use the matcher.
- `POST /api/lorebooks/:id/export` accepts `versionId` and merges
  `extensions.rm` additively (`version: 1`, `originId`) for CCv3 and ST native,
  preserving unknown keys.
- `POST /api/conversations` accepts `greetingIndex` (0 = `first_mes`, `i >= 1` =
  `alternateGreetings[i-1]`); out of range is 400 `INVALID_GREETING`.
- `GET /api/lorebooks` pushes `limit`/`offset`/`filter` into SQL and returns real
  `usageCount` and `usageVersionCount`.
- No new migration: the `0020` schema already covers soft delete, usage, restore
  and matching. A `deleted-different` import gives the new book a fresh
  `origin_id`, including `extensions.rm.originId` (`8196a9e`).

### Shared and frontend

- New DTOs: `LorebookUsageDTO`, `ImportLorebookPreview`, `ImportLorebookResult`,
  `LinkLorebookInput`, `ImportLorebookAction`, `greetingIndex`.
- Lorebook shelf with real usage ("Used by N characters · M versions" / "Unused")
  and standalone import.
- Detail sections Identity, Settings, Entries, Versions, Link and Danger;
  previous versions are read-only and offer "Restore as a new version".
- Link dialog with the "this creates a new character version" warning.
- Delete dialog with the `docs/16` §5.1 warning; a deleted book is restored by
  re-importing it.
- `AlternateGreetingPicker` in `components/shared/`, wired at character detail,
  the versions section and the library.
- S134 placeholders (`linkDeferred*`, `versionsDeferred`, `characters.tabCards`)
  removed; the obsolete `**S134**` CHANGELOG entry is gone.

## Tests and verification

- `pnpm check`: architecture 7/7, typecheck 5/5, lint 5/5.
- `pnpm --filter @workspace/backend test`: 166 files / 1078 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @workspace/frontend exec vitest run`: 93 files / 488 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @workspace/backend eval`: 1 file / 33 tests passed.
- `pnpm build`: 4/4 tasks successful. The build refreshed
  `packages/website/src/data/release.json` (1.47.0 → 1.57.2); that generated
  snapshot was restored and is not part of the slice.
- `pnpm audit --prod`: no known vulnerabilities.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- No release dry-run: the slice does not change `package.json`,
  `pnpm-lock.yaml`, native modules or packaging.
- No manual browser run in this session; UI behavior is covered by the RTL suites.

## Review

- `docs/10-slices/S134-review.md` (`bf52267`): **PASS WITH NOTES**, no blockers and
  no majors.
- Fixed before close: MINOR 1 (stale `extensions.rm.originId` on a fresh new book,
  `8196a9e`), MINOR 2 (dead i18n keys, `eeb05e4`) and NIT 3 (import `format` type
  alignment, `455680c`). Delta re-review found no new findings.
- Deferred: NIT 4 (`IMPORT_STALE_MATCH` only covers `reuse` + `deleted-identical`;
  other incompatible transitions are `IMPORT_ACTION_MISMATCH`) and NIT 5 (fresh
  books may have `origin_id = null` by design).

## Deferred / out of scope

- Card import matching (`PUT /characters/:id/card` unchanged).
- Internal export schema v2 (`EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` untouched).
- N3 (`extensions.rm` emitting `null` subtitle/instructions), physical drop of
  `lorebooks.character_id`, orphan-version cleanup, `nickname`.
- Multiple lorebooks per character version, groups, timed effects, probability,
  decorators, V3 assets, ST prompt manager.

## Release

No version bump, tag or release in this PR: the CHANGELOG entries live under
`[Unreleased]`. Publishing `1.58.0` is a separate `/release`.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes locally (architecture, typecheck, lint).
- [x] Tests added or updated where it makes sense (backend and frontend).
- [x] Docs updated (`docs/10-slices/S134-*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
      `docs/10-slices/WORKFLOW.md`).
- [x] Commits use the conventional style.
- [x] No version bump and no manual release.

Originally the policy-guard enforce flip — but this repo is public, and a public repository cannot call a private repository's reusable workflows. Both the `review` call in pr-checks.yml and the policy-guard caller have made their workflow files fail at startup on every PR since Nov 8: no jobs ran, the required `check` context never reported, and every PR was blocked. This PR removes both calls so pr-checks parses and its `check` job gates merges again. The repo's main-gate ruleset keeps `check` as its required context (the policy-guard context was dropped — it can never report here).

author: jakubanderwald
body:
## Summary

Fixes for problems that came up while shipping #861 (PR #877) through the factory flow from an interactive session. None of them change app behaviour.

- **Stale CocoaPods cache (desktop Fastfile).** The post-merge desktop beta failed in the primary checkout. Its gitignored `apps/desktop/macos/Pods` dated from react-native-macos 0.81 (`hermes-engine 0.81.6`), while `Podfile.lock` pins `0.14.1`, so CocoaPods refused to install. `build_and_submit` now calls `clear_stale_pods_cache!` before CocoaPods. When `Pods/Manifest.lock` is missing or differs from `Podfile.lock`, it deletes `macos/Pods` and `macos/build`. That is the same rule as the factory's `_beta_root_drop_stale_pods`. A source-level test in `desktop-native-build-config.test.mjs` checks the guard runs before `cocoapods(`.
- **Retire the one-time fossil step.** The primary checkout's `node_modules` was already on rnm 0.83.0 and the standard pnpm store, and post-merge betas `desktop@0.4.6+94` and `+97` shipped on 0.83 (96 opened notes). `CLAUDE.md`, `apps/desktop/CLAUDE.md`, `desktop-build-fossil.md` and `builds-and-releases.md` now mark the step done. If `FACTORY_INTEST_BETA_DESKTOP=0` is still set on the Mac mini, it can go back on.
- **Scripts test independent of `/tmp`.** `dispatch-release.test.mjs` used a fixed `/tmp/x` as a log dir that `laneLogPath` runs `mkdirSync` on, so it failed with EEXIST on any machine where `/tmp/x` is a file. It now uses a fresh temp dir.
- **`apps/web/AGENTS.md`.** Next 16's `next dev` writes this file when it detects an AI agent, which left it untracked in every agent worktree. It's committed exactly as Next writes it; a second `next dev` leaves it unchanged. It's added to `.prettierignore`, and `local-dev-setup.md` has a short note on it.
- **In-Test scenarios and the number locale.** Under pl_PL, `awk printf "%.4f"` printed `0,0037`, so the #861 scenario reported false FAILs. `lib/common.sh` now exports `LC_NUMERIC=C` for every scenario and unsets an inherited `LC_ALL`, after copying it into `LANG` when `LANG` is unset, so UTF-8 survives.
- **Runbook: "Driving a card from an interactive session".** The steps #861 used: `factory-pause` first, the plan marker, Status changes via `factory-project.mjs set-status` together with the `status:*` label, the pre-merge beta with `DRAFTO_INTEST_ISSUE`, the In-Test markers, `/merge`, the post-merge beta, and unpausing. It's linked from `dark-factory.md` → Kill switches.

## Not in this PR: the flaky web E2E run on #877

Attempt 1 of run 44913155545 failed 18 tests, all redirected to `/login`. The dev auth logs show the cause: a global `POST /logout` at 14:20:34Z from the iOS app (an iOS-simulator run of the Maestro flow `apps/mobile/e2e/11-sign-out-confirm.yaml`, confirm leg) on the shared dev E2E user. That revoked the session CI was using. A second global logout came from the Android run at 14:30:44Z. The fix is a separate decision and gets its own PR or issue.

## Testing

Local results:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Scripts | 5018 pass / 0 fail with `/tmp/x` present (5063 / 0 after rebasing onto #834) |
| Desktop | 969 |
| Web | 1816 unit + 115 Playwright E2E |
| Shared | 705 |
| Mobile | 1061 |

`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm format:check` are clean. A read-only dry run of the new Pods rule against the primary checkout returns "manifest differs", so it would clear the stale cache. The #861 scenario's `--preflight` passes with `LC_ALL=pl_PL.UTF-8`.

author: arvinpaundra
body:
## Problem

A Learner adding several words had to loop over `POST /words`, which saved the words before a duplicate stopped the loop, so the request was not all or nothing.

## Solution

`POST /decks/:deckSlug/words/batch` saves 1 to 50 words in one transaction, or none. The use case builds each word's keys, names every word that collides with a live word of the deck or with another word of the batch (both sides of an intra-batch pair), and only then inserts. The check is one query over the batch's keys. A word that a concurrent request takes after the check fails the batch and rolls it back. Saved words come back in request order.

Rejected alternative: looping `createWord` in a transaction. It stops at the first duplicate, so it can't name every colliding word.

## Changes

- be/library: `createWords` use case, `findTakenKeys` on the `WordRepo` port and its SQL, `DuplicateWordsError` domain error, and the `createWords` handler mapping to `DuplicateWords` (409) and `NotFound`.

## Verification

```
verify: all green
```

none

Closes #265

author: zcanann
body:
The UEFI table validator reads `HeaderSize` as `u32`, guards it against the length of its byte slice, and passes the exact widened size to the checksum routine. The standard-library check refuses that call because the order established on the original integer is unavailable on the converted argument.

The checker traces either endpoint of `<` or `<=` to its actual exact cast or widening equation. It proves the original order while preserving the other endpoint and submits the conversion witness to the existing `IntegerCastBound` verifier. A size narrowed by masking or a bound on another slice supplies no such fact. This uses Omega’s existing mixed-integer comparison and cast semantics.

On the previous integrated compiler `48a0f512148`, an ordinary Build containing byte-identical copies of `source/library/std/uefi_x86_64_integrity.omg` and `source/library/std/targets/uefi_x86_64/integrity.omg` reproduces the refusal at the original checksum call. The entry constructs a 24-byte header with the specified CRC, an oversized declaration and a truncated view. The short numeric and byte-slice sources also reproduce the refusal. The Stage06 checker and its test targets pass an exact-branch typecheck at `ddb6d1ce1bc`. The owner requested merging after typechecking. The runnable source suite and both-engine UEFI application were skipped at merge.

Gate: RC-SOURCE-SEMANTICS | An exact conversion must preserve a guarded order with the same byte-slice extent.
Spec: wiki/spec/language/numeric_values.md#arithmetic-and-comparisons, wiki/spec/language/numeric_values.md#computational-conversions, wiki/spec/proofs/classicality.md
Proof: omega run --both <isolated UEFI Build>, omega --check <mixed guard and exact cast>, mbx test --locked -p lowered-program-to-checked-program --lib an_exact_cast_transports_the_guard_for_the_same_byte_slice | three independent baseline refusals reproduced and checker plus test code typechecked. Candidate execution was skipped at merge.

author: convertedbv
body:
## Google Analytics 4 tools

Adds GA4 reading and management to the same server and login as Google Ads, behind `GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_ANALYTICS` (`off` by default, `read`, `full`).

- **analytics_reporting**: list properties, metadata, compatibility, run_report, pivot, realtime, funnel (v1alpha), quotas
- **analytics_insights**: property_overview, channel_performance (per channel/month incl. key events per event), tracking_health
- **analytics_admin**: full property setup, 35 resource types (list/get/schema), change history, access report
- **analytics_management** (`full` only): propose & confirm (validate → change_items → checksum) for key events, custom dimensions/metrics, annotations, property settings, retention, Ads links, data streams, enhanced measurement, user access, and a generic manager for the other resource types. Deleting accounts/properties and creating properties are blocked.
- Optional allowlist `GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_ANALYTICS_PROPERTY_IDS`.

### Login / rollout safety
Analytics scopes are **requested** at login but **not required** on the token (`ads_mcp/auth_provider.py`). Existing sessions keep working for Ads without reconnecting; a user who unticks Analytics, or a pending Google verification of the sensitive scopes, never blocks the Ads tools. GA4 tools return a clear "reconnect" message when the scope is missing.

### Tests
416 passed, 2 skipped (`pytest tests --ignore=tests/smoke`); `black -l 80 --check .` clean. New: `tests/tools/analytics_test.py` (29), `tests/auth_provider_test.py` (5).

Docs: `docs/ANALYTICS.md`. Production env `GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_ANALYTICS=full` is already set in Vercel and takes effect with the deploy of this merge.

body:
Tanda 2 · carril L4L6. Este PR es independiente: se basa en `origin/dev` y no está apilado sobre los otros. **Conviene mergearlo antes que #426**, porque el job OSV de #426 está en rojo por esto. Después lo incorporo en las ramas apiladas.

## Causa
El job «Dependencias vulnerables (OSV-Scanner)» corre cuando cambian `packages/` o `apps/`. Hoy falla con 8 avisos nuevos en `yarn.lock`, que ya estaban en `dev` y que este carril no introdujo:

| Paquete | Versión | Quién lo trae | Arreglo |
|---|---|---|---|
| hono | 4.13.11 (5 avisos) | `packages/simulado`, `@scalar/mock-server` | 4.13.19 |
| @hono/node-server | 2.1.3 (2 avisos) | `packages/simulado` | 2.1.11 |
| minimatch | 10.2.6 (1 aviso, CVSS 6.9) | `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree` (^10.2.2) | 11.0.9 (en 10.x no hay parche, la corrección arranca en 11.0.1) |

## Cambio
Solo se tocaron `resolutions` en el `package.json` raíz, que es la práctica que ya sigue el repo, y `yarn.lock`.

## Verificación (local, Node 22 + yarn 4.18)
```
yarn turbo run lint       (11 paquetes JS/TS) -> 8/8 successful
yarn turbo run typecheck  -> 11/11 successful
yarn turbo run test:front -> 11/11 successful
yarn turbo run test:a11y  -> 11/11 successful
```
Los paquetes Dart (`movil`, `diseno-flutter`) no dependen de npm. Localmente fallan `--fatal-infos` por el SDK 3.50.1, que es más nuevo que el de CI y marca `material.dart` como deprecado. Ese fallo es ajeno a este cambio, así que el dato que vale es el del CI.

## No cubierto
- No corrí OSV-Scanner localmente. Lo valida el job del CI.
- minimatch 11 es un salto mayor que typescript-eslint no declara. El lint de los 8 paquetes pasa, pero conviene retirar la resolution cuando typescript-eslint suba su rango.

Largo plazo: los avisos de OSV se resuelven con resolutions acotadas, que se retiran en cuanto el paquete padre actualiza su rango.

body:
Closes #181

## 계획

`docs/exec-plans/completed/20261122-gates-current-head.md`(소규모 계획). 위험도 높음(기계 판정이 어느 커밋을 판정하는지를 바꾼다. 보호 경로 `scripts/**`).

## 이 PR의 경과

- 구현 판정 1회차: Claude 승인, Codex 수정 요청(P0 하나, P1 하나). 둘 다 맞는 지적이라 고쳤다.
  - F1(P0): `pr-state`의 안내 줄이 PR 브랜치 이름을 인용 없이 셸 명령에 넣었다. → 안내 줄을 `gatesMissingLine`으로 빼고 브랜치 이름을 있는 `shellQuote`로 낱말 하나로 인용한다. 제어 문자가 든 이름은 넣지 않는다. 특수 문자가 든 이름 여덟 개로 인용의 꼴을 보고, 실제 `sh`가 그 낱말을 이름 그대로 읽는지(다른 명령이 실행되지 않는지) 본다.
  - F2(P1): 조회 응답의 head 저장소가 이름 없는 객체면 포크로 보고 조용히 건너뛰었다. → head 저장소가 `null`이거나 이름이 다른 리포로 확인될 때만 포크로 본다. 이름이 없거나 글이 아니거나 빈 글이면 예외다.
- 구현 판정 2회차: Claude 승인, Codex 수정 요청(P1 하나). F1·F2는 닫혔다.
  - F3(P1): head 저장소의 이름이 `owner/name` 꼴이 아닌 글(`invalid`)이어도 다른 리포로 보고 건너뛰었다. → 이름이 `owner/name` 꼴이고 이 리포와 다를 때만 포크로 본다. 그 밖에는 예외다.
- 구현 판정 3회차: 두 검증자 승인(지적 없음). 그 뒤 main을 병합했다(#183 병합 뒤. CHANGELOG의 충돌은 두 줄을 병합된 순서로 두었다. 코드 변경 없음).
- 구현 판정 4회차(main 병합 뒤): Codex가 F4(P1, `scripts/gates/doc-lint.ts`의 머리말 정규식)를 냈다. 이 PR이 바꾸지 않은 파일(main의 #183에서 왔다)이라 반박했고, 5회차에서 받아들여졌다(두 검증자 승인).
- PR #184 병합 뒤 main을 다시 병합했다. 설계서 버전을 v0.7.73으로 옮겼다(#184가 v0.7.72). 코드 변경 없음.
- v0.7.73으로 옮긴 head에서 두 검증자 승인. 제작자의 지시로 PR #171의 병합을 기다렸고, 병합 뒤 main을 다시 병합했다(CHANGELOG의 충돌은 두 줄을 병합된 순서로 두었다. 코드 변경 없음).
- 그 head에서 두 검증자 승인. 승인을 요청하려는데 PR #187이 병합되어 main에 뒤처졌다. main을 다시 병합했다(`architecture.md`의 표 충돌: `runner/*` 행은 이 PR의 것, `ci/*` 행은 main의 것. 코드 변경 없음).

## 무엇을

- **`scripts/ci/pr.ts`의 `resolvePr`**: `gates` 워크플로가 `pull_request_target` 이벤트로 돌 때도 이벤트에 담긴 head를 그대로 쓰지 않는다. 이벤트의 PR 번호로 `repos/<리포>/pulls/<번호>`를 조회해 응답의 head SHA·base SHA·head ref·본문을 낸다.
  - 이벤트의 PR이 포크 PR이거나 형식이 틀리면 전처럼 API를 부르지 않고 건너뛴다.
  - 응답이 객체가 아니거나, 번호가 이벤트의 번호와 다르거나, 형식이 틀리면(head·base SHA, head ref) 건너뛰지 않고 예외를 던진다. 실행이 실패로 드러난다.
  - 응답의 head 저장소가 지워졌거나(`null`) 이름이 다른 리포로 확인되면(`owner/name` 꼴이고 이 리포와 다르다) 포크 PR로 보고 건너뛴다. 이름이 없거나 그 꼴이 아니면 예외다.
  - PR 번호는 양의 정수만 받는다(조회 경로에 들어가는 값이다).
  - `workflow_run` 경로와 그 밖의 이벤트는 그대로다.
- **`scripts/runner/pr-state.ts`의 `gatesMissing`**(새 순수 함수)과 **`pr-state` 명령**: 필수 체크에 든 검증자 판정이 모두 났는데(승인이든 수정 요청이든) 상태가 없는 게이트가 있으면 필수 체크 목록 아래에 한 줄을 낸다(게이트 이름, 기다려도 오지 않는다는 것, 실행을 찾는 명령과 다시 돌리는 명령. `scripts/commands/pr-state.ts`의 `gatesMissingLine`이 만든다. 명령에 넣는 브랜치 이름은 셸의 낱말 하나로 인용한다). PR의 분류(`classifyPr`)는 바꾸지 않았다.
- **문서**: 설계서 10.4절(v0.7.73), 절차서 5절, `architecture.md`, CHANGELOG.
- 워크플로 파일은 바꾸지 않았다. "판정할 PR 정하기" 단계에는 이미 조회용 토큰(`pull-requests: read`)이 있다.

## 왜

Issue #181. PR #177의 4라운드에서 본문을 고친 직후에 push했더니, 본문 수정의 실행(1초 늦게 만들어졌다)이 push의 실행을 취소하고(같은 PR의 실행은 하나만 남는다) 이벤트에 담긴 지난 head에 상태를 기록했다. 새 head에는 게이트 상태가 없는 채로 남았고, `pr-state`는 계속 "CI 대기"로만 보였다(약 2시간 40분 대기). 어느 이벤트의 실행이 남든 실행 시점의 head를 판정하면 현재 head에 상태가 기록된다. `workflow_run` 경로는 이미 그렇게 한다(페이로드를 믿지 않고 조회한다).

## 바뀌는 테스트 (R5)

- `scripts/test/risk-gate.test.ts`의 "resolvePr: pull_request_target은 이벤트에서, 포크는 건너뛴다"를 새 동작의 테스트 넷으로 바꿨다. 이 테스트는 "API를 부르지 않는다"와 "이벤트의 값을 낸다"를 단언했는데 바로 그 동작이 바뀐다. "포크는 API를 부르지 않고 건너뛴다"는 단언은 남겼다. `workflow_run`과 그 밖의 이벤트의 테스트는 고치지 않았다.
- `scripts/test/pr-state.test.ts`에 `gatesMissing`·`gatesMissingLine`의 단위 테스트와 `pr-state` 명령의 테스트를 더했다(있던 테스트는 고치지 않았다).

## 검증

- 테스트 먼저: 구현 전에 새 테스트를 돌려 `risk-gate.test.ts`의 새 테스트 4건이 실패하고 `pr-state.test.ts`가 `gatesMissing`이 없어 실패하는 것을 확인했다(계획의 진행 로그).
- `node --test scripts/test/risk-gate.test.ts scripts/test/pr-state.test.ts` 통과(42건). `node scripts/harness.ts check` 통과(test 전체), `node scripts/harness.ts self-test` 통과(시나리오 10개).
- **병합 뒤 확인이 남는다**: `gates`는 main의 스크립트로 돌므로 이 변경은 병합 뒤의 실행부터 적용된다. 병합 뒤 실제 PR에서 본문 수정 직후 push해 새 head에 게이트 상태가 기록되는지 확인하고 Issue #181에 댓글로 남긴다(Issue의 수용 기준).

## 자체 리뷰 (scripts/cross-review/checklist.md)

- [x] 수용 기준 충족·근거: 계획의 "검증 결과". 병합 뒤 확인 하나가 남는다(위).
- [x] 정확성·엣지 케이스: 응답이 `null`·`undefined`·문자열·배열·다른 번호·틀린 SHA·틀린 ref인 경우, 응답의 head 저장소가 다른 리포·`null`인 경우, API가 던지는 경우, 닫힌 PR, 번호가 문자열·0·소수·음수인 이벤트, head 저장소의 이름이 없거나 글이 아닌 응답, 셸의 특수 문자가 든 브랜치 이름을 테스트에 넣었다.
- [x] 테스트 실효성: 새 테스트는 main의 코드에서 실패한다(`check`의 test-effect가 확인했다).
- [x] 아키텍처 경계·황금 원칙: `gatesMissing`은 `runner/pr-state.ts`의 다른 함수처럼 순수 함수다(네트워크·git 호출 없음). 새 의존성 없음.
- [x] 범위 밖 변경 이유: 없음.
- [x] 문서 갱신(또는 불필요한 이유): 설계서 10.4절, 절차서 5절, `architecture.md`, CHANGELOG.
- [x] 보안: 포크 PR을 판정하지 않는 조건은 그대로다(이벤트로 먼저 거르고, 응답으로 한 번 더 거른다). 조회 경로에 넣는 번호는 양의 정수인지 확인한다. 안내에 넣는 브랜치 이름은 셸의 낱말 하나로 인용한다. 판정 job의 권한·토큰은 바뀌지 않는다.
- [x] 발견 사항 처리: 계획의 발견 사항에 처리를 적었다.
- [x] 보호 경로 변경: CHANGELOG 갱신, 검사를 약화하지 않음(게이트의 판정 기준은 그대로다. 판정할 커밋을 이벤트의 head에서 실행 시점의 head로 바꿨다. 조회 응답이 맞지 않으면 건너뛰지 않고 실패한다).

## 알려 둘 것

- 조회가 실패하면(API 오류) `evaluate`가 실패하고 `record`가 오류 상태를 쓴다. 전에는 `pull_request_target`에서 조회가 없었으므로 새로 생긴 실패 경로다. 이벤트의 head로 조용히 넘어가면 이번 문제가 되풀이되므로 실패로 드러내는 쪽을 골랐다(계획의 의사결정 로그).
- `record` job은 `evaluate`가 head를 내지 못하면 이벤트의 head에 오류 상태를 쓴다(워크플로의 `needs.evaluate.outputs.head_sha || github.event.pull_request.head.sha`). 이벤트의 head가 지난 것이면 지난 head에 쓴다. 고치려면 워크플로 변경이 필요해 이 PR의 범위 밖이다(계획의 발견 사항).
- `.github/workflows/gates.yml`의 단계 이름과 머리 주석은 `workflow_run`만 조회한다고 적혀 있다. 봇은 워크플로 파일을 고칠 수 없어 그대로 두었다.

## 제작자에게

- 위험도 높음이라 제작자의 head 승인이 필요하다. 두 검증자가 승인한 뒤 초안을 풀며 한 번에 요청한다.

author: in0ho1no
body:
## 関連 Issue

Closes #16

## 変更内容

- `MascotJevServer` は、Windows では `SO_REUSEADDR` を付けずに待ち受ける（`allow_reuse_address = sys.platform != 'win32'`）。Linux・macOS では、これまでどおり付ける。
  - Windows では、`SO_REUSEADDR` 同士なら待ち受け中のポートにも bind できてしまう。付けなければ、使用中のポートでは `cli.py` の既存の処理に乗り、メッセージを出して終了コード `1` で終わる。
  - 標準ライブラリの `socket.create_server` と `asyncio` の `create_server` も、Windows では付けない。
  - `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` は使わない。確かめたどの組み合わせでも、付けない場合と結果が同じだった（利用者の判断で、付けない案を採用）。
- `src/tests/test_server.py` の `TestListening` に3件のテストを追加した。起動しないことを確かめる2件は、退行で起動できてしまった場合もサーバーを閉じる。
  - `SO_REUSEADDR` 付きで待ち受けているポートでは、`EADDRINUSE` で起動しない（Issue の再現条件）
  - 待ち受け中の `MascotJevServer` と同じポートでは、`EADDRINUSE` で起動しない（`mascot-jev` を2つ起動した場合）
  - サーバー側から接続を閉じて TIME_WAIT が残っても、閉じた直後に同じポートで待ち受け直せる
- `docs/records.md` に、判断の根拠と bind の挙動の検証結果を記録した。

### CI での扱い

CI（`tests.yml`）は `ubuntu-latest` だけで動く。追加したテストは、どの OS でも同じ結果を期待するため、skip の条件は付けない。

- 起動しないことを確かめる2件は、Linux では修正の前から成り立つ。Windows で問題が戻っていないかは、手元の Windows での `uv run pytest` で確かめる（修正前の Windows では2件とも失敗することを確かめた）。
- 待ち受け直す1件は、Linux で `SO_REUSEADDR` を外すと失敗する（WSL の Ubuntu で、同じ手順を標準ライブラリだけで再現して確かめた）。CI はこのテストで、Linux で付けたままであることを確かめる。

### 残る挙動（範囲外）

別のサーバーがワイルドカードで同じポートを待ち受けている場合、Windows では今回の修正後も起動することがある。確かめた構成は次のとおり（詳細は `docs/records.md` の「既知の限界」）。

- 先のソケットが `0.0.0.0` か、IPv4 も受ける `[::]` で、`SO_REUSEADDR` を付けたか何も付けない場合：`127.0.0.1` への bind は、後のソケットの設定によらず成功した（`SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` を付けても成功）。先のソケットが `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` を付けた場合は失敗した。
- `--bind` を付けない `python -m http.server 8017` は、IPv4 も受ける `[::]` で `SO_REUSEADDR` を付けて待ち受け、修正後の `MascotJevServer` も同じポートで起動した。`127.0.0.1` への接続は `MascotJevServer` が、`::1` への接続は `http.server` が受けた。`mascot-jev` が表示する `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` は `mascot-jev` につながる。
- `0.0.0.0` だけで待ち受けるサーバーとの組み合わせで、どちらが接続を受けるかは確かめていない。

## マージ後の影響範囲

- 利用者: Windows で、ほかのサーバーが `127.0.0.1` の同じポートを使っていると、`mascot-jev` は起動せずにメッセージを出して終わる。`--port` で別のポートを指定する必要がある。Linux・macOS は変わらない。
- 機能: 影響なし。
- 運用: #8 のコメントにある「#16 が直るまでは、README で、ほかのサーバーと同じポートを使わないよう注意する」は、このPRのマージ後は不要になる見込み。ただし、上の「残る挙動」は README で触れる余地がある。#8 そのものには手を付けていない。

## 検証

- Windows 11・Python 3.14.3：`uv run ruff check src/`、`uv run ruff format src/`、`uv run mypy src/`、`uv run pyright src/`、`uv run pytest`（208件）、`node --test "src/tests/js/*.test.js"`（82件）がすべて通った。
- Windows での実機の確認（Issue の再現手順 1・2）
  - `python -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1` を起動したまま `mascot-jev ..\check-4-build\_build\full` を実行すると、`mascot-jev: 127.0.0.1:8000 で待ち受けを開始できません: [WinError 10048] ...` を出して終了コード `1` で終わった。`netstat` の `LISTENING` は `http.server` の1件だけだった。
  - 逆の順番では、`mascot-jev` が待ち受けている間、`http.server` は `PermissionError: [WinError 10013]` で起動せず、2つ目の `mascot-jev` も `WinError 10048` で終了コード `1` になった。
  - 確認で起動したプロセスは、すべて止めた。
- bind の挙動（Windows と WSL の Ubuntu）は、使い捨てのスクリプトで確かめた。結果は `docs/records.md` に記録した。
- 未検証：macOS での挙動。Windows で、別のユーザーや管理者権限のプロセスと同じポートを使う場合。

## スクリーンショット

なし（CLI の出力は「検証」に記載）。

## 確認事項

- [x] 破壊的変更を含まない (含む場合は変更内容に記載した)
- [x] 依存パッケージを追加していない (追加した場合は承認済み)
- [x] トークン・パスワード等の機密情報を含まない

author: butahlecoq
body:
Refs #993. Stacked on #1181.

## Summary

Check the exact review-tool bytes before a live MPC-06 render creates output. If they disagree with the verification receipt, the command points to the matching archived renderer or a fresh receipt. Both renderer copies, their fingerprint, and the portable receipt come from the validated byte snapshots. The renderer rechecks the copied measurement inputs against that receipt.

## Evidence

- A regression test showed that the previous live command returned success with an archived receipt and wrote a report whose copied tools could not verify it.
- The current command rejects that pairing before creating the requested destination. Both the archived and current matching tool paths round-trip and verify all 180 saved QPs.
- Tests simulate an edit to the receipt and renderer after validation. The report still uses the checked source and receipt bytes. A first-read receipt with altered JSON number types and a stale digest is rejected. All 22 tests passed on Python 3.11 and 3.12. The frozen evidence trees and archived binaries were untouched.

## Delivery impact

A mixed-tool invocation now fails early. The documented replay paths retain their behavior. No native capture, public API change, or release is required.

author: alovida-salud
body:
Tanda 2, lote L1. Hallazgo `ANF-DINERO-006` (S3).

## Problema (verificado en `dev` 50cf3be9)
`CU51EjecutarCierreDiario.selloDe` calculaba `SHA-256(cuentaId | fecha)`. Ese sello no cubría el saldo que pretendía proteger: si alguien cambiaba el saldo de un día, el sello seguía siendo el mismo.

## Qué cambia
- **`SelloDelDia`** (dominio puro, nuevo). Firma `cuentaId | fecha | moneda | disponible | retenido | sello anterior`. Los importes van en forma canónica, con escala 2 y `toPlainString`. El primer día de una cuenta firma `-` en lugar del sello anterior.
- **Encadenamiento.** CU-51 guarda el sello del día anterior en `hash_anterior`, una columna que ya existía en `saldo_diario_billetera` pero nadie llenaba. **No cambia el esquema.**
- **Verificación.** `CU51.primeraRuptura(cuentaId)` recalcula la cadena de la cuenta y devuelve el primer día alterado. También detecta un eslabón reemplazado: si alguien vuelve a sellar un día con datos falsos, la cadena se corta en el día siguiente.

## CA
Dado un cierre sellado, cuando se altera el saldo de un día anterior, la verificación de la cadena falla y señala esa cuenta y esa fecha.

## DoD (salida en `docs/trabajo/2026-11-21-tanda2-l1/evidencia/M13-sello-cierre.txt`)
```
SelloDelDiaTest 6/6. Cubre: cambiar el disponible, el retenido, la moneda o el sello anterior cambia el sello;
  un saldo alterado señala su propio día; un eslabón re-sellado corta la cadena en el día siguiente; material canónico.
Integración contra PostgreSQL 16 real (base limpia):
  CU51SelloEncadenadoTest 2/2. Dos cierres seguidos quedan encadenados y la cadena no tiene ruptura;
  un saldo diario de 9999.00 insertado por fuera hace que la verificación señale ese día.
  CU51* 24/24 y CU15* 12/12 (el extracto lee esta tabla). Las que ya existían siguen en verde.
Control negativo (material = cuentaId|fecha, el sello viejo): fallan 5 unitarias y la integración del adulterado.
nucleo-financiero: spotlessCheck + test 100/100 + webTest 82/82 + testBarrido 2/2 · verificar_seguridad y verificar_criterios en verde
```
Para correr la integración apliqué solo durante la corrida el gancho `APORTAYA_TEST_DB_URL` de `BaseDeBilletera`. Ese gancho se agrega en #425 y no lo dupliqué en este PR.

### Regla 91.6
Este PR no mueve dinero: solo sella la foto diaria del saldo. Puntos 1 a 4: no aplican. Punto 5 (redondeo): los importes se sellan con `setScale(2, UNNECESSARY)`, así que un importe con más de dos decimales hace fallar el sellado en vez de redondearse en silencio.

## No cubierto
- Las filas que se cerraron antes de este cambio conservan el sello viejo y `hash_anterior` en nulo. Si se verifica una cadena que incluye días anteriores al deploy, aparece la ruptura en el primero de ellos. Es intencional, no está migrado y queda declarado.
- Por ahora solo las pruebas llaman a `primeraRuptura`. Falta un trabajo programado o una consulta para Auditoría que la corra.

Largo plazo: exponer la verificación como trabajo diario, con alerta si encuentra una ruptura. También conviene sumar la cantidad de movimientos al material firmado cuando CU-51 la calcule (hoy registra 0).

## Was ist neu
**Lagezentrum – Russland:** Die Kartendaten springen an der Datumsgrenze (180°) von +180 auf −180. Leaflet (Detailkarte) und MapLibre (3D-Gelände) haben diesen Sprung als waagerechte orange Linie quer übers Land gezeichnet. Neu: `ohneDatumsgrenze()` in `dashboard/lagezentrum.js` macht jeden Ring durchgehend und schiebt ihn neben die Landesmitte. Betroffen waren Russland, Fidschi (und Alaska-Inseln der USA); geprüft mit world-atlas 110m und 50m: danach 0 Sprünge. Antarktis bleibt unverändert (Ring um den Pol).

**Werkstatt – „Der Bauplan war leer“:** Kevins Foto (22:31) stammt von vor PR #74 (gemergt 23:00). Auf aktuellem main greift die Vorlagen-Rettung: mit einem Probe-Claude, der genau wie damals nur Titel/Steckbrief ohne Bauteile liefert, baut Friday den Sportwagen (54 Teile) mit Claudes Titel. - `werkstatt.js`: Rettung liest auch Claudes Kurzbeschreibung und Einleitung.

author: hiobi
body:
Lot 3 du jalon M6 : rendre le plan de recherche visible dans la vue **Tâches** de Gramps Web, sans rien d'automatique.

## Réglage

`GENEALOGISTE_GRAMPS_TACHES` (`config.py`, README, `.env.example`, `docs/gramps-web.md`, wiki Configuration, `diagnostic` → `valeurs.gramps_taches`). Valeur inconnue refusée au démarrage.

- **désactivé (défaut)** : aucune source lue ni écrite comme tâche ; une source `ToDo` reste une source ordinaire, ses attributs `Status` / `Priority` intacts ; `ajouter_tache` / `modifier_tache` refusés ; sorties de `arbre_recherche`, `arbre_lacunes`, `enquete_*`, `gramps_synchroniser` identiques à main (tests).
- **activé** (backend gramps) : opérations et correspondance ci-dessous. Toute création, modification ou clôture passe par `arbre_proposer` (diff + accord + `arbre_appliquer`), annulable.

## Faits amont (lus dans le code, pas devinés)

Frontend gramps-web `v26.11.0` (`8df68202`, image épinglée) et `v26.11.3` (`20c7655d`, `src/taskConstants.js`) ; Gramps `v6.0.8` (`maintenance/gramps60`, `32aa2962`).

| Point | Constat | Source |
|---|---|---|
| reconnaissance | source avec l'étiquette **`ToDo`** (nom exact, sensible à la casse) ; liste : `GET /api/sources/?rules={"rules":[{"name":"HasTag","values":["ToDo"]}]}&locale=…&sort=-gramps_id&extend=tag_list`, puis tri local par statut (Open 1, In Progress 2, Blocked 3, autre 4, Done 5) puis par priorité | `GrampsjsViewTasks.js:72-103`, `taskConstants.js:88-135` |
| statut | `SrcAttribute` de type **personnalisé (chaîne)** `Status` ∈ `Open` / `In Progress` / `Blocked` / `Done` ; tout autre statut est affiché tel quel | `taskConstants.js:17`, `GrampsjsTask.js:211-217` |
| priorité | `SrcAttribute` `Priority`, valeur en chaîne : l'interface écrit `"1"` (High) / `"5"` (Medium) / `"9"` (Low) ; < 5 = haute, 5 = moyenne, > 5 = basse ; absente ou non numérique : sans priorité | `taskConstants.js:19-25, 73-86` |
| valeurs par défaut | création : `Priority "5"` puis `Status "Open"` (dans cet ordre) | `GrampsjsViewNewTask.js:22-25, 172` |
| description | **première note** de `note_list` ; note de type **`To Do`**, avec les mêmes étiquettes que la tâche (donc `ToDo`) | `taskConstants.js:64-71`, `GrampsjsViewNewTask.js:195-201` |
| confidentialité de la description | suit la tâche **seulement à partir de v26.11.3** (v26.11.0 : note créée sans `private`) | `GrampsjsViewNewTask.js:200` (v26.11.3), `GrampsjsViewTask.js:68-101` |
| changements en lot | **aucune transaction** : une requête `PUT /api/sources/<handle>` par tâche (objet complet, l'attribut retiré puis remis **en fin de liste** ; `{_class: "SrcAttribute", type, value}`, en v26.11.0 `{type, value}`) | `GrampsjsViewTasks.js:105-129`, `GrampsjsTasks.js:549-557` |
| liens vers d'autres objets | **aucun** : l'interface ne rattache pas une tâche à une personne | `GrampsjsViewTask.js`, `GrampsjsTask.js` |
| Gramps Desktop | pas de vue Tâches ; le gramplet « To Do » liste les **notes** de type `To Do` (`HasType(["To Do"])`) | `plugins/gramplet/todogramplet.py:98-107` |

## Opérations

- `ajouter_tache` : `titre`*, `description` (première note, `format_texte` possible), `statut` (défaut `Open` ; alias `ouverte`, `en_cours`, `bloquee`, `terminee`), `priorite` (`haute`/`moyenne`/`basse` → `1`/`5`/`9`, ou entier 0-9), `prive` (**défaut true**), `tags`, `personnes` (nommées dans la description, car l'interface ne prévoit aucun lien), `enquete` + `element` (ligne de référence `Enquête Genealogiste : <id> · t1`), `ref`.
- `modifier_tache` : `statut`, `priorite`, `titre`, `description` (la ligne de référence d'enquête est gardée), `prive`, `tags`, `tags_retrait`. Choisi plutôt que `modifier_source` : statut et priorité ne sont pas des champs de source du modèle, et l'opération dédiée se lit mieux dans le diff.
- `ajouter_source` avec `tags: ["ToDo"]` (réglage activé) : tâche comme celle de l'interface (privée, Open, 5). Poser `ToDo` sur une source existante en fait une tâche sans statut (rien n'est inventé).
- Backend fichier : refus explicite (comme `ajouter_billet`).

**Format écrit** : la source reçoit `Priority` puis `Status` (`SrcAttribute`, type personnalisé) ; la note de description a le type `To Do`, l'étiquette `ToDo` et la confidentialité de la source. Seul l'attribut modifié est retiré puis remis en fin de liste, comme le fait l'interface.

## Mécanique du billet généralisée (`objets_interface.py`)

Une seule implémentation pour les billets et les tâches : texte en première note (`_Writer.billet(..., etiquette)`, `_Reader.corps_interface`), confidentialité qui suit la source, garde des vivants (`controler`), exclusion de la preuve (`evidence`, poids 0, `taches_citees`) et des notes de recherche (`notes_generer`, index), objet inchangé jamais réécrit. Messages des billets inchangés (tests #303 verts, sans modification).

- **Notes `Genealogiste:auto`** : aucune note générée n'est ajoutée à une tâche, et une note générée déjà présente est gardée telle quelle. Sinon, un « Lien : … » deviendrait la description affichée. Vérifié en `true` et en `modifies`, et après `gramps_recalculer_notes`.
- **Vivants** : une tâche publique qui nomme une personne présumée vivante ou privée (nom, lien interne, **identifiant seul** `I9`, `personnes`) est refusée ; une tâche privée reçoit un avertissement.
- **Diff** : une ligne `@@ tâche S5 (créée) : statut Open, priorité 5 (moyenne) @@`, ou `statut Open → Done`. Sans elle, ces changements seraient invisibles dans le GEDCOM.
- **Lecture** : `arbre_recherche(etiquette="ToDo", objet="source")` ajoute `tache` (statut, priorité, libellé, ouverte) pour les tâches seulement.

## Correspondance enquête ↔ tâche (aucune écriture cachée)

- **Proposer** : `enquete_reprendre(id, taches=true[, elements])` renvoie `taches_a_proposer`, c'est-à-dire des opérations prêtes pour les pistes et tâches manuelles ouvertes sans tâche liée. Elles passent ensuite par `arbre_proposer`, avec accord.
- **Mémoriser le lien** (côté local) : `enquete_noter(id, tache|piste={id, tache_gramps})`, nouveau champ, `""` pour délier. Sans lien mémorisé, la ligne de référence de la description suffit à retrouver la tâche (`lien: "reference"` + `a_memoriser`).
- **Écarts signalés** dans `enquete_etat`, `enquete_reprendre` (`taches_gramps`) et `gramps_synchroniser` (`taches_ecarts`) : tâche `Done` alors que l'élément est ouvert, l'inverse, ou tâche supprimée / qui a perdu `ToDo`. Chaque écart donne les deux sens, `vers_gramps` (`modifier_tache`) et `vers_enquete` (`enquete_noter`), **jamais exécutés**. Vérifié : le fichier d'état et les transactions Gramps sont inchangés.
- Correspondance des statuts : tâche manuelle `a_faire` ↔ ouverte, `faite`/`abandonnee` ↔ `Done` ; piste `trouve`/`negatif` ↔ `Done`.
- **Pas de nouvel outil** : de simples paramètres sur des outils existants, de même classe (lecture). Catalogue, hooks et `make hooks` sont inchangés.

## Lacunes priorisées

`arbre_lacunes(id, taches=true)` → `taches_a_proposer` : une opération par action, priorité Gramps tirée de la priorité de lacune. Table documentée : 0-1 → haute `1`, 2 → moyenne `5`, 3+ → basse `9`. Uniquement à la demande, une personne à la fois. Il n'existe pas de lacune « source orpheline » dans le code, donc rien à exclure de ce côté.

## Tests

- `tests/test_taches.py` (43 tests) : réglage et diagnostic, désactivé = sorties identiques, création et défauts, statuts et priorités, refus, personnes et référence avec Markdown, modification, étiquette posée ou retirée, vivants (nom, identifiant, `personnes`, passage en public), preuve, notes, format Gramps (attributs, note To Do privée, relu sans réécriture en modes `true` et `modifies`), statut changé comme l'interface, tâche saisie dans l'interface remise en ordre, statut hors liste conservé. Côté serveur (faux Gramps Web) : création de bout en bout, recalcul sans effet, changement par l'interface relu sans réécriture, annulation (et conflit attendu quand l'interface a modifié la tâche), dépôt en file d'une simple modification de s

### Native multi-material and painting integration — work in progress (22 Nov 2026)

**Upstream reference comparison:** CI obtained BambuStudio's own v02.09.01.70 `resources/calib/pressure_advance/auto_pa_line_dual.3mf`. Its project config has **446 keys**, 8 filament IDs/colours/types, 16 filament-self-index/extruder-variant entries, plus referenced 3D object resources. Our initial safe synthetic core3MF has only the small project vector subset, and still SIGABRTs in the upstream CLI. The next engineering milestone is native Bambu project assembly/import parity with this reference, then a passing actual two-tool and painted-facet G-code audit. This is documented in private `MakerVault-Development/CURRENT_STATUS.md`. No Bambu UI enable flags will be added.



- Bambu now shares MakerVault's **owner-verified ordered filament palette**, explicit slot→logical-tool mapping, native per-object `extruder` and clipped `paint_color` 3MF facets; backend and worker carry 2–16 mapped filaments with exact first-profile identity, checksums and existing no-network isolation.
- Added Bambu-native `Metadata/project_settings.config` with bounded actual printer/process/filament identifiers and per-tool colour/type/diameter vectors. Worker validates that Bambu-only native project metadata is complete, with Bambu-specific support for structurally validated joint colour/support/seam/fuzzy facet attributes. These are internal features of the same existing UI—**no Beta settings or new checkboxes**.
- Added Bambu binary CI fixture for **two independently assigned objects** and **one object with painted facets**, including expected actual T0/T1 extrusion and two model-region deposition audits. Unit-level worker contracts and 3MF generation are committed.
- **Real binary acceptance currently FAILS:** official pinned Bambu Studio 02.09.01.70 AppRun exits **-6 (SIGABRT)** on the first synthetic two-tool 3MF before emitting G-code. This persists with complete basic Bambu project filament vectors, distinct job-local filament identities, `--slice 0` or `--slice 1`, and with/without `--export-3mf`. Official single-material STL and fixed core3MF still slice successfully. Known upstream issues [#12872](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/12872), [#12998](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/12998), [#12958](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/12958) indicate similar native 3MF/count assumptions; do not treat this as completed multicolour support.
- Next: compare with vendor-authored genuine two-filament 3MF or Bambu source, resolve native SIGABRT, then verify actual dual-tool deposition and separately confirm painted facet output. Maintain PR **draft**, leave staging installations untouched. CI failure is a real implementation blocker, not a cosmetic Beta gate.

---

## Bambu Studio 02.09.01.70 — integrated engine for MakerVault v1.7.0

**Merge base reconciled:** explicit merge commit `7acd7520384557499db7bb13022986f335484a94` includes the latest merged PR #192. PR #191 now shares `main` ancestry with no prior engine-management changes lost. Existing four-container `makervault-slicer`, Orca and Creality remain unchanged on the user's staging machine.

### Standard interface; no extra Beta switches

- Bambu Studio participates in the **same engine selection, install/update/uninstall, native profile search/import, build-plate and print-review UI** as OrcaSlicer/Creality Print. No Bambu-only opt-in checkbox, Beta label or remembered environment flag is required.
- The normal combined installer lists the exact official 02.09.01.70 AppImage, downloads and verifies it, extracts/probes the native AppRun, then publishes to the existing versioned engine store. `SLICER_BAMBU_BETA_ENABLED` and `MAKERVAULT_SLICER_BAMBU_BETA_ENABLED` have been removed.
- Worker and app recognise Bambu as a standard engine when its installed version, native executable checksum and authenticated health are validated. Full worker/network isolation remains unchanged.
- Real official BBL native **machine, filament and process** catalogue/import support with complete same-source inheritance and included template resolution. Manual owned native Bambu imports and safe custom/process profile edits are supported as for other engines.
- Same native bed selector/filament temperature checks, resolved Bambu build-volume display and normal STL/3MF build plate and G-code library workflows.
- No Bambu-only print-action ban: user-initiated upload/print follows the existing explicit confirmation, printer connection, firmware and G-code validation path. Nothing auto-prints.

### Real executable evidence

- Official Bambu Studio Ubuntu24 AppImage SHA-256: `668dabb1be53c758189ed6bc89935285dea5e0af46216546b1bafd6882e9aff0`; extracted AppRun SHA-256 `eaf5a1c6ff4f0d49d6e0c0bacf106309daa2c822ca1ebe8739067699e6cdaef4`.
- Pinned real X1 Carbon / 0.20mm Standard / Bambu PLA Basic profile inheritance produced extrusion-validated **STL (137,742 B)** and **core 3MF (137,694 B)** G-code in [offline container CI 44983450397](https://github.com/gavrd7/MakerVault/actions/runs/44983450397).
- Both formats also passed in the *same immutable Orca-based image* as the production combined slicer with the worker's outbound network filter: [CI 44983920228](https://github.com/gavrd7/MakerVault/actions/runs/44983920228).

### Remaining verification before review/merge

- Complete latest-head worker/backend/frontend, isolated container, Orca regression and Bambu real-binary Actions. Fix test failures; earlier green candidate smoke is not the same as all integration CI passing.
- Stage on the user's Debian test server via the normal combined image rebuild, install Bambu using the existing engine manager, import a native printer/process/filament and slice one actual STL. Verify Orca/Creality remain healthy; do not remove volumes.
- Real multi-filament/toolchange and object-paint semantics still need Bambu-specific exporter and regression coverage. Unsupported native payloads must error rather than silently discard the user's material/paint choices; this is a technical capability constraint, not a Beta activation flag.
- Review G-code/printer compatibility before physical print. No tests have sent commands to a live printer. No PR merge until owner acceptance.

The separate operator guidance is in `docs/development/bambu-studio-staging.md` and future docs PR #40. **This PR remains draft until CI and staging acceptance.**

This layer covers the recommended configuration, analytics, SQL queries, and exporting guides.

These pages read like a list of system facts. This rewrite makes them read like a teammate explaining how to get something done: it talks to you directly, joins related facts, and leads with the task. Commands, flags, config keys, links, anchors, and code blocks are unchanged except for the corrections below. Gemini 4 Neon wrote the prose; Claude Opus checked every claim against the code and every rewritten sentence against the original meaning.

## Fact corrections

- Setup prints one provider probe (the Voyage multimodal probe) that needs private seed files, not two.
- `list-labels` shows up to 50 labels by default, not all of them.
- CSV and table query output prints the publication time, cache generation, and stale reason to stderr, but not pending additions.
- The list of known `message_type` values now matches the code.
- `export-attachment`: `--json` and `--base64` can't be combined, and neither works with an `--output` file path; `-o -` works with both.

Model used: Gemini 4 Neon (writing), Opus 5.5 (fact checks)

author: saltedtan
body:
## Intent

Add tracked local pre-commit and pre-push Git hooks in .githooks/, Makefile install-hooks and print-format-exclude targets, automated tests in test/test_git_hooks.py, and contributor docs.

## What Changed

- Adds tracked Git hooks under `.githooks/`. `pre-commit` builds `build/virgil-lsp` and runs `format --check` on the staged index content of `.v3` files, skipping the directories in `FORMAT_EXCLUDE`. When a staged file is under `clients/vscode/`, it also runs `npm run check` there; if `node_modules` is missing, it prints a notice and continues. `pre-push` runs `make check-format` and `make test-unit` on the working tree. When the pushed commits touch `clients/vscode/` and `node_modules` exists, it also runs `npm run check && npm test`. A push that only deletes refs or has nothing to update skips every check.
- Adds two Makefile targets. `install-hooks` runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. `print-format-exclude` prints the `FORMAT_EXCLUDE` list so that `pre-commit` and `make check-format` use the same exclusions.
- Adds `test/test_git_hooks.py` to the `SUITES` list in the Makefile. It runs both hooks in temporary repositories, using stand-in `make`, `npm` and `virgil-lsp`. Contributor docs (`docs/development.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`) and `CHANGELOG.md` now describe the hooks and how to skip or disable them.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The hooks are opt-in local tooling for contributors and don't affect the server, CI, or users. Round 1's fixes check out: no-op pushes are skipped and tested, actionlint is gone, the docs say which checks read the index and which read the working tree, and the exclude-list test now compares against `make -n check-format`. What remains is workflow friction and a missing notice, not correctness.

## Testing

I ran the new `test/test_git_hooks.py` suite (23 tests, all passing), then drove the hooks for real in a throwaway clone of the target commit, using the real Virgil submodule and a local bare remote. `make install-hooks` set `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks`, and `print-format-exclude` lists the same directories that `make -n check-format` excludes. Pre-commit rejected unformatted staged .v3 content and printed the fix hint. It judged the staged content, not the working tree, in both partial-staging directions. It skipped directories in `FORMAT_EXCLUDE`, and `--no-verify` bypassed it. Without node_modules it printed the VS Code skip notice. With node_modules installed it rejected a staged TypeScript type error and accepted valid TypeScript. Pre-push blocked a push whose tree had an unformatted file. It called `make` zero times for an up-to-date push and for a deletion-only push. A clean push ran `make check-format` and `make test-unit` (1287 unit tests passed), and a push touching clients/vscode also ran `npm run check && npm test` (358 passed, 0 failed); both pushes succeeded. Every scenario passed. The transcripts are in the evidence directory; there is no UI surface. The throwaway clone has been removed and the worktree is unchanged.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 14 of 14 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Contributor runs `make install-hooks` in a fresh clone: core.hooksPath becomes .githooks and the skip/disable hint is printed | ✅ pass | live | install-hooks.txt |
| `make print-format-exclude` lists exactly the directories `make check-format` passes as :(exclude) pathspecs | ✅ pass | live | install-hooks.txt (print-format-exclude vs make -n check-format) |
| Committing an unformatted staged .v3 file is rejected with the `format --write` hint (real built formatter) | ✅ pass | live | pre-commit-real.txt S2 |
| Adversarial partial staging: staged copy unformatted, working tree fixed but not staged, so the commit is still rejected; staging the fix lets it through | ✅ pass | live | pre-commit-real.txt S3/S4 |
| Staged copy formatted, working tree edited to be unformatted: commit accepted because the index is what gets checked | ✅ pass | live | pre-commit-real.txt S5 |
| Unformatted .v3 under the excluded test/fixtures/ directory is committed without a format failure | ✅ pass | live | pre-commit-real.txt S6 |
| `git commit --no-verify` bypasses a failing pre-commit | ✅ pass | live | pre-commit-real.txt S7 |
| Pushing a branch whose tree has an unformatted .v3 is blocked by `make check-format` and the remote ref is unchanged | ✅ pass | live | pre-push-real.txt P3 |
| Adversarial: a push with nothing to update ('Everything up-to-date') runs no checks (0 make calls) | ✅ pass | live | pre-push-real.txt P1 (PATH shim make log empty) |
| Adversarial: a deletion-only push skips every check even with an unformatted working tree | ✅ pass | live | pre-push-real.txt P2 |
| Pushing a clean branch runs `make check-format` then `make test-unit` (1287 unit tests) and the push succeeds | ✅ pass | live | pre-push-real.txt P4, p4-push-output.log |
| Committing a clients/vscode change without node_modules prints the skip notice and lets the commit through | ✅ pass | live | vscode-hooks.txt V1 |
| With node_modules installed, a staged TypeScript type error is rejected by `npm run check` and valid TypeScript is accepted | ✅ pass | live | vscode-hooks.txt V2/V3 |
| Pushing commits that touch clients/vscode also runs `npm run check && npm test` (358 pass, 0 fail) and the push succeeds | ✅ pass | live | vscode-hooks.txt V4, v4-push-output.log |

author: oghenenoghie
body:
Stage C of ADR 0008, the last of the three integration stages: the first endpoints a school's SIS, LMS or portal can call with its API key. They read the school's classes, sync students, and read released results.

## Decisions (made on 2026-11-21)
- **A student added by an integration gets an account without a password.** The integration sends the student's ID, name and username. A school admin sets the password in the web app (or SSO, later), so passwords never pass through the other system.
- **Only school admins deactivate students.** Integrations add, update, enrol and move students, but never disable an account. A faulty sync can't lock students out before an exam.
- **Results are scores only:** score, total marks, percentage and times, per student and exam.

## What's in it
- **Endpoints** (`app/integrations/public.py`). Each needs one permission, sees only the key's school, counts against the rate limit and writes an audit entry, reads included.

  | Endpoint | Permission |
  |---|---|
  | `GET /api/v1/academic-sessions`, `/classes`, `/subjects` | `classes:read` |
  | `GET /api/v1/candidates`, `/candidates/{external_id}` | `candidates:read` |
  | `PUT /api/v1/candidates/{external_id}` | `candidates:write` |
  | `GET /api/v1/released-results`, `/released-results/{exam_id}`, `/candidates/{external_id}/results` | `results:read` |
- **Student sync** (`PUT /candidates/{external_id}`, with `display_name`, `username` and optional `class_id`):
  - External IDs belong to each integration, so two systems' IDs never clash.
  - An unknown ID with an unused username creates a student account without a password (201, `created`).
  - An unknown ID with an existing **student** account's username links that student (`linked`), so schools that already enrolled students don't get duplicates. Staff accounts are refused, and so is a student who already has a different ID from this integration.
  - A known ID updates the name and username, and the class: it enrols the student, or moves them within the session (`updated`, or `unchanged` when nothing changed).
  - Never: passwords, disabling or re-enabling accounts, or removing a student from a class.
  - Repeating the same request changes nothing, so retries are safe.
- **Results:** only published exams whose release policy shows scores, either released by a teacher or set to show immediately. Scores include teachers' marks, as students see them. An exam not yet released is 409. Responses contain no questions, answers or answer keys.
- **Error envelope** (`app/integrations/envelope.py`):
  - Every integration endpoint, `/integrations/me` included, answers errors as `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id"}}`.
  - Validation errors add `details` (the field and why, never the value sent).
  - `X-Request-ID` is echoed, or a `req_...` one is made. It's also stored on the audit entry.
  - Bodies over `INTEGRATION_MAX_BODY_KB` (default 64) get 413.
  - Endpoints for people keep FastAPI's `{"detail": ...}`.
- **Docs:**
  - ADR 0008: stage C decisions 7 to 11, and stages A to C marked built, since PR #32 built B.
  - The API README: an endpoint table and the error codes.
  - The integrations guide and API contract: what's live.
  - `.env.example`.
  - CLAUDE.md: its stale integration notes, and garbled arrows and ≥ signs repaired.
  - The project skill.
- **No migration:** students reuse `candidate_external_identities`, with the integration as source system.

## Testing
- `tests/test_integration_api.py` has 57 tests. They cover:
  - each endpoint refusing a key without its permission, and every endpoint refusing a missing key;
  - another school's key seeing nothing;
  - the envelope and request ids;
  - 413 before reading a large body;
  - the rate limit on public endpoints;
  - sessions, classes and subjects;
  - every sync case: created without a password, repeated unchanged, updated, class kept when left out, linking an existing student (one with a candidate record, and one without), one ID per student per integration, another integration's own IDs, staff usernames refused, username clashes, bad input refused with no rows written, validation details without values, external ID characters, never disabling or unenrolling, classes in another session;
  - listing and reading students;
  - results waiting for release, immediate results, scores only (no keys or answers), unpublished exams, unknown students;
  - audit entries for reads and their activity view, no entry for refused requests, a disabled integration refused everywhere.
- `tests/test_integration_auth.py` and `tests/test_integrations_admin.py` now expect the envelope.
- The integration tests pass on SQLite and PostgreSQL 16.
- `ruff check .` passes. The full backend suite was still running locally on SQLite and PostgreSQL when this was opened; CI runs both.

This pull request exists to show a **failing test** being caught by the required CI checks. It is a deliberate demonstration introduced by the project owner for the assignment. It must not be merged, and it will stay open.

One assertion in `backend/test/config.test.js` (the test "falls back to the default for a non-numeric port") was changed from `toBe(3000)` to `toBe(3001)`. The application code in `backend/src/config.js` is **not** changed and correctly defaults to 3000, so the test now asserts a wrong value.
