author: jason733i
body:
Closes #377

## What shipped

A profile opts in with `explore: base` (it needs `app` and `flavour: web`). The plan job then boots the base revision's app, serves it to the planner over the exploration channel (#87), and the planner plans its flows from what it was shown. Absent or `explore: off`, every new step skips and the plan step's container is the one it was.

- **Profile.** `explore: base | off`. Refused on a target or client profile, without `flavour: web`, and for any other value (there is no `head`).
- **The channel reaches nare for real.** Before this, qare handed nare the channel as `QARE_EXPLORATION_*` environment variables that no nare release reads, with `--tools none`, so a real session never saw a tool. Now a bridge (`startExplorationBridge`, `packages/core/src/explore-bridge.ts`) runs on loopback inside the plan step and speaks MCP Streamable HTTP. `NareAgentRunner` hands nare `--mcp-config` naming it and `--tools explore__observe,explore__snapshot,explore__navigate`, and nothing else. Each call crosses the channel through the channel's own client, and every result comes back fenced as untrusted data. I checked the bridge against the official Python MCP client (`mcp` 2.3.0, the library nare's client is built on): initialize, list, call and error results all worked. `capture` is left out, because nare hands an MCP result to the model as text and a screenshot would arrive as a page-sized base64 string.
- **Selectors come from the explored page (criterion 2).** An element reference may carry `page` (a path on the app, such as `/settings`) beside `at` (its snapshot path). The bridge records every page it snapshotted and the node paths each held. When the plan explored, `exploredGap` checks every role and name element of a flow or visual check against those records: no page or no path, a page never snapshotted, a path not in that page's snapshot, or a test id (which a snapshot does not show) is corrected once and then refused, like every other plan gap.
- **CLI.** `qare explore boot` boots and seeds the base app from the base tree, then exits, writing `app.json` and `isolation.json`. `qare explore serve` drives a browser on the app with `navigate` held to the app's origin, and serves the channel until it is stopped. `qare plan --explore <endpoint>` checks that the channel answers, starts the bridge and plans through it. It refuses an endpoint when the profile does not explore.
- **Pipeline (plan job).** New steps: read the profile switch, pull the web image by digest, find the runner's docker, boot, serve, then tear down and upload `exploration-logs` (both `always()`). The plan step gains `--network host` and `--explore`, and nothing else.

## Trust boundary (criterion 4)

Recorded as ADR-0011. Rule 7 is about pull request code, and the plan job only checks out the base. The design keeps every rule:

- No pull request code runs in the plan job. The app is built from the base checkout, never from the prebuilt `base.image`: that image is trusted by the revision label its pusher wrote, which is enough in execute (which holds nothing) but not beside the model key. The build cache is not read either.
- The boot and serve steps name no secret and run before the plan step writes the key file. The boot is the only step handed the runner's docker, and it has exited before the key exists. The serve container (browser and exploration server) gets no docker access and mounts only its ready-file directory, so nothing qare starts can `docker inspect` the planner's container while it holds the key.
- `navigate` is held to the app's origin on both sides (serve and bridge), so a prompt injected through the diff cannot point the browser at the runner's metadata service.
- If the boot, seed or channel fails, the plan job stops by name. It never plans blind.

What remains, and pipeline.md says so: the base revision's own compose services run on the machine while the plan step holds the key. That is merged repository code, the same trust the plan job already places in the base checkout's profile.

## Out of scope

- Exploring the head (the sandbox split #87 describes).
- The host MCP channel (#93) has the same unread-environment gap. Filed as #399 instead of widening this PR.

## Tests

- core: `explore-bridge.test.ts` (3), `explore-page.test.ts` (3), `plan-explored.test.ts` (4), and new cases in `profile.test.ts`, `plan.test.ts` and `nare-runner.test.ts`.
- cli: `explore-command.test.ts` (4), `plan-explore-command.test.ts` (4: a fake nare that really speaks MCP to the bridge), `pipeline-explore.test.ts` (4: the switch, no secret in any exploration step, no docker access for serve, and the plan step's docker arguments off and on), plus a web-image pull case in `workflow-images.test.ts`.
- Linux preflight (node:22-bookworm, non-root, with docker): lint, build and typecheck, and the full test suite all passed.
- End to end in CI: `scripts/explore-boot.sh`, a new step of the `electron-driver` job, which already builds the web image. It runs the plan job's own exploration steps (read the switch, find docker, boot, serve, tear down) against `examples/compose-app/explore`. The base app really boots under compose and a real Chromium is served beside it. The serve container is checked to have no docker socket and nothing in its environment beyond its image's and `HOME`. The real page's heading is read over the channel, and navigation off the app is refused. `qare plan --explore` then runs with a nare stand-in that speaks MCP: a plan naming the heading the page showed is kept with `page: "/"`, and one naming an element the page did not show is refused. Teardown is checked to remove the browser and take the app down. I ran it locally against images built from this branch, and it found a real bug the stubbed tests missed: `qare explore boot` probed the health URL without the run's values filled in. That is fixed, with a test.
- QARE self-check: `.qa/checks/explore.mjs` (`pipeline` and `plan`; the channel hand-off is proven by the end-to-end CI step), declared as `explore-check` in `.qa/config.yml`. It runs the checkout's source without a build, and I ran it in the published image.

### Quality gate changes

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: adds one step, `scripts/explore-boot.sh`, to the `electron-driver` job. It only adds a check and changes no existing one.
- `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml`: #377 asks for this. The plan job gains the exploration steps, each gated on `explore: base`, and the plan step gains `--network host` and `--explore` only when exploration is on. No check, gate or job is weakened, and no step continues on error.
- `packages/cli/test/workflow-images.test.ts`: the pin "all later pipeline containers receive the immutable digest reference" now expects `steps.explore-image.outputs.digest` for exactly the plan job's three exploration containers (named in the test) and `steps.image.outputs.digest` for every other container, as before. Those three steps run the web image, which carries the browser, pulled by its own step. That step gets the same resolve-then-pull-by-digest tests as every other pull, so the pin is extended, not loosened.
- `packages/core/test/nare-runner.test.ts`: the #87 case that pinned the exploration channel to environment now pins it to `--mcp-config` and an explicit `--tools` allowlist, and asserts the environment is not set. The old pin described a contract no nare release implements.
- `packages/core/test/explore.test.ts`: two prompt pins now expect the tool names the session calls (`explore__observe` and so on) and no endpoint URL, since the model cannot call a URL.
- `.qa/config.yml`: adds the `explore-check` command for the QARE self-run.

### Disclosure review

The tests and the check use loopback addresses and `169.254.169.254`, the well-known link-local metadata address, as a navigation target that must be refused. None of them is a real host.

### Code review gate

Gate: `self` (`VIVI_REVIEW_TOOL=self`). I reviewed the diff

author: filiphsps
body:
Every positional random draw (`XoroshiroPositionalRandomFactory.at`) builds its source through `XoroshiroRandomSource.fromLanes`. That called `new XoroshiroRandomSource(0n, 0n)` to get the all-zero substitute state, and then overwrote the lanes. The constructor ran `asLong` twice and a BigInt OR every time, just to detect the zero seed.

`fromLanes` now sets a module flag while it constructs, and the constructor then starts from the substitute state without reading its BigInt arguments. Seeds passed to the constructor directly are unchanged.

## Counts

`chunkGeneration` benchmark, 64 chunks: 1,413,654 sources per run (3,272 per terrain tile) skip the BigInt checks. The surface pass's vertical gradients make most of them; the aquifer, ore veins and surface depth make the rest.

The chunk digest is unchanged (`b7740abd…`). A new test checks that a BigInt-seeded source built after one from lanes still reads its seed. The existing tests already hold `at` to the BigInt reference and the all-zero lanes to Java's substitution. The worldgen, prismarine generator and parity `worldgen.*` suites pass (77 files, 998 tests).

Indicative only: in a Bun CPU profile of the terrain stage, the constructor fell from 3.5% to 0.2% of samples, and the run's total samples from 12,259 to 11,765, at load average 4.5–5.

author: thenetherwatcher
body:
Fixes #2140.

`sumWeights` comes from `floats.Sum`, which on amd64 adds in a different order than the running sum in `empiricalQuantile` and `linInterpQuantile`. The running sum can end one ULP short of `p*sumWeights`, so the loop falls through to `panic("impossible")`. Both now return the last sample instead, as `type7Quantile` already does.

Added `TestQuantileWeightsRounding`; it fails on amd64 without the change (passes on arm64 either way). `go test ./stat/...` passes on amd64 and arm64.

author: itechmeat
body:
- `o2b search status` and the expand surface no longer refuse an index of
  the previous schema with advice to rebuild: they perform the same
  in-place upgrade a query performs. An index no upgrade can repair keeps
  the rebuild advice.
- The MCP server start no longer launches a background rebuild for such an
  index; the first read upgrades it in place, as on the command line. One
  shared plan decides between current, upgrade in place, refresh in place
  and rebuild.
- A rebuild that finds both parked names held and unreleasable refuses
  before the build instead of after it, with the same message, and writes
  no staging file. The checks only the swap can make (the live index's
  integrity, a removal that fails) stay at the swap.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Older search indexes are upgraded in place when possible, preserving stored embeddings.
  * Search status and reads handle older schemas consistently, and status provides rebuild advice when an index cannot be upgraded.
  * Reads retry after another process upgrades the index.
  * Background maintenance repairs indexes that need more than a schema upgrade.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Rebuilds can refuse before building when parked indexes prevent a safe swap, without changing existing parked files.
  * Rebuilds continue to restore a parked index when the live index fails its integrity check.

author: shahbaz242630
body:
S209 tamper re-run (ST10), TR-1 part A: the jobs copy never forgets the chain heads it saw when it loses the lease. Phase 6 (6F1 gate prep). BR-12, BR-13, BR-15 (security-critical).

**The hole (fresh gap map, real):** the digest kept seen heads only in memory and wiped them (`forget()`) whenever the jobs copy lost its lease; the database owner can make it lose the lease with one UPDATE to `platform_controls.job_lease`, then cut a chain back above the last anchor and have money handed off.

**The fix (plan `TR1-Plan.md` §1.3 A):**
- No forget: heads, facts and coverage survive a lease loss; a `writes` option gates only record, flush, deltas and snapshots.
- A jobs copy that doesn't lead follows the store like a web copy (`anchors_follow`, gated by the new `onlyWhileNotLeading`), so rebases are still read.
- A snapshot only after a whole read made while writing (review finding); the delta look-back moves only at the end of a whole listing, and from the snapshot after a quiet start (review findings).
- New error `jobs.lease_taken_early` (plain words): the lease refused while our own term still runs can only be someone else's hand. Its Sev-1 alert comes with part B's infrastructure.

**Proof:** new `lease-taken.db.test.ts` end to end: the owner takes the lease, the copy leads again, a cut back is refused (no rail call, alarm, organisation held); on the old code the same test paid. Independent review, two fix rounds each re-reviewed; an independent mutation pass 11/11 killed (plus the builder's own).

The witness log for split copies (parts B-D) follows in its own PRs; part B's infrastructure needs the partner's access + deployers + Approve.

author: reynanfc
body:
Closes #17

## Motivo
A convocação (RET-01) reserva o objeto, mas o funcionário ainda não tinha como fechar o ciclo no balcão. Este card fecha o fluxo principal da demo: objeto achado → sugestão → convocação → **retirada**. É caminho crítico e destrava o RET-04 (#18).

## O que muda

| Rota (só funcionário e admin) | O que faz |
|---|---|
| `GET /summons` | Convocações Ativas, das que vencem primeiro, cada uma com o checklist |
| `GET /summons/{id}` | Convocação com o risco, o que conferir e as verificações que bastam (RF28) |
| `POST /summons/{id}/pickup` | Retirada com documento, matrícula e verificação (RF29) |
| `POST /summons/{id}/refusal` `{"reason": "..."}` | Recusa com motivo (RF31) |

```
POST /summons/{id}/pickup
  → @Valid: documento, matrícula e verificação (400)
  → convocação existe? (404)
  → a verificação basta para o risco? VerificationRule.requireAccepted (400, nada gravado)
  → Summons Ativa → Concluída, gravada primeiro com @Version (409 se já decidida)
  → objeto Devolvido, sugestão Concluída, perda Concluída, Pickup gravada, histórico
  → PickupRegisteredEvent (retirada.registrada)

POST /summons/{id}/refusal
  → Summons Ativa → Recusada (com motivo)
  → objeto Disponível; sugestões Em espera do objeto → Nova (RN18)
  → perda → Recusado (final) e as outras sugestões dela → Encerrada (D26)
  → recusa conta para o estudante; na 3ª, ele não registra perdas (RN12)
```

### Por partes (um commit por etapa)
1. **Strategy por risco** (`pickup.service.verification`): `VerificationRule` com `LowRiskRule`, `MediumRiskRule`, `HighRiskRule` e `DocumentRule`. Cada uma traz o checklist, as verificações aceitas e o que o estudante leva. O `VerificationRules` recusa subir se faltar regra para algum risco. O `WhatToBring` do RET-01 foi absorvido.
2. **APIs dos módulos**:
   - `founditems.api`: `handOver` e `release` em `FoundItemReservations`.
   - `lossreports.api`: `complete`, `refuse` e `release` em `LossReportSummons`, e a interface nova `StudentRefusals`.
   - `matching.api`: `complete` e `refuse` em `SuggestionSummons`.
   - Tudo com `MANDATORY` e histórico. As recusas ficam em `LossReporter.refusals`, a linha do limite de 5 registros.
3. **`CounterService`**: retirada e recusa numa transação. A `Summons` é gravada primeiro, então retirada e recusa simultâneas disputam a mesma linha e só uma passa (teste em Virtual Threads).
4. **Rotas** com Swagger em `CounterApi` e testes MockMvc (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409).
5. **Documentação** (abaixo).

### Decisão da equipe: a perda recusada se encerra
A seção 6.2 mandava a perda voltar a Aberto depois da recusa, mas aí ela ficaria editável, contra a RN06. Agora a perda passa a **Recusado**, uma situação final nova, e o estudante registra de novo se ainda procura o objeto. O vencimento (RET-02) continua devolvendo a Aberto. Está registrado na **D26**.

### Para o RET-02 (@p1lloww)
- `FoundItemReservations.release` e `LossReportSummons.release` já existem para o vencimento.
- A `Summons` tem `@Version`. Grave-a primeiro (`saveAndFlush`), como o `CounterService`, para o vencimento disputar a mesma linha que a retirada e a recusa.

### Fora deste card
- Desbloqueio pelo administrador → #75 (ADM-07, novo)
- Encerrar as outras sugestões do objeto entregue (RF33) → RET-06 (#46)
- E-mail de confirmação → AVI-02 (#47)
- Atalho de balcão sem convocação → RET-04 (#18)

## Documentação
- **Novo:** [`docs/tecnico/retirada.md`](docs/tecnico/retirada.md), com diagramas UML:
  - de onde vem o risco;
  - o diagrama de classes do Strategy;
  - as sequências da retirada e da recusa;
  - a concorrência, as rotas e os testes.

  **Confira se os diagramas Mermaid aparecem desenhados no "Files changed".**
- **POOA:** seção "Strategy: conferência por risco no balcão", com diagrama e perguntas prováveis, mais o lock otimista do balcão.
- **D26**, nota na D25, glossário, índices (`docs/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), `convocacao.md` e declaração de IA.

## Testes
`./mvnw verify` local: **580 testes, 0 falhas**. Novos:
- `VerificationRulesTest`: 14 testes;
- `CounterServiceTest`: 15 testes, inclusive o de concorrência;
- `CounterControllerTest`: 12 testes;
- casos de bloqueio em `LossReportServiceTest` e `LossReporterRepositoryTest`;
- a situação Recusado em `LossReportStatusTest`.

Banco local: as colunas novas aceitam nulo ou têm valor padrão. Não precisa de `docker compose down -v`.

body:
Merges current `origin/main` into `phase-1-proven`, so the M74.1 PRs get #7271 (12 GB of swap for the rust test parts; the 12 GB compile no longer kills the runner, exit 143). Same pattern as #7223. `phase-1-proven` has moved twice while this was open; each time its new tip was merged in (one trivial both-tests-kept conflict each: `hooks/tests.rs`, `eventlog/tests.rs`).

## Conflicts with `main` and how each was resolved (11 files, 19 hunks)

Both sides kept throughout. `phase-1-proven` added `timings` and the scenarios' resolver seam `names`; `main` added the `network` lift (Q308 follow-up item 5, #7105).

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `tools/ci-scope.mjs`**: `phase-1-proven` moved the macOS confinement steps into the `macos-sandbox-tests` composite action; `main` added a ports-off step and widened the scope regex. Kept the action call, took `main`'s regex additions (`floor_tests|codex|opencode|claude`, `names.rs`), and moved `main`'s new ports-off step into `.github/actions/macos-sandbox-tests/action.yml` (id `ports-off`) so the sandbox scenarios' macOS job and the nightly run it too.
- **`sandbox/plan.rs`**: `Telling` and `Hearing` carry `network` beside `timings`/`names`, in the struct, the (hand-written) `Default` impls, `Hearing::here` and `Plan::serving`.
- **`sandbox/egress.rs`**: `Serving` has both `names` and `network`; `Allowed` gets both.
- **`sandbox/hosted.rs`, `sandbox.rs`, `app/.../chats.rs`, `hostedconfinement/tests.rs`, `hostedsessions/tests.rs`**: initialisers take both `timings`/`names` and `network`.
- **`sandbox/egress/tests.rs`, `sandbox/hosted/tests.rs`**: both sides' tests kept.

## What the merge needed beyond the textual conflicts (each found by a red check)

- **Signatures**: `main`'s new egress tests call `Serving::of` / `Serving::confined` without timings (pass `Timings::production()`); `session::Confine` gained `lifted` (added in `fake-harness/tests/under_the_wrap.rs`, `tests/recordings/tests/record.rs`); `Settings` gained a private field, so `scenarios/host.rs` reads the policy with `Settings::from_text`.
- **Recorded harness sessions re-recorded (contract moved)**: `main`'s forge lock (#7241) gives a chat on a repo that claims the merge lock `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GLOBAL/SYSTEM/KEY_0/VALUE_0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT`, `GLAB_CONFIG_DIR` and an empty `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`. Checked in the harness-recordings job's artifacts for claude 2.1.325 (`recording.json`, `asks-recording.json`), codex 0.169.0 and opencode 1.19.5 (`recording.json`), and, after the second base merge, claude's `recording.json` again. Each diff is additions of those variables (`<withheld>`) and nothing else; turns unchanged.
- **`tools/sandbox-scenarios.test.mjs`**: finds the rust job's build command inside the memory-sampling script `main`'s #7200 made of that step.
- **`sandbox/claude_tests.rs`**: `main`'s #7105 test expects `Edit(//**/purlis-serve/**)`; `phase-1-proven`'s fewest-rules folding (#6961) writes the folder's own rule, `Edit(//**/purlis-serve)`, which holds the same. The test asserts that.
- **Scenarios** (`app/src-tauri/src/scenarios/`): `resolved_under` takes the sandbox level from the project's own `[sandbox] mode` (it outranks the template's since #7105), and "under strict every family is enforced" compares each family's mode (`Resolved::all` carries level `Floor`); `switches.json` lists the five test-only seams #7105 added on a scenario's path; the forge cells run the real `glab` by path, since #7230 puts a refusing shim named `glab` first for a persona that declares none (the shim's words are `tools.rs`'s tests), and read the merge hold's new "cannot name the request" wording (#7195).

## Open: one scenario red, a gap between `main` and the Linux wrap, not caused by this merge

`scenarios::a_chat_runs_under_the_template_its_scenario_names` (sandbox-scenarios-linux; the other 83 of 84 pass). Under the `open` template `ports` is off, and `main`'s #7105 then writes `(deny network-outbound (remote unix-socket (path-regex …)))` (`seatbelt::every_local_held`) into the profile. The Linux supervisor's reader (`crates/linux-sandbox/src/profile.rs`, `remote()`) knows only `path-literal` there, so it fails closed: "the sandbox profile could not be read: the socket filter …, so nothing was started". A Linux chat under `open` (or any `ports = "off"`) does not start on `main` either; `main` has no Linux scenario for it. The fix is to read `path-regex` there as `Filter::Unix` over the regex crate it already uses for file paths, with a test; it is Linux sandbox code, so it is left for a decision and not made here.

## Checked locally

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. purlis-core lib tests: 16,588 passed, 1,005 failed, all in tests that bind sockets, run git or read vaults and are refused by this sandbox ("Operation not permitted"); CI is their judge, and all four rust test parts, which this change's swap keeps alive, pass there.

author: itsmrad
body:
## Context
Users can stop renewal or undo scheduled cancellation without changing settled access. HOLD-FOR-USER. Stacked on #939 feat/dodo-billing-operator; preserves #927's hold. Fresh main and operator 4b26970ce990a153c5b645e6f1a47475d12b1697 merged normally with no conflicts; no deletion implementation merged.

## Approach
Claim the caller's active subscription atomically, dispatch one PATCH, and verify fresh subscription/customer reads. Each claim persists a 60-second dispatch deadline matching route maxDuration. The trusted adapter deadline prevents dispatch at entry/pre-PATCH after expiry and aborts at min(15 seconds, remaining window). Confirmed/unknown/crashed claims clear only on canonical readStartedAt strictly after max(write deadline, recorded result time), never by time alone. Definite refusal releases; revision checks reject late results. Optional deadline is absent for deletion executor calls, preserving that adapter contract.

Pending poll findings emit claim/read-specific receipt IDs even for unchanged active status, so lost/crashed route results reach normal fenced reconciliation. Reread IDs use Set deduplication before the three-resource cap. Canonical cancelAt uses only settled paidThrough; no settled period means no earned cancellation timestamp. Uncancel requires an unexpired settled period, active canonical provider state and no hold. Optional fields/index need no backfill; existing claims lacking the new deadline use claim time +60 seconds.

Management retains strict empty JSON, established same-origin guards, Clerk JWT plus internal key, rate limits, no-store and validated config independent of checkout flags. Feature-local authorization follows billingCheckout's validateInternalKey→verifyAuth→both owner token and subject checks; unrelated admin/auth consolidation is outside this change.

## Out of scope
Portal (10a2), deletion implementation, runtime provider calls, deploy/env, merge or ready. No control changes settled periods, grants/lots, recovery markers or refunds. Client deadline/abort prevents late dispatch but cannot establish when an already accepted provider request finishes: the operational window is not provider transaction fencing; late completion behavior remains a stage-13 test/support gate.

## Verification
Added pure, mocked adapter/route and convex-test regressions: pending poll→unique receipt→reconcile despite previously processed active receipt; route crash/unknown/lost refused result; second revision; Set dedupe; deferred PATCH with interleaved canonical read/opposing claim; expired dispatch/abort boundaries; post-window fresh read; late result thresholds/revision fences. Both held-first-payment/no-earned-period and prior-settled-P1/blocked-P2 cases remain, preserving money and processed-cancellation assertions.

No local typecheck/lint/test/build/install/server/deploy runs per instruction. Exact-head CI PASSED on 97a963346345a42067fc3834538a204a85199ecf: Typecheck, lint, test, build and Mobile typecheck and lint (run 44934199354). Independent review requested changes on the earlier head; fixes await lane re-review. Pinned published dodopayments@2.63.0 source evidence is in docs/billing-stage10.md (subscription PATCH/echo; customer business binding; immediate payload reserved for deletion). Scoped-key permissions and real cancellation timing remain stage-13 gates.

author: autumnsgrove
body:
Part of #1677 — the evict-and-assert criterion.

## Why the flush was not enough

`TenantDO` caches config in memory and in its own SQLite. #1696 fixed `refreshConfig()` so a D1 miss clears both — but the only evidence a removal ever had was "the flush returned 200". Nine subdomains answered `200` with the deleted account's name for two weeks after their rows were gone, and every signal said they had been removed.

So eviction now has two steps: **flush, then ask the site.**

## What it does

After a successful flush, the ops worker fetches `https://<subdomain>.grove.place/` and decides:

| answer | meaning | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `404` | Aspen's answer for a subdomain with no active tenant (#1734 made it a real 404, not a 200 page saying so) | gone |
| `410`, or any `3xx` | an old subdomain redirected elsewhere is not serving *this* grove | gone |
| `200` | the deleted tenant is still online — the shape of the original bug | **failed step** |
| `5xx`, `403`, timeout | we cannot tell | **failed step** |

A failed step is the existing machinery doing what it already does: the removal reports incomplete, **the account holder is not emailed** (the #1737 rule), and the login is kept. Not-confirmed is not confirmed.

It goes out over the public internet rather than a service binding on purpose — a binding skips the edge cache and would answer a kinder question than the one an operator is asking.

`SITE_FETCH` on the worker's `Env` is the injectable so no test reaches the network; production leaves it unset. The fetch is explicitly `.bind()`-ed, because a detached binding `fetch` throws *Illegal invocation* (#1740).

## Tests

Four new cases in `tenant-remove.test.ts`: 404 succeeds and probes the right URL, 302 succeeds, 200 is recorded as `the site is still serving` and suppresses the email, and an unreachable site fails closed with `could not confirm`. 213 pass in the service.

## Still open on #1677

The issue also asks for a regression test that creates a fixture tenant, warms `/config`, deletes the row and asserts a 404 end to end. That is an integration run against the dev stack (the TenantDO-level half is already covered by `TenantDO.test.ts:107`), so I would run it live on a fixture and record the result on the issue rather than pretend a unit test is the same thing.

author: ewerttonbravo
body:
## Task 02: Read products CSV
The domain turns the lines of a products CSV into `Product`s and reports every invalid line with its line number and reason, never dropping one silently. Reading the file stays outside the domain (task 03).

### Acceptance criteria
| # | Criterion | Evidence (test/command/checklist) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `P001;Arroz tipo 1 5kg;10063021;25.90` after the header becomes `Product(P001, Arroz tipo 1 5kg, 10063021, 25.90)` with scale 2 | `ProductCsvTest.validLineBecomesAProduct`, `priceIsKeptWithScaleTwo` (`7` → `7.00`, `10.5` → `10.50`, `0.01`) |
| 2 | A line breaking any rule lands in `rejected` with its file line number and reason, not in `products` | `invalidLineIsRejectedWithItsLineNumberAndReason`: 24 cases with the boundaries (3/5 fields, trailing `;`, spaces around the code, NCM 7/9 digits, dots, letter, space; price `abc`, `1E3`, `-1`, `--1`, ` 5`, `10.005`, `0`, `0.00`) |
| 3 | N data lines give products + rejections = N, in file order | `everyDataLineEndsUpAsAProductOrARejectionInFileOrder`, `wrongHeaderRejectsEveryLineSoSwappedColumnsAreNeverRead`, `emptyInputIsRejectedAsAMissingHeader` |
| 4 | The domain rule runs without `allowEmptyShould`, PIT without `failWhenNoMutations=false` | `./mvnw clean verify` green: 39 tests, JaCoCo met, PIT 28/28 mutations killed (100%) |

### Commit trail
- `45b6ad1` red: `ProductCsv` and `Product` did not exist (no compilation).
- `1af519f` red: 21 invalid lines, 15 accepted as products and 6 crashing with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.
- `a5ebbec` red: a wrong header and an empty input passed without rejecting line 1. The mixed-file test passed on the first run: characterization of cycle 2.
- Review fixes, test first: a swapped header produced products with code and description inverted (red, then fix); `" P001"` and `"P001 "` were accepted as codes distinct from `P001`, and `-1` got the format message (red, then fix; `--1` is a characterization).

### Failure scenario
Not applicable.

### Review
`/code-review high`: 2 important and 7 nits.
- Important: a wrong header still read the data lines in fixed order, so swapped columns were imported as valid products. Fixed test first: every data line is rejected with `not read: the header is wrong` (decided by Mr. Bravo, replacing the approved rule that read them).
- Important: spaces around the code made `P001 ` a different product from `P001`, breaking updates (T14) and idempotency (T11). Fixed test first: rejected, never trimmed (decided by Mr. Bravo).
- Nit, fixed: a negative price now gets `price must be greater than zero`.
- Nit, deferred to task 03: a UTF-8 BOM makes the header check fail. The BOM is a property of the file, so the adapter that reads it strips it.
- Nit, justified: `Product` has no invariants of its own. The parser is its only producer for now; constraints move into the record if another entry point appears.
- Nit, justified: no upper bound on price or field length. The catalog is fictitious, and an absurd value is rejected by the calculator (task 08) on the same product.
- Nit, justified: a `null` line throws instead of being rejected. The task 03 adapter reads with `Files.readAllLines`, which never yields `null`.
- Nit, justified: a blank line is rejected, as approved in the plan (never dropped silently). A file ending with one newline produces no blank line.
- Nit, justified: `ProductCsvResult` does not copy its lists; `parse` already returns immutable copies and is its only producer.

`/security-review`: no findings. The parser does no I/O, deserialization, query building or command execution; NCM and price only reach `BigDecimal` after a full-match digit pattern.

### Deviations from the plan
- A wrong header now rejects every data line, not only line 1 (review finding, decided by Mr. Bravo).
- New rule: spaces around the code reject the line (review finding, decided by Mr. Bravo).
- A negative price reports `price must be greater than zero` instead of the format message.

author: matthen
body:
This PR rewrites the tutorial for people new to coding, adds challenges to it and a Buffers lesson, makes places in the app linkable from code comments, and fixes a few things on phones.

Each tutorial step that changes the previous step's code now opens by showing the lines it changes, then says what's new and what you'll see. New functions get a worked value, such as `fract(2.7)` is 0.7, and each number to try says what it controls. Lessons 1 to 8 each have a Challenges step, before the example to explore, with two or three things to try on your own, some of them open-ended, like making a pattern look like a flower. Their hints stay hidden until you press Show hints, and there are no answers. The new Buffers lesson builds a heat map that a moving dot paints into a buffer, then spreads it out and moves shared code into the Shared tab.

Web addresses in comments are now links. A menu item or tab named in square brackets, like `[Help → Tutorial]` or `the [Sliders] tab`, opens it, and the examples use these links to point at the timeline, sliders, textures and code tabs.

On a phone, the welcome screen no longer has a ✕, which looked like it would close the website, and its Tutorial, tour and Continue buttons stay pinned to the bottom. The timeline's add-a-row button is no longer clipped, and the canvas's aspect ratio picker and size box stay hidden until you tap the canvas. On every screen, the Textures tab starts with three slots and a button to add the next, and the welcome dialog's Documentation and Source code links move to a small line under the examples.

author: seabbs
body:
Part of #512, item 2 of the order proposed there: the package's device forward pass against a bare kernel.

## What I found

Profiled on OpenCL (pocl, CPU device) at main f458e186, T = 200, L = 10, minimum of 20 synchronised runs, in µs.
A plain renewal call, `Recurrence(pmf)(R; history = h)`, is compared against a bare kernel doing the same steps in the same time-first buffer.

| S | bare kernel | package call | gap | `_public` (copy, then `permutedims`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 1,984 | 3,250 | 1,266 | 526 |
| 10,000 | 8,158 | 10,864 | 2,707 | 4,052 |

On device arrays, `_public(H, rows, h)` was `permutedims(H[rows, :])`: indexing the rows copies them, then `permutedims` copies again.
That is two passes and two allocations of the output's size.
It is the largest single part of the gap, and most of it at large S.
Setting up the buffer and loading the history cost 153 and 375 µs.

## What changes

`ext/ComposableRecurrencesGPUArraysCoreExt.jl` (+6) adds one method:

```julia
function ComposableRecurrences._public(H::AnyGPUArray, rows, h::AbstractMatrix)
    return permutedims(view(H, rows, :))
end
```

- It transposes a view of the rows, so there is one pass and one allocation.
- It runs wherever a device run returns its output, which covers recurrences, convolutions and their rule paths.
- No `src` file changes.
  The method dispatches only on device arrays, and host buffers keep `_public(H::Array, …)` or the generic method.

## Results

The same profile on this branch:

| S | package call: main → branch | `_public`: main → branch | rule-path forward (`_run_forward`): main → branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 3,250 → 2,532 | 526 → 294 | 5,139 → 3,194 |
| 10,000 | 10,864 → 8,590 | 4,052 → 1,174 | 19,126 → 12,758 |

The gap to the bare kernel drops from 1,266 to 654 µs at S = 1,000, and from 2,707 to 800 µs at S = 10,000.
pocl is a CPU device, so on a GPU the absolute numbers differ, but the pass and the allocation saved are the same.

## Tests

- `test/unit/device_rules.jl`: a new item checks that a JLArray buffer's rows come back as a JLArray, equal to the host's `permutedims(H[rows, :])`.
- Every device output test now goes through the method.

Local results at the branch commit, on main f458e186:

- the new item and the convolution, recurrence, dense coupling, time-varying, coupling over time, built-in and user modifier, traced, routes and routing items, with every Standards item, Aqua, explicit imports, import centralisation, extension ambiguities and formatting: 1,025 pass and 27 broken (the existing ones);
- OpenCL: forward 346 pass and 3 broken (the same as main); rule passes 344/344.

## Host

No `src` file changes, and the new method dispatches on `AnyGPUArray` only, so the host compiles the same code.
I did not run a timing A/B for that reason.
The whole BVD model as the benchmarks call it (`bvd_patches_call`, T = 200, L = 20), in bytes, is identical on main ad16b790 and the branch:

| | S = 1 | S = 5 |
|---|---|---|
| evaluation | 18,376 | 86,048 |
| ForwardDiff gradient | 8,288,232 | 195,274,016 |

The head is ab6c854e, merged on main ad16b790 (#814); I am rerunning the items on it.

## Line count

6 lines in the extension, comments included.

author: tlamadon
body:
Adds a `bujo` command line for this journal, usable from a terminal and by an agent (Hermes), on top of a shared core that the PWA now uses too.

## What changed

| Commit | |
|---|---|
| Extract domain logic into `@bujo/core` | `packages/core`: ids, tags, CRUD, reschedule + ghosts, migration, date-range queries. `createBujo(db)` takes any PouchDB-compatible db. `src/db.ts` only owns the local db and sync; the views are untouched |
| Keep entry refs stable across reschedules | A move only swaps the date prefix of `_id`; the `createdAt:uid` tail never changes. The 6-char `uid` is the short ref |
| Add dropped, priority, goals and event times | New optional fields, plus their display in the PWA |
| Add the bujo CLI | `packages/cli`, bundled into one self-contained file |
| Fix the Docker build for npm workspaces | `npm ci` ran before the workspace manifests were in the image |
| Accept Cloudflare Access service tokens | Verified JWT + explicit allowlist in the middleware |
| Document the CLI and add an agent guide | README section, `docs/AGENT.md` |

## Design decisions

**Refs.** `_id` stays `<date>:<createdAt>:<uid>`. Existing documents already have that shape, so they get stable refs with no data migration. Commands accept the short ref, the full id (an id from before a move still resolves through its tail) or a unique text fragment; ambiguous matches change nothing, list the candidates and exit 2.

**Goal key format.** A goal has `status: "goal"` and `date` set to its period key: `2026-W47` (ISO week) or `2026-11` (month), with `_id` `<periodKey>:<createdAt>:<uid>`. One prefix query returns a period's goals. A month key sorts right after its own days; a year's weeks sort after its months. Progress is in `goalState` (`achieved` / `dropped`, absent = open), since `status` is taken.

**Future log.** Plain tasks can be dated to a month (`2026-12`), which is what `bujo schedule` and `--date 2027-02` do.

**No local replica.** The CLI talks to CouchDB through a small fetch client (no PouchDB at runtime), directly with basic auth or through the Hono endpoint with a service token.

## Behaviour changes worth knowing

- Moving a task back onto a day it left removes its ghost there. Before, it left a ghost pointing at itself. Stable ids made a decision necessary here, since the ghost id would otherwise collide.
- Rescheduling to the date an entry is already on is a no-op (it used to add a history entry and a ghost).
- Migration leaves a month-dated task alone until its month is over, and never moves goals.
- Writes retry on `_rev` conflicts, and a change made through a stale copy follows the entry if another client moved it meanwhile. The same move made on two devices converges on one document instead of duplicating the task.
- An out-of-date cached copy of the PWA (old code) that reschedules an entry will drop `priority` / `time` on it, because the old code copies fields one by one. The service worker auto-updates, so the window is short.
- `bujo review --dry-run` is accepted but does nothing: review never writes.

## Service tokens

Off unless `CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN`, `CF_ACCESS_AUD` and `BUJO_SERVICE_TOKENS` (`clientId=userId` pairs) are all set; with none of them, the middleware behaves exactly as before. A service token is identified by the signed `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` (RS256 against the team's keys, issuer, audience, expiry) and gets its `userId` only from the allowlist — an email header sent along with it is ignored. No new dependencies (WebCrypto).

## Testing

- `npm test`: 201 tests — core on `pouchdb-adapter-memory`, the CLI in-process, the HTTP client against a fake CouchDB, the built binary as a subprocess (exit codes, stderr, env/file config), and the middleware auth.
- With `BUJO_TEST_COUCH_URL` set, the HTTP client suite also runs against a real CouchDB: 208 passing against `couchdb:3`.
- `npm run build`, `npm run lint` and the middleware build are green. The production image builds from a clean clone and serves the app.
- PWA checked in a browser after each stage: add, tags, migrate, ghosts, status cycling, reschedule, delete, all five views, then goals / priority / dropped / event time. A fresh browser profile synced CLI-created entries from CouchDB and rendered them; completing one in the PWA showed up in the CLI.
- **Not tested against real Cloudflare Access.** The service-token path was run end to end — CLI → a stand-in edge that checks the token headers and attaches a signed JWT → the real middleware → CouchDB — using the JWT shape from Cloudflare's docs. `bujo doctor` is the first thing to run once the real token is configured.

## Demo

```console
$ bujo add "Call plumber about the leak #house" --priority
added  we6zzh  *• Call plumber about the leak #house

$ bujo add "Dentist" --time 14:30 --date mon
added  jj30j4   ○ 14:30 Dentist  on 2026-11-23

$ bujo add "Renew passport" --date 2027-02
added  9jo9em   • Renew passport  on 2027-02

$ bujo goal "Ship the bujo CLI #bujo"
added  tfsegb   ◇ Ship the bujo CLI #bujo  goal for 2026-W47

$ bujo today
Sat 21 Nov 2026 · today · 2026-W47

  we6zzh  *• Call plumber about the leak #house

## Summary
Adds one self-contained module, `assets/motion-20261121.js` + `.css`, wired into `index.html` with one `<link>` and one `<script>`. It watches the DOM and does not touch the React bundle, so it stays out of other threads' way.

- **Price drop:** on a live price change the number counts from the old to the new price, a green "▼ amount" chip appears, and the card flashes once. The initial count-up from vivid is not affected.
- **Discount badge and favorite heart:** the badge pops with a sheen when the discount grows. A favorited game's heart beats and sprays small hearts when its price drops, and beats softly on discounted favorites.
- **Skeleton loading and page transition:** shimmering skeleton cards while the grid loads, a thin top progress bar for route changes and loading, and staggered block entrance.
- **Scroll parallax covers:** card covers drift ±5% inside the card (visible cards only, one rAF).
- **Fly to wishlist:** the cover arcs to "İstek Listem" (bottom nav or Menü on mobile) and the target bumps. There is no cart in the app, so this covers the favorite flow.
- **Theme sweep:** a light streak crosses the screen when Klasik/Sade, OLED or the site theme changes. It does not run on load.
- **Achievement badges:** staggered reveal, sparkles on rare and above, glow on legendary, and an unlock animation (spin-in, halo, confetti) for newly earned badges. Seen badges are kept in `radar-mo-badges`, and a first visit marks none as new.

All motion rules require `html.mo-par`, which is set only when neither `prefers-reduced-motion` nor the site's reduce-motion setting is on. Under reduced motion the skeleton shows static and nothing else animates. Checked in Klasik and Sade, TR and EN, desktop and 390px mobile.

body:
> 🤖 Opened by Aria's agent swarm, Dyna, not by Aria.

Refs #3938 (5a) · Refs #3728

`BlockPart::bounce_restitution` now gets the `getOnPosLegacy` position and state that the move selected before fall handling. The body retains its ground/support state from one move to the next and selects support with its post-move collision context. The read-only level is the real level on the simulating side. The event shape is unchanged; version 2 records the additional call coverage and contextual reads.

Items, TNT, experience orbs, falling blocks, boats, minecarts, fireworks and fishing bobbers share the post-collision solver in their base moves. The block coefficient is scaled in float precision before widening for a nonliving body. A successful bounce runs the block's `bounce_on`, emits `BOUNCE`, requests a position sync and writes the resulting velocity in vanilla's order. Server fall callbacks run first; a TNT cart discarded by its fall never asks for restitution. A custom ray hit, packet interpolation and a piston's direct slime launch are not block restitution. Only the selected state's subscribed Parts dispatch. The movement path keeps one retained support state, with no per-contact allocation or all-mod scan for dispatch. Step-on remains separate.

**Reference:** Vanilla 26.3 `Entity.move`, `Entity.checkSupportingBlock`, `Entity.getOnPosLegacy`, `Entity.restituteMovementAfterCollisions`, `PistonMovingBlockEntity.moveEntityByPiston`, `AbstractArrow.move`, `FarmlandBlock.fallOn`, `ShelfMushroomBlock.bounceOn`, `MinecartTNT.causeFallDamage`, `FallingBlockEntity.tick`, and `FireworkRocketEntity.tick`; NeoForge `IBlockExtension.getBounceRestitution`, `IBlockStateExtension.getBounceRestitution`, `IEntityExtension.getBlockBounciness`, and the `Entity.java` move patch.

This replaces the slime-only numerical path introduced by `fd855f88156` without changing the piston's direct slime launch, and keeps the level/landing-entity context introduced by `ef39dcec99d`. The step-before-inside contract from `58f3f290e63` is not changed here.

Vanilla's `AbstractHorse.getControllingPassenger` requires a saddled horse before a player rider owns its motion. The occupied-horse piston fixture now saddles the horse to exercise the observing server copy; an unsaddled passenger cannot suppress server restitution on the post-move slime contact.

A piston or lid keeps stable identities across the writable `BOUNCE` callback, and resolves them again before moving or retract-fixing each target. The prepared boat kind is borrowed from shared storage. A shulker-box lid uses collision on the controlling client's boat; it does not bounce observing copies. The self-move, native move, piston and box-lid routes share the TNT-cart fall/removal phase. `EntityRef::move_by` and `EntityRef::on_block` document collided restitution and retained support respectively.

author: mattbusel
body:
The Binance spot, Binance US and USD-M streams only read `u` from depth updates. `U` and `pu` are ignored, so one dropped @depth@100ms frame leaves wrong levels on the DOM until restart.

This follows Binance's diff-depth procedure through crypto-orderbook's `BookSync`. It buffers events, bridges the REST snapshot, and checks `U`/`u` on spot and `pu` on USD-M for every event. On a gap it clears the DOM, marks it offline and fetches a new snapshot (at most one request per second). The tests cover a dropped spot frame and a broken USD-M `pu` chain.

Adds `crypto-orderbook = 0.5.2` (default-features off; it uses rust_decimal, which you already have). I'm Matthew Busel, and I maintain crypto-orderbook.

author: cyberadvisor
body:
Milestone 16, PR 1 (v1.8.0): formatted notes.

Task and project notes show light Markdown once you leave them: `**bold**`, `*italic*` or `_italic_`, bullet and numbered lists (`- ` or `1. `), and links written as `[label](url)` or as a bare address (`https://`, `www.`, `mailto:`). Clicking a link opens it in a new tab. Clicking anywhere else on the note, or tabbing to it, turns it back into the text box exactly as typed, with the caret at the end. An empty note stays a text box, so its placeholder shows. Notes are still stored as plain text, so sync, backup and import don't change, and there's no schema change.

- `src/lib/model/markdown.ts`: parses a note into a tree. Only http, https and mailto links are made; anything else, such as `javascript:` or a relative address, stays text.
- `NoteText.svelte`: draws that tree with escaped text, never inserting HTML.
- `NotesField.svelte`: switches between the formatted note and the text box, which grows with its text. Pressing a link doesn't take focus. Used in `TodoCard` and `ProjectView`. Quick Entry stays plain.
- `focusCycle.ts`: Tab reaches the formatted note.

**Tests:**
- Unit tests in `tests/markdown.test.ts` (8), including hostile links. 563 unit tests pass.

_Requested by **Jacques** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MDNbhmXKWoJcJmCmCaThy6?thread=cmsg_01MDNbhmXKWoJcJmCmCaThy63eCy4VB93WFuGWvkfWiD71)_

## Problème
La fiche `Lien-Communaute` dessine une rangée « Actif » : l'animateur doit pouvoir suspendre le lien d'entrée de sa communauté sans la désactiver (`isActive` est la désactivation ADMINISTRATIVE, #8876) ni toucher à ses membres. Rien côté passerelle ne le permettait (#19661).

## Mise en œuvre (passerelle, première moitié de #19661)
- `Community.joinLinkPausedAt DateTime?` — nul ou absent = actif. Champ additif sur MongoDB : aucune migration.
- `PUT /api/v1/communities/:id/join-link { paused: boolean }` (`routes/communities/join-link.ts`) : réservé aux intendants (créateur, admin, modérateur ACTIFS, porte `isCommunitySteward` des entrées) d'une communauté ACTIVE. Tout autre lecteur : le même 404 qu'une communauté absente. Seul l'état part. Une pause déjà posée garde son instant ; relancer l'efface.
- `POST /communities/:id/join` avec `via: "link"` sur un lien en pause : 403 `COMMUNITY_LINK_PAUSED`, AVANT toute adhésion ou demande d'entrée.
- Le détail et la liste (`communityForViewer` → `joinLinkStateFor`) servent `joinLinkPaused` à tout lecteur, et l'instant `joinLinkPausedAt` aux seuls intendants.
- Manifeste de routes et catalogues régénérés (TS, Swift, Kotlin) ; l'entrée `communities.byIdJoinLink` est déclarée en attente de client (#20255) dans les deux cliquets d'entrées mortes.

## Décisions
- La pause ne ferme que la porte du LIEN : une communauté publique reste joignable directement, une privée reste sur invitation. C'est un réglage d'acquisition, pas une garde de confidentialité.
- Une demande faite par le lien AVANT la pause reste acceptable (geste d'intendant).
- Reste de #19661 : « Supprimer ce lien » (révoquer l'adresse). #19661 reste ouverte.

## Alternatives écartées
- Réutiliser `isActive` : il désactive la communauté entière et appartient à l'administration.
- Un booléen + horodatage : interdit par la règle du dépôt, un `DateTime?` suffit.
- Servir l'instant à tous : il dirait quand un geste de modération a eu lieu (relevé par la revue adversariale).

## Sécurité / vie privée
Garde fail-closed testée sur chaque rang (créateur sans ligne, admin, modérateur, membre, non-membre, communauté désactivée, invité sans compte) ; rien n'est écrit sur un refus ; la réponse ne porte que `joinLinkPausedAt`. Revue `auditeur-adversarial` avant la PR : non bloquante, son seul correctif (instant visible de tous) est dans le lot.

## Accessibilité
Aucun écran dans ce lot ; les clients (#20255) porteront la rangée et le message de l'arrivant.

## Tests
- `join-link-pause-19661.test.ts` : 23 témoins. Rouge prouvé : module absent ; puis 2 échecs sous chacune des mutations « garde du join retirée » et « instant servi à tous ».
- Passerelle : suites communautés, routes, manifeste, `tsc-never-loaded-tests-ratchet`, `community-member-writer-sweep` ; `tsc --noEmit` vert.
- `packages/shared/__tests__/ci` : 216/216 ; `check-ts-catalog-dead-entries` et `check-swift-catalog-dead-entries` conformes.

| cas | passerelle | web | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| suspendre / relancer | ✅ | #20255 | #20255 | #20255 |
| entrée par le lien refusée | ✅ | client n'envoie pas encore `via: "link"` (#20255) | idem | idem |
| état lu au détail | ✅ | #20255 | #20255 | #20255 |
| révoquer l'adresse | #19661 | — | — | — |

Refs #19661 (reste ouverte : révocation). Suivi : #20255.

author: xiaobingan
body:
## Problem and outcome

The global search shortcut fires during an input-method composition. Its own comment states the intent — "An IME composition in flight keeps the keystroke" — but the check reads only `event.isComposing`, and browsers report a composition in flight two ways: the flag once composition state is updated, and the legacy `keyCode` 229 on the key event that is otherwise shaped like the shortcut. With a Simplified Chinese, Japanese or Korean IME open, a `k` inside a candidate window can arrive as `keyCode` 229 with `isComposing` still false, so Cmd/Ctrl+K opens search, the composer loses the keystroke and the composition is interrupted mid-word.

Both signals now keep the keystroke. Everything else is unchanged: the meta/ctrl requirement, the alt/shift rejections, the `k`/`K` match and the capture-phase listener that stops editors from also handling the key.

## Evidence and validation

Base: `2f03b64f56f1e7a116d5b19f20a1f3a5fe07b63c`. macOS (darwin arm64), Node.js 26.4.0, pnpm 11.7.0.

- **Negative control:** with only `isComposing` checked, the new case fails with `AssertionError: expected true to be false` on the `keyCode` 229 events, and the outside-composition case passes. With the change both pass.
- The cases build real `KeyboardEvent`s in the jsdom environment the Web suite uses: a composition flagged by `isComposing`, one flagged only by `keyCode` 229 on both Cmd and Ctrl, then the controls that must still open search (`Cmd+K`, `Ctrl+K` with a normal key code) and must not (no modifier, `Shift`, `Alt`).
- Focused test: `pnpm --filter @linger/web test src/features/search/search-shortcut.test.tsx` — **2 passed**.

## Contract and boundary impact

No export, listener or key binding change; only the guard inside the predicate. No documentation states the shortcut's composition rule, so none changes. No network round trip, file walk or migration is added.

## Not verified here

- No real IME was driven; the case reproduces the event shape browsers send, which is what the predicate reads.
- Firefox and Safari were not run; the legacy key code is the widely supported signal for this state and costs nothing where it is absent.

## Author readiness

- [x] Focused tests for the changed behavior
- [x] `make check BASE=origin/<target-branch>` or the fast checks of every touched app (`pnpm --filter @linger/web typecheck` and the focused test above)
- [x] Contracts regenerated if `contracts/openapi/` changed (not applicable; contracts unchanged)

author: sc30gsw
body:
## Why

The owner's rule until release is that every dependency is on its newest release within the one-day release age (`minimumReleaseAge: 1440`). `scripts/check-newest-releases.ts` holds that rule, but only in the `pins` job of the weekly `Newest releases` workflow. So a pull request can merge with a pin behind, and nothing says so until the next Monday.

This pull request alone makes the check run on every pull request and on its pushes, and show red on the pull request when a pin is behind. It does not block a merge: that needs `newest-releases` among `main`'s required checks. The owner has deferred making it a required check until this job has run here (Q158).

This pull request targets `main`, which #38 has reached. #38 moved the Solid line and `solid2-agent-kit`: `solid-js`, `@solidjs/web` and `@solidjs/signals` to 2.0.3, and `@solidjs/compiler` to 2.0.2, its newest release. This branch moves every other pin, `@babel/core` to 8.1.3 among them, so the check exits 0 on `main` with this branch merged, as of 2026-11-21 17:40Z.

## What changed

- **The job, in a workflow of its own.** `.github/workflows/newest-releases-on-pr.yml` holds one job, `newest-releases`, which runs `node scripts/check-newest-releases.ts` set up as the weekly `pins` job is. The script exits non-zero when a pin is behind a release old enough to install and not held back, so the job's run fails. `ci.yml` is left as it is on `main`, so its `verify` workflow may still take `concurrency`, `env`, `defaults` or `run-name`.
- **The failure message.** Each problem the check finds has a kind: `behind`, `ahead`, `unknown` or `hold`. `unknown` is a pin whose newest release on its channel cannot be told: a package with no registry document, a release with no publish time, a channel with no release, or a Node index with no LTS. A source that cannot be fetched is not a problem of any kind: the check stops with its URL and causes before it compares. On a pull request with a pin behind, the run also says that the pin is behind on the base branch that `GITHUB_BASE_REF` names, and that the fix is a `build(deps)` pull request of its own to it. A run that fails only on a hold, a pin ahead or an `unknown` pin adds nothing.
- **The test.** `tests/ci-workflow.test.ts` finds the job in every workflow that runs on `pull_request`. It holds, by allowing rather than forbidding, that exactly one job runs the check, in a workflow that holds no other job, and that:
  - the `pull_request` trigger sets only `types`, and they include opening, each push and reopening;
  - the workflow sets only `name`, `on`, `permissions` and `jobs`;
  - the job sets only `runs-on`, `timeout-minutes`, which it must set, `steps` and `permissions`, which only read;
  - its steps are exactly `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0`, and `persist-credentials: false` if it likes, `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` with `node-version-file: package.json` and `cache: true`, and the check, each setting nothing else but a `name`; every other `with` input is refused, `with` is compared by value whatever its key order, and an action's name without case;
  - nothing in the job reads a secret.

  `gateJobProblems` in `tests/support/workflows.ts` holds any gate job, so the weekly `pins` and `revisits` jobs are held by the same predicate; the commands live in `tests/support/release-checks.ts`. Spelled-out workflows show each refusal by its message, among them every bypass the two reviews found. A test also shows that `ci.yml` may set workflow-level `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress`, `env`, `defaults` and `run-name`. The rewritten `AGENTS.md` rows name these checks.
- **Release sources.** `fetchedJson` in `scripts/release-sources.ts` gives each fetch an `AbortSignal.timeout` of 30 s and, after two seconds, tries once more. Every failure it throws names the URL and the cause of each try. The registry documents and Node's release index are fetched together. `scripts/held-back-releases.json` is read against its type, so an entry of the wrong shape fails by its place and its name. `tests/release-sources.test.ts` holds the fetch with a stubbed `fetch`.
- **The pins, one `build(deps)` commit each, with what each changelog says:**
  - `axe-core` 4.14.0 → 4.14.1. A fix release; some fixes can move contrast and target-size results. Every story's and the focus trap's WCAG 2 A and AA scans still pass.
  - `fast-check` 4.10.2 → 4.10.3. Fixes only; nothing touches `interruptAfterTimeLimit` or async properties.
  - `modern-web-guidance` 1.0.0 → 1.0.1. New and updated guides, and an updated skill that the workspace does not link (`skills: false`).
  - `storybook-solidjs-vite` → `11.0.0-next-20261117161333`. It builds against Storybook 11.0.0-beta.3, adds docgen reporting and live snippets, and drops the `experimentalCodeExamples` switch, which this repository never set.
  - pnpm (`packageManager`) 12.21.0 → 12.22.0. It closes a way to skip the `minimumReleaseAge` check after a registry change. Its other changes reach nothing this repository uses.
  - `@babel/core` 8.1.2 → 8.1.3, once it became old enough at 2026-11-21T17:26Z. Spec and bug fixes in the parser, the generator and transform plugins; nothing is marked breaking. The StyleX build and the Solid plugin pass on it.
  - `@ui-sdk/core` and `@ui-sdk/solid` 0.1.0-beta.6 → 0.1.0-beta.13, together, since the Solid binding asks for core `^0.1.0-beta.13`. The changelog marks no change as breaking. The Tabs, dialog-focus and `<Loading>` fixes are the ones that reach the library. The SDK file the nonce seam relies on is byte for byte the same.
- **One pin held back, while a condition holds.** `@vitest/browser-playwright` stays at 5.1.0. The reason: the vite-plus the catalog pins depends on vitest 5.1.0 exactly and asks for `@vitest/browser-playwright` 5.1.0 as its peer, so 5.1.1 would install a second vitest. The entry names that as a `while` condition: vite-plus requires vitest 5.1.0 exactly. `holdsWhoseConditionFailed` reads it through `exactlyRequiredBy` from vite-plus's manifest at the pinned version, and fails the check by name once it is false.
- **Merges.** The branch was stacked on #38 while #38 was open, and merged it three times as it moved. It then merged `main`, once #38 had reached it as one squashed commit, and merged `main` again after #41 and #42 landed. In that last merge the only conflicts were eight skills' "Last confirmed" lines, and each took the later commit, which the branch now contains. Against `main`, the branch changes only these: the new workflow and its test; the release check's scripts and their tests; the `tests/support` modules those tests share (`workflows.ts`, `weekly-workflow.ts` and the new `release-checks.ts`); the `AGENTS.md` rows; the pins above, with the lockfile; the one held-back entry; and the "Last confirmed" lines of eight verification skills. The lockfile was installed again on the merged catalog each time.

## Scope

- I gave the job a workflow of its own rather than a place in `ci.yml` or `pull-request.yml`. In `ci.yml`, the gate's allowlist would constrain `verify`'s workflow too. `pull-request.yml` runs on `opened`, `edited` and `synchronize` only, so a reopened pull request would skip the check, and `tests/pull-request-checks.test.ts` pins those types exactly. The new workflow runs on the default activities, which include `reopened`. It does not run on pushes to `main`; the weekly `pins` job covers `main`.
- The weekly `pins` job stays as it is.
- The hold-back and until-stable lists still fit the owner's rule:
  - Every held-back entry has its reason and a `liftWhen`.
  - The until-stable channel holds only the Storybook app's prerelease pins, and follows their newest release.
  - Three channels follow a narrower line than "the newest stable release": Solid 2, the Solid plugin's pinned major, and the major of Node's newest LTS. None of them hides a newer major today.

## Tradeoffs

- The check reads the npm registry and Node's release index, so this job fails

author: jakkaj
body:
Delivers: none
Fixes: F254, F262, F265

A chore PR with four small items: F254, F262, F265 and S307-N1, plus a port retry for one flaky test. S307-N1 is a review note, not an F-item, so it is not on the Fixes line.

| Item | Fix | Test (RED→GREEN) | Mutant (FAIL) |
|---|---|---|---|
| F254 (S302-N1): the log trim must read only the file the lock proved | `sync` proves the path's dev/ino under the lock and passes it to `rotate` → `keep_tail`. `keep_tail` opens with `O_NOFOLLOW \| O_NONBLOCK` and reads only a regular file with that dev/ino, else InvalidInput ("daemon.log is not the file the lock proved it named"). | `the_trim_reads_only_the_file_the_lock_proved`, `the_trim_never_waits_on_a_fifo_at_the_path`, `a_planted_trim_record_is_never_followed_or_waited_on` (symlink, FIFO, directory); `the_trim_never_follows_a_symlink` now passes the target's dev/ino | no dev/ino check; no O_NONBLOCK; no O_NOFOLLOW: each FAILS its witness |
| F262: AGENTS rule 6 named killing by pattern, not deleting | Rule 6: never kill **or delete** by pattern in a shared root (`/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`, tmux's socket dir); delete only paths you created and recorded. Ledger row D-F262-1. | doc | — |
| F265: a reused key's stale status file read as this launch's exit | A launch for a key with no row removes any status/log at its evidence paths before its wrapper starts. | `a_reused_keys_stale_status_file_is_never_read_as_this_launchs_exit`: an earlier `exit_code=7` at the paths; the launch now times out on its own wait (504) and never reports exit 7 or the old log | no removal: FAIL (502, the stale exit) |
| S307-N1: `passDir` with no HOME | Fallback `join(tmpdir(), "pij-rs-no-home", ".pij-rs")`, matching pij-rs `default_state_dir` (a stand-in HOME with `.pij-rs` under it). | `lives under pij-rs's state dir` (`passDir({})`) | the old fallback: FAIL |
| flaky `two_daemons_started_together…` | The race test retries on a fresh port when both daemons exit unbound (a port taken between pick and bind), up to 5 tries. | the test itself | — |

Policy vs brakes:
- The trim's rotation is the POLICY, unchanged.
- The dev/ino match, O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK are BRAKES: each can only refuse a trim.
- F265's removal deletes only the two paths derived from this launch's own key, and only when the key has no row. It is the launch's own evidence and is never removed by pattern.

Cost:
- The trim adds one fstat on a file it already opens, once per rotation.
- F265 adds two unlink calls per fresh-key launch.
- No loop, timer or launch. No per-seat scaling.

## Worker v4.1 — multi-language + two-stage cinema polish (integrated from `repo1-worker-v4.1-multilang.zip`)

The uploaded archive was extracted over the repo root, then audited, hardened, documented and CI-covered. **The archive itself is deleted**; only the 752-byte synthetic `tests/fixtures/pack.zip` remains. `.github/` and `.gitignore` were preserved (they were absent from the zip).

### What ships
- **`worker/src/languages.js`** — 18 languages with OpenSubtitles ISO-639-2B, SubDL + NMT ISO-639-1 codes, script classes, RTL (`ar`/`ur`) and per-script line budgets (CJK 18 / si 42). **Fix:** Russian now has a real `cyrillic` script class instead of being mislabelled `latin`.
- **`worker/src/cinema.js` + `pipeline.js`** — two-stage delivery: validated base NMT `.srt` is playable immediately (`X-Sub-Quality: base-nmt`, `X-Polish-Status: pending`), resumable LLM-only polish (`providerKind: 'llm'`) hot-swaps the **same** token via `publishSrt(force)`, per-cue validator falls back to the clean NMT draft, worst-case 15 subrequests (≤25).
- **`worker/src/providers.js`** — translate-pa OFF by default (`ENABLE_TRANSLATE_PA`), tags raw / text entity-escaped, ≤500-line batches with exact multi-line rebuild, then `azure → google_v3 → gemini → workers_ai`. **Fix:** any 4xx/5xx now trips pa's 10-minute breaker on the first answer (no retry storm), then fails over.
- **Backward compatibility** — `si` keeps bare v4 job ids; `?lang=` + `?register=` on `/subtitles/:type/:id.json` and `/api/subs-direct`; `/api/paired/:jobId.json` accepts the `:lang` suffix.

### Security
- **Fixed an SSRF bypass in `fetchUpstreamSub`:** an explicit `allowHttp: false` from `/api/fetch-sub` could be overridden into a loopback `http://` fetch, and implicit loopback access ignored `ALLOWED_SUB_HOSTS`. Now `false` is authoritative and implicit loopback requires the operator to allowlist the literal host — production default is blocked. Two regression checks added (security 48 → 50).
- Full SSRF audit unchanged otherwise: https-only, strict allowlist, private/link-local rejection on **every redirect hop**, 5 MB download+decompression caps, `..` traversal blocked, 2 MB upload cap, `textContent`-only UI.

### Labs / CI
- Both live labs now spawn `wrangler dev` **detached** and `killTree()` the process group, so `workerd` is reaped instead of leaking the port and letting a later run silently test a stale worker; a port preflight makes that fatal instead of silent.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` upgraded: `npm ci`, zero-`AIza…` literal scan, tracked-archive check, syntax gates for every worker module/UI/lab/py, `node tests/run-all.js`, `local_server_test.py`, pinned `./node_modules/.bin/wrangler deploy --dry-run`, **and** a live-labs job running `verify_worker_v4_e2e.mjs` + `verify_worker_v41_e2e.mjs` on real workerd with loopback mocks (no keys, offline-safe).

### Docs / housekeeping
- `package.json` + `package-lock.json` synced at **4.1.0** (wrangler pinned `4.166.0`).
- Release report moved to `docs/RELEASE_REPORT_v4.1_v2.2.md`.
- README + `docs/SETUP-EN.md` + `docs/SETUP-SI.md` document 18 languages, two-stage polish, `SUBS_KV`, provider secrets and optional `ENABLE_TRANSLATE_PA` / `TRANSLATE_PA_KEY`.

author: isayev
body:
Refs #163.

## Summary

- `AIMNet2Calculator.extract_features(data, *, validate_species=True)` returns `aim` (per-atom embeddings), `charges` (equilibrated partial charges), and `atom_mask`; spin-polarized models also return `spin_charges` (alpha minus beta) and need `mult`, as in `eval`. Atom axes match the caller's input layout: `(N, D)` for one structure or a flat `mol_idx` batch, `(B, N, D)` for rectangular batches. Internal padding is removed, and caller padding is kept, marked false in `atom_mask`, with zero outputs.
- `AIMNet2.forward` now calls `forward_features_prepared` and then the output heads, so feature extraction and ordinary inference share one message-passing implementation. `AIMNet2Base` declares `forward_features`; `AIMNet2.forward_features` leaves its input dict unchanged.
- Output heads, external Coulomb/dispersion and long-range neighbor lists are skipped. Charge equilibration stays part of the feature computation.
- Padded batches that the calculator would flatten (CPU, above `nb_threshold`, periodic) are packed to their real atoms first, so padding never enters charge equilibration. Dense CUDA batches keep mode-0 masking. Explicit mode-1 neighbor matrices must list every real atom before one final dummy row; other layouts raise.
- Inference is eager and no-gradient. Training calculators, legacy TorchScript models, and models whose output heads write `aim`, `charges` or `spin_charges` raise instead of returning features that would not match `eval`.
- `prepare_input` and `make_nbmat` keep their public signatures; feature-only preparation goes through private helpers.

## Fix: shared periodic cell in a batch

A batch of several periodic systems with one `(3, 3)` or `(1, 3, 3)` cell applied that cell to the first system only. `eval` silently returned wrong energies, forces and charges for the later systems (Ewald and `(1, 3, 3)` cells raised an index error), and stress came back as one `(3, 3)` tensor for the whole batch. `mol_flatten` now copies a shared cell to every system, so results match an explicit `(B, 3, 3)` cell and stress is `(B, 3, 3)`. This changes `eval` behavior and has its own CHANGELOG `Fixed` entry.

## Not covered here (#163 follow-ups)

- Legacy `.jpt` models are rejected rather than supported.
- Other per-atom head outputs are not exposed.
- Requesting `aim` through `eval`'s `keys_out` still returns it in the internal layout.
- `eval` treats caller padding as real atoms when it flattens a padded batch: #165. `extract_features` packs around it, so the two can disagree on padded CPU batches until #165 is fixed.

## Tests

`tests/test_features.py` covers:
- batch vs single-structure agreement, flat-batch ordering, and charges against `eval`;
- translation, rotation and permutation invariance;
- heads and long-range modules not called;
- rejection of invalid atomic numbers, ambiguous molecule indices, misaligned mode-1 neighbors, unsupported models, training mode, and heads that overwrite features;
- `validate_species`, and calculators built with `compile_model=True` or `cuda_graph=True`;
- mode-2 padding, including an all-dummy system;
- shared cells for features, energy, charges, forces and stress (DSF and Ewald);
- GPU dense (mode 0) and sparse paths, padded and unpadded, asserting which path ran;
- registry weights (`aimnet2`, `aimnet2-nse` with spin charges) on CPU and CUDA. These run in CI's core job.

Local results:
- `pytest -m "not gpu and not network and not slow"` (CPU): 1261 passed, 20 skipped, 41 s.
- CI's PBC-on-CPU set (`-m "ase and gpu and not sella and not slow"`): 54 passed.
- GPU (L40S): features, PBC, calculator, long-range, neighbor and model tests 396 passed; CUDA-graph suites 268 passed; compile, mode-2 and geometry-carry GPU tests 57 passed.
- `make check` and `mkdocs build --strict`: clean.
- `mypy`: 25 errors, the same as `main`.

author: bhoudebert
body:
## Summary
A repository's checks ran in the worker, which has no Docker and none of the step's tools home, so a repository whose tests need a database could never pass them (work `10e71c02c4a8` looped developer and checks until the round limit on exactly that). In container mode each check command now runs as a `check` step in a container of its own:

- **Runner.** A new kind, `check`, runs one shell command in the clone under the same fixed container rules as an agent step (and the step's Docker daemon when the operator turned it on, with the host's profile). It refuses a model credential and a GitHub token (`ANTHROPIC_*`, `CLAUDE_CODE_*`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`) and a request without a command.
- **In the container.** A small program, `shelf-check`, reports one `check` line (exit code and the end of the output, redacted on arrival). The step ends well whatever the command did: a failing command is a result, not a failure of the step.
- **Worker.** A `CommandRunner` port and a `ContainerCommands` adapter run each command through the runner with the clone, the repository's tools and no credential. The command is not wrapped in the worker's own paths (the step has its own home and tool shims). A step that did not end properly (a broken stream, a timeout, an unreachable runner, a clone outside the shared volume) is a failed check that says why, never a pass. In the sandbox mode the checks run in the worker as before.
- The Docker wrapper now runs the program it is given (`shelf-step` or `shelf-check`).

## Decision and spec
Decision 0019 (stage 3b, `kind=check`) and decision 0020; the steps and deployment specs, and the code map for the new files.

## Verified
- Full gate: ruff, format, pyright, import-linter, pytest (1524 passed, coverage 93.9%), on the branch merged with `main`.
- **A real end-to-end run**, with the live runner check (`scripts/check-runner-live.py`, real Docker, no Kata): a check runs as the step's user, in `/work`, with the step's home, can write the tool folders, has no credential, returns its own exit code and what it wrote on standard error, the container is gone afterwards, and a `GH_TOKEN` in a check is refused by name.
- Unit tests for each part: the stream event, the runner's rules (kind, credentials, command, program), the in-container program, the worker adapter (every way a check can fail is a failure), `Steps` (checks go through the runner, unwrapped, with the same report) and the wiring.

## Not verified
- **A check with Docker inside a Kata step.** The Docker daemon in a step was proven separately on a real host (`sh deploy/host-runtime.sh` reports `a Docker daemon inside a step runs a container (profile standard)`), but a whole `docker compose up -d --wait && ./mvnw -B verify` as a check has not been run.
- `kind=setup` (the tool installation) still runs in the worker, and so does the tools step before the checks.
- The loop limit (stop after N identical failures) is unchanged.

## Why

After #244 a real refresh placed 405 of 675 sessions by their claude.ai project. The 270 left to the model came out as many small topics for one product, and some of them were runs nobody typed.

## What

- **Codex desktop projects as topics.** `codexProjects()` reads `projects` and `project_roots` from Codex's index. `folderTopics()` puts a session no topic has yet, of any agent, in the topic named as the project whose directory it worked in (deepest root wins; a Codex worktree copy is matched by the root's name). It runs after `projectTopics()` and before an agent is asked. The mapping is kept in `TopicStore.projects` under `codex:<id>`, so renames and merges hold.
- **More automated sessions known.** A Codex thread with an empty `thread_source` that the desktop app's server ran for another program, and Muse Code sessions made by its probe client or on its `echo` test provider, carry `automated: true`. Threads started by genaicode stay: they are somebody's chat in an app built on it.
- **Sorting prompt** asks for few, broad topics.
- **`genaicode topics`** drops the directory column and shows names up to 48 characters.

## Checked

- `npm run type-check`, `npm run lint` pass.
- `npm test`: 976 of 977 pass here. The one failure, "stops the shell runner and its test process on cancellation" (from #239), also fails alone in this container and does not touch this change; CI decides.
- Markers measured on a real machine (30 days): Codex `thread_source`/`originator` had no false positives among 141 top-level threads.

## Not in this PR

- Antigravity gives no project name in its store, only a UUID; its conversations still go by folder or by the model.

author: realtolufash
body:
# Description

On Android, selected text in any field drew as a solid black block and the selected words vanished into it (QA's #80257 on **Sign in**, sc‑79989). Android's `selectionColor` is the highlight painted behind the text, at whatever opacity it is given, while iOS draws its own see-through tint from the same colour; the kit handed both platforms full ink.

The kit's field defaults now take the platform:

- `FIELD_DEFAULTS` becomes `fieldDefaults(os)`; `passwordProps` and `codeProps` take `os` first. Every `TextInput` in the app already spreads one of the three, so every field gets the fix at once.
- On Android the highlight is ink at 25% (`${colorInk}40`), and `selectionHandleColor` and `cursorColor` are full ink. Without `selectionHandleColor`, React Native colours the handles with `selectionColor`, which would have made them translucent.
- On iOS `selectionColor` stays full ink, so the caret, handles and tint look as they do now. `selectionHandleColor` and `cursorColor` are Android-only props, so iOS ignores them.
- The kit guard that makes every `TextInput` spread the kit defaults now looks for `fieldDefaults(`.

# Risks

- Android 9 (API 28) cannot recolour handles or the caret (React Native skips it there), so on that version the handles keep the platform's colour. The highlight is fixed on every version.
- I checked the 4.5:1 contrast by working it out over the card and inset fills in every scheme, not from a screenshot. QA's screenshot measurement is still the check the AC asks for.

# References

- https://app.shortcut.com/soirely/story/80268
- Found by sc‑79989 (#80257); designer's spec on sc‑79989 (#80265); the kit's caret rule dates from sc‑35256.

# Evidence of work

- `npm test -w apps/mobile -- src/kit/kit.test.ts src/kitGuard.test.ts`: 315 passed.
- New in `kit.test.ts`: every field's defaults on both platforms keep the ink caret and handles; iOS selects in ink; Android highlights in ink at 25%; the selected ink text stays at 4.5:1 or more over the Android highlight on `colorCard` and `colorInset` in every scheme.
- `npm run typecheck`, `eslint`, `prettier --check` and `lint:comments` on the changed files: all exit 0.
- I did not run it on a simulator or device (QA does that pass).

# Next Steps

None.
