author: engahmed121314
body:
## Bug (F-07)
ACIBeam.calculateDevelopmentLength had the Table 25.4.2.4 size factor branches swapped: ψs=1.0 for bars ≤22 mm and ψs=0.8 for larger bars. The code (bilingual ACI 318M-14, printed p.655 — rendered and read directly) requires ψs=0.8 for No.19 and smaller, ψs=1.0 for No.22 and larger. Effect: 25/29/32 mm bars got development lengths 20% shorter than required (unconservative); small bars 25% longer (wasteful).

## Fix
Flip the branch. With the fix, the unified 1.7 denominator yields 2.125 for small bars (vs table's 2.1, conservative) and 1.7 for large bars (vs 1.65, conservative) — matching Table 25.4.2.2's favourable-confinement case.

## Verified clauses (CLAUSE_LOG A-13, printed pp.652-655)
- Table 25.4.2.2 simplified cases + Eq 25.4.2.3a general form
- Table 25.4.2.4: ψs/ψt/ψe values, ψtψe ≤ 1.7
- §25.4.2.1: ℓd ≥ 300 mm floor

## Golden vectors (hand-computed)
16 mm → 650, 25 mm → 1275, 32 mm top epoxy → 2525, 12 mm fy=280 → 325.

## Documented limitations (need interface inputs)
- Poor-confinement 'other cases' (denominators 1.4/1.1) not covered — engine assumes favourable confinement.
- ψe=1.5 for epoxy with cover < 3db not covered — engine uses 1.2.

author: anielsud
body:
Niam keeps getting flung off the stunt park's "dirt bowl". That's the **east banked turn** (after the loop), not the concrete wall-ride bowl. It's the same at every park, because the turn is shared. At the Grand Canyon he also ends up heading for the canyon jump when he meant to take the turn.

## Cause

Measured on `main` by riding from the start arch at full gas, steering down the lane to the loop, then **hands off**. That's how Niam rides.

- **Nothing gets round the turn.** Every stock car and bike, in Arcade and Pilot, at all 4 parks, runs wide over the top of the berm and leaves the park: 32/32 runs. The same happens even with a good steering line, and in Sim. Coming off the loop and the rumble strip, cars reach the turn at 21–27 m/s and bikes at 23–33 m/s. A 30 m bend at that speed needs 1.5–3.7 g. The steering is speed-limited to about 1 g, and 20° of banking adds little.
- **The barrier was in the wrong place.** The tyres and the 1 m collision barrier stood on the ground at the berm's *foot* (TW+3.3). The berm's top edge is about 5 m higher (14 m × tan 20°). Cars flew off the top, 7–9 m up, and cleared the barrier easily.
- **The Grand Canyon fork.** The link lane to the canyon jump runs straight on, and the banking only started 30 m after the fork. Hands off, every vehicle went down the link lane (the probe ended at x≈130 on the link).

## Fix (`src/stuntPark.js`, plus a small `wallLine` change in `src/stuntKit.js`; same rules for every park)

- **Berm:** banked at 26° (was 20°). The banking now ramps up over 32 m and back down over 40 m (was 16 m). A fast twist in the banking acted as a kicker on the way in and dropped away under the bikes on the way out. The tyres and the collision barrier now sit **on the berm's top** (`wallLine` takes a height function).
- **`bankGuide` (Arcade/Pilot only, the same approach as `bowlGuide` in the bowl):**
  - It turns the car and its velocity round the bend, at a line up the bank that suits the speed, and back to the middle for the exit.
  - It keeps turning to the very end. Easing off early sent cars straight up the bank as it flattens.
  - Speed is capped to what the bank and the tyres can carry (μ = 1), eased off at 14 m/s² like a rider braking.
  - It holds the car on the bank surface, so the bank can't launch it like a kicker.
  - It keeps tall trucks flat on the bank, so they don't roll.
  - For bikes it adds the bend's own turn rate, because bike.js sets a bike's yaw rate from the rider's steering.
- **`bankCatch` (every mode):** a catch fence at the kerb, like `rimCatch` in the bowl. It only acts on vehicles riding the turn, not on the link lane.
- **The fork (Grand Canyon):**
  - The turn is now the default: hands off, the guide takes you round.
  - **Holding right for 0.2 s** at the end of straight 1 picks the link lane, and the guide lets go.
  - The fork zone only starts 12 m before the turn. Steering while coming out of the loop doesn't count.

## Before → after (physics probe, all 4 parks)

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Arcade/Pilot, 4 stock vehicles, hands off after the loop | all over the barrier (max 16+ m out, 7–9 m up) | all round; max 1.2–4 m out (kerb at 7), out on straight 2 at z ≈ −30, upright, nothing broken |
| Same at 25 and 22 fps steps | over | round |
| Grand Canyon, hands off | link lane / canyon jump | the turn |
| Grand Canyon, steering right at the fork | link lane | link lane, onto the jump's run-up |
| Real game loop, CPU ×4, gas key held, no steering, Grand Canyon | Sport Bike and Dune Buggy down the link lane | Sport Bike round onto straight 2; Dune Buggy still in the turn 1 m out when the 40 s timer ran out (never wide) |

## Tests

New checks in `tools/test/stunts.js` / `stunts.py` (README updated):

- **`turnRun`**, every park, 4 vehicles, Pilot and Arcade: start arch → loop → banked turn, hands off. It must get round, never past the kerb, and come out upright onto straight 2 with nothing broken. At the Grand Canyon that also means it didn't go down the link lane.
- **`forkRun`**, Grand Canyon: hold right at the fork, then the vehicle must reach the canyon jump's run-up.

`stunts.py` on `main` with the new tests: 526/559; all 32 `turnRun` checks fail (plus 1 shader-compile flake). On this branch: all new checks pass (556/559 before the rebase; the only failures were "no shaders compiled mid-flight" at 3 locations, 1 shader each, under heavy machine load; `main` had the same flake at islands).

## Tradeoffs

- In Arcade/Pilot, the assist now drives you round the turn. Kids hit it flat out without steering, so this follows the bowl's approach.
- **Sim** gets only the catch fence. A Sim car that hits the turn at 25 m/s is kept in, but it can roll over on the berm, and that's realistic. At the Grand Canyon a Sim car that doesn't steer goes straight on down the link lane, as before.
- The berm is a bit taller at its peak (6.8 m at the outside edge, was 5.1 m), and the tyres moved up onto its top.
- At the Grand Canyon the banking's ramp-up (s = 30–62 m) overlaps its ramp-down (54–94 m), so that turn never reaches the full 26°. The guide and the catch fence still get everything round.

author: zhihus
body:
## Problem

The hook runner writes the task JSON to the child process stdin before collecting its exit status. A hook that exits immediately with a non-zero status can close stdin before the write completes; the parent then reports Broken pipe instead of the hook's actual rejection. This makes completion errors nondeterministic and caused an existing Unix CI test to fail intermittently.

## Change

- Capture the stdin write result.
- Always wait for the hook process and prioritize its non-zero exit status.
- Report a stdin write error only when the hook itself exits successfully.

The existing before-done-openspec rejection test exercises this case.

## Validation

GitHub Actions passed on Ubuntu and Windows:
- cargo test
- cargo build --release
- cargo install into an isolated directory
- installed binary --help and version smoke tests.

author: phpcraftdream
body:
## Summary
The `ghost-zero-cost` gate compares total callgrind Ir of `examples/ghost_zero_cost_probe.rs` built from base and head (the probe is taken from the head for both sides; tolerance 0.1 %). The probe ran all phases in one `main` frame, and two extraction PRs in a row went red because of register selection in that frame (P2.2: +42 543 Ir; P2.3: +49 215 Ir = 0.48 %; +49 152 of it was one extra instruction per iteration in the loops of `main`), not because of allocator code. P2.3 was cured with a fitted `#[inline]` set.

The plan requires gate policy to change in a separate PR before the PR it judges, so this goes in before P2.4. **Gate script, policy and tolerance are unchanged**; only the measurement probe changes: growth, churn and the Large round trip become `#[inline(never)]` functions that receive the allocator and the buffer through `black_box`. The workload and its coverage are the same (16 384 x 16 B growth and free; 65 536 churn iterations over 16..2048 B with the same xorshift sequence and a 256-block live window; one 1 MiB Large round trip; one local `SeferAlloc`, no global allocator, no maintenance thread).

## Evidence
Throwaway branch, CI run [44928351811](https://github.com/PHPCraftdream/sefer-alloc/actions/runs/44928351811) (source `f6aef10dc301f18683e97b2fc032404cc4efdf2a`), 4 probes x 4 base/head pairs, one sample per arm:

| Probe | P2.3 without cure | P2.3 with the `#[inline]` set | P2.2 without cure | control (same SHA) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| old (current) | +49 215 | -332 | +42 543 | 0 |
| new (this PR) | -2 133 | -2 543 | -4 383 | 0, `.text` equal |

The old probe reproduces the historical deltas, so the harness is valid; the new probe's worst case is -0.042 % (-4 383 / 10 412 221) against the 0.1 % tolerance, with no `#[inline]` cure. Two other candidates were measured: one drifts -0.645 % on the clean extractions (rejected); one qualifies but executes 12.1 M Ir instead of 10.4 M and adds helpers. These are total callgrind instruction counts on one x86_64 Linux series, not wall time, and not a per-function attribution.

`docs/perf/GHOST_ZERO_COST_PROBE_STABILITY_20261121.md` holds the full table, calibration, toolchain versions and provenance; the 16 run lines are committed verbatim (`docs/perf/_raw_ghost_zero_cost_probe_stability_20261121.log`) with a summary CSV. `scripts/ghost_probe_stability_report.mjs` derives the tables from the raw lines, recomputes every delta and ratio and fails on any mismatch, on a calibration drift, or on a candidate beyond the threshold; `tests/ghost_probe_stability_report.test.mjs` has the counterfactuals (tampered delta, tampered ratio, drifted calibration, one instruction past the threshold, a control mismatch).

## Gate on this PR
Production code is untouched; the gate requires the exact proof here (identical normalized `.text` and Ir with the same probe on both sides), which CI judges. No Rust test or evidence-registry row is affected (no scope or recipe names the touched files), so no EV-1 request. `cargo check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` of the example with `--features production` passed locally.

author: fabian4
body:
## Summary

Fix the Delivery read existence oracle: an unknown `GET /v1/deliveries/{id}` and a Delivery whose Task is outside the caller's authorization boundary now return one identical non-disclosing `404`, while genuine Store failures remain `5xx`.

## Linked Issues

Part of #146

## Implementation & Impact

**Root cause.** `get_delivery` reads the Delivery by id before authorizing its Task. An unknown id failed as `BrokerDeliveryError::StaleDelivery` (`404 {"error":"DeliveryNotFound"}`); an existing Delivery whose Task was outside the caller's Scope, ownership, or active assignment failed as `BrokerTaskError::NotFound`, which `store_error` mapped to `404 {"error":"TaskNotFound"}`. Comparing the two bodies confirmed cross-boundary Delivery existence.

**Fix (`apps/hub-daemon/src/task_api/read.rs`).**

- Added `delivery_not_found()` as the single non-disclosing 404 response.
- `delivery_error` maps a missing row (`StaleDelivery`) to it; every other `BrokerDeliveryError` remains 5xx.
- Added `delivery_task_error`, which maps `BrokerTaskError::NotFound` from `get_authorized` to the same response and delegates every other error to the existing `store_error` mapping, so database failures remain 5xx.
- `get_delivery` uses `delivery_task_error` instead of `store_error`.

No DTO, Store schema, OpenAPI, Client, lifecycle, reconciliation, or WorkerVisibility changes. No new authorization abstraction: the fix reuses `TaskRead`, `TaskAccessFilter`, ownership/revision fencing, assignment fencing, and `WorkerVisibility`. Authorization is still decided once, in the Store predicate.

`docs/development/e2e-cases.yaml`: registered the new suite under `HUB-OWNER-SCOPE-AUTH` so conservative E2E path selection and the ownership-inventory check pass. All 74 Rust test sources now have exactly one owner.

**Tests.** New `apps/hub-daemon/tests/delivery_read_non_disclosure_test.rs` exercises the actual HTTP route:

- Authorized Owner reads an accessible Delivery (`200`).
- Unknown Delivery, same-Scope unauthorized Task, foreign-Scope caller, and a foreign-Scope Delivery all return the identical `404` body; no Task ids leak.
- A current configured Assignee and the one-time assignment grant read the Delivery.
- WorkerVisibility redaction is unchanged: `workerId`/`slotId`/`connectionEpoch` are null, nested Executor/Model/Harness/registration metadata is removed, `dataRedacted` is true, and Task-owned content remains.
- A revoked configured Assignee gets the identical `404`; a revoked grant no longer authenticates (`401`) without resource identity.
- A former Owner gets the identical `404` after ownership transfer; the new Owner can read.
- A Task-store failure and a Delivery-store failure both remain `500` (`TaskStoreUnavailable` / `DeliveryStoreUnavailable`).

**Limitations.** A caller can still distinguish a global Store outage (`5xx`) from a not-found; that is an availability signal, not resource existence, and the objective requires preserving 5xx. The pre-existing `beforeSequence > i64::MAX` → `500` boundary is untouched. The broader Delivery detail projection gaps (selected Executor, result/cancellation/rejection/reconciliation) remain in the separate #146 workstream.

## Verification

- Checks run:
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
  - `cargo clippy -p myrlet-hub-daemon --all-targets` — clean

author: nuraatwork
body:
## What

**@SatStartBot** for students: link by code, evening reminders about the trainers, cabinet and trainers open right inside Telegram (Mini App).

- **Linking**: each student has a one-time 6-character code (no look-alike characters). The student sends it to the bot, or taps “Подключить Telegram” in the cabinet (`t.me/<bot>?start=<code>`). The code is consumed on success; the tutor can unlink and issue a new code. At most 5 wrong attempts per hour per Telegram account.
- **Reminders**: once a day at the student's hour (19:00 by default, time zone taken from the student's browser), **trainers only** (grammar + vocab), and only if there is something due/new and the student hasn't practiced today. Commands: /today, /stop, /remind, /help.
- **Mini App**: inline buttons and the per-chat menu button «Кабинет» open `SITE_URL?open=<route>`; `prepareTelegramEntry` turns that into the hash route and strips Telegram's `tgWebApp…` params from the hash.
- **CRM**: «Telegram» block in the student card (code, copy link, reminder on/off and hour, reset).
- **Cabinet**: «Напоминания в Telegram» card on the home screen.

## Server

- Schema block «Telegram-бот» in `supabase/schema.sql` (already applied): tables, bot RPCs granted to `service_role` only, `telegram_portal` for the cabinet, `telegram_reset` for the tutor, pg_cron job `telegram-remind` (hourly, via pg_net).
- Edge Function `telegram` (deployed, `verify_jwt = false`, own auth): webhook checks a secret derived from the bot token; `?task=setup` registers webhook/commands/description; `?task=remind` is idempotent (`telegram_reminders_claim` hands out each student at most once a day, in their hour).

## Config (all variables, nothing bot-specific hardcoded)

- `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` — Supabase secret (set by the owner)
- `SITE_URL` — optional, defaults to the GitHub Pages URL
- repo variable `TELEGRAM_BOT` → `VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT` (set to `SatStartBot`); empty hides the Telegram UI

## Checks

- `npm run lint && npm run build` pass
- `?task=setup` → webhook registered for SatStartBot, no errors; unsigned POST → 403; `?task=remind` → runs
- Rolled-back SQL tests: code linking, one-time code, wrong code, rate limit, cabinet status, reminder claim (sent only to a student who hasn't practiced today; second claim in the same hour returns nothing)
- Browser: cabinet demo shows the Telegram card; `?open=me/demo` / `?open=grammar/demo` with Telegram hash params route correctly
- Not checked: a real Telegram account pressing Start and opening the Mini App (needs a phone)

body:
The option #431 asks for: a Home Settings row, *Sharp background*, off by default, that builds a pick's backdrop background the way an own photo's is already built — the lightly blurred 480×270 image (`reduce(out, GW, GH, 1, 1)`, one blur pass) instead of the heavy frost (192×108, three passes) upscaled to the screen. The photo reads as a photo again, with the same whitening ramp as the own-photos treatment so the clock, date and weather stay readable and the left side fades less toward the right.

What deliberately does not change:

- The bottom drawer's frosted glass and the Liquid Glass under the shelf and cards: they keep the 192×108 frost — that blur is what keeps text on glass readable, and it is what the drawer slides over.
- The Continue Watching design (a flat tint, no photo) and the own-photos background (it already had this treatment).
- Everything for anyone who leaves the row off: the frost stays, byte for byte.
- The web app (LG, Samsung): its background is drawn tiny and stretched, which is soft by construction — a sharper version there would be its own change.

Mechanics: `Backdrop.make` takes the own-photos branch when the pref is on (the branch is verbatim the shipped own-photos code); `Recs.invalidateBackdrops()` clears the cache on OK so the backdrops rebuild from their photos at once, the way the design flip clears them.

**Tested on:** built with `./build.sh --generic`; `tools/check.sh android` and `tools/check.sh web` pass; catalogues match (468 keys). The picks need a TMDB key, which this build doesn't carry, so the before/after on a real TV is the one thing left — @reporter, a build with the row on (For You tab, any TV) is what the change looks like: the photo behind Home sharp instead of frosted, drawer and cards as before. The treatment itself is the one own-photos backgrounds have had since the light design shipped, so the look is a known one.

author: thezedrem
body:
## Problem

With Ctrl+Tab set to sidebar order, the keys also go through the tabs inside closed folders. Pressing Ctrl+Tab then lands on tabs you can't see in the sidebar, and you have to press it again and again to get past a closed folder.

## Solution

Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab in sidebar order now pass over the tabs of closed folders, including folders nested inside a closed one. If the active tab is itself in a closed folder, the round goes on from there.

The sidebar keeps each folder's open or closed state itself (in `localStorage`). It now reports that state to the app with a new `set_folder_open` command: when a folder opens or closes, and once when the sidebar first shows it. The app keeps the closed folders in memory only, so nothing new is saved or synced. Cmd+1 to Cmd+9 still count every tab, as before.

## Testing

- `scripts/linux-container.sh test fmt clippy test ui` passes (Linux, Magnetite's CEF), with a new unit test for the skipping.
- Manual check on Linux (Wayland): with a folder closed, Ctrl+Tab passes over its tabs. Not tried on macOS or Windows.

body:
Closes #186.

The live-run scorer counted every line of a `profile.ts draft` command's result as a summary line the reply had to relay. When the coach chains a `write` or a `drop` with the draft in one command, that result also holds the command's own `written: <file>` or `dropped: <file>` line, which is not part of any summary, and the scorer reported it as dropped.

## What changed
- `scripts/lib/profile-lines.ts` holds the words the profile command prints for a write, a refused write and a drop, and `isWriteOrDropLine`, which tells those lines apart. `scripts/profile.ts` builds its output from the same functions, so the scorer and the command cannot drift.
- `draftsIn` (`examples/live-run/run-folder.ts`) leaves such lines out of a turn's summaries, whether they come before or after the draft's own output. `summary-whole` and every other rule reading the summaries are unchanged.

## Before and after on the baseline onboarding run (fbd35e8, the maintainer's run folder)
| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| all FAIL rows | 49 | 47 |
| line 4 rows | 4 | 2 |

Removed: `line 4 FAIL T38 "written: profile/identity.yaml"` and `line 4 FAIL T39 "written: profile/search.yaml"`. Added: none. Every other row is identical, including the two line 4 rows at T41 (`----` and the "Nothing you wrote changes..." line).

## Tests
`scripts/__tests__/live-run-score.test.ts`: a chained write and a chained drop, each with a reply relaying the draft's summary whole (no line 4 finding), each with one summary line left out (exactly that line is the finding), and a write line that prints after the draft.

Two drafts chained in one command: the baseline run does not show it, so no issue opened.

Closes acailic/SayItErmano#14

[SIET-5](https://chose-detective-singh-screw.trycloudflare.com/c709759a-9a73-47c9-9c16-beab1d1f6447/workspaces/siet-ms8it4bo/work-order/5)

Charging money raises the cost of a broken first install to a refund plus a bad review (#14). Every route a paying user can take must work on machines that are not the developer's — this adds the verification matrix as tooling plus committed evidence, with the fresh-VM execution itself reclassified as owner work (per the 2026-11-21 refinement: no root, no GUI, no VM on this run).

## What's in the change

**`scripts/qa_matrix.py`** — the harness. Six routes (one-shot user-space, one-shot `--system`, official .deb, AUR, pipx, Flathub) × three distros (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora, Arch) = 12 rows, each driven through **install → first-run onboarding → dictation → update** where the current environment can exercise it. Where it cannot, the row records `SKIPPED` with one deterministic, first-failing reason: wrong distro ("needs a fresh X VM — owner pass"), missing route tools (the one-shot is deb-based: bash+curl+dpkg/dpkg-deb, amd64-only), root required (`--system`/deb), makepkg refusing root (AUR), no display (onboarding), or the Flathub listing still pending (#12, probed live and never punished as a hard "no" when offline). Real per-route commands are resolved lazily — a skipped row makes no network calls and builds no commands (pinned by a test). Dictation is `MANUAL` by design (one real take on a GPU machine AND on a CPU-only machine), so an otherwise-green row rolls up to `PENDING` until the owner fills it; `FAIL` is the only red row. `--check` is the release gate: non-zero exit on missing evidence, stale schema, or any red row.

**Evidence baseline** — `docs/quality/install-matrix/`: one JSON per route × distro (all 12 committed, honestly `SKIPPED` with reasons — generated on this runner, which is Debian 12; that is precisely the owner's fresh-VM worklist) plus the generated `README.md` with the summary table, the red-row policy (zero ❌ at a paid launch; every red row fixed or documented as a known issue **with a workaround** in the install guide), and the per-distro fresh-VM checklist with copy-paste install/update commands.

**Install-guide ordering pass** — `docs/guides/install.md` gains a "Routes at a glance — best-converting first" table (one-shot user-space → one-shot `--system` → .deb/apt → pipx → AUR → Flatpak-planned → source); the README install section and the docs/evidence indexes now link the matrix. The Flathub row is listed as *planned, not yet published* so nothing unshipped is advertised.

**`tests/test_qa_matrix.py`** — 26 tests using fake environments and a fake exec runner (no root, no network, nothing spawned): skip-reason precedence (distro before privilege), each route's gates, step flow (failed install red-rows the row and skips downstream steps; deb URL-resolution failure is red, not a crash), evidence file shape, README table/checklist content, the `--check` gate's red/missing/stale cases, and os-release parsing for all three distros.

## Verification

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_qa_matrix.py -q` — **26 passed** (venv provisioned on this runner: Python 3.11, pytest 9.2.0).
- `.venv/bin/ruff check .` — clean.
- `scripts/check_docs_links.py` — all relative links and anchors resolve (new table anchors included).
- `scripts/validate_requests.py` — 40 briefs ok.
- `scripts/qa_matrix.py` then `scripts/qa_matrix.py --check` — 12 rows written, exit 0; gate green ("all 12 route x distro rows evidenced, zero red rows").
- Full unit tier (`scripts/test_tier.py unit -q`): 3627 passed / 35 failed — the 35 failures (test_insertion/test_recorder/test_preview/test_overlay: missing `xdotool`/`pw-record`/X11 tooling on this runner) reproduce **identically on base `linux` @ `43a0013`**, verified in a throwaway worktree with the same venv — pre-existing environmental, none introduced here.
- Not run: display/process/integration tiers (`just test-ui`/`test-process`/`test-integration`) — they need a display server or real mic/model hardware; this change touches no executable app code path.

## Constraints and remaining owner actions

No `.github/workflows/` edits; no root, GUI, or VM was used. Remaining for the owner: run the harness on fresh Ubuntu 24.04 / Fedora / Arch VMs (GPU + CPU machines), do the manual dictation takes, fill each row's `notes`, rerun after the next release ships to verify the update step, and commit the regenerated evidence — the flatpak rows unblock together with #12 (Flathub route).

author: helliott20
caretaker-janitor
body:
```console
$ ./create-sbuild-chroot-unshare.py --config janitor.conf bookworm 2>&1 | grep '^Unknown'
Unknown option: extra-repository
```

`create-sbuild-chroot-unshare.py` passes each `extra` suite to `mmdebstrap` as `--extra-repository`. `mmdebstrap` has no such option (`sbuild-createchroot` does), so the script fails for any distribution with an `extra` suite.

This passes each `extra` suite to `mmdebstrap` as a `deb` line. `mmdebstrap` copies a `deb` line as it is, without the `signed-by` it can add to a plain mirror URI. If the distribution sets `signed_by`, the distribution itself also becomes a `deb` line, every line gets `[signed-by=...]` with that path, and a setup hook copies the keyring into the tarball at the same path. Without `extra` and `signed_by`, the `mmdebstrap` command is the same as before.

Tested in the worker image with `mmdebstrap` 1.5.7. Both blocks use this `janitor.conf`, and the keyring is a copy of `debian-archive-bookworm-automatic.gpg`.

```
distribution {
  name: "bookworm"
  archive_mirror_uri: "http://deb.debian.org/debian"
  signed_by: "/etc/janitor/keys/debian-bookworm.gpg"
  component: "main"
  chroot: "bookworm-amd64-sbuild"
  extra: "bookworm-backports"
}
```

```console
$ ./create-sbuild-chroot-unshare.py --config janitor.conf bookworm > /dev/null 2>&1; echo $?
0
$ tar -xJOf ~/.cache/sbuild/bookworm-amd64-sbuild.tar.xz ./etc/apt/sources.list
deb [signed-by=/etc/janitor/keys/debian-bookworm.gpg] http://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm main

deb [signed-by=/etc/janitor/keys/debian-bookworm.gpg] http://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm-backports main
$ tar -tJf ~/.cache/sbuild/bookworm-amd64-sbuild.tar.xz ./etc/janitor/keys
./etc/janitor/keys/
./etc/janitor/keys/debian-bookworm.gpg
$ sbuild -v --chroot-mode=unshare -d bookworm --no-run-lintian hello_2.12.3-1.dsc 2>&1 | grep -E '^Get:.* InRelease|^Status: '
Get:1 http://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm InRelease [151 kB]
Get:2 http://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm-backports InRelease [59.4 kB]
Status: successful
```

author: benjithompson
body:
Replaces #66. That PR was merged into the `game-round` branch instead of `main`, so its changes never reached `main`. This is the same commit, rebased onto `main`.

## Shapes saved without a size
A shape's default size now comes from one place in `shared/layout.ts`: `treeSize`, `semicircleSize`, `radiusOf`, `heightOf` and `BUSH_TALL`. The defaults used to disagree. The lights of a tree with no `radius` spread 80 from its middle, but the editor's outline, handles, width field and the yard view drew it 60 wide, and "Make it a bush" turned it into a 60 bush. Everything now matches the lights. The editor and the yard view no longer write the 0.72 bush height or the 60/80/240 sizes as bare numbers.

## The layout schema follows the types
- The server's zod schemas for these types are now checked against the shared types with `satisfies SchemaOf<T>` (`server/src/schemaOf.ts`):
  - the layout and each of its objects
  - effect settings, light strings, designs and the aerial picture
  - sequences, with their clips, tracks, audio and markers
- Before, a field added to a type but not to its schema was silently dropped by zod on save. Now it doesn't compile, and neither does a schema field the type lacks. I tried it: adding a field to `Fixture` alone makes `tsc` fail at the schema.
- The enums for kinds, patterns, tree shapes, spins, zigzags, sides and units come from the same shared lists that the types are built from.
- Two `as Sequence` casts in `app.ts` are gone.

## Smaller cleanups
- There's one copy of each object kind's icon and name on the web (`web/src/lib/kinds.ts`). Before, the layout editor and the sequence panel each had their own.
- The "Make it a…" menu uses `SHAPE_KINDS` instead of its own list.
- Code that spelled out `roof || line` now calls `isLine`.
- A bare `2000` is now `MAX_FIXTURE_PIXELS`.

## How it was checked
- `npm run check` passes: 427 tests and the build. There are new tests for a tree saved without a size.
- I hashed what the layout code produces for about 100 shapes: every bush pattern, tree pattern and tree shape, and every semicircle zigzag, each with and without radius and height set. That covers their LED positions, outlines, paths, lengths, stage and kind changes. Before and after match exactly, except for a tree without a radius changing kind, which is the fix.
- The game frame hashes from #65 are also unchanged.
- I didn't open the layout editor in a browser. The web changes are only these defaults, constants and imports, and the build passes.

author: nivedn08
body:
Adds the Phase 1 practice environment: a two-joint arm that has to hold its fingertip on a target, written directly on MuJoCo and Gymnasium, with tests written first.

It includes a closed-form inverse-kinematics oracle, a checks module (zero agent, random agent, oracle, determinism, speed), a Stable-Baselines3 PPO training script with a target-hidden ablation, and the `env-check` skill. All numbers are in `results/reacher.json`, each with the command that produced it, and the gate is computed from that file by `faultladder.results.reacher_gate`.

Phase 1 gate, 1,000 evaluation episodes each on an M2 CPU: oracle 1.000 (needs at least 0.95), PPO 0.987 (at least 0.90), zero agent 0.007 and random agent 0.000 (at most 0.05), target-hidden PPO 0.000 (at most 0.10).

Two things worth knowing. PPO with Stable-Baselines3 defaults reached only 0.69, below the gate; adding observation normalisation (`VecNormalize`) is what gets it to 0.987. Six settings were compared on a separate set of evaluation episodes before the recorded run, and each PPO number comes from one training seed. Also, the tests caught a units bug in the first version of the model file: MuJoCo read the elbow range as degrees, so there are now regression tests for it.

author: brunoccalmeida
body:
Closes #40

## What changed
- **README rewritten for clients:** the problem in one sentence, what a client gets, how well it works, what it does not do yet (receipts only, public Malaysian receipts, English text only, a command rather than a service), and a link "For developers". No "Work in progress" banner; no SROIE values.
- **`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`:** every section removed from the README (At a Glance, Why this exists, Status, setup and commands, logging, configuration, Eval, Data), with links rewritten relative to `docs/`.
- **README numbers written by the eval** (`evals/readme.py`): the summary sits between `eval-summary` markers and is rewritten by `uv run poe eval --update-readme`. A full run that passes the baseline fails when the README block differs from the run, naming the fix. Below the baseline the README is neither checked nor rewritten: the fix for a worse score is the code, and rewriting would publish the worse numbers. `--ids` leaves the README alone; `--update-readme --ids` is refused (exit 2). A cost that rounds to zero reads "under $0.01", not "$0.00".
- Re-recording steps in `docs/DATA.md` now include `--update-readme`; decision recorded as D17 in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## Decisions
- **Generated block plus check, not hand-typed numbers** (chosen by the project owner): the recordings only exist in the `eval` CI job, so the check runs there, the same snapshot pattern as the committed JSON Schemas (D8). Hand-typed numbers go stale silently on a re-recording or a price change.
- **`DEVELOPMENT.md`, not `CONTRIBUTING.md`:** the project does not seek outside contributors. Source: [GitHub blog, collaboration-ready repository checklist](https://github.blog/enterprise-software/collaboration/a-checklist-and-guide-to-get-your-repository-collaboration-ready/) (README says what the project does; long setup goes in a separate file).
- **Deliberate content change in the moved "At a Glance":** the live counts (accepted, review, cost, tokens, 14 `needs_review`) were dropped there, since the README block now owns them and is gated; the table is labelled as the #26 comparison and points to `evals/baseline.json` for current values.
- **No demo video in the README.** The project owner watched the #39 video and found it unclear; its frames show a developer-facing script (command lines, `git diff`, "baseline 19/20", no problem stated, receipt and result never side by side). Rewriting it is #45, P1. The issue scope listed the video; this is the one item not delivered.

## How RED was seen
- `tests/test_readme_summary.py`: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'evals.readme'`, then against an empty stub every test failed on its own assertion (`assert [] == ['Measured on...`, `DID NOT RAISE ReadmeMarkerError` x4, the replaced block still holding `old numbers`).
- Sub-cent cost: failed with `- **$0.00 for the whole set**, about $0.00 per receipt.` before `_dollars`.
- `tests/test_eval_script.py`: the stale/update/subset tests failed with `unrecognized arguments: --readme`. Born green, proven by mutation: `test_update_readme_refuses_a_subset` failed with `DID NOT RAISE SystemExit` when the guard was disabled; the LF assertion failed on `'# Title\r\n\r\n...'` when `newline="\n"` was removed; `test_update_readme_below_the_baseline_leaves_the_readme_alone` failed when `--update-readme` wrote on a regression (README rewritten with the worse numbers).
- Regression advice: `test_a_regression_does_not_advise_updating_the_readme` failed with ``'update-readme' is contained here: ...oe eval --update-readme` and commit it`` before the check was limited to passing runs. Found by watching the demo's regression shot, which showed that advice next to the real failure.
- **Gate proven on the real eval:** with the new README and an empty block, `uv run poe eval` exited 1 with `README.md: the eval summary is out of date; run uv run poe eval --update-readme and commit it`; after `--update-readme` it exited 0. The block matches the report: 97/100 correct, 70 accepted (0 wrong), 25 to review (3 wrong), 5 empty, $0.63 ($0.03 per receipt).

## Reviewer findings (`mission:reviewer`)
Fixed:
1. README claims had no evidence link (REVIEW.md: "afirmação no README tem link de evidência"): links added to the CI runs on `main` (eval job summary), to the scoring method and to the known limitations in `docs/DATA.md`.
2. "20 public receipts" was typed outside the generated block and would go stale when the golden set grows (#35): the count was removed from that line.
3. No test for "below the baseline the README is not rewritten": added, proven by mutation.
4. D17 still said the README had a video: corrected.
6. The At a Glance table in `DEVELOPMENT.md` claimed to be the gated baseline while being a hand copy: relabelled as the #26 comparison, pointing to `evals/baseline.json`.

Answered: 5. "RED not visible to the reviewer": recorded above.

author: aq-azimsofi
body:
## Summary

Adding a reader tool used to take about eight coordinated edits in `app/read/page.tsx` and `ReaderFAB`, and one overlay had already been missed. This PR pulls the reader state into a few small, tested modules. Every localStorage key and value format stays the same, so returning readers keep their settings, their saved FAB and sticky-note positions, and their starred words.

- **Preferences** (`lib/preferences.ts`, `app/hooks/usePreference.ts`, `app/read/readerPreferences.ts`): each reader setting now has one table entry with its key, default and a validating parser. That covers furigana, font size, line height, display mode, AI explanation, theme, audiobook, audiobook content mode and sticky notes collapsed. `usePreference` is built on `useSyncExternalStore` and also listens to the `storage` event. `page.tsx`, the settings panel and the sticky notes read and write through it, and the mount effect plus the per-handler `localStorage.setItem` calls are gone. A stored `NaN`, an out-of-range number or an unknown value now falls back to the default. On main, `reader_font_size=abc` rendered an empty font size.
- **showRephrase** is now derived from `displayMode`. The duplicate state and its three hand-written syncs are gone. `readerThemeFrom`/`storedDarkModeFor` are replaced by the theme entry, and their compatibility tests moved into the table tests.
- **activePanel** (`app/read/readerPanels.ts`): `activePanel: 'settings' | 'explanation' | 'ruby' | 'copyRange' | null` replaces the four open booleans. The audio keyboard guard is now `acceptsAudioShortcut(activePanel, target)`, which also covers the copy dialog that the old guard missed. I checked the current behavior first: on main, panels stacked. The ruby lookup opened underneath the settings sheet, the copy dialog opened over the explanation, and Ctrl+K toggled the ruby lookup underneath the copy dialog. Now opening a panel replaces the open one.
- **FAB actions** (`app/read/readerMenuActions.ts`, `FabIcon.tsx`): `ReaderFAB` now takes `actions: FabAction[]` (id, icon name, label, onSelect, active, keepMenuOpen, beta). The list is built in one tested function instead of 18 props. The menu renders the same buttons in the same order in every state I checked.
- **Bookmark scroll**: the scroll-to-bookmark effect now runs only when the page or the bookmark changes. Audio state is read through a ref, so ending playback, a playback failure or closing the player no longer smooth-scrolls back to the bookmark.
- **useDraggablePosition({ storageKey, size, defaultPosition })** (`app/hooks/`, math in `lib/utils/draggablePosition.ts`): one copy of the drag logic (5px threshold, 100ms click suppression, mouse and touch, viewport clamp, persistence) now serves both `ReaderFAB` and `FloatingStickyNotes`. The FAB position key is now `STORAGE_KEYS.FAB_POSITION` (`'fab_position'`, same value). A saved position that is not `{x, y}` numbers now falls back to the default instead of producing `NaNpx`.
- **useStarredWords(directory, bookName)** (`lib/starredWords.ts`): owns the starred-words key, parsing and change notification, and is used by `FloatingStickyNotes` and `RubyLookupSidebar`. `toggleStar` now computes the next set and writes it outside any setState updater. The `'starredWordsChanged'` window event is gone.

Visible differences from main, all deliberate:
- Opening a panel closes the one that was open (see above).
- With the copy dialog open, audio shortcuts now do nothing.
- Invalid stored settings fall back to defaults.
- Stopping, failing or closing audio no longer scrolls back to the bookmark.
- Starring a word or changing a setting now also updates other open tabs, through the `storage` event.
- One corner case: when the sticky notes are restored already expanded, the saved position is clamped against the expanded width. On main it was clamped against the collapsed width.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run`: 54 files, 892 passed, 9 todo (main: 48 files, 786 passed). New tests cover:
  - `lib/preferences.test.ts` (parsers, defaults, invalid values, write notification, storage event)
  - `app/read/readerPreferences.test.ts` (each key and default matches the old format, NaN and unknown values, theme round trip)
  - `app/read/readerPanels.test.ts` (toggle and close transitions, the keyboard guard for every panel and for text inputs)
  - `app/read/readerMenuActions.test.ts` (menu order and labels in each state)
  - `lib/utils/draggablePosition.test.ts` (clamp math, drag threshold, stored position parsing)
  - `lib/starredWords.test.ts` (key, parsing, toggle, write notification)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` after `rm -rf .next`: clean.
- [x] `npm run lint`: 0 errors. The 4 warnings are the ones already on main, none in changed files.
- [x] Browser check with Playwright and system Chrome against `next dev` on port 3335, with every `/api` call answered from fixtures or aborted. 0 API requests reached the server and nothing was written to a database. I ran the same script on main and on this branch and compared the results:
  - [x] Settings persist across a reload: font 18, line height 1.5, Expanded, AI explanation, furigana off, dark. Stored values and rendered styles are identical to main.
  - [x] Opening each panel closes the others. Main left `settings+ruby` and `explanation+copyRange` open together, and once `ruby+explanation+copyRange`. Now exactly one panel is open at every step.
  - [x] Keyboard shortcuts do nothing while any panel is open. ArrowRight in keyboard mode fired 0 TTS requests with settings, ruby, explanation or the copy dialog open. On main the copy dialog let 4 through. The no-panel controls still fired 4.
  - [x] FAB menu: same buttons, order, labels and active states as main in 7 states (bookmark here, bookmark elsewhere, no bookmark, everything on, after copy, copy feedback cleared, analysis running). Page copy keeps the menu open.
  - [x] FAB and sticky notes: the mouse drag, click suppression after a drag, a 3px move still counting as a click, the viewport clamp (1228/748 at 1280x800), drags of the collapsed and expanded sticky notes, positions after reload and a touch drag at 390x844 all give results identical to main.
  - [x] Starring 素直 in the ruby lookup moves the sticky badge from 2 to 3 and stores `["窓","練習","素直"]`. Unstarring updates it too, and the sticky notes hide when the list is empty. Same as main, and a second tab now follows as well.
  - [x] Stopping audio does not scroll back to the bookmark. After closing the player, scrollY stays at 7957 (main jumped back to the bookmark at 1708). After a failed playback it stays at 7062 near the last tried sentence (main: 1708). A bookmark change still scrolls to the new bookmark (4270, same as main).

body:
Every ask now reads as one family: the dock's permission and question asks, the start ask, the settings ask, the hooks offer and the editor's leave sheet share one card and one row of choices (`AskChoices`, `AskKey`). The yes is always first and is the narrowest grant; wider and refusing answers sit behind More.

A usage limit is said calmly in a notice of its own, with "Continue when it resets" where a reset time is known. Its Continue and Cancel set only that conversation's choice, never the default for new ones.

Worth a close look:

- The digits were renumbered, so 4 is no longer Deny. A digit of a choice behind More only opens More: focus stays where it was, the row takes no answer for a 500 ms settle, and a held digit answers once at most. The docs give the numbering.
- The settings ask waits while any start ask shows, docked or floating, and a floating ask stands above the composer or dock of the session on screen instead of over it.
- Each new ask is announced once to a screen reader through one polite live line; the digit is left out of a choice's name.
- The hooks offer says it reaches every project, and the start ask's lasting answer says whose starts it allows.

Every preview of the web chat widget (the Device tab in Sediba Flows, and in the bot flow viewer) made a new **active** contact called "Web preview", so they piled up in Contacts. Production has 21.

- **The ones already there:** on update (`comm_chatbot_web` 18.0.1.0.1) a migration **archives** them, it does not delete them. A contact is only touched when it is nothing but a preview's: it came from a preview session, or it has exactly the preview's default name and number. Real visitors are unchanged: each still gets its own "Web visitor" contact.

author: ty0x7
body:
Refs #131.

## Reproduction and cause

On main `67e617f`, a project reviewer first promises to review a checklist. After the parent explicitly resumes the review, the reviewer reads the actual file. The model cannot mark it complete and the artifact guard skips the otherwise valid byline. A direct parent's frozen tool grant lacked the child's `complete_task` tool. A related group regression closed a promised-only subtask before the group orchestrator could send it back.

## Change and boundaries

Reserve the bookkeeping tool in work grants that expose native delegation. Only an eligible child's tools include it in direct-project conversations. The original grant, project membership, file and terminal tool permissions, and approval checks still govern the work. Keep a promised-only group subtask open for the existing continuation path. Unrelated and incomplete retries still cannot authorize the signoff.

## Verification

- The new direct-project test failed on main because the child did not receive the tool. It now uses two native handoffs, verifies the actual file read and completion, and reads the exact on-disk byline.
- In a separate real API replay, the retried reviewer used the tool and the signoff was written. The parent was still unable to call the completion tool in the direct-turn test.
- The existing group promise regression passes with the same continuation path. The combined source gate passed 482 tests with six skips. It initialized the production tool registry inside isolated pytest state.
- Extracted AppImage backend passed its self-check. The completed retry read the file, recorded a typed completion and wrote the exact reviewer byline. Unrelated/incomplete and clean authorized controls also passed.
- The combined Linux desktop and TUI used the same isolated backend at tree `05f514f6e4defde9f946733b5e04f3a29edeaf75`. All four TUI integration tests passed. The bounded 16K campaign independently passed 16/16 trials on both installed source and candidate source, including 4/4 held-out. The raw weighted score was 9.43 → 9.32. Two candidate deductions were verifier false negatives tracked in #147.
- Review is pending for both exact PR heads. The owner installation is still 11.15.0 at `563afaa`.

Terminal-generated attribution and independent review quality remain tracked in #131. Zero separately billed APIs.

author: bobdub
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"bobdub"} -->
_Requested by **bobdub** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Nf9uwE9PUffwKUWn2pvDuE?thread=cmsg_01Nf9uwE9PUffwKUWn2pvDuEWgj7wsffLTsMhep26JSawq)_

Phase 2 of the sea / wake / magma plan. It builds on the tide from #409.

## What changes
- `WakeTrail` (`src/lib/brain/sea/wake.ts`) now records each wake point's bow position, heading and speed. A new `ripples()` method builds one small 5×5 grid patch per point, which keeps the flat cells within centimetres of the curved sea.
- **Kelvin wedge from the rings.** Each ring's front grows at a third of the speed the boat had when she left it, so overlapping rings fan into the asin(1/3) ≈ 19.47° V on their own. Nothing paints the V directly.
- **Crests.** Crests are drawn as `sin(k·r − φ)`, running outward at the deep-water phase speed √(gλ/2π), which is faster than the front. They fall off as 1/√r and with age, and the middle of each ring goes calm once the energy has passed.
- **Wavelength.** It is a third of the transverse 2πU²/g, clamped to 0.9–3.2 m so it reads on screen. Faster boats make longer ripples.
- **Rendering.** `rippleMaterial.ts` is a tiny shader. `DockLayer`'s `BoatWake` draws all of a boat's rings in one extra draw call, under the existing foam ribbon. Rings and ribbon both sit on the shared tide. It stays purely visual and per viewer, so nothing is sent.

## Checks
- A new wake test covers the wedge angle, ring growth and fade, crests outrunning the front, patches sitting on the sea, and expiry. The sea suite passes (79 tests).
- Rendered a boat at 6 m/s in headless Chromium with no shader errors.
- No live session was opened.

author: mattiasaan
body:
## Cosa cambia

### Deploy
- Il frontend viene pubblicato su GitHub Pages con una GitHub Action (`.github/workflows/frontend-pages.yml`).
- Il backend può essere esposto tramite Cloudflare Tunnel. Guide aggiornate in `deploy/README.md` e `readme.md`.

### Interfaccia
- Palette più sobria: grigi neutri, superfici piatte senza gradienti e glow, angoli meno arrotondati, numeri in Inter con cifre tabulari.
- Colore dell'app selezionabile (blu o verde) da **Profilo → Impostazioni**. La scelta è salvata sul dispositivo e vale anche al login (`src/lib/theme.js`).
- Accessibilità: niente più `opacity` sulle righe attenuate (lezioni completate o annullate, voti annullati); `--quiet` schiarito. Contrasto ≥ 4.5:1 ovunque.
- Performance: Google Fonts caricato da `index.html` con `preconnect` invece che con `@import`; animazione degli skeleton con `transform`.
- Lighthouse sulla build di produzione: Performance 100, Accessibility 100, Best Practices 100.

### Documenti legali
- Informativa privacy, cookie policy e termini di servizio, in `frontend/src/legal/*.md`.
- Consultabili nell'app anche senza login (`#privacy`, `#cookie`, `#termini`), con link nel footer del login e nel profilo. Sotto il pulsante di accesso c'è la nota di accettazione dei termini.
- Mini renderer Markdown (`src/lib/markdown.jsx`) che produce elementi React: niente HTML grezzo né link `javascript:`. Ha i suoi test.
- `robots.txt` e `<meta name="robots">`: niente indicizzazione né crawler AI.
- `legal/README.md` con la checklist prima dell'apertura al pubblico. Registro dei trattamenti e procedura data breach sono documenti interni, esclusi da git.

### Sicurezza backend: password ClasseViva cifrata in memoria
Prima la password restava in chiaro nella RAM del server per tutta la sessione (fino a 7 giorni). Ora:
- al login viene cifrata con AES-256-GCM, con una chiave casuale per sessione, e tolta dall'oggetto `Utente`;
- il testo cifrato è legato a `sid` e username;
- la chiave sta **solo nel JWT** (nuovo claim `k`, obbligatorio): il server non la conserva;
- a ogni richiesta `ActiveSession` unisce la sessione e la chiave del token. La password viene decifrata solo durante la chiamata a ClasseViva e poi rimossa;
- una copia della memoria del server non rivela più le password.

author: mincuties
body:
The server centre-crops every photo to a square, so an eye near the edge of a wide photo could be cut off before the model saw it. This change fixes that in the browser, without changing the server.

What the page now does:
- After a photo is chosen, it shows a square box with a dashed circle as a framing guide.
- The user drags the box (or moves it with the arrow keys) and sets its size with a slider. "Center" puts it back.
- Only that square is uploaded, at most 1600 px a side.
- The default box is the same centre square the server would take, so a photo sent without changes is handled as before.
- Moving the box clears an old result.
- All text is in English and Vietnamese.

Details:
- The crop is stored in pixels of the upright photo and mapped onto the bitmap decoded with EXIF orientation. If the two sizes do not match, nothing is cropped and the server falls back to its centre crop.
- The box never gets smaller than 20% of the short side or 64 px, which is the server's minimum.

MediaPipe was not used: it needs the whole face and fails on close-ups and everted eyelids, the photos this app asks for. Letterboxing instead of the centre crop is added to a new README section, "After retraining the model", because the current model was trained on centre crops.

Checks:
- 152 pytest and 16 node tests pass. The new node tests cover the default crop, clamping, resizing and mapping onto a bitmap.
- In a headless browser, I dragged the box onto an off-centre red disk in a wide photo, then did the same on a photo with EXIF orientation 6. In both cases the uploaded image was a 300×300 square containing the disk. With the box left in the centre, the disk was not in the upload.
- Also checked: arrow keys, and the Vietnamese layout at phone width.

author: magto
body:
Refs #488

## Merge brief

**What and why**
After the update to 4.10 on tubal-cain, a Start-menu start brought back the old hidden app window as it was: header "ledung v4.9", "Failed to fetch", no update banner, until Martin pressed Ctrl-R. The fix of #479 (PR #487, in 4.10) never ran.

**Cause, confirmed from the code:** a second start of the app is handled by the copy of the app that is *already running*, with the code it was started with. The hidden window had been started on 4.9, and 4.9's handling of a second start only showed the window (checked: the 4.9 publish commit's app code has just "show the window" there). PR #487's restart is 4.10 code, so it can only run in an app that was itself started on 4.10 or later: the 4.9 → 4.10 update could never use it. Assuming Martin used the app's own Start-menu entry ("Ledung app" → Ledung, which starts the app itself; the other "Ledung" entry runs `ledung`, which would have started Ledung and logged `#456` at once), that is why `restart.log` has no `restarting the app … (app only)` line and there is no `EXERCISED #479` (both are 4.10 code too). The `#456`, `#407` and `#455` lines in that start's log most likely come from Martin's **Ctrl-R** (inferred from the code and their timing, 20:19:31Z, just before his 21:21 message, not confirmed): on 4.9, Reload after an update restarts the app into the installed version (#455), and that restart, also 4.9 code, writes no "restarting the app" line. Ledung itself was not running until then (`#456`, "Ledung started in the background", is logged by that same restart), which is why the shown window said "Failed to fetch" and never got a banner. Martin's app now runs 4.10, so the next update is the first that can exercise #487's restart.

What this PR changes is the page side Martin decided on: "c — Banner only" (Martin, 2026-11-21 21:25, Ledung question #112 on tubal-cain, relayed by tubal-cain's manager and recorded on #488): "Keep the banner only, but retry faster (every 0.5 s while the server is away), and fix the Start-menu restart"; note: "I like the banner better, just make sure we get it..". The 2026-10-13 decision stands: the page offers a reload and never reloads under the person's hands.

**How it works now**
While the page has lost Ledung, it tries to reconnect every half second, every time; before, the wait doubled up to 10 seconds. While it waits, the page reconnects at once when it is shown again, gets the focus (a hidden desktop window brought to the front by a second start is shown and focused) or the network comes back. As soon as it reconnects to a Ledung of another build, the existing update banner appears; the page never reloads by itself. The desktop app is unchanged: an app running 4.10 or later still restarts itself into the installed version when a start reaches it hidden and out of date (#479).

**Calls it made**
- No code was added to the desktop app for the restart: nothing a new version ships can change what an already-running older app does on a second start, so the issue's last Done bullet is met by explaining the cause (the bullet's second branch), not by new code.
- Retries never slow down, taken as Martin's "every 0.5 s while the server is away" (no back-off to 10 s). The page can't tell "away" from "refused": a connection a running Ledung turns down (a signed-out or removed browser, a refused address) is also tried every 0.5 s instead of every 10 s, for as long as the page stays open, and from a phone or another computer that goes over the network or through the relay. A cap (0.5 s for the first few minutes, then slower) would limit that; not built, since it goes against the decision's words. Martin's call if wanted.
- "Shown again" counts focus and the network coming back as well as the tab becoming visible, because a hidden desktop window counts as "visible" to its page (the app keeps hidden windows running at full speed), so only focus tells the page it was brought back.
- The retry timing moved out of the page's connection code into a small module of its own, so a test can drive it with a fake clock.
- The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions.md` as a 2026-11-21 row.
- Filed rather than fixed here: a second start that reaches a hidden, up-to-date app with Ledung stopped shows the page with no server behind it and starts nothing (#490).

**Review findings**
Self-check round 1 (the builder's own check, before review): four Minor findings, all in this brief, all fixed. (1) The retry trade-off for refused connections and the relay was not named: now under Calls it made and What it touches. (2) The cause called confirmed partly rests on inference: the shortcut assumed and the Ctrl-R attribution are now marked as inferred. (3) The fourth Done bullet had no test plan line: added. (4) The revert check only shows the module is needed: the test plan now says what the code tier covers. Code reviews: none yet.

**Done-conditions**
- *On Windows, after X, `ledung stop`, `npm install -g ledung@dev` and a Start-menu start, the app opens on the new version or the banner shows within about a second; never a stale version with "Failed to fetch" and no banner* — **can't verify here**: needs Martin's Windows PC, and only from an app already on 4.10 or later (see What and why). The page half (banner within about a second of Ledung being back) is met in the code tier.
- *While the server is away, the page retries every 0.5 s (no back-off to 10 s); a hidden window shown again reconnects at once* — **met**: new tests drive the retry with a fake clock (21 tries 0.5 s apart; at once on shown, focus and online; nothing while connected).
- *The page never reloads by itself* — **met** by reading: the banner path is unchanged and nothing here reloads.
- *A Start-menu start reaching a hidden out-of-date instance logs the restart line and `EXERCISED #479`; or the PR says why with evidence* — **met by the second branch**: the start reached an instance running 4.9 code, which has no such restart; evidence above.

Evidence: CODE-ONLY — the retry is proven in the code tier; the Windows start after an update can only be judged on Martin's PC, from the next update on.

**What it touches**
Shared interfaces: none. Data and migrations: none. Permissions and security: no change to what is allowed; a refused connection is retried more often (see Calls it made). Config: none. Other people's code: the page's live-connection setup. Undo: revert the PR; the page goes back to the doubling wait.

**Try it**
1. In the desktop app (now on 4.10), close the window with X, run `ledung stop`, then `npm install -g ledung@dev` once this ships.
2. Start the app from the Start menu: it should restart into the new version by itself (`restart.log` gets a `restarting the app <pid> (app only)` line, exercised.log `EXERCISED #479`).
3. Separately, with the window open, run `ledung stop`, then `ledung`: the page should be back within about a second, with the update banner if the version changed.

**Left over**
- #490: a second start reaching a hidden, up-to-date app with Ledung stopped starts nothing and shows no Start Ledung.
- #485: the Mac twin (a Dock click reaches the app as "activate").
- An app still running 4.9 or older code can't be helped by any update; Ctrl-R (Reload) restarts it into the installed version.

## Class

- **Property** — every reconnect loop on the page waits the same short time between tries while Ledung is away, and tries at once when the page comes back into view.
- **Search** — `grep -rn -E "Math\.min\([a-zA-Z]+ \* 2" web/src src desktop` → no output after the fix (the one doubling wait was `web/src/useLedung.ts`); `grep -rn -E "new WebSocket\(" web/src` → `web/src/api.ts:202:  const ws = new WebSocket(url);` (the one live connection, opened only from `useLedung`).
- **Disposition** — no other occurrence; check: `test/page-reconnect.test.ts` (the 0.5 s step and the at-once tries).

author: nawid3333
body:
Follow-up to #798: an 8 GB laptop froze with "RAM for buffered video" at 20 GB, and nothing on the options page said that was too much for it. Firefox gives extensions no RAM size (no `navigator.deviceMemory`), so the user is asked.

**This computer's memory**
- Asked once on the welcome page (first install) and in Options > General, right before the RAM field: Not set / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 GB or more (sizes formatted by the browser in the page's language).
- An answer sets the RAM for buffered video to an eighth of it, at most 4 GB (500 MB / 1 / 2 / 4 GB), and turns "Keep video on disk when this RAM is full" on. "Not set" leaves the RAM as it is.
- New option `computerMemory` (GB, 0 = not given).

**Warning under the RAM field**
- Above 4 GB, or above a quarter of the memory given: "This much video in RAM can freeze a computer…" (`options_general_rambudget_high`).
- The no-limit hint now names the freeze and says to set a limit.
- "No limit" stays available (owner's choice).

**Lines the lists leave out**
- Auto-enable URLs, the mpv list and the custom source patterns dropped lines they could not read without a word. The page now names those lines under the field, on load and after each change (`IgnoredLines.mjs`).

**No guard while playing** (measured, owner's decision): in a memory-capped test (3 GB RAM + 2 GB swap), the player's timers ran at most ~0.9 s late while RAM and swap filled, and 13-62 s only once it was frozen; a 5 s sleep gives the same spike. A 1 GB limit kept the same video smooth (34 ms). Numbers in storage.md.

8 new strings and 1 rewritten, in all 16 locales; combined-locales regenerated. Tests: `RamGuard.test.mjs` (sizes, thresholds, the welcome page saving over the stored options), `IgnoredLines.test.mjs`, page wiring. Docs: storage.md (the budget), player.md (options lists).

## Summary

author: patrickbrandao
body:
## Resumo
Task 361 (revisão completa de 2026-11-21). A trava `/tmp/fs-load-running` era só uma convenção dos scripts de carga: `make deploy` e o passo e2e do `verify-full` não a consultavam, e o `test/load/run.sh` matava o `loadmon` de outra carga, sobrescrevia a trava e a apagava ao sair. O `budget.sh` recusava, mas o `cleanup` dele apagava a trava e o diretório da outra carga do mesmo jeito.

- **Deploy**: `deploy.sh` recusa (saída 3, com a data da trava) antes do build, e o `remote-install.sh` recusa de novo já sob o `flock` (`load_lock_refuse` em `install-lib.sh`), para fechar a janela do build e do rsync. `FORCE_DURING_LOAD=1` passa por cima.
- **e2e**: `verify.sh` (`e2e_tests`) recusa o passo com a trava; `FS_E2E_DURING_LOAD=1` passa por cima.
- **Scripts de carga**: `test/load/loadlock.sh`, comum a `run.sh` e `budget.sh`, toma a trava de forma atômica (`set -C`) com um token próprio, recusa sem tocar na outra carga (nem trava, nem `loadmon`, nem diretório remoto) e só apaga a trava se o token ainda for o seu.
- **F8**: o `f8-side.sh` segura a trava entre as rodadas; o `run.sh` passa a precisar de `FS_LOAD_LOCK_HELD=1` nesse caso (exige a trava, não a cria nem a apaga). Comentário do `f8-side.sh` atualizado.
- **Spec 017 RF-13**: a trava vira regra (alteração delegada pela tarefa, papel architect).

## Testes
- `deploy/deploy_test.go`: `deploy.sh` com `ssh` local e `make`/`rsync` falsos (com a trava: sai 3 sem build; sem ela ou com `FORCE_DURING_LOAD=1`: segue); `load_lock_refuse` e a ordem no `remote-install.sh`.
- `scripts/verify-test.sh`: o passo e2e com a trava recusa sem rodar o `go test`; com `FS_E2E_DURING_LOAD=1` e sem a trava, roda.
- `test/load/loadlock_test.go` (pacote novo, sem build tag): duas cargas (a segunda recusa sem tocar na primeira), token, vigia (`FS_LOAD_LOCK_HELD=1`) e os dois scripts usando a trava comum (falha contra os scripts anteriores).

## Verificação
- `make verify-quick`: **verde** (nível quick, inclui `verify-test`, `deploy` e `test/load`).
- `shellcheck` dos scripts tocados: limpo (o SC2046 do `remote-install.sh` é anterior e de linha não tocada).

author: rabbiveesh
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"rabbiveesh"} -->
_Requested by **Veesh** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WEHwB3HeRRGSuYYjuwAQou?thread=cmsg_01WEHwB3HeRRGSuYYjuwAQou1PRthHJZ8BYQew4JAdJCoa)_

Layer 1 of the position-keyed joins stack (`design/position-keyed-joins.md`, group A). The ratchet `build_facts_are_not_keyed_by_position` drops from 45 to 38 sites.

## What changes

`SkeletonAnalysis::into_file_analysis` rebuilt six facts by matching spans after the tree was dropped. The extractor has each of them on one node, so it now states them on the row.

| Was (span join at assembly) | Now (minted in the extractor) |
| --- | --- |
| `by_span`: body scope → its callable | `SkelSymbol::body`, set when a `@scope.sub` opens on a def's own node |
| `written`: read tokens an assignment writes | `VarRead::written` |
| `write_sites`, `init_sites`, `written_members` | `SkelRef::access` (`Write` / `WriteIfUnset`) |
| `decl_name_spans`: a `@ref.type` on a def's own name | the ref is not minted (`refs::drop_declarations`) |
| `flow.rs` `reads`: member read by span | the minted read carries its row |

`Minted` now links each def node to its `symbols` row and its name token. `ExtractState::retain_symbols` is the one place rows are dropped during extraction, and it renumbers that link, so the facts are read off the defs that survive dedup. `resolve_returns` no longer depends on running before dedup.

`write_sites` and `init_sites` are gone from `SkeletonAnalysis`, and with them their span remap in `language_driver.rs`.

## Evidence

`scripts/equiv/run.sh origin/main` (features `cpp,php,python`), base e3c3b630 against this change:

```
== cli inputs (fixtures, gold substrate, grammar corpus) ==
equiv: 576 inputs in base, 576 in head: 576 identical, 0 changed, 0 dropped, 0 new
== cargo test inputs ==
equiv: 3027 inputs in base, 3027 in head: 3027 identical, 0 changed, 0 dropped, 0 new
```

Limits of that run:
- This box has no gold substrate (`gold-corpus/local`) and no real corpora, so the CLI side is 576 inputs, not the ~3,900 of a full run. PHP and Python are covered only through the `cargo test` inputs.
- `cargo test` under the dump has one failure on both sides, base included: `live_window_tests::a_chain_build_reads_each_write_a_bounded_number_of_times`. I did not chase it. CI will say whether it is the dump environment.

## Points to discuss

**Cost.** `Minted` grows by four `Option<usize>` and two `bool` per capture event. It lives for one extraction and is freed with it. `retain_symbols` is one pass over the events per call, and it is called twice. No cache or memo is added. I have not measured wall or RSS; say if you want a 3-rep A/B.

**Interactions.** The flags are minted from the extractor's own captures. Rows another lane adds after extraction carry none: the C++ macro lane's injected symbols and `VarRead`s, and slot symbols `declare_slots` adds at assembly. The old span sets could match those by coincidence of position, and after a macro remap folded spans together. The dumps show no input where that happened, but the nets here hold little macro-heavy C++.

**Ordering.** Three orderings are assumed:
- A def is handled before the `@scope.sub` on its node. The existing `tie_rank` enforces this.
- `unify_assigned` marks assigned tokens before `flow::finish` reads them. This is by call order in `extract_in` only.
- `refs::drop_declarations` runs last, because it shifts `refs` rows that `Minted::ref_row` points at. This is by call order and a comment only. A `retain_refs` helper like the symbols one would enforce it, if you want that.

**Remembering.** New fields on `SkelSymbol` and `SkelRef` are forced through the exhaustive destructures in `remap_skeleton`. A new site that drops `symbols` rows during extraction must go through `retain_symbols`; nothing enforces that beyond there being no other `retain` in `extract/`.

**Not in this PR.** `into_file_analysis` has other joins by span containment that the ratchet does not count, because they are not maps: def arity from `param_sigs`, class bodies, an enumerator's enum. They are the same class of thing. I left them for a decision on whether this stack takes them.

author: luseefor
body:
Native mode relies on undocumented macOS interfaces, and when it broke on a display the user got at most one in-app alert, and nothing at all if the extension simply stopped serving a display. This makes those failures visible, falls back automatically, and puts Restore Original Wallpaper within reach.

- **Failure notice:** each time native assignment or verification fails on a display, LumaWall posts a macOS notification (with a Restore Original Wallpaper action) and shows a banner in the main window and the menu bar popover. Both name the display and say it moved to Safe mode. A display is reported once per failure episode; turning native mode off and on starts a new one.
- **Extension health (ADR 0003):** while native mode is visible, the app posts a `healthPing` Darwin notification every 10 s; the extension answers by writing `lumawall-health.json` (pid, rising sequence, displays with a live surface). A watched display missing from answers for 20 s moves to Safe mode. No probes while locked, asleep or in the screen saver; wake, unlock, display changes, Space switches, screen-saver end and every WallpaperAgent restart start a 30 s grace. The rules are in `ExtensionHealth` (LumaWallCore) with tests.
- False-trigger guards: silence counts only once this build's extension has answered (remembered per build); a display that some Space shows a non-LumaWall wallpaper on is never fallen back; a verdict is dropped if the store was written or a disturbance arrived before it is acted on; native work already running can't write a fallen-back display back.
- **Restore** is now in Settings whenever a backup exists, in the popover footer (↩, two clicks), and on the notice. It turns native mode off if it is on and **stops LumaWall's playback** (clears the per-display assignments and any playlist), then puts the backup back; otherwise Safe mode's windows would cover the restored wallpaper. This changes the existing Settings button, which used to leave the overlay playing.
- `docs/testing/native-mode-matrix.md` is the live checklist for macOS 26 and 27, with nothing filled in yet. Row 17 (quit the extension) is the forced-failure check from the issue.

Verification: `ExtensionHealthTests` covers the timeout, the grace after disturbances, cancelled probes, relaunched and never-answering extensions, and the answer file's size limit. `HealthReplyTests` covers the extension's answer and throttle; `NativeModeGateTests` covers the notice text and that the health fallback does nothing without a native host. Nothing here was run against a live native wallpaper: the app can't be installed on this machine. The matrix is how this gets checked.

Risks: the app asks for notification permission the first time native mode fails. A Space whose wallpaper isn't LumaWall's can make macOS drop the extension's surface there; if that lasts past the grace period, the display moves to Safe mode (noted in the ADR).

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Settings, native mode on | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Luseefor/LumaWall/702ec2683d890b5ea2d373f79a509a37b349d0ba/01a1ffdc-7aeb-796b-a475-e1d0372ac48a.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Luseefor/LumaWall/702ec2683d890b5ea2d373f79a509a37b349d0ba/01a1ffdc-7b15-7714-b5f4-4347e5f27226.png) |

New banner, main window and popover (rendered offscreen; previously an alert with no actions):

![banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Luseefor/LumaWall/2c90272946ec4d67b39a6325144960d85815f709/01a1ffdc-cb31-7c0a-aa5f-0a75e3044b12.png)

![popover banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Luseefor/LumaWall/2c90272946ec4d67b39a6325144960d85815f709/01a1ffdc-cb71-763c-a6ed-c7fbe24687c6.png)

Left open (from the Codex review):
- A Settings picker preview on a display keeps that display in the extension's answer, so it can mask a failed desktop surface while the preview is open.
- A display with a non-LumaWall wallpaper on any Space is skipped by the check, even while a LumaWall Space on it fails.
- On the first launch of a new build, an extension that never answers isn't caught by the ping (assignment and verification failures still are).
- If an apply is mid-deploy when Restore runs, it undoes its sessions and assignment afterwards, but its poster may already be in the macOS store.
- The answer file is read with `O_NOFOLLOW` on the file only; a symlinked Documents folder could redirect the read. It's only parsed as a small JSON reply, so nothing leaks.

Part of #107: the matrix still has to run on both macOS versions.

body:
Replaces #67, which closed when its base branch was deleted. **This branch includes the v2.43.2 commit, so merge v2.43.2 first.** Until then, this PR's diff also shows that commit.

This is the first slice of moving the logic that needs no screen out of the 5,500-line `LayoutPage.tsx`, so it can be tested. Nothing changes for the person editing.

## What moved
- **Line edits:** these went to `shared/layout.ts`, next to `extendLine` and `insertPoint`:
  - `splitLine`: cut a line at a corner
  - `removePoint`
  - `pinPoint` / `unpinPoint`

author: opherdonchin
body:
Part of #21

## Purpose

[Issue #21](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/issues/21), approved by the researcher on 2026-11-21, lists small gaps in HILD's tooling. This PR fixes the two that concern the wiki status tool, `wiki_status.py`, which builds the wiki's Status board. It also fixes a Windows line-ending defect in the same tool, found on 2026-11-09. The issue's other two items are handled elsewhere: item 1 by [scope #22](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/issues/22), item 3 by [scope #16](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/issues/16).

## What you should understand

1. Text inside backticks or code blocks on a wiki page no longer counts as a link to another page.
2. A new test fails if the wiki page templates and the tool stop agreeing on the header format.
3. On Windows, the tool now writes files with ordinary Unix line endings.

## Summary

- **Code is no longer read as links.** Before reading links, the tool removes fenced code blocks and inline code spans. A page that shows the syntax, for example `` `[[Name]]` ``, used to put a missing page called `Name` on the Status board. That happened on 2026-11-21. Inline spans are kept to one line, so a stray backtick cannot hide real links further down.
- **The templates are tested against the tool.** The test fills in both wiki page templates and checks that the tool reads their kind and status, and, for the code-page template, the files covered and the commit described. If someone changes a template's header table, the test fails.
- **Line endings.** `--write` called `write_text` without `newline`, so on Windows it wrote CRLF line endings. Git then warned on every wiki commit. Both writes now use `newline="\n"`, and an existing test checks that no carriage returns remain.

## Walkthrough

- **Load-bearing: read this.**
  - [`wiki_status.py` L37-L40](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/blob/18df93a67ff3efdf7ff8f888370802692934331b/HILD/scripts/wiki_status.py#L37-L40): the two patterns for code blocks and inline spans.
  - [L149-L152](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/blob/18df93a67ff3efdf7ff8f888370802692934331b/HILD/scripts/wiki_status.py#L149-L152): `strip_code`.
  - [L155-L172](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/blob/18df93a67ff3efdf7ff8f888370802692934331b/HILD/scripts/wiki_status.py#L155-L172): `not_written`, which now reads links from the stripped text.
- **Boilerplate: skim.** The `newline="\n"` arguments at [L182](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/blob/18df93a67ff3efdf7ff8f888370802692934331b/HILD/scripts/wiki_status.py#L182) and [L298](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/blob/18df93a67ff3efdf7ff8f888370802692934331b/HILD/scripts/wiki_status.py#L298).
- **Tests:** [`tests/test_wiki_status.py`](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/blob/18df93a67ff3efdf7ff8f888370802692934331b/tests/test_wiki_status.py)
  - `test_link_syntax_in_code_is_not_a_link` covers spans, double-backtick spans, fenced blocks, a stray backtick and a real link.
  - `test_templates_filled_in_are_read_correctly` is the template test.
  - Two line-ending assertions were added to `test_large_change_is_stale_and_write_marks_it`.

## Evidence

- Run locally on Windows (Python 3.14) at `18df93a`: `pytest tests/test_wiki_status.py tests/test_session_context.py` gave 17 passed; `pytest tests/test_install_hild.py` gave 19 passed.
- The stray-backtick case was checked against the old pattern: with the old pattern the real link disappears; with the new one it is kept.
- CI runs on this PR.

## Consequences

- The Status board's list of missing pages now contains only real links.
- Wiki commits made on Windows no longer produce line-ending warnings.
- The branch history contains a commit that added `__pycache__` files by mistake, and a later commit that removes them. The squash merge carries neither. This repository has no `.gitignore`. Adding one would be a new kind of file, which is a stopping point, so it is not done here.

## Wiki pages

- **Relevant:** [Concept-understanding-map](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/wiki/Concept-understanding-map) (`needs-review`). It describes how this tool finds missing pages, and once this merges it should also mention code spans.
- **Proposed:** `Code-wiki-status` (`not-written`), already in the [scope #20 page plan](https://github.com/Motor-Learning-Lab/HILD/issues/20#issuecomment-7066388119). It is written after the integration branch reaches `main`.

## Review track

**Proposed: fast.** The change is small and covered by tests. On the fast track you would confirm what it is for, what goes in and comes out, and what it affects. **Full** is the alternative if you want to explain it back in your own words.
