author: wsdo
body:
## What changed

Stacked on fastagi/zmail#65. Prepares the source interface for real Gmail, Outlook, and IMAP adapters.

- `Fetch` takes a request with the account address, backfill window, and sync time.
- A fetch may return `More`: the connection is fetched again at once, so a long backfill proceeds page by page and resumes after a restart.
- A fetch may return a rotated refresh token, which is sealed and saved in the transaction that stores the page.
- `ErrExternalMailCursorExpired` restarts the sync from an empty cursor without duplicate copies.
- Real connectors register a builder from their own file with `registerExternalMailConnector`, so adding a provider touches no shared file.
- `EXTERNAL_MAIL_PROVIDERS` accepts `gmail`, `outlook`, and `imap`. OAuth connectors need their client id, secret, and the redirect URL; `fake` cannot be combined with a real connector.
- Adds `docs/plans/mail-connectors-loop.md` and the progress log used to run the rest of the roadmap.

## Why

Microsoft rotates refresh tokens, large mailboxes cannot be backfilled in one call, and Gmail and Graph cursors expire. Without these the first real adapter would lose accounts or stall.

## Verification

- Three new service tests (paged backfill, token rotation, cursor expiry) and config tests.
- `go test` for the mailbox, config, bootstrap, and starter packages passes against PostgreSQL.

## Reviewer notes

- No adapter is compiled in yet, so listing `gmail` or `outlook` enables nothing until those PRs land.
- Sync run records, rate budgets, and attachment metadata are left for a later task.

## Summary

`POST /v1/outfit-plans` now looks at the wardrobe photos, not just the text labels.

- For each wardrobe item, the service downloads its `imageUrl` and sends the photo to Gemini (`gemini-4-hydrogen`) with the item's id.
- The new prompt (`outfit_planning_v2`) uses the photo to judge real color, cut, warmth and formality, and trusts the photo over the label when they clearly differ. Only the labelled item counts as owned, even if the photo shows other things.
- If a photo can't be downloaded (bad URL, host not in `MEDIA_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, wrong type, over 10 MB), that item is planned from text and a warning is added. A photo problem never fails the request.

## Changes for B

All additive and optional:
- Request: `useWardrobeImages` (default `true`).
- Response: `wardrobeImagesUsed`, the ids whose photo Gemini actually saw.
- B needs to send real, readable `imageUrl`s for wardrobe items, from a host listed in `MEDIA_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

## Result on the demo trip

Same 3-day Kyoto trip and 10-item wardrobe, one run each:

| | With photos (~27 s) | Text only (~21 s) |

| Purchases suggested | 1 (rain coat for the 70% rain day) | 2 (rain coat + navy trousers) |

author: pedrorezendefig
body:
## 💬 Valor entregue

**O que muda:** No caso do paciente que conta uma conduta grave de um profissional, o ouvidor aperta Sinalizar ao Canal de Conduta e o Comitê de Conduta recebe o relato para apurar, sem o nome nem o contato de quem reclamou. A manifestação continua aberta na Ouvidoria, e o histórico dela registra a sinalização.

## 🎯 Contexto

Fatia do PRD #1786 (Canal de Conduta), ADR 0097 decisão 14: a segunda exceção ao sigilo do relato. Manifestação de paciente sobre conduta grave continua na Ouvidoria; o ouvidor sinaliza ao Canal, o Comitê recebe o relato integral sem quem manifestou, e o ouvidor não passa a ver o caso do Canal.

O que mudou:
- `POST /api/ouvidoria/manifestacoes/{id}/canal-de-conduta` (gate do Perfil da Ouvidoria) e o serviço `ouvidoria_canal_de_conduta.sinalizar`: cria o caso pelo `casos.registrar_caso` com origem `ouvidoria`, carimba `conduta_sinalizada_em` e grava o movimento na trilha sem trocar o estado. Nada do caso volta na resposta.
- Migration 202: `conduta_casos.origem` e `manifestacao_id` (índice único parcial, CHECK que só a origem `ouvidoria` leva vínculo) e `ouvidoria_protocolos.conduta_sinalizada_em`. A coluna nova está classificada na retenção.
- Dossiê: bloco `BlocoDoCanalDeConduta` com confirmação; depois de sinalizado mostra o aviso e o botão some. Lista do Comitê mostra "Origem: Ouvidoria" (`origem` entra em `CAMPOS_DA_LISTA`).
- `test_conduta_varredura`: a rota da Ouvidoria tem "conduta" no caminho e cairia no detector de rota fora do módulo; ela entra numa exceção explícita, e um teste novo confere que a exceção só grava (POST) e pede o Perfil da Ouvidoria.
- Kit de conhecimento `ouvidoria.md` diz o comportamento novo.

Decisão de implementação: "relato integral" segue o precedente do envio ao Núcleo (#1997): o texto vai como foi escrito, e os campos de nome, e-mail e telefone de quem manifestou nem são lidos. Se o próprio relato citar o nome de quem escreveu, ele vai junto. A sinalização não depende da chave de abertura do canal público (ela só fecha a página pública); sem a chave de cifra a rota responde 503 e nada é gravado.

## ✅ Critérios de aceite

- [ ] O botão aparece no Dossiê para quem tem o Perfil da Ouvidoria.
- [ ] O caso criado traz o relato integral e não traz nome nem contato de quem manifestou.
- [ ] A manifestação não muda de estado e ganha um movimento registrando a sinalização.
- [ ] O ouvidor recebe 403 ao tentar abrir o caso no Canal.
- [ ] Sinalizar duas vezes a mesma manifestação não cria dois casos.
- [ ] O texto do Produto Ouvidoria no kit de conhecimento diz o comportamento novo.

## 🔎 Evidência

- **Antes:** `POST /api/ouvidoria/manifestacoes/{id}/canal-de-conduta` respondia 404 (`test_ouvidor_sinaliza_e_o_caso_nasce_na_triagem_com_o_relato_integral_e_a_origem_ouvidoria` falhava com `assert 404 == 200`); o Dossiê não tinha o botão (`o botão aparece no Dossiê do caso que ainda não foi sinalizado` falhava); o Dossiê não trazia `conduta_sinalizada_em` (KeyError).

author: a1d4r
body:
A text query like `Ru 2019 S01` (title, year and season, the way AIOStreams sends it) parses into title `Ru 2019` and original title `S01`. When the exact card search found nothing, the original title was added to the fuzzy query variants on its own, and `Key.Contains("s01")` returned the first season of every unrelated show: hundreds of results.

This PR skips title variants made only of S/E season-episode tokens: `S01`, `s1`, `S01E02`, `E05`, and ranges or tails such as `S01-S03`, `S01E01-02`, `S01.`. Real titles like `4x4` or `Season 1: Origins` are kept. The v1 fuzzy pairs (`V1SearchPairs`, used with `mergeV1=true`) get the same check, since the bare token could end up there as the search term or the altname. The stripped variants (`Ru 2019`, `Ru`) and an explicit `q=S01` are searched as before.

Tests: `IsSeasonEpisodeOnly`, `BuildQueryVariants` and `V1SearchPairs` cases, plus a FileDB-backed `SearchCombinedAsync` test that seeds an unrelated `… S01` show and checks that it is no longer returned.

author: isaacennalsbray
body:
## Why
Crawlers were downloading **every** chronicle file (316 files, 446 MB) every few days, and daily by 17–20 November. Each download ran through `/chronicles/[id]/download`, which fetched the file from Blob and sent it back out, so it counted against both Fast Origin Transfer and Blob Data Transfer. On 20 November the team went over the free plan's 10 GB Fast Origin Transfer and Vercel paused **all** of its projects (they return 402 until 20 December).

`robots.txt` alone isn't enough, because crawlers can ignore it. So the expensive part now needs a login, which crawlers can't get past.

## What changed
- **Text stays public.** 293 of the 308 imported PDFs (and all new chronicles) already show their text on the page; that's unchanged.
- **Files need a login:** `canDownload` in `src/lib/access.ts`. Logged-out visitors to `/download` are redirected to `/login?next=<chronicle>` and come back afterwards.
- **Logged-out pages don't load files:** the button says "Log in to download PDF/image/audio", and the 15 text-less scans, 7 photos and 1 recording show a "Log in to see it" note instead of the viewer.
- **Photos no longer link straight to Blob** (anyone with a Blob address can download from it). They go through `/download` too.
- **`robots.txt`** asks crawlers to skip `/chronicles/*/download` and `/login`. Downloads also send `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.
- **Cache:** downloads are now per-user, so they're `private` (only that browser keeps a copy; Vercel's CDN must not share it).

## Screenshots (logged out)
![Text-less scan, logged out](https://github.com/isaacennalsbray/chronicle/blob/screenshots/pr-32/logged-out-scan.png?raw=true)
![Chronicle with text, logged out](https://github.com/isaacennalsbray/chronicle/blob/screenshots/pr-32/logged-out-text.png?raw=true)

## Tested locally (`vercel dev`)
For one chronicle of each kind (PDF with text, scan, photo, recording, new chronicle):
- Logged out: the page shows text or the login note; `/download` returns 307 to the login page.
- Logged in: the page shows the viewer and download button; `/download` returns 200 with the right content type, `private` cache and `noindex`.

No Vercel preview: the team is paused, so Vercel isn't building previews right now.

author: kaiserwilhelmi
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"kaiserwilhelmi"} -->
_Requested by **DAwso** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FFX6iidoY4WEHgHARfkrsD?thread=cmsg_01FFX6iidoY4WEHgHARfkrsD8QhDpnWDhKtFg8mGb7fUCE)_

## What changes
- **Custom weights:** "How the score works" is now an editor. Each KPI has a weight box (the weights must total 100%) and an on/off tick. Unticking a KPI shares its weight across the others, and a button resets to the research-based defaults. The page remembers the choice in the browser.
- **Downloadable template:** The .xlsx and .csv are built in the browser from the current weights, using a small .xlsx writer with no library.
  - **Data:** only the columns the enabled KPIs need, plus 9 fictional rows marked "SAMPLE -". Excel flags bad entries as you type.
  - **Instructions:** what each column means, its unit, and the rule it has to pass on upload.
  - **KPI definitions:** formulas, the chosen weights, cited sources and a worked example.
  - **Sources:** full references.
  - **Settings:** the weights. The page reads them back when the .xlsx is uploaded.
- **`agreed_value` replaces `contract_value`:** It means qty × the contract, quote or PO price, and files that still use `contract_value` load fine. The column is optional: rows without it are left out of the price KPI, and a supplier with none is scored on its other KPIs, reweighted to 100%.
- **Upload checks:** Every problem is listed with its spreadsheet row number:
  - missing columns, explained in terms of which KPI needs them
  - values that aren't numbers, negative values and fractional counts
  - counts above their base, such as on_time_pos above pos
  - bad months and duplicate supplier-month rows
  - suppliers whose totals are zero
  - a warning if SAMPLE rows are still in the file

  Months still load if Excel turned them into dates.
- `score.py` takes `--weights` and handles blank values. The sample data columns are renamed, and regenerating the data gives identical values.

## Sources (KPI definitions)
- APICS (2017), SCOR v12: the four perfect-order components
- Mena, van Hoek & Christopher (2021), Table 3.2 and pp. 70–71
- Weber, Current & Benton (1991), *EJOR*
- Ho, Xu & Dey (2010), *EJOR*
- Gunasekaran, Patel & McGaughey (2004), *IJPE*
- Dickson (1966)
- Monczka et al. (2021)
- Datar & Rajan (2021)

The default weights, floors, targets and tier cut-offs are labeled as the tool's own choices, not published benchmarks.

## Testing
`python tests/roundtrip.py <xlsx.full.min.js 0.18.5>` drives the real page in headless Chromium and runs 66 checks, all passing:
- the weights editor
- the default and custom-weight downloads: valid zip/XML, columns, weights and the worked example compared against `score.py`
- uploading the templates, a filled-in file with Excel-date months, a CSV using the old column name, blank agreed prices and several broken files

The page's scores matched `score.py` in every case.

## What

Ports the deterministic pieces of `vendor/claude-code-mini/src/logCondenser.ts` into a pure, dependency-free module `lib/harness/log-condenser.ts` (no LLM step, no wiring — the task explicitly defers wiring).

`condenseLog(raw: string): string`:
- strips internal runtime frames (`node:internal`, `node_modules`, `at async Promise`);
- keeps failure-clue lines, capped at `MAX_FAILURE_LINES` (40);
- falls back to a deterministic head/tail splice (10 head + marker + 15 tail) when no failure clues are found;

author: zsomborrajki
body:
## What this changes

The hike screen's *Offline* tile shows and downloads each area as the list has it now, looked up by its code. It works out its coverage again whenever the list's entries change, not only when their codes change. Fixes #1532.

## Why

The tile kept whole `Country` values from the list it last read, and keyed that work to the route revision and the areas' codes. A refresh that brought a new build under the same codes left the key unchanged. The dialog then showed the old build's size, and its Download button sent the old build, whose files the server deletes once it has moved past them.

- `OfflineCountries.catalogRevision` counts the changes to what `listed` is read from. A read of the list that brings back what it already held does not count, so the tile's coverage (worked out on the main actor) runs again only when something changed. An area landing or being deleted counts too, because `listed` keeps downloaded areas the server no longer offers.
- `listedCountry(_:)` and `missing(from:)` give the dialog each area as the list has it now, at its current size.
- `downloadListed(_:)` looks the area up again at the tap. A dialog opened before a refresh cannot send a deleted build, an area the list no longer holds is not downloaded, and neither is one downloaded since the dialog opened.
- The tile's task key no longer sorts every area by its localized name on each body pass. It used to, and during a download that ran on every progress tick.

## How it was verified

- [x] `Scripts/lint.sh` passes
- [x] The app and widget unit tests pass (pool device, `-derivedDataPath DerivedData`, `-only-testing:OpenHikesTests -only-testing:OpenWidgetTests`): 6,544 tests in 690 suites and 141 in 15, exit 0
- [x] New behaviour has a test: `OfflineCountriesNewBuildTests` builds the same-code replacement (build `20261117` replaced by `20261201`, with a basemap of another size). It checks that the revision moves only on a real change, that a line's crossings found before the refresh are offered as the new build at the new size, and that a tap from before the refresh asks for the new build's file names and writes it as the pending download. It also covers an area the list dropped and one downloaded since the dialog opened.

These tests call the new API, so they cannot be run against `main`. The old tile filtered `coverage.crossed` directly and passed the kept value to `download(_:)`, which is the path the issue traces.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

- The `didSet` on `offered` compares the whole list, outlines included, on each read. That is one deep comparison per list read, and it keeps an unchanged read from making the tile recompute coverage. A `didSet` on an `@Observable` property fires for subscript writes and `removeValue` too; I checked that with a scratch build before relying on it.
- Out of scope, and unchanged: the tile reads the server's list only when nothing is listed. A device holding a cached list that is days old can still start a build the server has since deleted. That download fails with a 404, and *Try Again* (`retry(_:)`) reads the list and moves to the current build.
- #1531 is open in another session on `OfflineCountries+Coverage.swift` and `OfflineRouteCoverageTests`. This PR touches neither file.

author: gabriela-miranda-leite
body:
## Objective

Importing/creating two mocks for the same route used to coexist silently: `MockEngine.match()` picked whichever rule happened to come first in insertion order, with no warning and nothing in the UI telling you a conflict existed. This surfaced while debugging why a one-shot error mock never fired next to a "success" mock for the same `httpbin.org/get` route.

## What changed

- `MockRule.conflictsWith()` (core): two **active** rules conflict when they share the exact `urlPattern` and an overlapping `method`. A one-shot rule paired with a non-one-shot rule for the same route is exempt — that's the deliberate "fire once, then fall back to this response" pattern, not a conflict.
- `MockEngine.addRule()` now auto-disables any existing active rule the new one conflicts with, and emits a new `conflictResolvedEvents` `SharedFlow` describing what got disabled.
- `DebugOverlay` shows a warning toast when a conflict is auto-resolved (mirrors the existing "mock used up" toast).
- The Mocks list (`MockRuleRow`) and detail screen (`MockRuleDetailScreen`) now show a persistent warning icon on any rule that **currently** shares its route with another active rule — not just at creation time, so it stays visible if a conflict reappears later (e.g. re-enabling an old rule).

author: yoavbendor
body:
## Summary

`reader::open("s3://bucket/key.parquet")` (and the C entry points, which call it) reads the object by range instead of in memory:

- The footer is read from the object's tail. If the footer is larger than 64 KiB, it is read a second time.
- For each row group, the column chunks the read needs are fetched together, in one range, when that range is at most twice their bytes. A sparse projection keeps one request per chunk, so it does not fetch bytes it does not need.
- Each chunk's bytes are freed when the chunk has been decoded.
- Local files are unchanged: they keep the memory map, and the decoder reads the same bytes as before.

Off by default. `-DP2N_S3=ON` enables it and needs libcurl. It fetches nanos3reader at `65aa2e7` with the bundled SHA-256 (no OpenSSL). Without the option, an `s3://` path fails with a clear message.

Internal changes: the decoder takes its chunk from a `chunk_range()` helper, which the reader also uses; `mapped_file` is back to its original form; `decode_leaves` takes the row group's prefetched bytes (forward-declared in the public header).

## Dependency

Pins nanos3reader commit `65aa2e7` (yoavbendor/nanos3reader#8). Switch the pin to the tag once it exists.

## Testing

- Default build: all 5 tests pass, including the pyarrow differential tests and the 76-file parquet-testing corpus.
- `P2N_S3=ON`: all 6 pass against moto, including `s3_read`. It writes a 60,000-row table with four row groups and a 1,500-column table whose footer exceeds 64 KiB, uploads each, and checks that the full and projected reads equal pyarrow's read of the local file. A missing key must fail with HTTP 404.
- Memory and time on a 712 MB, 40-row-group file, streamed batch by batch (moto):

| Build | Time | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|
| Whole object (previous commit, `eb66dc1`) | 37.0 s | 783 MB |
| One request per chunk | 50.1 s | 112 MB |
| Coalesced per row group (this PR) | 16.7–17.8 s | 121 MB |

- Local reads: unchanged within noise (0.15–0.18 s on a 39 MB file).

moto's per-request cost grows with object size, so the timings are not representative of real S3. Memory is the more reliable result: the reader holds one row group's projected chunks, not the object.

## Notes

- The default branch of this repository is `claude/nanom-lance-parquet-enhancements-2erjot`, so this PR targets it.
- Writing to S3 is not part of this PR; that is yoavbendor/nanoarrow2parquet#17.

author: tonysimpson
body:
A follow-up to #5. There, once a rich compare slot that may run Python code declines, the rest of the comparison is made at run time. object_richcompare, called as an operand's own slot, never runs Python code (its != calls the same slot for ==), but every call counted as one that might, so `a == b` and `a != None` on plain objects went to the run-time path: about 94 more instructions per loop iteration of the two in a micro-benchmark on 3.10 (161 to 255). With this the count is back to main's (153).

make check passes on 3.10.

This adds the threshold calibration panel. An analyst can preview how a module threshold trades false positives against missed violations, then save it. It completes the dashboard features in `web/CLAUDE.md` "Done", all on the contract mock server.

**Stacked on #40** (itself on #39). Merge in order: #39, #40, then this.

OpenSpec change: `calibration-panel` (archived in the last commit), new capability `web-calibration`. No new dependency: the Recharts chunk is shared with the trend.

## Behaviour changes
- **Kalibracja progów section** (lazy-loaded, below the findings):
  - Module switch: M2 first, then M1, M3.
  - A keyboard slider that moves only between the points of `GET /calibration`. It starts at the point nearest `current_threshold`.
  - TP, FP, FN, TN, precision, recall and F1 shown exactly as returned, each next to its value at the current threshold. When the saved threshold is not on the curve, the comparison is labelled as the nearest point.
- **Chart:** precision and recall against the threshold, with markers for the current and the selected threshold, plus a data table as text alternative.
- **Save:** `Zapisz próg` sends `PUT /settings/thresholds` with all three thresholds, only one changed. The button is described by a warning that the change is global (every finding's risk level and the alert threshold). After a save, findings, stats, calibration and settings refetch. Save feedback does not carry over to another module.
- **Calibration also refetches after a status change:** `PATCH /findings/{id}` (`enhanced.ts`) and `finding.updated` from #40 now also invalidate `calibration`, because analyst labels feed the curve (integration-plan §5). This is recorded in `.claude/rules/web-dashboard.md`.

Reapply SQLiteMemoryStore's constructor-bound Path identity. author: discordwell
body:
## Why

A red test run should mean a real bug. Two Claude credential tests failed every time in the Docker harness, which runs as uid 0, because root reads the mode-0 file they treat as unreadable.

## Cause

`TestClaudeReauthStopsWhenTheProfilesCredentialCannotBeRead` and `TestClaudeAddKeptAfterAnUnreadableCredentialIsPublished` made the profile's `.credentials.json` unreadable with `chmod 0`. As root the store read it anyway. The re-auth then ran its browser login, and the add confirmed its login, so both tests failed with no regression.

## Fix

Test only. No production code changed.

Both tests now put a directory where the credential file belongs. The store refuses it with EISDIR, which `credentialFileRefused` classifies with EACCES, so the store gives the same verdict as root and as any other user. The tests take the same production branch everywhere and need no root skip. `TestACredentialsFileTheFileSystemRefusesIsAVerdict` in `internal/agents/claude` already uses a directory as one of its refusals.

A directory holds no token. So the re-auth test now checks that the unreadable credential was left in place, instead of reading back the old token after a `chmod 600`. `writeProfileCredentialFile` loses its mode parameter, since its only other caller passed `0o600`.

## Proof

All runs in Docker, as root, with `./deploy/docker/test.sh ./cmd/subrouter -run '<the tests>' -race -timeout 0 -v`.

| Code | Run | Result |
|---|---|---|
| main | `-count=1 -cpu 1` | both fail: `the browser login ran although the old credential could not be read: <nil>` and `add = <nil>; want the profile kept` |
| this PR | `-count=20 -cpu 1,2,4` | 60 of 60 pass for each test |
| this PR, production guards removed (temporary, reverted) | `-count=1 -cpu 1` | both fail: `the browser login ran although the old credential could not be read` and `the kept profile was not published after the login` |

The guard mutation ignored the pre-login `ReadCredential` error in `addOAuth`, and dropped the `publishProfileCompletion` call on the kept-profile branch. It shows the rewritten tests still catch the regressions they guard.

`TestClaudeReauthThroughTheTUIWaitsForTheNewLogin` ran in the same stress run and failed once in 60 with a data race. The race is in that test's output buffer, not in this change, and it gets its own PR.

author: cosnicolaou
body:
## Overview
Adds a new `query` package that defines a row model (prefixes, users, groups and hotspots) over idu's analyzed data. The MCP server now uses it for its tools, and gains a general `query` tool and hotspot rankings.

## Key Changes
**query (new package)**
- `Engine.Run(ctx, Query)` returns rows from the `prefixes`, `users`, `groups` or `hotspots` tables. A query sets a scope (`self`, `children` or `subtree`), an `OrderBy` column (`total_*` or `direct_*` for each metric), an optional UID/GID, a `Level`, a `Filter` and a `Limit`.
- When it can, a query is answered by looking up data that analyze maintains: summaries, recursive totals, a best-first subtree search, top-N rankings, per-user and per-group totals, or a fresh snapshot.
- Otherwise it falls back to a pass over the summaries, or over file metadata when there is a filter.
- `WithLookupsOnly()` disables the fallback passes; those queries then fail with `UnsupportedError`, which wraps `ErrUnsupported`. `WithSnapshotDir()` sets where snapshots are looked for.
- `Result.Source` reports where the rows came from (`Source*` constants), and `Result.Exact` says whether they are known to be exactly the top rows.
- Column helpers: `Direct`, `Total`, `ParseColumn`, `Columns`.
- Tests cover prefixes, children, levels, rankings, users and groups, passes, filters, hotspots, lookups-only mode and unsupported queries.

**mcpserver**
- New `query` tool (`QueryArgs`, `QueryResult`, `QueryRow`) that exposes the full row model.
- `usage`, `children` and `top_n` are now built on `query.Engine`, which removes the ranking, heap and snapshot code that was duplicated here.
- `top_n` adds `by=hotspot`. With a user or group, `by=prefix` now works beneath any prefix, not just the filesystem root; beneath a non-root prefix it uses a pass over the summaries.
- The server instructions and tool descriptions now cover hotspots and the cost of lookups versus passes.
- Tests updated, and `TestQuery` added, which also checks hotspots from a snapshot.

**Misc**
- `Makefile`: generates the README for `./query`.
- `main.go` / `cmdusage.go`: the `mcp` command summary mentions hotspots and the query tool.

## Breaking Changes
None to the Go API. MCP clients may notice these changes:
- `top_n` returns different `source` strings, for example "a best-first search of the recursive totals" or "the per-user and per-group totals maintained by analyze".
- `top_n` validation error messages have changed.

author: eddiectc-acode
body:
Replaces the redundant `known_hosts` file bind with a single `~/.ssh`
directory bind.

Binding the directory already delivers `known_hosts` at the path ssh reads by
default: `ssh -G github.com` reports `userknownhostsfile
/home/acode/.ssh/known_hosts`, and `~` there is the passwd entry's home, not
`$HOME`. The nested file mount therefore asked the reader to reason about a
file mount inside a directory mount for no gain, and only made sense for a
setup that binds the key alone.

One directory bind also keeps the key and the host keys together, which is how
they have to be created on the host anyway.

The read-only argument is unchanged and now covers the pair. ssh writes to
`known_hosts` only while learning an unseen host, and pre-populating removes
that write, so a writable mount would buy nothing and would let an injected
instruction re-pin `github.com` to a key of its choosing -- the exact attack
the file exists to prevent. Keys come from GitHub's published list over HTTPS
rather than `ssh-keyscan`, which trusts whichever host answers first.

Verified end to end in the container rather than argued: with `known_hosts`
inside a read-only `~/.ssh` directory bind, `ssh -T git@github.com` and
`git ls-remote github` both succeed with no `UserKnownHostsFile` or
`StrictHostKeyChecking` override at the default checking level, while an empty
`known_hosts` and one holding only a wrong key both fail with "Host key
verification failed".

author: mangod12
body:
## What changed

Analysts can now pivot from exact event evidence to other owned records with the same saved source IP, destination IP, hostname, username or domain within an anchor-derived UTC time window.

- Explicit read only. The server rereads the owned anchor, derives its current exact field value and a bounded 1 to 168 hour window on each side, excludes the anchor, and pages timestamp/ID ordered records.
- Same-field literal equality only. No case folding, IP canonicalization, cross-field matching, external lookup, AI call, inferred attribution or state changes.
- Only bounded event metadata is returned. No raw payloads, byte counters, user IDs or source credentials.
- UI separates unapplied field/window choices from results, rejects malformed/incomplete responses, ignores late reads after clear, handles shrinking pages, and warns if the anchor changed since the evidence above was loaded.
- Links open original event evidence. JSON download contains only the currently loaded page and its exact scope, with no extra fetch and a sensitive-data warning.

## Validation

- 39 backend tests covering this endpoint and existing event evidence/export behavior.
- 69 frontend tests covering the component, event evidence, event list and event source routes.
- Production frontend build, focused ESLint and full backend Ruff passed.
- Actual desktop/mobile browser flow: event 99 to exact domain/one-hour pivot, second-page original event link, parsed one-row loaded-page JSON, draft guards, no implicit or extra export reads, no writes, no console errors or horizontal overflow.
- Desktop and mobile screenshots visually inspected, including readable selected field and applied current anchor/window.

Page numbers are bounded before database offset calculation; extremely large page requests return validation errors rather than database integer errors. Rebased onto actual merged #542 and all feature validation repeated.

No README, demo credentials, billing or deployment/infrastructure changes.

author: krutik460
body:
An outside review found eight problems in the widget engine that would get expensive once real users or sharing exist: a look with an endless loop could hang the widget, nothing capped memory at render time, synced rows could be misread or touch the wrong dataset, an old button could run a newer action, and nothing covered tinted or dark mode. This PR fixes them and runs the app and widget on the iOS simulator for the first time.

- **JavaScript engine.** Looks now run in QuickJS-ng (vendored, MIT) with step and memory budgets, so a runaway look stops in milliseconds instead of spinning a thread forever.
- **Render caps.** One image pixel budget per render, a 1 MB cap on the look's input, a static cell cap, and the `full` proof state now writes text at the real limit.
- **Sync safety.** Cells carry their kind, every row change names its dataset, future-stamped and oversized remote input is held back, and a design that arrives by sync is proved on this phone before it draws.
- **Taps carry their revision**, so what the user pressed is what runs.
- **Tinted and dark mode.** Color pairs, `accent`, image `tint`, and proof cells that reject a look whose tinted render is blank or one flat sheet.
- **The app.** `App/project.yml` (XcodeGen) builds an app and a widget extension. On an iPhone 18 Pro simulator, home screen taps change data and redraw in about a second without opening the app, and extension memory is 18 MB against the 30 MB cap.
- **Leftovers.** All 12 allowlisted fonts ship on iOS (new test). The habit widget's today square stays visible in tinted mode, and done to-do titles no longer wrap. Water now runs on the home screen in small and medium. That check showed the water plus vanishing in Clear mode, where `accent` does not separate colors, so the plus is now a cutout and `look.md` teaches that. It also showed the plus moving when the minus appeared, so a quick second tap undid the drink.

`scripts/check` passes: 231 engine tests and a warning-free app build. Still open: the physical device step. Two things to confirm there: a tapped face sometimes keeps its old picture on the simulator until the home screen is shown again, though the timeline is right, and the gallery's default widget can be stale.

A review guide with a diagram per entry point is in `docs/pr/1-phase-1d-review-fixes.md`. Details and decisions are in `tasks/todo.md` (phase 0 and phase 1d).

author: ashprabaker
body:
Step 1 of #11. The tool discovers Tokyo Digital Twin 2024 sheets, assigns them to OSM ward boundaries, extracts crowns, merges adjoining sheet fragments and writes deterministic TKTR v1 tile packs. Successful sheets are cached individually. No raw LAS or whole-ward pack is included.

Six offline tests passed, covering cones and round crowns beside flat and pitched roofs, building masks, adjoining sheet fragments, exact binary records, one-to-one reference matches, Tokyo ward disambiguation and a 48 m real Shibuya crop. The source index decoded to 5,672 sheets. The Kanto OSM extract dated 2026-11-20 supplied the ward polygons. A repeat pack from cached results reproduced every tile byte-for-byte. The additional retry test selects one evidence sheet out of two. An unchanged retry makes zero source reads. A damaged overlay or changed reference rebuilds only that sheet. Ward runs can request three review overlays with `--evidence-mesh`. I also reproduced an unreadable cache stopping a whole retry and a misplaced cache duplicating another sheet’s geography. At 4c77c73, both recover by reading just the affected sheet; incomplete bounds and an overlay attributed to the wrong sheet have regression coverage. All six offline tests pass. I repeated this with the real Shibuya source pair and three other sheets’ cached results. Only Shibuya’s DEM and LAS were read. All three output tiles and the 2,941-candidate manifest were byte-identical to the original four-sheet pack. A second retry read zero archives. The temporary survey archives were then deleted.

The real-sheet run used buffered OSM building footprints and natural=tree nodes from the BBBike Tokyo extract dated 2026-11-14. It produced 2,941 candidates across four sheets. Green outlines are detected crowns, yellow dots mark apexes, and pink rings mark mapped reference trees. Matching used 3 m maximum distance and one-to-one assignment.

| Scene | Sheet | Candidates | Matches / mapped trees | Precision vs mapped | Recall vs mapped |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Residential Nakano | 09LD0673 | 936 | 1 / 3 | 0.11% | 33.3% |
| Shinjuku office towers | 09LD1648 | 799 | 35 / 51 | 4.38% | 68.6% |
| Yoyogi Park | 09LD2618 | 678 | 12 / 15 | 1.77% | 80% |
| Shibuya commercial streets | 09LD2659 | 528 | 9 / 9 | 1.70% | 100% |

The mapped inventory is sparse, especially in Nakano. Nakano's count fell from 3,149 to 936 with footprint masking, but linear structures and building edges still generate false positives. Yoyogi's open field stays mostly clear, while dense overlapping crowns can split at multiple peaks or hide smaller stems. Ground-truth precision, species and trunk counts remain unverified. Ward-scale runtimes and packs belong to step 2 after integration.

author: ruthhilary
body:
## What this is

A public page at `/register-interest` where a branch pastor or leader can put their branch forward to run the pilot, and the admin queue that receives them. Built from `Kairos rollout plan.pdf` — every commitment and every selection note on the page comes from it.

The rollout plan is blunt about why this exists: *"the announcement should go out early even if the app is not ready, because nothing else can be arranged until we know which branch is first."*

## The flow

**Step one — what the pilot asks of a branch.** Six commitments, read rather than ticked. They were checkboxes at first; that turned reading into a task to be got through, and a stored tick would have recorded a promise nobody is held to. What survives in the record is `requirements_version`, so a later edit to the page cannot rewrite what a branch was shown.

**Step two — the form.** Who they are, their branch, how many fellowships and departments, who would act as head of admin, whether a safeguarding lead is already in post, earliest they could start. Every field carries an info button explaining in plain terms what to put in it.

**On submit.** The row is written, and `tech@kharis.org` is emailed the whole submission — not an alert saying a form arrived, because that only sends the reader hunting for the admin queue, which is the delay the notification exists to remove.

Subject: `Pilot interest: Kharis Croydon - Pastor Derin`

`PILOT_INTEREST_NOTIFY_TO` overrides the address so staging does not mail the real inbox.

**Admin queue** at `/admin/pilot-interest`, behind `requireRole('admin')`. Who else has volunteered is not a branch's business, so a member with branch grants cannot read it.

## Decisions worth a reviewer's attention

**The submission is never lost to a mail failure.** A send error is logged, never raised. The branch offered to go first; losing that because SES was down would be the worst possible trade.

**An unconfigured mailer is loud.** With no AWS credentials the mailer logs the send at `info` and returns as though it worked, so a misconfigured environment would have dropped every notification with nothing above `info` to say so — and the catch would never fire, because nothing threw. The notification path now checks `isMailerLive()` first and raises, which the caller logs as an error.

**No de-duplication, deliberately.** Two leaders from the same branch both writing in is a signal worth seeing, and the same person submitting twice usually means they thought of something after the first. The admin queue groups by branch rather than the database refusing the row.

**The branch id is resolved, not trusted.** The form is public, so the id arrives from a dropdown the caller could have edited. The typed name is always the record; the foreign key is a convenience once it resolves.

**No member link and no cascade.** Whoever fills this in has no account — members sign themselves up only once a branch is chosen and seeded. The row is evidence of an offer and must outlive any account later created for the same person.

**Size is collected but is not a criterion.** The plan rules it out in both directions. The member count is optional and the hint says so.

## Shared changes

Three components gained one optional prop each. No existing caller changes.

| Component | Prop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Halo` | `durationMs`, `reverse` | The Register Interest beacon spins anticlockwise at 2s against 3.6s clockwise on the Get Started buttons beside it. Changing the shared keyframe would have flipped all four. |
| `DateSelect` | `triggerClassName` | Its trigger is sized for the dashboard; the pilot form's fields are taller and more rounded. |
| `CustomSelect` | `triggerClassName` | Same reason. |

## Two bugs fixed in passing

**`apps/web/tailwind.config.ts` was CommonJS in a `.ts` file.** Under Node 26 a `.ts` config loads as ESM, so `module.exports` threw `ReferenceError: module is not defined` — and **every CSS rebuild killed the dev server**. Proved with `touch src/app/globals.css`: before, the process was gone; after, 200/200 and still alive. This made CSS iteration impossible and looked like broken stylesheets.

**`next dev` and `next build` both owned `.next`,** so building while the dev server ran produced `__webpack_modules__[moduleId] is not a function`. `next.config.ts` now takes `NEXT_DIST_DIR`.

## Before merging

- [ ] **Run migration `0071_pilot_interest.sql`.** It has never been applied anywhere. Until it is, every submission fails before it reaches email. Hand-written and idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS` throughout) because `db:bootstrap` replays every file in the directory.
- [ ] **Confirm SES reaches `tech@kharis.org` in the target environment.** It uses the same mailer as sign-up verification and password reset, so if those arrive, this will. The one exception is SES still being in sandbox with that address unverified.
- [ ] Submit a test form on staging. That exercises the migration, the SES identity, the configuration set and the recipient in one go.

## Tests

18 for pilot-interest — 13 router, 5 service, covering the public submit, the admin gate, the notification address and subject, HTML escaping, the override address, a failed send, and an unconfigured mailer.

`npx vitest run packages/types apps/api/src/pilot-interest` → **204 passed**.

**Pre-existing and not caused by this branch:** `apps/web` and `packages/ui` test suites fail to load with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Symbol(Node prepared with document state workarounds)')` and `document is not defined`. I stashed this work and re-ran: identical failure counts on a clean tree. It looks like a jsdom/testing-library version mismatch in `node_modules`. Worth its own fix.

## Not done

- No reminder or escalation if a submission sits unread. The email is the only prompt.
- The admin queue has no export.

author: juangmz7
body:
## Why

The `post-command-service` images published from `main` compile but do not start as a native image, so the dev pod (Argo CD deploys `:latest`) is in CrashLoopBackOff. CI only checked that the image builds.

## What

**Fixes so the native image starts and works**
- Inject `self` through `ObjectProvider<Self>` instead of `@Lazy` class injection (CGLIB proxy clash in native) in `PostMediaVerificationService`, `FailedPostPurgeService`, `PostMediaCleanupService` and `RefreshUploadUrlsUseCase`. `NativeImageCompatibilityTest` fails if `@Lazy` comes back on a non-interface type.
- `HibernateRuntimeHints`: arrays of `@Id` types (`UUID[]`), `@EntityListeners` and their callbacks (the outbox destination resolver, which made likes return 500), JSON column payloads.
- `EventMessageRuntimeHints`: binding hints for every `EventMessage`, so events serialize (posts stayed `PENDING`).
- Properties that decide beans live in `application.yaml` (Spring AOT evaluates conditions at build time with no profile): JWT `issuer-uri` + `jwk-set-uri` (dev's in-cluster `JWK_SET_URI` was ignored), OTLP endpoints, virtual threads, `open-in-view: false` (+ `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` on `CheckPostCollabLinkStatusUseCase`).
- Dockerfile: both stages pinned to Oracle Linux 10 (`native-image:25-ol10` / `oraclelinux:10-slim`, same glibc).

**CI**
- New `native-image` job on PRs: builds the native image and runs `native-e2e/e2e.sh` against it, without pushing.
- `publish` on `main` runs the same e2e before pushing, so an image that doesn't start never reaches Docker Hub / dev.
- `docker-publish.yml` gains optional `build-args`, `e2e-script` and `push` inputs; the other callers are unchanged.
- `native-e2e/e2e.sh` runs the image with the chart's pod settings (user 10001, read-only root, `/tmp` emptyDir, no capabilities, 1 GiB) and the dev chart's JWT setup, and covers startup, health, auth, the RabbitMQ consumer, create post → SAS upload → verification → outbox, likes, reports (JSON snapshot) and ShedLock jobs.

**Tests**
- `PostMediaVerificationOutageIT` points at port 1 instead of 10000 (a local Azurite turned the outage into "blob not found"); `RedisConfigIT` gets `@ActiveProfiles("test")`.

## Verified locally
- `./mvnw test -Dspring.profiles.active=test`: 776/776 (also twice pinned to 4 CPUs).
- `docker build --build-arg NATIVE_IMAGE_OPTIONS=-J-Xmx10g`: OK, ~5.5 min, peak RSS 12.7 GB.
- `native-e2e/e2e.sh`: 20/20, startup 1.7 s, 121 MiB.
- AOT bean set with the dev and prod chart env: identical to the build (886 beans).

Not covered: prod's Azure Workload Identity path (prod is not deployed).

author: kp77c
body:
This PR adds complete PS Vita ports for WarCraft III (1.27a) and Deus Ex (GOG GOTY), building on the existing StarCraft port infrastructure. Both ports run unmodified Windows x86 binaries through dynamic recompilation to ARM.

## Key Changes

**New WarCraft III Vita Port (wc3vita/)**
- Boot harness (`boot.cpp`) that loads War3.exe and game DLLs into guest address space
- Game-specific Win32 shims for WarCraft III features:
  - `w3_shims.cpp`: MSVCR120 runtime, Storm 1.27, Game.dll-specific functions
  - `w3_gl.cpp`: OpenGL 1.3 fixed-function rendering via vitaGL
  - `w3_mp3.cpp`: Native MP3 decoding for in-game music (replaces x87 Miles decoder)
  - `w3_net.cpp`: Offline Winsock implementation
  - `w3_dshow.cpp`: DirectShow filter graph stub for movie playback
  - `w3_softfloat.cpp/h`: Native software float routines for deterministic game state
  - `w3_trace.cpp`: Logging hooks for file/memory tracking
- Vita-specific presentation (`sc_present_vita.cpp`): P8 texture rendering with sharp bilinear scaling at 725x544, 60 Hz locked display thread
- Input handling (`sc_input.cpp`, `sc_input.h`): Controller-to-keyboard/mouse mapping
- Build system and test automation scripts

**New Deus Ex Vita Port (dxvita/)**
- Boot harness for DeusEx.exe and System folder DLLs
- Game-specific shims:
  - `dx_shims.cpp`: Deus Ex-specific Win32 functions
  - `dx_gl.cpp`: OpenGL support via vitaGL (generated from `opengldrv_names.txt`)
- Simplified input scheme for Deus Ex gameplay
- Shared presentation and infrastructure with StarCraft port

**Shared Infrastructure Updates**
- Both ports reuse `sc_kernel32.cpp`, `sc_user32.cpp`, `sc_ddraw.cpp`, `sc_misc.cpp`, `sc_input.cpp` from StarCraft with minimal game-specific variations
- Vita presentation layer (`sc_present_vita.cpp`) handles GPU buffer management in CDRAM
- Host test builds (`sc_present.cpp`) for development

**Engine Modifications**
- `custommem.c`: Added includes for `sched.h` and `time.h`; conditional compilation for jump table default (`WX86_JT3`)
- `dynarec_arm_helper.c`: Added jump-table entry helper for x3 register
- `dynablock.c`: Added block retirement wave handling
- `bridge.cpp/h`: Extended shim infrastructure for game-specific traps
- `dyn86_emitprof.h`, `dyn86_intrin.h`: Increased profiling and intrinsic limits
- `dynarec.c`: Enhanced EIP trap handling
- `dynablock_private.h`: Added dirty block tracking
- `win32_shims_memory.cpp`: Adjusted heap allocation base

**Build and Test Infrastructure**
- Build scripts for both ports (`build.sh`)
- vitaGL build helper (`build_vitagl.sh`)
- Test pad automation files for menu navigation and gameplay
- Replay tools for snapshot debugging (`w3replay.py`, `dxreplay.py`)
- Engine patch files for single-SMC mode

**Third-party Headers**
- Added Mesa GL headers (`gl.h`, `glext.h`) for OpenGL definitions
- Added minimp3 header for MP3 decoding

## Notable Implementation Details

- Both ports use the same cooperative scheduler and guest memory model as StarCraft
- MP3 decoding is offloaded to native code to reduce CPU load on the single guest core
- Display thread on Vita runs independently on its own core, avoiding vblank waits in guest code
- OpenGL sh

author: mansi2221
body:
## Description

Fixes #7259

When multiple agents share the same `LLM` instance, `calculate_usage_metrics()` calls `llm.get_token_usage_summary()` once per agent. Since the `BaseLLM` object accumulates token usage across all calls, the same cumulative totals are added N times — inflating reported usage by Nx.

**Example:** 3 agents sharing one LLM that used 110 tokens total → reported as 330 tokens (3x inflation).

## Root Cause

```python
for agent in self.agents:
    if isinstance(agent.llm, BaseLLM):
        llm_usage = agent.llm.get_token_usage_summary()  # same object, same totals
        total_usage_metrics.add_usage_metrics(llm_usage)  # added N times
```

## Fix

Track already-counted `BaseLLM` instances by `id()` and skip duplicates. Same dedup applied to `manager_agent`.

```python
counted_llm_ids: set[int] = set()

for agent in self.agents:
    if isinstance(agent.llm, BaseLLM):
        if id(agent.llm) not in counted_llm_ids:
            counted_llm_ids.add(id(agent.llm))
            total_usage_metrics.add_usage_metrics(agent.llm.get_token_usage_summary())
```

## Tests

3 new tests in `test_usage_metrics_shared_llm.py`:
- **Shared LLM not double-counted** — 2 agents, 1 LLM → usage counted once
- **Separate LLMs counted independently** — 2 agents, 2 LLMs → both summed
- **3 agents, 1 LLM** — confirms no Nx inflation with N > 2

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

author: ztrange
body:
## Bug

`rebase-onto-default.sh` re-records `.tdd/issue-<n>-branch-base` on exit 0 (rebased) and exit 3 (up to date), but not on exit 1 (conflict). On a conflict, DRAFT-PR.md hands it to a `develop-rebase` leaf, which resolves it with `git rebase <onto-sha>`. After that the branch sits on `<onto-sha>`, but the record still names the old base. A stop or resume, and every phase that takes `--branch-base`, reads the stale base.

## Fix

- New mode `rebase-onto-default.sh --resolved <onto-sha>`. It fetches nothing and rebases nothing. It re-records the run's branch base as `<onto-sha>` through the same `record_branch_base` the exit-0/3 paths use, then exits 0. On stdout it prints the sha the record held before; nothing is printed when there was no record.
- It refuses with exit 2, leaving the record untouched, in four cases:
  - the argument is missing;
  - the argument is not a hex commit name;
  - HEAD does not contain `<onto-sha>`;
  - the record cannot be written.
- DRAFT-PR.md, conflict path: runs `--resolved <onto-sha>` as soon as the leaf has resolved, before the regrade block and `verify-rebase`. Its exit 2 bails `no-verdict`.
- DRAFT-PR.md, `rebase-unresolved` reset path: after `git reset --hard <pre-rebase-sha>`, it restores the replaced base with `--resolved <replaced-base>`. Without this step the record would name `<onto-sha>`, which is no ancestor of the reset branch, and `preflight.recorded_base` would refuse the resume with exit 2.
- SCRIPTS.md documents the flag. New rows: DP361 and SC623. DRAFT-PR.md and SCRIPTS.md were regraded and both PASSed.

- The shim header of `rebase-onto-default.sh` names `--resolved`, matching the module's USAGE.

## Rejected

- **Re-running plain `rebase-onto-default.sh` after the leaf.** It fetches again, so it could rebase onto a newer `origin/<default>` than the one the leaf resolved against, which would change the code `verify-rebase` judges.
- **Recording only after the `verify-rebase` PASS.** The issue asks for the record to hold the new base once the conflict is resolved. Recording after the PASS would also leave the stale record in place for the whole revise loop.

## Tests

- Process case `test_rebase_onto_default_process.py::test_main_resolved_re_records_the_branch_base_as_the_onto_sha_a_hand_resolved_conflicting_rebase_landed_on_and_exits_0_4553`. It uses a real git conflict, resolves it by hand, asserts the stale record (the bug), then asserts the re-record. It was watched red.
- Unit cases in `unit/test_rebase_onto_default.py`: the three refusals, and the replaced-base readout with and without a prior record. All were watched red.
- Review follow-up: the case `test_resolved_exits_2_naming_the_resolved_re_record_when_the_branch_base_record_cannot_be_written_4553` (a record write raising OSError gives exit 2 and a message led by `--resolved <sha>`) and the case `test_resolved_exits_2_with_its_usage_when_given_more_than_one_onto_sha_4553`. Each one kills a mutant that had survived: `return 2`→`pass` for the first, `!= 1`→`< 1` for the second.

## Not fixed (noted)

- The exit-0 path has the same reset hazard. When the rebased-tip suite comes back red, `git reset --hard <pre-rebase-sha>` runs after the record was already moved to onto. That predates this PR and is outside #4553's scope.

Closes #4553

## Review

- Review: on a branch that is not a run's, `--resolved` exits 0 silently and records nothing.
- Review: if the conductor resumes during the revise loop it has lost `<replaced-base>` (the stdout of the earlier `--resolved` call), so a later reset cannot restore the record.
- Review (outside #4553's scope): after a `rebased-tip-red` reset on the exit-0 path, the record still names the onto sha, so a resume exits 2 — same family of bug, not fixed here.
- Review: `veri/README.md:789` does not mention `--resolved` (not a doc-miss site).
- Review: one surviving mutant, `rebase_onto_default.py` `resolved()` (`if issue else ""`→`"x"`), changes only the stdout of a branch that is not a run's; no exit code or record.
- Review: earlier blocking findings (record-write failure, extra onto-sha argument) are now pinned, each watched red under its mutant; re-review OK at f91a2b6e62.

body:
## What

- **Shift+↑ / Shift+↓** with an idea selected grows or shrinks a run of selected sibling ideas, starting from the idea it began on. It stops at the first and last sibling; a central idea or a focused branch's idea has no siblings, so nothing happens.
- **Coloring many ideas:** a color picked in the style panel goes to every selected idea ("These ideas") or every selected branch ("Their branches"), as one undo step. This works for a sibling run and after Ctrl/Cmd+A, which now also shows the style panel. Hovering a color previews it on all of them; when their colors differ, no swatch shows as current.
- **Delete, copy and cut** act on the whole run, as they already did after Ctrl/Cmd+A. After deleting a run, the selection moves to the next sibling, else the previous one, else the parent.
- **Esc** shrinks a run to the idea the keys moved to; plain arrows, clicks, typing and Alt+arrows end it.
- **Undo/redo** restore the run or select-all that an edit was made with.
- The shortcuts dialog lists Shift+↑/↓.

## Why

Recoloring all or some siblings meant coloring them one at a time.

## Testing

- New browser test in `e2e/editor.browser.ts` covers growing and shrinking the run, coloring ideas and branches, undo, Esc, copy, delete, and coloring after Ctrl/Cmd+A.
- `bun run check` and unit tests pass in `webapp`; `bun run check` and the full browser suite (20 tests) pass in `e2e`.
- Checked by hand in the dev server on a small map.

author: aleinto97
body:
Brings `ci/windows-macos` (18 commits) and `feat/video-surface-crates` (4 commits) into `main`, ending with **Release 0.8.0**. Merging with **rebase** keeps that commit on top, so `release.yml` publishes 0.8.0 with its message as the notes.

## What's in it
- **macOS** (Apple silicon): `Veylo.app` build and `install.sh`; the picture inside the window through a Core Animation OpenGL layer, with HDR through EDR; macOS self-tests (OpenGL context, an HDR10 clip rendered as PQ). The macOS app updates itself from `veylo-macos-arm64.zip`, which the release builds.
- **Windows and macOS CI**: each OS builds, runs clippy and the tests, installs with the real installer, self-tests the installed copy and runs launch checks.
- **`crates/video-surface`**: the desktop picture paths moved out of `video.rs` behind a small `Host`/`Player` API. A failing path is logged, skipped for the rest of the run, and the next one is tried (on Wayland, the GL area). Paths are only chosen before a title plays.
- **`crates/picture-check`** and the **picture test**: a clip of six colour bars, with a check that a real screenshot shows them in order. It's required on Windows and macOS, and only reports on Linux, where the runner's software GL leaves the GL area black.

## Tests
- CI on the branch: all jobs green. Picture test `PASS` on Windows and macOS (checked in the logs), blank on Linux (report only).
- Locally on Linux: clippy and tests for both workspaces. The two crates also pass clippy for macOS and Windows targets. The app passes `cargo check` for Android. The picture test passes on Xvfb, on X11 through XWayland, and through the Wayland GL area fallback.

## Known issue, left for later
On Hyprland, the Wayland **subsurface** path (the default on Wayland) shows no picture, in 0.7.0 as well. It reports no error, so the fallback doesn't kick in. The picture test found it.

author: ouvarov
body:
## What

Stage 4.1a: harden the API before the Vercel frontend (`web/`) goes live.

- `helmet()` on every response (nosniff, CSP, no `X-Powered-By`, HSTS…).
- Cross-origin protection via Nest's `enableCsrfProtection` with `trustedOrigins: [WEB_ORIGIN]`. A cross-site browser POST now gets `403 {code: "forbidden"}`; same-origin requests, server-to-server calls and webhooks (no browser headers) pass as before.
- New required env `WEB_ORIGIN` (a bare origin, compared verbatim with the browser's `Origin`). Boot fails without it.
- Generic error map: 403 → `forbidden`, 429 → `rate_limited`.
- Paddle checkout page keeps its own CSP and gets `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin-allow-popups` for Paddle.js and 3DS/PayPal popups.
- `web/` ignored by root eslint, prettier, docker; Render `buildFilter.ignoredPaths: [web/**]` so web-only commits don't redeploy the API.
- README, `.env.example`, `docker-compose.yml`, `render.yaml`.

## Why

The browser will reach the API through a same-origin Vercel rewrite; no CORS. The CSRF check is the base for the 5.1 admin cookie; helmet closes the missing security headers.

## How it was checked

- `npm run check` (tsc, eslint, prettier).
- Unit: env schema (81).
- e2e on the Neon e2e branch: new `http-security` (headers, CSRF cases, 429 body), `paddle-flow` (checkout page headers, signed webhook without browser headers), `public-api`, `webhooks`, `health`, `app-env`.
- Red mutations (helmet removed, CSRF removed, empty trustedOrigins, COOP dropped, optional WEB_ORIGIN, web not ignored) each turn tests red.

## Not checked

- Docker build context (static `.dockerignore` only), Render `buildFilter` behaviour, a live Paddle payment with the new headers — after deploy.
- e2e files not run: create-payment, create-refund, reconciliation, stripe-flow, migrations, projects, provider-accounts (low RAM).

## Before merge

`WEB_ORIGIN` must be set on Render (the Vercel production origin), or the deploy fails boot and Render keeps the old instance.

author: chaksaray
body:
Closes #87

## What and why

Nothing tested the pre-commit hook, and no workflow ran a test of it. A removed `additional_dependencies` entry, a renamed entry point or a scanner release that moves a symbol the hook imports would be found by a user. This adds the tests and a workflow that runs them, including the real `pre-commit` tool.

Two commits:

1. `54df75a` test: `tests/test_pre_commit_hook.py`, 10 tests, standard library only.
   - `HookDefinition` (4): every hook in `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` is complete, declares `bawbel-scanner` in `additional_dependencies`, and its entry is a `[project.scripts]` entry pointing at a callable.
   - `EntryPoint` (4): the installed `bawbel-pre-commit` script on a clean file, a hostile file, no files and a file that does not exist.
   - `RealPreCommit` (2): `pre-commit try-repo` on this repository, with an empty cache, on a clean and on a hostile file.
2. `71b4692` ci: `.github/workflows/hooks.yml`, two jobs (`definition and entry point`, `real pre-commit`). Triggers: pull requests, pushes to `develop` and `main`, `workflow_dispatch`, and a weekly schedule (Mondays 05:23 UTC). `BAWBEL_HOOK_TESTS_REQUIRED=1` is set for the whole workflow. The one action, `actions/checkout`, is pinned to the commit the other workflows use (`3d3c42e5...`, `# v7.0.1`).

## Differences from the runbook

- **`unittest`, not pytest.** The runbook's prototype is pytest with an `integration` marker registered in `pyproject.toml`. Both existing test files here are standard-library `unittest`, and #86 (open) makes the `Pins` job run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, which does not run pytest-style functions (a file with one plain `test_` function gave `Ran 0 tests ... NO TESTS RAN`) and errors on a file that imports pytest where pytest is absent (`FAILED (errors=1)`), both checked in `python:3.12-slim`. These tests are `unittest` classes, so both runners run them (below), there is no marker, and `pyproject.toml` is untouched. The runbook's `-m "not integration"` becomes `-k HookDefinition -k EntryPoint`, and `-m integration` becomes `-k RealPreCommit`.
- **Skip or fail.** A test whose prerequisite is missing (the installed entry point, PyYAML, `pre-commit`, `git`) skips with the reason, so the `Pins` job and a bare checkout pass. With `BAWBEL_HOOK_TESTS_REQUIRED=1` it fails instead, so the new workflow cannot go green by skipping.
- **The hostile real-pre-commit test checks more than the exit code.** The runbook's prototype asserts `returncode == 1`. Measured on a hostile file with `pre-commit try-repo`: a good hook exits 1 and prints the finding; a renamed entry point exits 1 and prints "Executable `bawbel-pre-commitx` not found"; a hook with no `additional_dependencies` exits 1 too (the hook itself exits 2 and prints "bawbel-scanner not installed"). So the test also requires `Bawbel Scanner....Failed`, the line `- exit code: 1`, and a finding line.
- **The AVE id is matched by shape** (`[SEVERITY] AVE-YYYY-NNNNN  SKILL.md`), not by value. Which rule fires on a sentence is the scanner's own test, and the runbook prototype's fixed id would break this test on a scanner rule change that leaves the hook correct.

## Verify

**All prerequisites present**, clean virtualenv (`virtualenv`), this branch installed, `bawbel-scanner` 1.3.0 and `pre-commit` 4.7.0 from PyPI, `BAWBEL_HOOK_TESTS_REQUIRED=1`:

```text
$ python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_pre_commit_hook.py -v
EntryPoint:     test_a_file_that_does_not_exist_is_skipped, test_clean_file_passes,
                test_hostile_file_blocks_the_commit, test_no_files_is_not_an_error     ... ok (4)
HookDefinition: test_every_entry_is_a_console_script_this_package_declares,
                test_every_hook_declares_the_scanner, test_every_hook_is_complete,
                test_the_documented_hook_exists                                        ... ok (4)
RealPreCommit:  test_clean_file_passes, test_hostile_file_fails_with_a_finding         ... ok (2)
Ran 10 tests in 8.097s
OK                                                                                     exit=0
```

**pytest runs the same file**, same environment plus `pytest`: `10 passed in 8.06s`, no warnings.

**It bites.** One change at a time to the tracked files, the same environment, the package reinstalled for the two that change it, then `git checkout` (tree clean afterwards, and 10 of 10 pass again):

```text
A  delete additional_dependencies from .pre-commit-hooks.yaml          FAILED (failures=3)
     HookDefinition.test_every_hook_declares_the_scanner:
       hook bawbel-scan must declare bawbel-scanner, or it fails in a clean environment
     RealPreCommit.test_clean_file_passes: 1 != 0
     RealPreCommit.test_hostile_file_fails_with_a_finding: '- exit code: 1' not found (the hook exited 2)
B  rename the entry to bawbel-pre-commitx in .pre-commit-hooks.yaml    FAILED (failures=3)
     HookDefinition: bawbel-pre-commitx is not a [project.scripts] entry
     RealPreCommit (clean): 1 != 0
     RealPreCommit (hostile): no finding line in the output (it printed "- exit code: 1" and
       "Executable `bawbel-pre-commitx` not found", so the exit code alone would have passed)
C  pyproject.toml entry bawbel_pre_commit:main -> mainx                FAILED (failures=7)
     4 EntryPoint tests (1 != 0, ImportError: cannot import name 'mainx'), 1 HookDefinition
     ("... which is not callable"), 2 RealPreCommit
D  the hook imports SEVERITY_SCORESX (a scanner release moving a symbol)   FAILED (failures=5)
     3 EntryPoint tests (2 != 0, "bawbel-scanner not installed."), 2 RealPreCommit
     (test_no_files_is_not_an_error still passes: the hook returns before the import)
```

**Nothing installed.** `python:3.12-slim`, no PyYAML, no `pre-commit`, no `git`, no package:

```text
$ python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_pre_commit_hook.py -v
Ran 10 tests in 0.000s
OK (skipped=10)        each skip names its prerequisite, nothing errors on import

$ BAWBEL_HOOK_TESTS_REQUIRED=1 python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_pre_commit_hook.py
FAILED (failures=10)   "BAWBEL_HOOK_TESTS_REQUIRED=1 and PyYAML is not installed (pre-commit brings it)", and so on
```

**The whole suite, the way `Pins` will run it**, on the host (PyYAML, `pre-commit` 3.6.2 and `git` present, no entry point on `PATH`): `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests` gives `Ran 46 tests ... OK (skipped=4)`. 46 is the 25 pin-checker tests, the 11 in `test_docs_snippets.py` and these 10. The 4 skips are the `EntryPoint` group. The 2 real-pre-commit tests ran and passed.

**The first job's steps, in a fresh `python:3.12-slim` container** (`python3 -m venv`, `pip install . "bawbel-scanner>=1.0.1" pyyaml`, then the workflow's test command): `Ran 8 tests ... OK`.

**Pins.** `python3 scripts/check_pins.py` on the branch: `all references pinned (6 placeholder(s) to fill at release)`, exit 0. The new workflow has one `uses:`, with a SHA and a release comment, and no `pin-exempt`.

Dash scan of both commits' added lines and messages: 0 em or en dashes. Each commit carries a sign-off.

## Not verified

- **A red CI.** The four breakages above were run locally, with the tests the workflow runs and the same `BAWBEL_HOOK_TESTS_REQUIRED=1`. I did not push a broken change to a throwaway branch to watch the workflow itself go red.
- **The weekly schedule.** GitHub runs `schedule` triggers from the default branch's copy of the file (my understanding of the documented behaviour; not tested here), so the weekly run starts only after this reaches `main`.
- **Python 3.10**, which `pyproject.toml` still allows: there `tomllib` is missing and `test_every_entry_is_a_console_script_this_package_declares` skips (or fails under `BAWBEL_HOOK_TESTS_REQUIRED=1`). Not run.
- **The `bawbel-scan-all` hook** (extras `[all]`, heavy engines) is not exercised. It uses the same entry point.
- **The semgrep engine** of the scanner logs `Engine error: engine=semgrep ...` warnings on stderr in the ho
