author: teslatankx
body:
Closes #391

## What changes
A new **Objectives** panel lists every trigger shown as an objective, a header or an on-screen line, in the order the game lists them: higher Description Order first, ties in trigger list order. By default it is a tab behind the Status Log, shown only in Triggers mode. **View > Panels > Objectives** shows or hides it; closed by hand in Triggers mode, it stays closed until shown again.

- **The list:** Order, H, Obj, Scr, Mute, an eye (shown in the preview), Short description and Trigger.
  - Click a flag to set it; with several rows selected it sets them all.
  - Double-click the Order or the short description to edit it.
  - Triggers off at game start are greyed.
  - Selecting a row selects its trigger in the trigger list, and the other way round. The long Description stays in Trigger Details.
  - Columns can be dragged to reorder, and their order and widths are remembered (a local setting).
- **Ordering:** drag rows, or use the up and down buttons.
  - A moved row gets a Description Order between its new neighbours when there is room.
  - Otherwise it takes the value under the row above and the rows below move down one each until a gap, so a header further down (the 100 / 50 pattern) keeps its value. Only below 0 is the whole list renumbered.
  - **Renumber** counts down by 1 from the top value; with several rows selected, only those.
  - Orders stay within the field's u32 range.
- **Editing:**
  - **New Objective** and **New Header** add a trigger under the selected row with flags and text set; a new objective's text starts with "+ ".
  - **Add Trigger...** shows existing triggers as objectives.
  - **Remove** clears the flags and keeps the trigger.
  - Each action is one undo step.
  - A read-only scenario greys the editing controls; the list and preview still work.
- **String ids:** a short description with a language string id shows the game's string, in italics. Editing such a row asks whether to clear the id so the typed text shows; right-click > **Use My Text (Clear String ID)** does that for the selected rows. The official campaigns use string ids on every objective.
- **Preview:** the game's objectives box, **In dock**, **On map** (the map's top-right corner, also **View > Show Objectives on Map**) or **Off**.
  - **All objectives** or **At game start** (enabled triggers only).
  - A short description's leading **+** draws a square checkbox and **-** a round one (an optional objective); neither shows as text. Headers get no checkbox.
  - Colour tags show in their colours. **Variables** shows a `<name>` tag naming a trigger variable as typed, as its value at game start (0), or both.
  - Clicking a checkbox shows it done, and the eye column or right-click **Hide in Preview** leaves rows out. Both are preview only, never saved, and clear on another document or a structural edit.
  - A long box scrolls: in the panel with a scroll bar, on the map with the wheel over the box (elsewhere the wheel zooms as usual).
  - Text typed in Trigger Details' short description shows in the list and the box as it is typed.
- **Edit menu:** with the Objectives list focused, Select All and Deselect act on its rows, and Cut, Copy and Paste are off, so they never act on the trigger list's selection from there.
- **Saved layout:** a fifth dock bumps `WINDOW_STATE_VERSION` to 4, so an older saved layout resets to the default once.

How it works:
- `descape/objectives_model.py` (no Qt): rows, sort, box lines, the reorder, renumber and insert rules, the `+`/`-` marker.
- `descape/objectives_box.py`: the box, in the dock and as a map overlay (a MapView child like `InstructionOverlay`, mouse-transparent except a masked sibling over its checkboxes).
- `descape/objectives_panel.py`: the panel, passive like `MessagesPanel`.
- `descape/viewer_objectives.py`: a 20th `ViewerWindow` mixin. Every write goes through `_trigger_edit()` with `content_touched`, unchanged values filtered first; New Objective and New Header add their trigger through `structural_edit()` in the same record.
- Settings `objectives_preview`, `objectives_at_start`, `objectives_variables` (portable) and `objectives_columns` (local).

## Tests
- New `tests/test_objectives_model.py` (no Qt): sort and ties, box lines, gap, shift and renumber fallbacks, u32 cap, selection Renumber, insert orders, the marker.
- New `tests/test_objectives_panel.py`: one undo step per action and no phantom records, undo and redo refresh, save and reopen, drag and up/down, inline edits, string-id prompt, New/Add/Remove, selection sync, lock and read-only, preview places and the View menu, At game start, ticks and hiding, scrolling (dock, map wheel, over a checkbox, fractional scale), Variables, columns, dock tab and mode behaviour, the version-3 layout refused, Edit menu routing.
- Updated: `test_viewer_split.py` (20 mixins), `test_window_layout.py`, `test_keybinds.py`, `test_settings_file.py`, settings isolation, `config.example.yaml`.
- Quick suite on origin/main 011bac7 plus this change, Linux: 18319 passed, 690 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.

## Notes
- Suggested CHANGELOG line: "An Objectives panel lists every trigger objective in game order, with drag reordering, inline flags and text, and a preview of the game's objectives box in the panel or on the map (#391)."
- Not confirmed in game yet: how the game orders objectives with equal Description Orders (the preview assumes trigger list order), and whether a line with no `+` or `-` shows a checkbox (the preview shows none).
- The `+` and `-` markers come from in-game screenshots; a header starting with a sign is unconfirmed, so the preview gives it no checkbox.
- A Variables value assumes every trigger variable starts at 0.
- Trigger Details' Description Order spin box stops at 2147483647, so an order above that (settable from this panel, up to the u32 limit) shows clamped there.
- Saving with an Objectives inline editor still open drops the typed value, as the trigger list's inline rename already does.

author: petralithic
body:
When desktop Vulkan keeps several frames in flight, the next image acquisition can reuse the shared binary semaphore while the previous submission still has a pending wait. Vulkan requires that semaphore to be available for a new signal. The Android backend already tracks acquisition separately for each batch. [Vulkan image acquisition requirements](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkAcquireNextImageKHR.html)

Give each desktop submission slot its own semaphore and acquisition fence. Reuse a slot after its submission has consumed the semaphore and the acquisition fence has completed. The other slots can remain in flight. A failed frame recording or submission discards that recording and retires the acquired image with its swapchain. A failed fence wait preserves the pending objects and requests process exit.

## Verification

- Compiled the exact Vulkan backend on macOS, Windows and Linux.
- The production acquisition helpers passed simulated checks for three submissions in flight, slot-local reuse, synchronous reuse, abandoning an acquisition, and a failed fence wait during teardown. [Hosted verification](https://github.com/petralithic/RACiT/actions/runs/44963422135)


## Integration

The [desktop wheel and Vulkan branch](https://github.com/petralithic/RACiT/tree/integration/desktop-wheel-vulkan-fixes) combines this fix with the dynamic swapchain arrays, tear-free fallback and depth scratch cleanup. The combined backend compiled on macOS, Windows and Linux, and all three passed the acquire-state and 12-image swapchain fixtures. [Integration verification](https://github.com/petralithic/RACiT/actions/runs/44963818663)


A later integration with the same acquire helpers also passed a real Linux X11 window test on Lavapipe. The driver accepted 72 presentations per run across all three slots, with swapchain recreation in the middle. The check passed with both the default and bounded acquire modes while the Khronos validation layer was loaded. This uses a synthetic renderer window. [Windowed driver check](https://github.com/petralithic/RACiT/actions/runs/44966419828)

author: ivandemurard
body:
## What changes

One Listen component for the whole site, from boards R (component, tokens, states) and S (integration).

- **ListenRow** under the title of the three pages that have a summary (Harness, AX, /rose): 64 px, folded, transcript apart, no autoplay.
- **ListenPlayer** in the dock: one phrase at a time, previous phrase above, Listen / Read, 72-bar waveform (slider), -10 s, play, +10 s, speed, volume and mute (slider hidden on iOS), "Back to the conversation", "Ask Rose about it" at the end.
- **Mini-player**: while Rose reads, the dock bar is the player. One object, nothing stacked.
- **One reader** in a provider above the router: a page change does not cut the sound. The record in the header is held while Rose speaks ("record paused · Rose is speaking") and comes back at the end if it was playing.
- **Media Session**: title, "Rose", "ivandemurard.com", compass artwork (`public/rose-compass-512.png`), play / pause / seek ±10 s / seekto.
- **Contents line** "Listen · 1:14" (desktop "On this page"), **badge** "1:04" on index cards, "or 1 min to listen" after the reading time.
- **`listen_entry`** on listen events (`row`, `contents`, `index_card`, `dock_starter`, `answer`): migration 0014 and `rose-event` enum.
- Old `ListenSummaryBlock` and the old audiogram removed. Mirrors, `llms-full.txt` and MCP keep their "Listen summary" section unchanged.

## Where I deviated from the brief, and why

1. **Three token values** are not the board's. Calculated against the site's 4.5:1 text floor and 3:1 for bars: upcoming and ghost words at .30 measure 1.8:1 (Day) and 2.7:1 (Dusk); unplayed bars at .20 measure 1.5:1 and 1.9:1. Now: upcoming and ghost .66 Day / .54 Dusk (4.7:1), unplayed .52 Day / .42 Dusk (3.1:1 and 3.4:1). The faded words stay clearly lighter than the spoken ones (12:1), but less faint than drawn. Pinned in `listenComponentContrast.test.ts`.
2. **Phrase cutting is my reading** of "16 words at most, or a comma or colon if over 9": sentences up to 9 words stay whole; longer ones are cut after commas and colons, never leaving a piece under 3 words ("First," stays with what follows); no phrase over 16 words (cut in equal parts). To confirm.
3. **Waveform bars narrow to 2 px** on a phone: 72 bars of 3 px and 3 px gaps are 429 px, wider than the 440 px panel and a 390 px screen.
4. **The transcript prints the full notice** ("... validated 21 Nov 2026 · 1 min 04") and a "Listen summary" label, not only "validated <date>": the Markdown mirror carries both lines and the test "no text that is not on the page" requires the page to say them.
5. **Without JavaScript** the transcript opens (plain `<details>`) and links the mp3, but the play button is inert.

## The waveform

- **Summaries (Harness, AX, Rose): real waveform.** 72 bars computed from the recorded takes, committed in `6c560c1` (only the `bars` field is added to `public/listen/<slug>.json`; text, words and duration are unchanged). A test fails if a summary in `listenSummaries.ts` has no `.json` or not exactly 72 bars between 0 and 1.
- **Rose's answers: not verified.** `rose-listen` computes the waveform server-side from the audio (mpg123 decoder, loaded on demand as `npm:mpg123-decoder@1.0.1`). **Not run and not checked under Deno.** It does nothing until `rose-listen` is redeployed. If decoding fails for any reason, the answer has no `bars` and the player draws a progress line.
- `scripts/generate-listen-audio.ts --bars` stays as a tool for future takes (adds `bars` to existing takes without calling ElevenLabs). It needs `mpg123-decoder`, which is **not** in `package.json`; a new recording through the script also writes `bars` when the decoder is available.

## After merge (in this order)

1. Migration `0014_rose_listen_entry.sql`, applied by Lovable, with Ivan's agreement.
2. Redeploy `rose-event` (accepts `listen_entry`) and `rose-listen` (waveform of answers).
3. Publish the site.
4. At the first real answer read aloud, check that the decoder works under Deno: the response carries `bars` (72 values) and the player draws bars, not a line. If not, the answer still plays, with a progress line.

## Also open

- `docs/rose-listen.md` is not on `main` (it is on `rose/listen-docs`); it still describes the old audiogram and needs a pass once that PR is merged.
- Nothing was deployed or published from here.

## Checks

- `vitest run`: 1339 passed, 1 failed (`fieldNotesV2 > says the new title everywhere`, the known CRLF failure on Windows, also red before this change). `mcpBundleFreshness` passes. `bun run build` passes; the regenerated MCP bundle was restored, not committed.
- Style baseline 581 (same as `main`), no allowlist entry added.
- `check:journeys` OK (19 routes, 503 links, text floor at 1440 / 768 / 390). A separate measurement of the Listen UI in states the static check never opens (row, transcript, mini-player, player in Listen and Read, badge) found no text under the floor.
- Contrast by calculation, Day and Dusk, 12 tests.
- Measured in Edge at 1440 and 390, Day and Dusk: row folded and open, playing, player, mini-player on `/aetherix` after leaving `/rose` (sound continues), badges on `/journal` and `/case-studies`.
- **Not tested:** real iOS (volume slider hidden is tested by user agent only), Media Session on a real lock screen, the browser voice fallback in a real browser, `prefers-reduced-motion` in a browser (unit-tested only), screen readers.

## Screenshots

28 captures (1440 and 390, Day and Dusk) are in `C:\Users\ivand\dev\captures-listen-component\` on Ivan's machine, not committed (a public repository, and 28 images). To attach by hand. They were taken before `6c560c1`, so the player and the row show a progress line where the summaries now have bars.

Task 2 of `.kiro/specs/kinesis-independent-layers/` (Requirements 1.2, 3.1, 3.3), the prerequisite for task 6 (data-layer API).

## What
- `kinesis_data_access.hpp`: `data_access` (abstract; the task 6 hybrid access picks local or remote per call) with named, copy-returning queries: `find_stream`, `list_streams`, `streams(filter)`, `find_channel`, `find_channel_by_id`, `list_channels`, `shard`, `read_records` (records as stored, opened on the front end), `local_bytes`, plus `propose`, `transact`, `can_transact`, `group_of`, `leads`, `now_ms`. `data_result<T>` carries `unreachable` (own type: clang 18 over libstdc++ 13 has no `std::expected`).
- `local_data_access<Cluster>` over any `stream_cluster`; `kinesis_service` and `lease_api` take any `data_layer` (a cluster, wrapped, or a `data_access`), so existing callers and tests are unchanged.
- `kinesis_records.hpp`: `read_shard` = `read_shard_raw` + `open_shard_read`, so a data node can answer raw (sealed) records.
- All 26 `read_catalog` sites and the shard reads in the service now go through the queries. Maintenance, on-demand and channel delivery keep callbacks (they run beside a replica).

## Measurement (Requirement 1.2)
Median of five runs, g++-13 -O2, `local_stream_cluster` + segment store:

| Call | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| PutRecords (10) | 32.8 us | 32.9 us |
| GetRecords (100) | 145.3 us | 146.9 us |
| DescribeStreamSummary | 5.44 us | 5.70 us |
| ListShards | 10.49 us | 10.55 us |

## Tests
New `kinesis_data_access_test`. Locally all 21 Kinesis test binaries pass (g++-13), the module compiles under g++ and clang 18, and clang-tidy-18 is clean on the new test and the Lease API test.

author: esmuellert
body:
## Summary

Query the attached terminal directly when `ui.theme` is `auto` (and in `codediff doctor`) so terminals over SSH or without `COLORTERM` / `COLORFGBG` automatically get `catppuccin-mocha` on dark backgrounds and `catppuccin-latte` on light backgrounds.

- **`ui::theme::probe`**: Send OSC 11 (`\x1b]11;?\x07`), XTGETTCAP (`RGB` / `Tc`), and DA1 (`\x1b[c`) over raw `stdin`/`stdout` via safe `rustix` termios + `poll`, returning as soon as the FIFO DA1 reply arrives or after a 40 ms bound on silent/headless PTYs without touching the alternate screen.
- **`Theme::resolve` / `Theme::from_terminal`**: Use `Rgb::is_dark()` from OSC 11 for dark/light classification, infer 24-bit support from XTGETTCAP or RGB OSC 11 replies (excluding `Apple_Terminal`, `NO_COLOR`, and `dumb`/`linux`), and add modern `TERM` / `TERM_PROGRAM` / `WT_SESSION` fallbacks while keeping `Theme::detect` deterministic.
- **`ui::main` & `codediff doctor`**: Probe before `loom::run` spawns the input thread so there is no reader race, and report probed `background`, `truecolor`, and default `theme` in `codediff doctor`.
- **Tests**: Unit tests for OSC 11 (1–4 digit channels, BEL/ST), XTGETTCAP, DA1 framing, and `Theme::resolve`, plus real Unix PTY tests verifying 24-bit `catppuccin-latte` and `catppuccin-mocha` selection with stripped environment variables.

author: m0odpp
body:
Refs #1072

## What and why

First PR of the two-PR split proposed in #1072 (under 1000 added lines), implementing the replication and ECS engine foundation required by `docs/spec/command-swing.md` (`CMD-SWG-006`, `CMD-SWG-DEV-001`, `CMD-SWG-007`) on top of the ECS mob architecture (#1077) and the merged `docs/swing.md` design note:

- **Replication (`mcrs_minecraft_replication`):**
  - Add `SwingRecipients` (`Observers` | `SelfAndObservers`) to `PlayerData::Swing` so self-included swings encode a single shared `ClientboundSwingAnimation` `Bytes` buffer for both observers and the actor without duplicating delivery to the actor, including solo players with zero other observers, while still suppressing delivery on same-tick `Despawn` or `Hold::Lose` and never replaying on late join (`SWG-DST-001`, `SWG-DST-002`).
  - Add `MobSignal::Swing` handled in `MobTrackers` with single-buffer shared delivery and zero farewell/replay emission.
- **Engine (`mcrs_minecraft_engine`):**
  - Add `SwingEligibility` (`AliveActor` | `CommandTarget`, `#[non_exhaustive]`) and `recipients` to `SwingPlayer`. `SwingPlayer::new`/`default_main` keep observer-only delivery and the alive, non-spectator rule. `SwingPlayer::command` gives self-included delivery and accepts spectators and dead players until corpse removal.
  - Add `PlayerOrder::Swing(SwingOrder)` (`hand`, `animation`, `duration`) and `player_order::swing`, which queues `SwingPlayer::command` and returns `DimensionChangeError::NoSwingMessages` when the world has no swing messages.
- **Physics (`mcrs_minecraft_physics`):** add `CORPSE_REMOVAL_TICKS`, shared by mob death removal, `swing_mob` and the player command check.
- **ECS Mob Swings (`mcrs_minecraft_engine_physics`, `mcrs_minecraft_engine_entity_motion_replication`):**
  - `Mob` requires `MobSwing(SwingTracker)` via `#[require]`. Add `MobSwingSpec` and `swing_mob`, which accepts dying mobs until corpse removal, uses the shared cooldown window, scales by status effects with unscaled wire duration, and queues `Swung` in `MobChanges::swings`.
  - Forward `MobChanges::swings` through `take_mob_news` and `publish_motion` onto each mob's current published tile as `MobSignal::Swing` without emitting extraneous `EntityEvent::Move` state updates for stationary mobs.
  - Update `docs/swing.md` to document the ECS mob swing path.

Known gap: `PlayerFileState.death_time` is only loaded from the save file and no system advances it yet, so the corpse-removal check for players depends on that future death clock.

Follow-up PR 2 (`Closes #1072`) will add `minecraft:swing_animation`, the `/swing` command (`mcrs_minecraft_command_*`), and end-to-end server integration tests.

## Observable result

- `EntityCodec` delivers `SwingRecipients::SelfAndObservers` swings to the actor once (including solo actors) and shares one encoded `Bytes` buffer with tracking observers; same-tick `Despawn`/`Hold::Lose` and late joins emit zero swing packets.
- `EntityCodec` / `MobTrackers` deliver `MobSignal::Swing` to all tracking viewers using one shared encoded `Bytes` buffer without backlog replay or farewell delivery on despawn.
- `PlayerSwingPlugin` and `player_order::obey` enforce `SwingEligibility::AliveActor` (`SWG-DEV-003`) vs `SwingPlayer::command` (`CMD-SWG-006`: allows spectators and dead players before corpse removal, suppresses at `CORPSE_REMOVAL_TICKS`, shares one cooldown window and same-tick limit across all swing sources).
- Stationary ECS mobs swinging through `swing_mob` publish only `MobSignal::Swing` on `TileEvents` (no extraneous `EntityEvent::Move`) and enforce cooldown and effect-scaling windows (`SWG-STA-002`, `SWG-STA-004`, `SWG-STA-005`).

## How it was checked

```text
$ GITHUB_ACTIONS=true CHECKS_BASE_REF=origin/main scripts/hooks/run-checks lint
comments: ok (0.6s)
parity: ok (4.9s): 3883 files; 50 vanilla claims outside parity files
fmt: ok (5.8s)

$ cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p mcrs_minecraft_replication -p mcrs_minecraft_engine_world -p mcrs_minecraft_engine -p mcrs_minecraft_engine_physics -p mcrs_minecraft_engine_entity_motion_replication -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 16.42s

$ cargo nextest run --locked -p mcrs_minecraft_replication -p mcrs_minecraft_engine_world -p mcrs_minecraft_engine -p mcrs_minecraft_engine_physics -p mcrs_minecraft_engine_entity_motion_replication -p mcrs_minecraft_server -E 'package(mcrs_minecraft_replication) | package(mcrs_minecraft_engine_world) | package(mcrs_minecraft_engine) | package(mcrs_minecraft_engine_physics) | package(mcrs_minecraft_engine_entity_motion_replication) | (package(mcrs_minecraft_server) & test(swing))'
     Summary [  11.164s] 213 tests run: 213 passed, 362 skipped

$ scripts/hooks/run-checks portability

no-std: ok (0.9s)

```

## Models

- Gemini (Antigravity): implementation, unit/integration tests, doc updates, and independent review pass.

author: choutkaj
body:
Chemistry-correctness fixes in the small-molecule readers and writers: normalization, XYZ, Molfile/SDF, SMILES and source stereo. Each fix comes with a test that fails on main.

## Findings

1. **Stated double bonds between aromatic atoms** (fixed). Localization ignored a stated double or triple bond on an atom that also carries aromatic bonds. Its inferred hydrogens did not count that pi bond, so such sources failed or gained hydrogens.
   - The stated bond is now that pi bond, but only where the atom's target valence leaves room for one: neutral C, N, N+ and the chalcogen cations.
   - Phenyl cations and anions and neutral boron now read correctly too. Main failed on them.

   Tests: `formats::aromatic_sources::stated_double_bonds_between_aromatic_atoms_meet_their_pi_bond`, `a_stated_double_bond_fills_a_charged_carbon_or_a_neutral_boron`.
2. **Aromatic O+ and S+** (fixed). Aromatic pyrylium and thiopyrylium oxygen and sulfur were given a target valence of 3, which added a hydrogen. They now take none. P and As no longer infer hydrogens on aromatic atoms either.
   Test: `formats::aromatic_sources::aromatic_positive_chalcogens_take_no_hydrogen`.
3. **SMILES writers dropped hydrogens on aromatic heteroatoms** (fixed). A Kekulé `P1C=CC=C1` was written as `p1cccc1`, and no reader can give that back its hydrogen. Any aromatic atom whose inferred hydrogens the organic form cannot carry is now written in brackets with an explicit count (`[pH]1cccc1`). This applies to the plain, isomeric and canonical writers.
   Test: `formats::writers::smiles_writers_round_trip_aromatic_heteroatom_hydrogens`.
4. **XYZ distance bonding** (fixed).
   - Bonds now use a firm tolerance of 0.3 Å.
   - A longer bond, up to 0.45 Å, is kept only between nonmetals whose largest valence allows it. Otherwise it is reported as `LongContactNotBonded` and left out.
   - Metal–carbon pairs bond within 0.2 Å, so Na and K no longer bond the carbon of a chelating carboxylate.
   - Metal–carbon contacts between 0.2 and 0.45 Å, such as Li–C at 2.28 Å in (MeLi)4, are reported as `LongContactNotBonded`.
   - Atoms beyond their largest valence are reported as `ValenceExceeded`.
   - Every frame reports `BondOrdersAndChargesUnknown`.
   - Resolution does not depend on atom order, and the brute-force cross-check in the unit tests covers the new rules.

   Tests: `formats::xyz::every_frame_reports_unknown_bond_orders_and_charges`, `bicyclopentane_bridgeheads_stay_unbonded`, `a_long_bond_within_valence_is_kept`, `atoms_beyond_their_largest_valence_are_reported`, `alkali_metals_do_not_bond_the_carbon_of_a_chelating_carboxylate`, `long_metal_carbon_contacts_are_reported_unbonded`.
5. **Molfile chiral flag 0** (fixed). Wedged stereo with an unset chiral flag was kept as absolute and nothing was reported. The stereo is still kept as drawn.
   - In a flat drawing, `MolfileInterpretIssue::AbsoluteStereoWithoutChiralFlag` now lists those elements and suggests an AND group.
   - 3D records never get this issue, because their coordinates specify the configuration.
   - The writer derives the flag from represented absolute stereo, so a rewrite sets it. An AND group keeps the relative meaning.

   Tests: `formats::molfile_stereo::an_unset_chiral_flag_keeps_wedged_stereo_and_reports_it`, `an_unset_chiral_flag_on_3d_coordinates_is_not_reported`.
6. **Wedges that marked no representable stereo** (fixed). A wedge at an atom without stereo used to fail the whole read. Examples are a wedge on CH2, a methyl, an sp2 C or an amine N.
   - Such a mark is now dropped with `NormalizationWarning::StrayWedge`, which Molfile reports as `MolfileInterpretIssue::StrayWedge` with its bond line.
   - A wedge at a stereocentre kekule cannot represent is reported as `MolfileInterpretIssue::UnrepresentableStereo { atom, bond, reason, location }`. The reason is one of:
     - a zero-order or dative bond, as on a P-chiral phosphine bound to Rh by a type-9 bond
     - more than four neighbors, as at an octahedral or trigonal-bipyramidal centre
     - several candidate atropisomeric axes
   - `StrayWedge` is now used only for atoms that cannot be stereogenic.
   - The parsers reject wedges on stated multiple bonds.
   - Atropisomer wedges on aromatic (type 4) bonds no longer depend on the Kekulé structure:
     - Both Molfile parsers now accept wedge codes on aromatic bonds.
     - Wedge assembly ignores the marked bond's order.
   - Marks that cannot be represented at all, such as `DoubleBondEither` on a stereo-capable bond, still fail.

   Tests: `formats::molfile_stereo::wedges_at_atoms_without_stereo_are_dropped_and_reported`, `wedges_marking_stereo_kekule_cannot_represent_are_reported`, `axis_wedges_on_aromatic_bonds_do_not_depend_on_the_kekule_structure`.
7. **Unpaired SMILES directional marks** (fixed). `C/C`, `C/C=CC`, `F/C=C` and a mark in a ring of fewer than eight atoms failed the read. Such a mark has no stereo meaning, so it is now dropped and listed in `SmilesInterpretationReport::unpaired_directional_bonds()`. Conflicting marks (`AmbiguousDirectionalBondMarks`) still fail.
   Test: `formats::smiles_stereo::directional_marks_without_a_partner_are_dropped_and_reported`.
8. **Optional: ambiguous hydrogen placement and declared valence on aromatic atoms** (not done).
   - Localization places no hydrogens, so there is no ambiguous placement to report. It fails only on odd pi demand.
   - Declared valence on aromatic atoms needs changes outside the cheap path, so it is left for later.

## API changes

- New `NormalizationWarning::StrayWedge { bond }`, `UnpairedDirectionalBondMark { bond }` and `UnrepresentableWedgeStereo { atom, bond, reason }`.
- Removed `SourceStereoNormalizationIssue::UnassembledTetrahedralBondMark` and `SourceStereoNormalizationIssue::UnpairedDirectionalBondMark`. Both are now warnings.
- New `MolfileInterpretIssue::StrayWedge { bond, location }`, `UnrepresentableStereo { atom, bond, reason, location }` and `AbsoluteStereoWithoutChiralFlag { elements }`.
- New public `kekule::molfile::UnrepresentableStereoReason` with `ZeroOrDativeBond`, `MoreThanFourNeighbors` and `SeveralCandidateAxes`.
- `MolfileBondStereo` Up, Down and Either are accepted on aromatic bonds. V2000 codes 1/4/6 and V3000 CFG 1/2/3 on aromatic bonds no longer fail.
- New `SmilesInterpretationReport::unpaired_directional_bonds()`.
- New `XyzInterpretIssue::BondOrdersAndChargesUnknown` (always first), `LongContactNotBonded { atoms, distance }` and `ValenceExceeded { atom, element, bonds, maximum }`.
- `XyzInterpretationReport::bond_tolerance()` is now 0.3 Å. New `long_bond_tolerance()` (0.45 Å) and `metal_carbon_bond_tolerance()` (0.2 Å).

Existing unit tests that relied on the old errors or tolerances were updated. `docs/stereo-support.md`, `docs/capabilities.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased → Fixed) describe the new behavior. The stereo-support doc now says that conflicting wedge marks are reported and only conflicting SMILES directional marks fail.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p kekule --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`: clean
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p kekule --no-deps --all-features`: clean
- `cargo test -p kekule --all-features`: all binaries pass (lib 1027, formats 267 with 2 ignored, doc tests 177)

author: urban233
body:
Step 1 of the plan to build the ready-to-run apps with Bazel (`.opp/plans/features/app-bazel-build.md`; this step's plan: `.opp/plans/app-bazel-runtime-bundle.md`, both committed here). The release path does not change: `build_app.yaml` and the cx_Freeze build are untouched.

## Summary

`bazel build //distribution/bundle` assembles a relocatable PyMOL-Open-Source app for the host platform, following the standalone-runtime design of kullik01/pymol-open-source-setup#8 with Bazel in place of uv and cx_Freeze:

```
PyMOL-Open-Source/
  PyMOL-Open-Source[.exe]   native launcher
  runtime/                  python-build-standalone CPython 3.13 (rules_python's own runtime)
                            with the app's packages and the in-repo PyMOL in site-packages
  licenses/                 README.txt index + one folder per bundled distribution
  manifest.json             app version, git commit, PyMOL wheel, lock SHA-256, target
```

- **Dependencies:** `distribution/requirements.in` lists the eight bundled packages at today's versions, locked for 3.13 by `bazel run //distribution:requirements.update` into `@app_pip`. `pymol-open-source-whl` is no longer pulled from PyPI: the app bundles `//tools/bazel/wheel:wheel` from the same commit.
- **One site-packages:** `merge_wheel_files` (`//tools/bazel:wheel_merge.bzl`, ported from open-protein-platform) copies the per-wheel extractions into one tree. PySide6 only finds shiboken6 and Qt when they are real siblings. Two wheels shipping the same path fail the build.
- **Overlays:** the files in `distribution/edited/` replace their originals. `edited/upstream.sha256` records the hash of each `modules/` original, so `edited_base_test` fails with porting instructions once an original changes. This replaces `EDITED_FOR_PYMOL_WHL_VERSION` for the Bazel-built app.
- **Launcher:** `distribution/launcher/launcher.c` sets `PYMOL_APP_ROOT` and runs `python -I -m pymol.startup_wrapper <args>`. On Linux and macOS it uses `execv`. On Windows it is a GUI-subsystem program that starts `pythonw.exe` with its command line verbatim and passes on its standard handles.
- **Licenses:** the rules of `setup_build_exe.py`, with one change: dist-info license files keep their folders, because numpy ships several `LICENSE.txt` files and flattening overwrote all but one. Python's license comes from the runtime repository itself (`tools/bazel/python_license.bzl`; rules_python does not export it). There is one repository per platform, so a build fetches only its own runtime.
- **CI:** `bazel.yaml` now also runs for app changes; only `distribution/docs/**` is ignored. The app's tests therefore run on Linux (manylinux_2_28), macOS arm64, macOS Intel and Windows.

## Test plan

- [x] `bazel test //...` on Windows: 15/15. New: `launcher_test`, `assemble_bundle_test`, `pyside6_import_test`, `edited_base_test`, `merge_wheel_files_test`, `bundle_smoke_test`.
- [x] `bundle_smoke_test` copies the bundle to a new folder and runs `smoke_test.py` headless with only the system folders on `PATH`: `SMOKE TEST OK (headless, PyMOL 3.2.0a, Python 3.13.13)`. It also fails on any `.pyc`, and on any text file naming Bazel's output base.

author: typoverflow
body:
This PR does three things:
- bumps RoboDojo to upstream main and its dataset to the latest revision;
- gives every simulator one way to describe an episode to its agent: the run log states it, and `rosbridge describe --domain-id N` prints it;
- gives the CLI the NumPy and SciPy that simulators' workspace hooks import.

It includes the former #53.

## RoboDojo upstream (cb2a37d → c3af1ac, 15 commits)
The five patches apply unchanged. The Isaac Lab and cuRobo pins are the same. XPolicyLab moved, but rosbridge doesn't export it.

- **Detailed instructions:** every task has `gen_detailed_instruction`, a description plus its scoring rubric. Upstream's policy receives it in `extra_info`. The instruction pair is drawn again on every reset, seeded by the layout.
- **Reworded instructions:** `fasten_screws` and `press_by_number`.
- **Stricter checks:**
  - `pour_by_language` scores and checks its order constraints only once *both* arms are home.
  - `solve_equation` needs one piece that is placed and aligned on both axes.
  - `make_kong` also keeps the standing pair `mahjong4_0/4_1` upright.
- **Articulation reset:** `reset_drive` objects (`press_by_number`'s and `swap_blocks`' buttons) start at their drive targets, pushed to PhysX on reset.

Scores of these five tasks before and after this PR are not comparable.

## RoboDojo dataset (0a709fe → 1127bda)
- Only mug 00014's `metadata.json` changed, and only the uncataloged `hang_mugs_random` uses that mug.
- `listing()` now replaces a cached listing from an earlier pin; before, it rejected it.
- The store adopted the new revision from a seed of hard links plus the one changed file, so the bump took no space.

## Task descriptions, every simulator alike
Before, every simulator did this its own way:
- RoboCasa and BiDex printed the instruction to the run log.
- HandsOn wrote `PROMPT.json`.
- The others gave none, although ABC's and RoboTwin's instructions change with the seed.

Now:

- **Backends:** each backend sets `description` after `reset`: `{"instruction": ...}`, read as upstream's evaluator reads it for its policy. A simulator whose evaluator gives more text adds it under its own name, such as RoboDojo's `detailed_instruction`. The worker proxies it.
- **Run log:** when the episode starts, the world node logs one `task description: {json}` line.
- **`rosbridge describe --domain-id N [--json]`:** reads that line back for the live run on the domain and prints it. It opens nothing (about 0.1 s) and writes no file. `rosbridge.runtime.description` writes and reads the line.

```console
$ rosbridge launch robodojo/stack-bowls --execution-mode stepped --domain-id 83 --detach
$ rosbridge describe --domain-id 83
Task: stack_bowls
Seed: 0
Instruction: Stack the three bowls together.

Detailed instruction:
## Description
...
```

| Simulator | `instruction` |
|---|---|
| ABC | The evaluator's prompt, without the checkpoint's `sim ` tag. `multi_drawer_search` lists every target in order (upstream advances them one at a time), as BiDex does with its segments. |
| LIBERO | The suite task's `Task.language`. |
| RoboTwin | Upstream's `build_instruction`, fed the expert dry run's episode info (seen, 100 episodes). |
| RoboCasa | `get_ep_meta()["lang"]` |
| BiDex | The task's language, as before. |
| HandsOn | The seeded `prompt`; `PROMPT.json` stays upstream's judge receipt. |
| RoboDojo | The layout's `instruction` and `detailed_instruction`; the `PROMPT.json` an earlier commit here added is gone. |
| BEHAVIOR | The activity's name; upstream gives its policy only a task id. |

## CLI dependencies
`rosbridge setup` runs simulators' workspace hooks in the CLI's interpreter, which had only PyYAML. HandsOn's hook imports NumPy and BiDex's also SciPy, so `rosbridge setup handson/…` and `rosbridge setup bidex/…` failed, on main as well.

Now:
- A `cli` extra declares NumPy and SciPy, and `tools/bootstrap.sh` installs `-e ".[cli]"`.
- The Pixi environments are unchanged; `pixi.lock` gains only rosbridge's two `extra == 'cli'` lines.
- Rerun `bash tools/bootstrap.sh`, then `rosbridge prepare <sim>` for each simulator (the ROS builds are stale; nothing downloads).

The docs' `../RoboEnv` asset-seed examples now name any verified depot, since RoboEnv is retired.

## Checks
- [x] RoboDojo: `prepare` covers all 42 tasks with no asset downloads.
  - Native smoke: 7 passed, twice.
  - The five affected tasks: 5 passed.
  - `test-ros`: 1 passed.
  - A native probe shows the new upstream checks are loaded.
- [x] `rosbridge describe --domain-id` printed descriptions of live LIBERO and RoboDojo runs in 0.11 s, with RoboDojo's full detailed instruction. All 8 backends produced their descriptions through their resets.
- [x] `rosbridge setup` for HandsOn and BiDex (`-ood --seed 1` and in-domain) works in 0.2–0.6 s. The profiles are byte-identical to the hooks' output inside the simulators' own environments.
- [x] All 8 simulators re-prepared after the dependency change, with no downloads.
- [x] Unit tests: 209 passed, 2 skipped. Shared ROS tests: 31 passed.
- [x] Native suites:
  - ABC: 38 passed
  - BiDex: 9 passed
  - RoboCasa: 9 passed
- [ ] Not run: the every-task RoboDojo sweep, and the native suites of LIBERO, RoboTwin, BEHAVIOR and HandsOn.

author: albertoriorda95
body:
**Summary**: the `proto` job fails with "had no .proto files" on the first PR that adds protobuf, because `buf breaking` has nothing on the base to compare with. The step now runs only when the base branch has .proto files.

**Evidence**

Before: failure seen on #59 (run 44948141057): `Failure: Module "path: "."" had no .proto files`.

After: the `proto` job was skipped on this PR (it does not touch `proto/`), so both branches were checked locally. The step's `run:` script was taken verbatim from this branch's `ci.yml` and run with `bash -e` (the Actions default shell), in a worktree of `feat/3-proto-buf-skeleton` (the head of #59), with buf 1.75.0 (the version pinned in that branch's `package-lock.json`):

```
=== BEFORE (old step), head = #59 branch, BASE_REF=main ===
Failure: Module "path: "."" had no .proto files
exit 1
=== AFTER, case 1: BASE_REF=main (no .proto on base) ===
No .proto files on main: skipping buf breaking
exit 0
=== AFTER, case 2a: BASE_REF=feat/3-proto-buf-skeleton (has .proto), compatible head ===
exit 0
=== AFTER, case 2b: same base, head changes the type of Ping.sent_at_ms ===
proto/demo/v1/ping.proto:13:3:Field "2" with name "sent_at_ms" on message "Ping" changed type from "int64" to "string".
exit 100
```

So a base with no .proto files skips the step, and a base with .proto files still runs `buf breaking` and fails on a breaking change.

**Merge danger**: two-way door. This only changes CI and is easy to revert. Blast radius: only PRs that touch `proto/` (the only ones that run the `proto` job). No service, user or client is affected.

**Not done**: nothing else changes in the workflow.

**Reviewer checks**
- Check that `git ls-tree` on `origin/${BASE_REF}` works with the checkout depth of the job. The `proto` job checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`, so the base branch ref exists. If that depth were ever reduced, `git ls-tree` would fail (`fatal: Not a valid object name`), `grep -q` would see nothing, and the step would **skip silently** instead of failing (checked locally with a ref that does not exist: exit 0). Keep `fetch-depth: 0` on this job.
- Check that the `.proto$` match on the whole base tree is the right condition (it is the same tree `buf breaking` reads through `.git#branch=`).

**Alignment impact**: none.

**Dependencies**: none.

## What and why

CI health check (last 100 CI runs: 92 passed, 3 failed, 5 cancelled; main has been green since). The two recent failures were the same kind: unit tests that hit the default 5 s timeout while building multi-megabyte ZIP fixtures.

- `tests/archivebombs.test.ts` "refuses a Word file with a part that expands past the per-file cap" (timed out at 5006 ms on Node 22 and 24) and `tests/epub.test.ts` "stops at a character limit..." (5258 ms). JSZip's pure-JavaScript deflate takes seconds on a busy runner with coverage on, so the tests failed on build time, not on what they check. (The third failure, an e2e run on Nov 20, has not recurred.)
- **Root-cause fix, no retries or longer timeouts:** `tests/zipfixture.ts` writes the same ZIPs with `node:zlib`. Measured locally: 51 MB manifest bomb 1.6 s to 0.26 s, 5001-file EPUB 2.5 s to 0.19 s, Word bomb 153 ms to 71 ms. The tests assert exactly what they did before; the manifest test's extra 30 s timeout is gone because it is no longer needed.
- **CI inefficiency:** `ci.yml` and `codeql.yml` now cancel a pull request's superseded run (group per PR number). Pushes to main use a per-run group with no cancellation, so every merged commit is still fully checked and the Deploy to Azure `workflow_run` trigger is unaffected. No check is removed or weakened.

Deploy to Azure workflow reviewed read-only: it needs the `production` environment approval, runs only for successful push CI on main in this repository, and serializes with `cancel-in-progress: false` (superseded pending runs show as cancelled by design). Not changed.

author: sargunv
body:
On the web, a map that loses its connection to the tile server shows nothing for tiles it no longer holds in memory, even when the browser's cache has them. Browsers don't serve an out-of-date copy unless the server allows it, and a failed check fails the fetch. Native shows its stored copy in the same situation.

Now, when a fetch can't reach the server and the map has no copy of its own, the transport fetches again in `force-cache` mode and uses the browser's stored copy. Copies whose server sent `must-revalidate` or `no-cache` are excluded, as on native. A copy of unknown age counts as expired, so the map keeps checking it with the server and swaps in the new one when the server answers.

Before and after: a map whose style and raster tiles were loaded once, then opened in a new tab after the server stopped answering (local server cutting connections, headless Chromium, WebGL2):

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: the style never loads](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cae04ab-e2ff-45dd-b181-512adcee3c96) | ![After: the stored tiles show](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f59f0a87-ee3a-418a-8469-dec6a84b03ec) |

The browser behavior this relies on, with the server cutting connections (Playwright, a persistent profile for WebKit):

| Out-of-date copy, server unreachable | Chromium | Firefox | WebKit |
|---|---|---|---|
| default fetch | fails | fails | fails |
| `force-cache` | stored copy | stored copy | stored copy |
| a `Cache-Control: max-stale` request header | fails (CORS preflight) | fails (CORS preflight) | fails (CORS preflight) |

A `max-stale` header doesn't help: it makes cross-origin requests preflighted, and Chromium's cache ignores it anyway.

author: mona-kecil
body:
## Why

Issue #15: Pocket 100M is the voice that can sound like you. It had only run from Python, and that was the riskiest assumption on the roadmap. This spike checks whether it runs from Swift, clones a voice, and keeps up with playback on an M1 with 8 GB.

## Answer

Yes. Through mlx-audio-swift 0.2.1 on the GPU, Pocket 100M starts speaking as fast as Python (0.08 s), clones a voice equally well (similarity 0.84–0.86 against Python's 0.857), and uses less memory (0.89 GB with a cache cap, against 1.17 GB). It generates about 20% slower than Python: 0.35 s per second of audio against 0.28 s. That still keeps up with playback up to about 2.8×.

The full table and findings are in [`spikes/pocket-mlx/README.md`](https://github.com/Mona-kecil/berang/blob/spike/pocket-mlx/spikes/pocket-mlx/README.md).

## How to review

This adds one standalone package under `spikes/pocket-mlx/`. It doesn't touch the app.

- `main.swift` times model calls the same way `bench/adapters/common.py` does. The part that matters for the app is `embedVoice`. It encodes the reference clip once into a 729 KB voice file. The library's public API re-encodes the clip on every call, which costs 0.3 s of first audio and 1.5 GB of memory.
- `README.md` has the numbers and what they mean for the app.

## Decisions this sets up

| For | Finding |
|---|---|

author: joyceyouu
body:
Closes #90

Only `backend/` changes. No shared contract touched.

## Why

First live ElevenLabs call through the proxy (2026-11-21 23:39 UTC, call `4f31c0a1-A`): the agent's configured first message was spoken, then every receptionist line ("Sorry?", "Okay.", "Okay, what's your-") was answered with the same greeting, three times, byte-identical, and question 1 was never asked. Six Lightning completions for three recorded agent turns: the other three were ElevenLabs re-sending the same conversation after the receptionist spoke over the agent, and the proxy generated a fresh reply each time while the recorder (rightly) ignored the duplicate position.

## What is different

- **Prompt** (`app/nemotron/prompts.py`): the line `Your first words on the call, exactly: "…"` is gone. The call-agent system prompt now says the call has already opened with the first message (quoted once), never to say it again, and that the next line is question 1 in one sentence. New rule: never repeat a sentence already said; if the receptionist did not catch it, say it differently and move on. The mock voice path never uses this prompt (it replays the fixture), so it is unchanged.
- **Replay on retry** (`app/routers/llm_proxy.py`): after recording the clinic's line, the proxy looks up `turns (call_id, agent_seq)`. If that position is already recorded it answers with the recorded text in the OpenAI shape ElevenLabs asked for (streaming: one content chunk, a stop chunk, `[DONE]`; non-streaming: a `chat.completion`), logs `replaying recorded turn N of call …; Lightning not called`, writes nothing and records no first-token metric. Speech and transcript therefore agree (product rule 3) and Lightning is never billed twice for one position.

## Tests (`backend/tests/test_llm_proxy.py`, 28 pass)

- `test_retry_replays_the_recorded_turn_without_calling_lightning` (replaces the old "different wording keeps one turn" case): a retry with the same history gets the recorded line as a well-formed SSE stream ending in `[DONE]`, Lightning saw exactly one request, the log names the replay, one turn and one event remain.
- `test_non_streaming_retry_replays_the_recorded_turn`: same for `stream: false`, and no second metrics row.
- `test_prompt_discloses_ai_and_never_books`: asserts the new wording, that `first words` is gone, and that the opening line appears exactly once.

## Commands run

```
export PATH=".claude/worktrees/.venv-joyce-builder/bin:$PATH"
scripts/check.sh   # ruff: All checks passed; pytest: 654 passed, 1 skipped; frontend lint: skipped, node_modules missing; secrets: ok
pytest -q backend/tests/test_llm_proxy.py   # 28 passed
```

## Not verified here

The third acceptance box (one live call after merge reaches question 1 with no repeated greeting) needs a real call once this is on main; I did not place one. Mocked in the tests: Lightning (`FakeLightning`), the database (`sqlite://`); no vendor request.

**Live verification (2026-11-22 00:05, coordinator).** Third acceptance box checked on the second live call (4a9ef935-A, backend 687121d with this PR): eight recorded lines, the disclosure spoken once by the first message and never repeated, no repeated agent line, question 1 (insurance) asked on the agent's first proxy turn, then price, then the slot question; no retry replays were needed.

author: phanmi
body:
## Related issue

Part of #113. This PR does not close it: two parts of step 13 remain, listed under Scope. #117 was the first part, #118 follows from it, and #119 and #120 came from this PR's first review.

## What changed

#117 split food verification into separate checks, all in the Python agent. This PR is steps 8 to 12 of `docs/VERIFICATION_OVERHAUL.md`: what those checks needed from Java and from the worker protocol, and one decision the eval led to.

- **Protocol version 3.** `contracts/agent/v2/` is renamed to `v3/` with `git mv` and edited in place. A version 2 peer fails with `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`.
- **A call's foods are saved in one transaction.** The operation `food.insert_all` replaces `food.insert`. It carries every food of one `recordFood` call, and `FoodService.insertFoods` saves the list in one transaction: when Java rejects one food, none is saved.
- **A failure code for a check the model cannot answer.** When the date check gets four answers it cannot use, the run fails as `provider/MODEL_ANSWER_UNUSABLE`. Java answers with HTTP 502 and its own text. Before, this was a provider failure with HTTP 500. The text ends with "Please try again" when the run saved nothing. When an earlier `recordFood` call of the same chat saved, it says that some foods may already be saved and to check the Calendar before sending the message again (R8).
- **The content check is forced off, and kept in the code.** The `run` payload has a required boolean, `checkNutrition`, and Java sends `false` in every chat. The check, its food correction and their tests are unchanged, and the eval harness still runs every case with the check off and on.
- **A database failure while the food transaction opens or commits** is reported as a failed database write, not as a worker failure.

## The content check: forced off

Decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-21, from the many-foods run under Eval results. #113's description records it.

- **Why.** Even on the low-cost models, the nutrition values the chat model estimates from the first prompt are good enough. With the check on, fully correct chats were level on `gpt-6-luna`, higher on `claude-haiku-5-5` and lower on `deepseek-flash`, for more than twice the model requests in each chat.
- **How.** #113 first asked for a Settings switch (from #98). It was built in steps 9 and 10, then removed with its endpoint and its file when the check was forced off. `PythonAgentService` sends the constant `CHECK_NUTRITION`, which is `false`.
- **What a chat loses.** Nothing after the chat model changes a nutrition value. In the run, the check fixed 6 wrong foods, all on `claude-haiku-5-5`, and made 10 correct foods wrong.
- **No frontend file changes.** The shared settings code the first review asked for (R5) was removed with the switch, so the provider settings code is what `main` has.

## Scope

- Included:
  - `contracts/agent/v3/`, with the schema and fixtures for `run.checkNutrition`, `food.insert_all` and the new failure code.
  - Java: the bridge handler `FoodInsertAllHandler`, `FoodService.insertFoods` and its transaction, the protocol classes, `PythonAgentService`, and `ProviderExceptionHandler` for the 502.
  - Python: the worker's validation and session for version 3, `recordFood` saving its list in one operation, the failure code, and the eval harness sending `checkNutrition`.
  - The docs for what changed, and the plan's record of steps 8 to 12.
- Explicitly excluded:
  - **The write-up of the 2026-11-21 run under `docs/evals/`** (step 13). The generated report is git-ignored. Its numbers are below, in #113 and in the plan.
  - **A run of #104's four categories with the name and count check off** (step 13). It is a paid run and has not been made.
  - A Settings switch for the content check. It was built and removed, as above.
  - Proving that the name and count check works, and switching it on (#118).
  - The workout plan's transaction failure (#119), and one list of write operations for both languages (#120).
  - The other failures after a save. They still answer "Please try again later" (R8 was fixed for `MODEL_ANSWER_UNUSABLE` only). No issue holds them yet.

## Acceptance criteria

From #113 as it is now worded. A box is ticked only where the criterion is met and a check was run for it.

- [x] A design for the overhaul is presented and approved before code. It says what result on the baseline run counts as done, and how it meets the requirements from #98, #100, #101 and #104's eval. *Met in #117.*
- [x] A `python -m evals --cheap-models --category many-items` run with the overhauled tool is reported in the PR beside the baseline. *See Eval results. The write-up under `docs/evals/` is not in this PR.*
- [x] No food is saved until every check that is switched on has run on it. A corrected value is saved without a second check.
- [x] Python tests drive the new behavior through the real agent loop, tool registry and `recordFood`.

**Dates and converted units (#104's eval)**

- [x] The overhaul has one tool that checks only that a record's date is correct. Python tests drive a record with an invented date through the real agent loop and that tool. *Met in #117.*
- [ ] The overhauled tool does not accept a record whose unit is converted from the user's. Python tests cover the grande latte saved as 16 fl oz. *Partially met: the name and count check does this and Python tests cover it, but the check is off in every run until #118.*
- [ ] The PR also reports a `--cheap-models` run of #104's categories beside #116's low-cost run. *#117 reports the run of 2026-11-18, made with the name and count check on. No run has been made with that check off.*

**Content check off, and protocol version 3 (#98)**

- [x] No chat of the app runs the content check or its food correction: Java sends `checkNutrition: false` in the `run` payload of every chat, and Java tests prove it. The date check still runs. *The name and count check is off as well (decided 2026-11-18).*
- [x] The content check, its food correction and their tests stay in the code, and the eval harness can run a case with the check on. *The run under Eval results did.*
- [x] The protocol version 3 schema and fixtures reject a `run` without `checkNutrition` or with a non-boolean value, the Java and Python fixture tests agree, and a version 2 peer fails with `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`.

**Tool results (#100)**

- [x] A food recorded from a file the chat model read in the same chat can be accepted and saved. *Met in #117.*
- [x] The checks and the corrections receive this run's tool results, and no keys. *Met in #117.*
- [ ] A food that matches neither the conversation nor a tool result is not saved. *Partially met: the name and count check does this and Python tests cover it, but the check is off in every run until #118.*
- [x] Python tests drive the file-based flow through the real agent loop, tool registry and `recordFood`. *Met in #117.*
- [x] Adding another tool needs no change to the registry or the agent loop. *Met in #117.*

**Partial saves (#101)**

- [x] A failure while checking a multi-food message saves none of its foods. *True for one `recordFood` call. The next criterion covers a message the chat model spreads over two calls.*
- [ ] Resending a multi-food message after such a failure does not create duplicate food records. *Partially met. For one `recordFood` call it is met: nothing of the call was saved. When the chat model spreads a message over two calls and the second fails its date check, the first call's foods stay saved. The error now says so and tells the user to check the Calendar before sending the message again (R8). A user who sends it again anyway still saves those foods twice.*
- [x] Java saves a message's foods in one transaction: when it rejects one, none is saved. The protocol version 3 contract covers the new operation.
- [x] The time a multi-food message takes with the checks on is measured before and after, and reported in the PR. *See Eval results.*

author: eelgaev
body:
On 27B over two Sparks, each W4A4 layer's last FFN sum used to travel with nothing left to compute, and it was half the step. Half 1's FFN now runs in three parts (5/8, 1/4, 1/8 of it), so that last sum is an eighth of the step and the bigger parts' sums travel during the next part's FFN. An 8K step goes 4,096 + 2,560 + 1,024 + 512. The mixer and its two half sums don't change.

Why it's exact: the split is by tokens only. The mixer/GDN run whole. Every FFN part is at least 512 tokens, so the W4A4 GEMM keeps the same tiles and K order (checked with `a4_dense` at every part size), and the norms, quant and residual adds are per token. Each sum keeps the whole step's wire type and rank order. The FP8-MLP layers 56-63 stay whole. Gemma and Flash-Next don't take this path.

Also in here:
- Chained finishes now point at the first finish, the one that owns the output memory. That's a no-op for the existing callers.
- A micro all-reduce reserves the larger half of the step, so small parts don't grow the pinned buffers.

Two Sparks, the docs command, ABBA, fresh server per arm (tok/s, two requests each):

| | 8K | 32K | 1 user |
|---|---|---|---|
| halves (`=2`) | 3,045 / 3,056, 3,037 / 3,050 | 2,846 / 2,839, 2,851 / 2,849 | 49.2 / 49.5 |
| half 1 in two (`=3`) | 3,217 / 3,234, 3,218 / 3,229 | 2,992 / 2,982, 3,000 / 2,988 | 49.5 / 49.9 |
| half 1 in three (`=4`, default) | 3,244 / 3,255, 3,258 / 3,262 | 3,032 / 3,024, 3,029 / 3,026 | 49.2 / 50.1 |

That's +6.7% at 8K and +6.4% at 32K, and decode ties. The logprob hashes for 8K and 32K prompts are identical in all three arms, and the 1-user deterministic text matches the reference.

Switch: `LEGION_DEBUG_QWEN35_TP_PARTS=2` on both ranks gives the old halves. `LEGION_DEBUG_QWEN35_TP_HALVES=0` still runs layers whole.

author: hyranno
body:
KiCad 10 allows several symbol pins with the same number but different names or types (10 symbols / 54 pads in both the KiCad 9.0.2 and 10 libraries, e.g. `Diode:BAT54SDW`, `74xx_IEEE:74278`). `kicad_part!` rejected them ("pin \"6\" is defined twice with different names or types").

## Approach

Each duplicate pin becomes its own pin of the part, connected to the others of its pad inside the part (like stacked pins). Public types are unchanged.

- **Order / IDs**: pins are ordered as KiCad picks the "first" pin of a pad for the netlist: by unit (0 first), then by library position in the unit (x ascending, then y descending), then file order. This rule was determined with kicad-cli on custom symbols (unit order vs. file order, x/y swaps, rotation, placement); for all 54 library pads it gives the same result as plain unit/file order. The first pin keeps the pad number as its ID (`6`), the others get `#2`, `#3`, ... (`6#2`). `pins:` renames them with the pad number (first) or `6#2`.
- **SPICE**: the model (`Sim.Pins` uses pin numbers) connects the first pin; the others are connected to it.
- **Runtime**: `KicadPartInfo::check_pins` accepts pins on one pad when they are in the same internal connection group (`DuplicatePad` otherwise). The `.net` writer emits one node per pad with the first pin in `Part::pin_ids` order, as KiCad does.

## Comparison with KiCad 10.0.8

`tests/golden/kicad_libraries_duplicate_pins.net` (BAT54SDW + 74278) matches `kicad-cli` on the nodes (`tools/compare_kicad_cli_netlist.py --library-symbols`), apart from tool limitations noted in the test. Accepted differences (documented in `doc/kicad_part_macro.md` and `doc/erc.md`):

- ERC does not report two outputs that are duplicate pins of one pad (KiCad: `pin_to_pin` when they are wired together), and reports a pad whose only pins are same-type duplicates as not connected.
- Automatic net names of multi-unit parts differ as before (KiCad adds unit letters, e.g. `Net-(D1A-K)` vs. `Net-(D1-A-Pad6)`); this is not specific to duplicate pins.

## Testing

- New tests: `symbol::tests::test_duplicate_pins`, `test_pad_of_two_pins`, `part::tests::test_duplicate_pins` (fixture `test:DUP_AMP`, first pin by position, rename, SPICE mapping), `kicad::part::tests::test_check_pins`, golden `kicad_libraries_duplicate_pins.net`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo test -p cuprite_wire_kicad_lib -- --ignored`, clippy, `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`

body:
## Zweck

`data ensure` lädt eine gecachte Datei neu, wenn ihr angefragtes Fenster ein Loch über 14 Tage hat, und hält es für einen fehlgeschlagenen Download. Hat die Quelle dort selbst keine Daten, hat die neue Datei dasselbe Loch, und jede Anfrage lud sie erneut.

## Änderungen

- Der Downloader hält Löcher über 14 Tage in `.quality.json` fest (`long_holes`). Ein Loch, das der vorige Download auch hatte, landet in `confirmed_holes`.

- Die 14-Tage-Grenze steht in `fwbg.data.quality.LONG_HOLE_DAYS`.

- Neu: `long_holes`, Bestätigung per Überlappung, drei Downloads hintereinander (Loch → bestätigt → gefüllt), `ensure` akzeptiert ein bestätigtes Loch, lehnt ein unbestätigtes anderswo ab und ignoriert einen veralteten Report.

author: someone1128
body:
## What this adds

Adds **i2v.ai** to the **Video Creation** section (and its Chinese counterpart, **AI 视频创作**), in both `README.md` and `README-CN.md`, using the canonical 4-column table schema, plus one line in `CHANGELOG.md` under November 2026.

Affiliation, as the contributing guide requires: **I maintain i2v.ai, so this is a self-submission.**

## Why it fits the inclusion criteria

**Unique and practical first** — the differentiator is not another model endpoint. Every paid task returns a USD quote *before* submission and accepts a caller-set `maxCostUsd` ceiling, so an agent can price a job and decline it up front instead of finding out the cost afterwards. The same pricing call backs the `estimate_cost` tool, so a client can budget without submitting anything.

**Broad applicability** — one endpoint and one API key cover 12 image models and 16 video models (28 total), spanning text-to-image, text-to-video and image-to-video, so a workflow that needs several models does not need several provider integrations. Two clients ship for the same model set: a remote MCP server with OAuth 2.1 + dynamic client registration, and a local stdio server started with `npx -y @i2v-ai/cli mcp`.

**Actually usable, with verifiable pricing** — pricing is per task in USD, quoted per model and per parameter set, and the machine-readable model catalogue is at https://i2v.ai/api/v1/generation-models . The endpoint answers requests without a token with `401` plus a `WWW-Authenticate` header, so a reviewer can confirm it is live without an account.

**Still alive** — actively developed; the MCP server is published in the official MCP registry as `io.github.i2v-ai/mcp` (v1.1.1), the CLI is on npm as `@i2v-ai/cli`, and the TypeScript and Python SDKs are on npm (`@i2v-ai/sdk`) and PyPI (`i2v-ai`).

## Popularity & traction (transparent about the current stage)

This is an early-stage product and the reach numbers are small, so I am stating them plainly rather than implying more:

- The MCP server is indexed in the official MCP registry and rated **A** by Glama's automated tool-definition scoring (3.9/5 across 14 tools) — https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/i2v-ai/i2v-cli
- The CLI and both SDKs are published and installable today (npm / PyPI), with MIT-licensed sources on GitHub.
- Usage is measured in API tasks rather than a seat count; I am not going to claim a user number I cannot verify.

If that is below the bar for this list, feel free to decline — but the capability described above (quote before charge, per-task cap, one key for 28 models, MCP-native) is real and testable, which is what the entry is meant to convey.

## Conventions followed

- Ran `python3 scripts/format_readmes.py` after the edit; it left the tables unchanged (both rows already canonical, 4 columns).
- Descriptions are within the limits: **569 characters** (EN, limit 600) and **310 characters** (CN, limit 450), measured as rendered text with markup and URLs excluded.
- No version numbers or release dates in the description, per the "stable descriptions" rule; the Fees column uses the broad label `Free/Paid` (免费/付费).
- Links point at the official site, the API docs and the MCP docs; all three resolve.
- No new `docs/` pages; no deep-dive discussion was created because this entry does not need one.

author: gijsrommers
body:
## What

A fork no longer copies what it will only read.

- **Function facts, loaded-file slots, trait method names**: held by the snapshot and its forks together (`SharedTable`, an `Rc<[T]>`: indexed like a `Vec`, no test per read). The request that first changes a table (loads a file, declares a class) copies it once; writes that change nothing are skipped. `trait_method_names` is a sorted flat array instead of a `HashMap`.
- **Caches a request fills** (site cells, method-site records, class checks, function links, native links, closure signatures): the snapshot keeps what the boot filled as `UnitCache::base` (without entries that hold objects); a fork starts empty and makes a cell from the snapshot's at the miss that already existed. Nothing a request writes reaches `base`.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/2026-11-22-a-fork-shares-the-code-table-and-fills-its-caches.md` (numbers, the three ways measured, what was turned down, the was/is table). `docs/architecture.md` 5.4 updated. Harness: `crates/runtime/examples/fork_cost.rs` (safe; the counting allocator is `unsafe` and lives outside the repo). Isolation test: `a_forks_code_table_and_caches_are_its_own_when_it_changes_them`.

## Numbers (main `78637583` against this branch)

| per fork, synthetic app (41 files, 3,700 functions, 328 classes) | main | this |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| bytes | 2,631,770 | 129,066 |
| allocations | 4,627 | 820 |
| instructions | 4,026,173 | 892,160 |
| time (10,000 forks) | 513 to 523 µs | 75 µs |

Gate (12 pairs, millions of instructions per request): `/api/hello` 31.847 → 30.779 (-3.35%), `/api/posts?page=2` 126.751 → 126.276 (-0.38%).

Benchmarks (median of 7 runs, instructions): hierarchy +1.02%, typed-objects +1.11% (main itself spans 6,109 to 6,253M there), closures +0.62%, properties +0.61%, function-objects +0.58%, objects +0.56%, fib +0.43%, the rest within 0.2%. **Two are over the 1% rule**: they read the most class checks and property sites (a null test on a lazily made array, two instructions per read, and +1 instruction per read of the facts through `Rc<[T]>`). The decision file shows the eager variant that has no test and what it costs in the gate.

Tests: `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 893 passed, the same 16 failures as the validation baseline on this machine; phpt 6,918 passed, 0 failed.

author: akmalmuhammed
body:
## What failed

`apps/api/tests/test_mcp_tools_read.py` went red when CI ran just after midnight in Doha (about 21:00 to 21:12 UTC): PR #329's `api` check on 21 Nov 2026 and, very likely, PR #332's shard 6.

## Root cause: the fixture, not the tools

- The tools are right. `owner/asks.py::_day` and `agent/facts.py` both work out "today" in the shop's own zone (`tenants.timezone`, Asia/Qatar) and bound it from that zone's midnight. The SQL day buckets cast with `at time zone <shop zone>`, and nothing reads `current_date` or `::date` in UTC. So there is no production bug and no CHANGELOG line.
- `tests/mcp_tools_support.py::seed_trade` seeded "today's" orders at `now() - 0.2h` and `now() - 0.1h` (12 and 6 minutes back). From 00:00 to 00:12 Doha that reaches back across Doha midnight, so the order is *yesterday's* in the shop's day and `today`, `orders {"when": "today"}`, `sales_summary {"period": "today"}` and the yesterday and named-date checks do not count it.

## Fix

`just_now(hours)` in `mcp_tools_support.py` returns "about `hours` ago, but never before the shop's day began". The age is cut to a share of the time the day has run (growing with `hours`), so the order stays today's and older seeds stay older than newer ones. `seed_trade` and the three other "placed just now" orders in the read-tools tests use it. A parametrised test (`test_orders_seeded_as_just_now_are_in_the_shops_own_day_at_any_hour`) pins it at nine clocks around the boundary, with no database needed.

The `hours_ago=3` order in the insights test is left alone on purpose: that test is about an order waiting too long, which is relative age.

## Proof

No time library is installed, so I froze the clock with a throwaway pytest plugin (not in the repo): it replaces `datetime.datetime` for every module and rewrites SQL `now()` to the frozen moment. `tests/test_mcp_tools_read.py`, whole file:

| Frozen clock (UTC) | Doha | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21:05:00 | 00:05 | 6 failed | 23 passed |
| 21:00:30 | 00:00:30 | n/a | 23 passed |
| 21:11:30 | 00:11:30 | n/a | 23 passed |
| 21:30:00 | 00:30 | 23 passed | 23 passed |
| 00:30:00 | 03:30 | 23 passed | 23 passed |
| 20:56:00 | 23:56 | n/a | 22 passed, 1 skipped (the next-booking test skips within 10 minutes of midnight, by design) |

With the new unit test the file is 32 tests, all passing at 21:05 UTC. So 21:30 and 00:30 UTC do not fail even before the fix; the failing window is only the 12 minutes after Doha midnight, 21:00 to about 21:12 UTC.

## Left as is

The other `datetime.now(QATAR)` and `date.today()` uses in `apps/api/tests` pair with production code that also uses the Doha day, or carry at least a one-day margin (`+ timedelta(days=2)`). Details are in the PR conversation.

body:
The docs half of batch B9 of the [living-documents cleanup](https://github.com/rusty-photon/rusty-photon/blob/main/docs/plans/living-documents-cleanup.md) (#1282), the last batch. B9 takes every living document that batches B1 to B8 did not name: the CI and runner skills, workspace.md's own history, the references, the READMEs under `tools/` and `packaging/`, and the design docs of crates and services no batch had (calibrator-flats, filemonitor, polar-align, zwo-focuser, the rp crates and others).

After this PR, a scan of all living Markdown with the guard's matcher finds only the four quoted "don't write this" examples in workspace.md (plus the excepted `#` inside one upstream URL in qhyccd-rs's README). **workspace.md**
- **§ Holding a transitive dependency back** described a rust-embed hold at 8.11.0. The lock has 8.14.0. The section now keeps the method and says no transitive crate is held. The `.bazelrc` notes that rest on the old hold are the build-and-CI code PR's.

**Skills, references, READMEs, crate and service docs.** Each was read in full. qhyccd-sdk-manual.md was the exception: it is vendor text, so only its own notes were read.

- **workflow-documents.md:** said "a human wires it into a registration", that all three trigger shapes ship, and that dispatch state lives in rp's counters. Each is corrected.

## For the owner

1. **The refvals test checks nothing.** `crates/rp-ephemeris/tests/reference_values.rs` compares against `refvals/*.json`, but no JSON file has ever been committed, so the test passes empty. The docs now say so. Should a reference set be generated and committed?
2. **`priority` is stored and editable, but no selection reads it.** `decision.rs` orders by transit, progress and the filter in the wheel. Is that intended?
3. **A factory-fresh QHY camera does not enumerate on a Mac.** qhy-camera does not call the SDK's `OSXInitQHYCCDFirmware*`. packaging-macos.md called wiring it "a tracked follow-up", but no issue exists. Should I file one?
4. **rp's primitive ephemeris tools check the ICRS bounds in their own `validate_icrs`.** They build `rp_ephemeris::IcrsCoord` instead of going through `rp_vocabulary::IcrsCoord::try_new`, which is the duplication rp-vocabulary exists to remove. The doc no longer claims every check goes through the crate.
5. **Smaller stale claims, left because the repository cannot settle them:**

body:
Closes the theme ticket from J Moore (support ticket `d14eae0b`, "I want a christmassy theme and a high school musical theme!"): two whole new looks, built the same way as the six that already exist.

## Christmas
Red, green and gold as the ticket asked:

- pine page with a faint snow, a threaded fringe of red/gold/green baubles hanging across the top, and a gold-and-red bead garland down the sidebar
- cards get a gold edge with a red ribbon across the top
- Fraunces headings
- palettes: **holly** (red), **gold**, **snow**

## Opening Night (High School Musical Jr)
The school-musical read, not the Disney logo:

- aubergine house lights down, one gold spot from above, red velvet at the wings
- plum curtain sidebar with a column of marquee bulbs down the edge
- gold playbill cards, serif titles
- palettes: **marquee** (gold), **curtain** (red), **spotlight** (warm white)

## What changed

| file | change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/lib/themes.ts` | the two theme entries, three palettes each |
| `src/index.css` | per-theme CSS for both, plus dark-mode restatements so the generic dark rules don't sand them off |
| `src/lib/theme.ts` | dark palettes for both |

author: hybridindie
body:
Closes #76

The pipeline corrected the run it was in but never learned. Confirmed causes now become constraints that every later plan and brief carries.

- **`.agents/plan-constraints.yaml`** holds `{paths, constraint, source, date}` entries, committed with the repo.
- **`dispatch.py learn --unit U --paths <globs> --constraint "..."`** appends a lesson. An identical one is kept once, and `prepare` doesn't treat the uncommitted file as a dirty checkout.
- **Briefs** (from `prepare` or `plan.py brief`) gain a "Lessons from earlier runs" section, limited to lessons whose paths overlap the track's `owns`.
- **`plan.py check`** prints `LEARNED <story>: ...` for lessons touching each story's `owns`, so story-decomposer applies them when splitting.
- **Validation:** a malformed file is a PlanError; a missing file means no lessons.
- **Skills:** wave-dispatcher 2.4.0 proposes a lesson when a block's cause is confirmed and records it only after a person approves. story-decomposer 6.3.0 applies the `LEARNED` lines. The schema doc describes the file.

## Test plan
- `pytest tests .agents/scripts/tests` (no global git config): 333 passed, 9 of them new. They cover recording, de-duplication, overlap-only surfacing in briefs and `check`, and malformed files.
- `lint-skills.py`, `sync-skill-wrappers.py --check`: PASS

body:
Release prep for **oats-bb 0.2.0**, step 3 of the plan in oats-project/oats#2074. It follows OATS 0.70.2, which is released and verified: npm `@awebai/oats` and `@awebai/oats-pi` 0.70.2 are built from 422461c5.

- **Versions:** 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 in `package.json`, `plugin/package.json` and its lock, `oats-package/oats-package.json` and the `oats.bb` capability.
- **Team image:** `@awebai/oats-pi` 0.70.0 → 0.70.2 in `container/package.json`, `container/pi-settings.json` and `container/package-lock.json`.
  - I edited only the lock's bridge entry: its version, URL and integrity, read from the registry.
  - I did not regenerate the lock: npm 10 here would drop the lock's `libc` fields.
  - 0.70.2 has the same peer dependencies as 0.70.0.
  - The image build checks the settings against the installed version.
- **pi contract test:** `test/contract/pi/Dockerfile` now uses `OATS_VERSION` 0.70.2. The contract run then tests the kernel and bridge the image ships, the new dialog claim included. The plugin's real run keeps the 0.70.0 floor.
- **CHANGELOG:** "Unreleased" becomes "0.2.0".
  - It gains an **Upgrade** section: the pin; oats.aweb >= 1.48.0, `@awebai/oats-pi` and `piAgentDir` for pi (`/state/home/.bb-pi` in the image); the macOS limit (oats-bb#22); respawn.
  - It gains a **plugin** section for #18 to #20: the agent panel and its page, the display filter, the faster status reads, 44 px targets, and the module split.
  - The provider sections are #21's and #23's, unchanged apart from the "checked against" versions.
- **README:** the release line, the install pin `@v0.2.0`, the real-run note, and the pi section's "checked against" line. It now says the dialog claim comes from `@awebai/oats-pi` 0.70.2.

Ran: `npm run validate` (manifests ok) and `node --test test/unit/container-image.test.mjs test/unit/container-pin.test.mjs` (6 pass). CI runs the rest, the image acceptance and the pi contract included.

Once this merges and main's CI is green, I tag `v0.2.0` on the merge commit. That tag is the release: there is no workflow and no GitHub Release.

author: pbxg33k
body:
Refs #86 (not closing: not yet confirmed in a browser)

**Cause:** `@api-platform/admin` only subscribes records to Mercure from its guessers (`ListGuesser`, `ShowGuesser`, `EditGuesser` call `useMercureSubscription`). The "All download jobs" list and show pages are plain react-admin `<List>`/`<Show>`, so they never opened a subscription. Server delivery, topics and cookie were fine.

**Changes**
- PWA: `LiveListUpdates` / `LiveRecordUpdates` (in `components/admin/downloads/common.tsx`) subscribe the shown records; ids are memoized so subscriptions aren't reopened on every render. `SubresourceList` re-fetches the Files/Events tabs when the job's `updatedAt` changes, keeping the previous rows meanwhile.
- New jobs: `AdminDownloadJobPublisher` also publishes inserted jobs on the collection topic `{origin}/admin/download_jobs` (already covered by the admin subscribe selector). The job list subscribes to it through the data provider's public `subscribe()` and re-fetches (debounced 500 ms).

**To verify:** with "All download jobs" open as an admin, start a download: the row should appear and its state change without reloading.

Tests: publisher test covers the collection topic; full PHPUnit suite green; `tsc` and lint clean.
